hayomYom.english: From a letter by my father:* The 19th of Kislev...the festival on which "He redeemed our soul in peace," and our soul's illumination and vitality were given to us, this day is Rosh Hashana for Chassidus bequeathed us by our sacred forebears, identical with the teachings of the Baal Shem Tov. "This day is the beginning of Your works," the fulfillment of the true intention behind the creation of man on earth, which is to call forth revelation of the light of the inward part of our holy Torah. On this day, that light is called forth, in a general way, for the entire year. It is our duty, on this day, to awaken our hearts with an innermost, elemental desire and will, in the very core of our heart, that G‑d illuminate our souls with the light of His Inner Torah. "From the depths I called to You, O G‑d," to elicit the depth and inwardness of G‑d's Torah and G‑d's mitzvot from the inwardness and essence of the Infinite (May He be blessed), to illuminate the inwardness of our souls. That all our being (meaning our total existence, the essence and the extensions) be devoted to Him alone, to banish from within us any of the natural traits that are evil and unworthy. Instead, all our works and affairs (our Avoda, meaning - davening and Torah and mitzvot, and our worldly undertakings necessary for the maintenance of the body), be with sincere intention for the sake of Heaven, as G‑d wishes. May G‑d the Merciful Father have compassion upon us and lead us along the good and righteous path and may we "see His face in uprightness.Tehillim 11:7. * Dated, Wednesday, Kislev 16, 5662. The chazan does not wear a tallit for Mincha or Maariv - neither on weekdays, Shabbat and festivals, or Rosh Hashana. Yahrzeit of the Mezritcher Maggid, Tuesday, Parshat Vayeishev 5533 (1772). He is interred in Anipoli. The Alter Rebbe was released from his first imprisonment, Kislev 19, Tuesday, Parshat Vayeishev 5559 (1798) towards evening. From the Alter Rebbe's letter: This indeed must be made known, that on the day G‑d made for us, the 19th of Kislev, Tuesday (the day on which "it was good" was said twice in Torah) yahrzeit of our holy teacher whose soul is in eden, while I was reading in the book of Tehillim the verse "He redeemed my soul in peace," before beginning the following verse, I emerged in peace by (the act of) the G‑d of peace. * * * A day of farbrengen and good resolutions towards establishing times to study the revealed Torah and Chassidus publicly, and in bolstering the ways of chassidim in true friendship. It is customary to apportion volumes for the study of the Talmud, according to the procedure set out in Igeret Hakodesh "Hochei'ach Tochi'ach". In Lubavitch, since the year 5663 (1902-03) this allocation was made on Tevet 24, yahrzeit of the Alter Rebbe, there not being time on Kislev 19.
hayomYom.hebrew:
ממכתב אאמו"ר:
… יט כסלו … החג אשר פדה בשלום נפשנו ואור וחיות נפשנו ניתן לנו, היום הזה הוא ראש השנה לדא"ח אשר הנחילנו אבותינו הקדושים זצוקלל"הה נ"ע זי"ע, והיא היא תורת הבעש"ט ז"ל.

זה היום תחלת מעשיך, שלימות הכוונה האמיתית בבריאת האדם עלי ארץ, להמשיך גילוי אור פנימיות תורתינו הקדושה, אשר נמשך ביום הזה בבחי' המשכה כללית על כללות השנה, ועלינו להעיר לבבנו ביום הזה בבחי' חפץ ורצון פנימי ועצמי באמיתת נקודת לבבנו, שיאיר נפשנו באור פנימיות תורתו ית'.

ממעמקים קראתיך ה', להמשיך בחי' עומק ופנימיות תורת ה' ומצות ה' מבחי' פנימיות ועצמות אוא"ס ב"ה שיאיר בפנימיות נפשנו, אשר כל עצמותינו (ר"ל כל מציאותינו, העצם וההתפשטות כו') יהיו אליו ית' לבד, לגרש מאתנו כל מדת רעה ומגונה מהמדות הטבעיות, כ"א כל עשיותינו וענינינו (הן בעבודה היינו תפלה ותומ"צ [ותורה ומצות], והן בעניני עולם המוכרחים לקיום הגוף) יהיו בכוונה אמיתית לשם שמים אשר חפץ ה' כו', והי"ת אב הרחמים ירחם עלינו וינחנו בדרך הטובה והישרה ישר יחזו פנימו...

שבת יט כסלו (תש"ג)
הפטרה: חזון עובדי'. אין אומרים אב הרחמים וצדקתך.

אין הש"ץ מתעטף בטלית למנחה או למעריב, לא בשויו"ט ולא בר"ה.

הילולא של הרב המגיד - ממעזריטש - ג' וישב תקל"ג, ומ"כ באנאפאלי.

אדמו"ר הזקן יצא לחירות ממאסרו הראשון - יט כסלו, ג' וישב, תקנ"ט, לפנות ערב.

ממכתב רבינו הזקן: ברם כגון דא צריך להודיע, כי יום אשר עשה ד' לנו יום יט כסלו, יום ג' שהוכפל בו כי טוב, יום הילולא רבא של רבינו הקדוש נ"ע, וכשקריתי בס' תהלים בפסוק פדה בשלום נפשי, קודם שהתחלתי פסוק שלאחריו, יצאתי בשלום מד' שלום.

***

יום התועדות וקבלת החלטות טובות בקביעות עתים לתורה הנגלית ודא"ח ברבים, וחיזוק דרכי החסידים באהבת רעים.

נוהגים לסדר חלוקת הש"ס, וע"פ הסדר המבואר באגה"ק ד"ה הוכיח תוכיח, בליובאוויטש משנת תרס"ג ואילך הי' מסדרים חלוקת הש"ס כ"ד בטבת - יום הלולא של רבינו הזקן - מפני אפס הפנאי ביט כסלו.
hayomYom.clear:
From a letter by my father [the Rebbe Rashab], dated Wednesday, 16 Kislev 5662:

...19 Kislev... the festival on which “He redeemed our soul in peace,” and the light and life of our soul were given to us. This day is the Rosh Hashanah of Chassidus, which our holy forefathers left to us as an inheritance. Chassidus is the very teaching of the Baal Shem Tov.

“This day is the beginning of Your works.” It fulfills the true purpose for which man was created on earth: to draw down the revealed light of the inner part of our holy Torah. On this day, that light is drawn down in a general way for the whole year. So on this day we must awaken our hearts with an inner, essential desire and will, from the true core of our heart, that G‑d light up our souls with the light of His inner Torah.

“From the depths I called You, G‑d”: to draw down the depth and inner part of G‑d’s Torah and mitzvos, from the inner essence of the Infinite Light, blessed be He, so that it lights up the inner part of our souls. So that all of our being (meaning our entire existence, the core and everything that extends from it) belongs to Him alone. To drive out of ourselves every bad and unworthy natural trait. Instead, all our actions and affairs (both our avoda, meaning davening, Torah and mitzvos, and the worldly matters needed to sustain the body) should be done with a true intention for the sake of Heaven, as G‑d desires. May G‑d, the Merciful Father, have compassion on us and lead us on the good and upright path, and may we “see His face in uprightness” (Tehillim 11:7).

The chazzan does not wear a tallis for Mincha or Maariv: not on Shabbos, not on Yom Tov, and not on Rosh Hashanah.

Hillula [yahrzeit] of the Maggid of Mezritch: Tuesday of Vayeishev, 5533 (1772). He is buried in Anipoli.

The Alter Rebbe was freed from his first imprisonment on 19 Kislev, Tuesday of Vayeishev, 5559 (1798), toward evening.

From the Alter Rebbe’s letter: But this must be made known. On the day G‑d made for us, 19 Kislev, a Tuesday (the day on which “it was good” is said twice), the great hillula of our holy teacher [the Maggid], while I was reading in Tehillim the verse “He redeemed my soul in peace,” before I began the next verse, I went out in peace, by the G‑d of peace.

* * *

A day of farbrengen and good resolutions: to set fixed times to study revealed Torah and Chassidus publicly, and to strengthen the ways of chassidim in brotherly love.

It is customary to divide up the Talmud for study, following the procedure in Igeres Hakodesh, the letter beginning Hochei’ach Tochi’ach. In Lubavitch, from 5663 (1902-03) on, the division was done on 24 Teves, the hillula of the Alter Rebbe, since there was no time on 19 Kislev.
translationNotes: Your file’s Hebrew for this day holds only the calendar line. The full Hebrew here is from chabad.org.
יום הילולא רבא: “the great hillula,” a celebration of the tzaddik’s soul ascending. Stronger than “yahrzeit.”
ברבים: study in public, in groups.
אהבת רעים: “brotherly love” between chassidim, more than “friendship.”

calendar.original5703: Haftorah: Chazon Ovadiah. Av Harachamim and Tzidkas’cha are not said. (5703: 19 Kislev was Shabbos.)
calendar.thisYear5787: This year 19 Kislev is Sunday, Nov 29. Vayishlach and its haftorah are the day before, Shabbos Nov 28.

hayomYom.english: The first printing of the "Book of the Intermediates" - Tanya - was completed on Tuesday, Kislev 20, 5557 (1796) in Slavita. It included Part I - Sefer Shel Benonim, - Part II - Chinuch Katan - and Shaar Hayichud Veha'emunah. Igeret Hateshuvah, first edition, was printed in Zolkvi 5559 (1799); second edition, first printing, Shklov 5566 (1806). Igeret Hakodesh, first printing, Shklov 5574 (1814). The corrected edition of all four parts was printed in Vilna (Rom edition) in 5660 (1900) and has been reprinted many times since.
hayomYom.hebrew:
הדפסת ספר של בינונים - תניא - בפעם הראשונה נגמרה יום ג' כ' כסלו תקנ"ז בסלאוויטא. וכולל:

חלק ראשון - ספר של בינונים, חלק שני - חנוך קטן ושער היחוד והאמונה.

אגרת התשובה - מהדורא קמא - נדפסה לראשונה: זאלקווי תקנ"ט; מהדורא בתרא - נדפסה לראשונה: שקלאוו תקס"ו.

אגרת הקדש - בפעם הראשונה - שקלאוו תקע"ד. תוצאה מתוקנת של כל ד' החלקים - ווילנא ראם תר"ס, וחזרה ונדפסה כמה פעמים.
hayomYom.clear:
The first printing of Sefer Shel Beinonim (the Tanya) was completed on Tuesday, 20 Kislev 5557 (1796), in Slavita. It included:

Part One: Sefer Shel Beinonim.
Part Two: Chinuch Katan, and Shaar Hayichud Veha’emunah.

Igeres Hateshuvah: the first version was first printed in Zolkva, 5559 (1799). The later version was first printed in Shklov, 5566 (1806).

Igeres Hakodesh: first printed in Shklov, 5574 (1814).

A corrected edition of all four parts was printed in Vilna (the Romm edition) in 5660 (1900), and it has been reprinted many times since.
translationNotes: מהדורא קמא / בתרא: first and later versions of Igeres Hateshuvah. The old English (“second edition, first printing”) is confusing.

hayomYom.english: Learn Mishna by heart, each person according to his capacity, and then while walking in the street, review Mishna from memory; you will thereby merit welcoming Mashiach. Chassidim must study Chassidus; all chassidim on Mondays, Thursdays, and Shabbat; T'mimim an hour every day.
hayomYom.hebrew:
מען זאל זיך אויסלערנען משניות בעל פה כל חד לפום שיעורי' דילי', און געהן אין גאס און חזר'ן משניות, דערמיט וועט מען זוכה זיין צו מקבל זיין פני המשיח.

חסידים דארפען לערנען חסידות: סתם חסידים - יום שני, יום חמישי ויום השבת, תמימים - שעה אחת בכל יום.
hayomYom.clear:
Learn Mishnayos by heart, each person according to his ability. Then go out in the street and review the Mishnayos. Through this you will merit to greet Moshiach.

Chassidim must study Chassidus. Every chassid: on Monday, Thursday and Shabbos. Temimim [students of Tomchei Temimim]: one hour every day.
translationNotes: מקבל זיין פני המשיח: to go out and greet Moshiach, as one greets a king.
סתם חסידים: ordinary chassidim, as opposed to yeshiva students.

hayomYom.english: A practice instituted by the Rebbe: Every morning after davening - including Shabbat, festivals, Rosh Hashana and Yom Kippur - say a portion of Tehillim as the book was apportioned for the days of the month. When Tehillim is completed with a minyan - Mourner's Kaddish is said. In a month of 29 days, say the last two portions on the 29th.
hayomYom.hebrew:
מתקנות כ"ק אדמו"ר שליט"א: לאמר בכל בקר אחר התפלה - וגם בשויו"ט [בשבת ויום טוב], ר"ה [ראש השנה] ויה"כ [ויום הכיפורים] - תהלים כפי שנחלק לימי החדש, ואחר אמירה בעשרה - ק"י [קדיש יתום].

בחדש של כט יום אומרים ביום כט השעור דשני הימים.
hayomYom.clear:
A practice established by the Rebbe [the Rebbe Rayatz]: Every morning after davening, including Shabbos, Yom Tov, Rosh Hashanah and Yom Kippur, say the portion of Tehillim set for that day of the month. When it is said with ten, say Mourner’s Kaddish after it.

In a month of 29 days, on the 29th say the portions of both days.
translationNotes: ואחר אמירה בעשרה: Kaddish whenever it is said with a minyan, every day. The old English “when Tehillim is completed” sounds like only when the whole book is finished.
כ"ק אדמו"ר שליט"א: the Rebbe Rayatz, who was alive when Hayom Yom was compiled.

hayomYom.english: From my grandfather's talks of Elul 5635 (1875): The three days before Shabbat are a preparation for Shabbat. The Zohar says about Shabbat that "from it are all days blessed." "All days" refers to the six days of the week on which G‑d conferred a general blessing - "G‑d will bless you in all you do." The blessing of Shabbat is for the days preceding it and the days following it. The preparations for Shabbat begin Wednesday, and are announced by the brief l'chu n'ran'na of three verses.
hayomYom.hebrew: משיחות אאזמו"ר [אדוני אבי זקני מורי ורבי] - אלול תרל"ה: ג' ימים קודם השבת הוא הכנה לשבת. אויף שבת זאגט ער אין זהר דמיני'[ה] מתברכין כולהו יומין. כולהו יומין איז כל ששת ימי השבוע, וואס אויף דעם האט דער אויבערשטער געגעבען א ברכה כללית וברכך ה"א [ה' אלקיך] בכל אשר תעשה, איז די ברכת השבת מלפניו ומלאחריו, די הכנה צו שבת איז מיום ד', און דער אנזאג איז דער קליינער לכו נרננה, וואס איז ג' פסוקים.
hayomYom.clear:
From my grandfather’s [the Rebbe Maharash’s] talks of Elul 5635 (1875):

The three days before Shabbos are a preparation for Shabbos. The Zohar says about Shabbos that “from it all the days are blessed.” “All the days” means the six weekdays, on which G‑d gave a general blessing: “G‑d your G‑d will bless you in all that you do” (Devarim 15:18). So the blessing of Shabbos reaches the days before it and the days after it.

The preparation for Shabbos starts on Wednesday, and it is announced by the “small L’chu n’ran’nah”: three verses.
translationNotes: The “small L’chu n’ran’nah” is the three verses (Tehillim 95:1-3) added at the end of Wednesday’s Song of the Day.
אאזמו"ר here is the Rebbe Maharash.

hayomYom.english: (Continuation of Kislev 23): An explanation of the three verses beginning l'chu n'ran'na, in a manner meaningful to everyone, is as follows: Wednesday, we begin thinking: What will we have for Shabbat? This is a concern in the literal sense and also spiritually, "how can we Shabbos" (i.e. make a real Shabbat)? After all, every person is quite different on Shabbat than on a weekday. So we become a bit despondent. The solution is l'chu n'ran'na ("Come let us sing"), have faith, trust. Comes Thursday, it is now closer to Shabbat and we still have nothing. It doesn't seem to "n'ran'na" so easily and we realize we must do something. So we study Chassidus Thursday night, so that by Friday we sense the depth of "...for the L-rd is a great G‑d and a great King..."; and with this a Jew "can Shabbos." During Mincha, tachanun is omitted.
hayomYom.hebrew:
[המשך]. ביאור ג' הפסוקים - לכו נרננה - ע"פ [על פי] מדה ממוצעת מדת כל אדם: מיטוואך, אז מען הויבט אן טראכטען וואו וועט מען נעהמען אויף שבת, הן בפשטות און הן מיט וואס וועט מען שבת'ן - יעדער איד איז דאך שבת גאר אנאנדערער - ווערט מרה שחורה'דיג, איז די עצה, לכו נרננה, בטחון. ווען עס קומט דאנערשטאג, עס ווערט נעהנטער צו שבת, און עס איז נאך אלץ ניטא, איז יעמאלט נרננה'ט זיך ניט, מען פארשטעהט אז מ'דארף עפעס טאן. איז אז מ'זיצט דאנערשטאג'דיגע נאכט און מ'לערענט חסידות, יעמאלט איז פרייטאג דערהערט מען כי א-ל גדול גו' ומלך גדול גו', און מיט דעם שבת'ט א איד.

במנחה אין אומרים תחנון.
hayomYom.clear:
[Continued from yesterday.] Here is an explanation of the three verses beginning L’chu n’ran’na [“Come, let us sing”], on the level of an average person, a level that applies to everyone:

On Wednesday you start to think: where will we get what we need for Shabbos? This is meant both simply, in the literal sense, and also: with what will we “Shabbos” [truly keep Shabbos]? After all, every Jew is a completely different person on Shabbos. So you become gloomy. The advice is: L’chu n’ran’na, trust in G‑d.

Then Thursday comes. Shabbos is closer, and there is still nothing. Now the n’ran’na [singing] doesn’t come so easily, and you understand that you have to do something. So when you sit Thursday night and study Chassidus, then on Friday you feel “For G‑d is a great G‑d and a great King.” And with this a Jew “Shabboses.”
translationNotes: מרה שחורה’דיג is literally “melancholy, gloomy.” Kehot’s “a bit despondent” softens it slightly.
נרננה’ט זיך ניט: the singing “doesn’t sing itself” anymore. Trust alone no longer flows easily.
דערהערט מען: you actually sense, “hear,” the greatness of G‑d on Friday.

calendar.original5703: At Mincha, tachanun is not said.

hayomYom.english: My father would kindle Chanuka lights between Mincha and Maariv; he was not particular whether the doorway was south-north or east-west. Haneirot halalu he said after kindling all the lights. He would sit near the lights for a half hour, except Fridays when he did not stay that long. He took care that the lights burned at least 50 minutes. The order we follow is: Mincha, Chanuka lights, then Shabbat candles.
hayomYom.hebrew:
אאמו"ר [אדוני אבי מורי ורבי] הי'[ה] מדליק נרות חנוכה בין מנחה למעריב, ולא הי'[ה] מדייק בפתח שיהי'[ה] מדרום לצפון או ממזרח למערב. "הנרות הללו" - אחר הדלקת כל הנרות. והיה יושב בסמוך להנרות חצי שעה - לבד מועש"ק [מו' ערב שבת קודש] שלא הי'[ה] מתעכב חצי שעה - מדייק שידלקו הנרות חמישים מינוט לכל הפחות.

מנחה, נר חנוכה, נר שבת.
hayomYom.clear:
My father would light the Chanuka lights between Mincha and Maariv. He was not particular about whether the doorway ran south to north or east to west.

Haneiros halalu [“These lights”] he said after lighting all the lights.

He would sit near the lights for half an hour, except on Friday, when he did not stay a full half hour. He made sure the lights burned at least fifty minutes.
translationNotes: On Friday the Hebrew says he did not stay “half an hour,” i.e. not the full half hour. Kehot’s “not that long” is the same idea.
מדייק: he was careful, exacting, that the lights burn at least fifty minutes.

calendar.original5703: Order: Mincha, Chanuka lights, Shabbos candles.

hayomYom.english:
Bless Rosh Chodesh Tevet. Say the entire Tehillim in the early morning.

Day of farbrengen. Tal umatar (Siddur, p. 54). Chanuka lights after havdala (p. 234), before v'yitein l'cha (p. 235). In shul, Chanuka candles before havdala. On Shabbat mevarchim, (when the new month is blessed) (Siddur, p. 191), Chassidim are to assemble in Shul early in the morning to say the entire Tehillim. Afterwards, study for about an hour a maamar Chassidus that everyone can understand, and then daven. The time to farbreng is to be determined according to the circumstances in the place they live (for material and spiritual success). After concluding the Tehillim on Shabbat Mevarchim, say Mourner's Kaddish; if there is a Yahrzeit or mourner - Kaddish after each of the five books of Tehillim.
hayomYom.hebrew: מברכים ראש חודש טבת. אמירת כל התהלים בהשכמה.
hayomYom.clear:
On Shabbos Mevarchim [the Shabbos when the new month is blessed], chassidim should gather in shul early in the morning to say the entire Tehillim. Afterwards, study for about an hour a maamar of Chassidus that everyone can understand, and then daven. The time for the farbrengen should be set according to the circumstances of each place, for success in material and spiritual matters.

After finishing the Tehillim on Shabbos Mevarchim, say Mourner’s Kaddish. If there is a yahrzeit or a mourner present, say Kaddish after each of the five books of Tehillim.
translationNotes: The Hebrew field here holds only the calendar line (מברכים ראש חודש טבת, אמירת כל התהלים בהשכמה). The Shabbos Mevarchim custom is translated from the Kehot English.

calendar.original5703: Bless Rosh Chodesh Teves. Say the entire Tehillim early in the morning. Day of farbrengen. Begin saying v’sein tal umatar [the request for rain]. Chanuka lights at home after havdala, before V’yiten l’cha. In shul, Chanuka lights before havdala.

hayomYom.dataFlag: Hebrew contains only the calendar line; the Shabbos Mevarchim instructions and tal umatar/havdala lines exist only in the English. Translation based on the English.

hayomYom.english: During the Alter Rebbe's second arrest in 5561 (1800) he was not incarcerated as harshly as the first time. However the charges were more ominous for they were aimed at the doctrines of Chassidus and the opposition was intense. He was held in "Taini Soviet" prison and released on the Third Light of Chanuka.
hayomYom.hebrew: במאסר השני של רבינו הזקן - בשנת תקס"א - לא ישב בתפיסא ומאסר כבד כבראשונה. אבל המלשינות היתה כבדה יותר, כי עיקר ההלשנה היה על תורת החסידות, וההתנגדות היתה גדולה במאוד. הי'[ה] תפוס "בטיינע סאוועט". יום שיצא לחרות: נר ג' דחנוכה.
hayomYom.clear:
In the Alter Rebbe’s second arrest, in 5561 (1800), he was not held in as harsh an imprisonment as the first time. But the accusations were heavier, because the main charge was against the teachings of Chassidus, and the opposition was very great.

He was held in the “Tainy Soviet” [the Secret Council].

The day he went free: the third light of Chanuka.
translationNotes: המלשינות היתה כבדה יותר: the informing itself was “heavier.” Kehot’s “more ominous” is close.
בטיינע סאוועט is the Russian Tainy Sovet, the Secret Council, not the name of a prison.

hayomYom.english: It was customary for the Tzemach Tzedek to have a sort of farbrengen on one of the evenings of Chanuka with his family, including his daughters-in-law. This was called "latkes evening." This was also the practice of the Alter Rebbe and the Mitteler Rebbe. Among the stories the Rebbes told at this meal were some which were widely talked about every Chanuka, though they had been discussed the year before. My father would give Chanuka-gelt on the evening of the fourth or fifth light.
hayomYom.hebrew:
הנהוג אצל הצ"צ [הצמח צדק], כי באחד מלילי חנוכה היו עושים כעין פארבריינגען עם בני הבית, והיו באים גם כלותיו, ונקרא "לאטקעס אווענט". וכן היה אצל רבינו הזקן ואדמו"ר [ואדננו מורנו ורבנו] האמצעי. בין הספורים שהיו הרביים מספרים בסעודה זו, היו ספורים אשר בכל חנוכה היו משוחחים אודותם, אף שכבר דברו מזה בשנה העברה.

אאמו"ר [אדוני אבי מורי ורבי] היה נותן דמי חנוכה בליל נר הרביעי או החמישי.
hayomYom.clear:
It was the custom of the Tzemach Tzedek that on one of the nights of Chanuka they would hold a kind of farbrengen with the family. His daughters-in-law also came. This was called “latkes evening.” The same was done by the Alter Rebbe and by the Mitteler Rebbe.

Among the stories the Rebbes told at this meal, there were some that were talked about every Chanuka, even though they had already been told the year before.

My father would give Chanuka gelt on the night of the fourth or fifth light.
translationNotes: Kehot says the stories were “widely talked about.” The Hebrew means they were retold at this meal every Chanuka.
עם בני הבית is “with the household,” the immediate family.

hayomYom.english: The sins of Israel in the time of the Greeks were: Fraternizing with the Greeks, studying their culture, profaning Shabbat and Holy Days, eating t'reifa and neglecting Jewish tahara. The punishment-tribulation was the spiritual destruction of the Sanctuary, death, and slavery in exile. Through teshuva and mesirat nefesh, that great, miraculous Divine salvation - the miracle of Chanuka - came about.
hayomYom.hebrew: די עבירות פון די אידען [אין דער צייט פון די יונים] זיינען געווען: דאס חבר'ן זיך מיט די יונים, לערנען זייער קולטור, חילול שבת ומועד, עסען טריפות, ניט היטן די אידישע טהרה. די שטראף-צרה איז געווען דער גייסטיגער חורבן פון בית המקדש, הריגה און שקלאפערי אין גלות. דורך תשובה און מסירת נפש איז געקומען די גרויסע ג-טליכע וואונדער-ישועה, דער נס חנוכה.
hayomYom.clear:
The sins of the Jews in the time of the Greeks were: socializing with the Greeks, studying their culture, desecrating Shabbos and Yom Tov, eating treif, and not guarding Jewish taharah [family purity].

The punishment and suffering was the spiritual destruction of the Beis HaMikdash, killing, and slavery in exile.

Through teshuva and mesirus nefesh came the great, miraculous Divine salvation: the miracle of Chanuka.
translationNotes: דאס חבר’ן זיך: becoming companions with the Greeks. Kehot’s “fraternizing” is right.
הריגה is “killing,” plainer than Kehot’s “death.”

hayomYom.english: It is customary that one not davening with a minyan says the opening (p. 241) and closing (p. 245) b'rachot of Hallel even on days when "half Hallel" is said. In the concluding paragraph, yehal'lucha (p.245) omit the word "Al." All tefillin should be worn (then, later, taken off) before Musaf (p. 245), but the daily Torah lessons are studied after concluding the entire service.
hayomYom.hebrew: נוהגים אשר היחיד מברך - בהלל - תחלה וסוף גם בימים שאין גומרים בהם את ההלל. הנוסח שאומרים הוא: יהללוך ה"א [ה' אלוקינו] כל מעשיך, בהשמטת תיבת "על". כל התפילין מניחים קודם מוסף, אבל השיעורים לומדים אחר סיום כל התפלה.
hayomYom.clear:
The custom is that an individual [davening without a minyan] says the blessings before and after Hallel, even on days when the full Hallel is not said.

The wording said is: Y’hal’lucha Hashem Elokeinu kol ma’asecha [“All Your works shall praise You, Hashem our G‑d”], leaving out the word “al.”

All the tefillin are put on [and taken off] before Musaf. But the daily Torah lessons are studied after finishing the whole davening.
translationNotes: היחיד מברך: the individual also says the blessings, not only the congregation.
כל התפילין means all pairs worn (Rashi and Rabbeinu Tam).

hayomYom.english: The campaign of the Greeks was aimed to "make them forget Your Torah and violate the decrees of Your will" (Sidur p. 59); as the Midrash (Bereishit Raba 16) puts it, (the Greeks demanded) "Write...that you have no share in the G‑d of Israel." It was a war against G‑d. "Let them study Torah," the Greeks implied. "Let them practice the justice-mitzvot and the 'testimonial' observances. But they must not mention that the Torah is G‑d's Torah and the mitzvot are the decrees of His will. Torah and mitzvot must be severed from G‑dliness."
hayomYom.hebrew: מלחמת היונים היתה "להשכיחם תורתך ולהעבירם מחוקי רצונך" וכמאמר [ב"ר פט"ז] כתבו כו' שאין לכם חלק באלקי ישראל. כל המלחמה היתה נגד אלקות, זאל מען לערנען תורה, זאל מען מקיים זיין מצות המשפטים והעדות, רק שלא להזכיר שהיא תורת ה' ושהמצות הם חקי רצונו יתברך, ניט דערמאנען אין תומ"צ [תורה ומצות] דעם ענין פון ג-טלכקייט.
hayomYom.clear:
The war of the Greeks was “to make them forget Your Torah and to force them away from the statutes of Your will,” as the Midrash says (Bereishis Rabba 16): “Write... that you have no share in the G‑d of Israel.”

The whole war was against G‑dliness. Let them study Torah. Let them keep the mitzvos of mishpatim [the logical laws] and eidos [the commemorative laws]. Only, do not mention that it is G‑d’s Torah and that the mitzvos are the statutes of His will. Do not mention G‑dliness in Torah and mitzvos.
translationNotes: חוקי רצונך: “statutes of Your will.” The chukim, beyond reason, are exactly what the Greeks opposed.
ניט דערמאנען: “not to mention.” The Greeks did not demand dropping Torah, only dropping any mention of G‑d in it.

hayomYom.english: (The notation for this day is a textual emendation of Torah Or, relevant only in Hebrew. Translator)
hayomYom.hebrew:
בתו"א [בתורה אור] ד"ה [דיבור המתחיל] ת"ר [תנו רבנן] מצות נר חנוכה "כי אין כדאי כל הדינים" צ"ל [צריך להיות] "כי כדאי כל הדינים".

שם ביאור לדיבור המתחיל רני ושמחי סעיף המתחיל ועתה נבוא "שהוא פנימית א"א [אריך אנפין]" צריך להיות "שהוא פנימית א"ס [אין סוף]".
hayomYom.clear:
Corrections to Torah Or:

Maamar Tanu Rabbanan mitzvas ner Chanuka: “for all the laws are not worthy” should read “for all the laws are worthy.”

Same place, in the explanation of the maamar Roni v’simchi, in the section beginning V’ata navo: “which is the inwardness of Arich Anpin” should read “which is the inwardness of Ein Sof.”
translationNotes: The old English skips this entry as “relevant only in Hebrew.” This is a direct translation of the Hebrew corrections.

hayomYom.english: The Rebbes of Chabad would review a parsha or two of the weekly sedra on Thursday night. On Friday afternoon they began again from the start and completed the sedra and haftora. Shabbat morning before davening they reviewed from Shevi'i to the end again. When there were two haftorot they said the one of the sedraon Friday and the other (for Rosh Chodesh, machar chodesh, etc.), on Shabbat. * * * There are good dreams in which Torah subjects are made known to the person dreaming. These generally occur through concentrated devotion to Torah study during the day. When someone studies Torah with great diligence or engages in "service of the heart" - prayer - with intense effort, then at night - when his soul ascends to draw forth life for itself from the supernal Life, as explained in Zohar - it is informed of novellae in Revealed Torah or Inner Torah, each person according to his diligence in his avoda during the day.
hayomYom.hebrew:
נשיאי חב"ד פלעגן מעביר זיין איין פרשה אדער צוויי דאנערשטאג ביינאכט אור ליום ששי. פרייטאג אחר חצות פלעגט מען אנהויבן נאכאמאל פון אנהויב, און מעביר זיין די גאנצע סדרה מיט דער הפטורה. שבת אינדערפריה פאר'ן דאוונען פלעגט מען מעביר זיין נאכאמאל פון שביעי. ווען עס איז אויסגעקומען צוויי הפטורות, האט מען געזאגט הפטורת הסדרה ביום ששי, און די אנדערע הפטורה [פון שר"ח [שבת ראש חודש], מ"ח [מחר חודש] וכו'] שבת.

החלומות הטובים בעניני תורה שמודיעים בחלום, בא ע"פ [על פי] הרוב ע"י [על ידי] שקידה גדולה בתורה ביום, דכאשר עוסק בתורה בשקידה גדולה, או עוסק בעבודה שבלב ביגיעה עצומה, הנה כאשר בלילה נשמתו עולה למעלה ושואבת לה חיים מחיי דלעילא כמבואר בזהר, הנה אז מודיעים לו חדושי תורה בגליא שבתורה או בפנימיות התורה, איש איש כפי שקידת עבודתו בעבודת היום.
hayomYom.clear:
The Chabad Rebbes would review one or two sections of the weekly sedra on Thursday night [the night before Friday]. On Friday after midday they would start again from the beginning and review the whole sedra together with the haftorah. On Shabbos morning before davening they would review again from Shevi’i [the seventh aliya].

When there were two haftorahs, they said the haftorah of the sedra on Friday, and the other one [of Shabbos Rosh Chodesh, Machar Chodesh, etc.] on Shabbos.

Good dreams, in which Torah matters are made known to a person, come mostly through great diligence in Torah during the day. When you study Torah with great diligence, or engage in avoda shebalev [service of the heart, davening] with tremendous effort, then at night, when your soul rises above and draws life for itself from the Life above, as explained in the Zohar, you are shown new insights in the revealed part of Torah or in its inner part. Each person according to the diligence of his avoda during the day.
translationNotes: אחר חצות is “after midday,” more precise than Kehot’s “Friday afternoon.”
ביגיעה עצומה: “with tremendous effort.” Yegia, toil, is the key word.

hayomYom.english: When Mashiach comes we will realize the greatness of hoda'a (acknowledgement, or belief) and t'mimut (earnestness), everyone's pure faith in G‑d and His Torah and mitzvot. Talmud - namely, human comprehension, even on its highest level - is limited. But hoda'a, faith, is a feeling that is boundless. Mashiach will explain the magnificent achievement of t'mimut - earnest avoda flowing from the heart.
hayomYom.hebrew: ווען משיח וועט קומען, וועט מען זעהן די מעלה פון הודאה און תמימות, וואס אלע גלויבען באמונה טהורה אין ג-ט ב"ה [ברוך הוא] און אין זיין תורה ומצות. תלמוד - פארשטאנד - איז דער גרעסטער פארשטאנד האט א גרעניץ. אבער הודאה - גלויבען - גלויבען איז א געפיהל אהן א גרעניץ. מלך המשיח וועט געבען צו פארשטעהן דעם מעשה גדול פון דער תמימות - הארציגער ערענסטער עבודה.
hayomYom.clear:
When Mashiach comes, we will see the greatness of hoda’ah [acknowledgment] and temimus [simple sincerity]: that everyone believes with pure faith in G‑d, blessed be He, and in His Torah and mitzvos.

Talmud, understanding, even the greatest understanding, has a limit. But hoda’ah, belief, is a feeling without a limit.

Melech HaMashiach will make us understand the great achievement of temimus: heartfelt, earnest avoda.
translationNotes: מעשה גדול: “a great deed, a great achievement.” Kehot’s “magnificent achievement” is fine.
תמימות is simple wholeheartedness, not just “earnestness.”

hayomYom.english: "Know the G‑d of your fathers and serve Him with a whole heart." Every sort of Torah knowledge and comprehension, even the most profound, must be expressed in avoda. I.e. the intellectual attainment must bring about an actual refinement and improvement of character traits, and must be translated into a deep-rooted inward attachment (to G‑d) - all of which is what the Chassidic lexicon calls"avoda".
hayomYom.hebrew: כתיב דע את אלקי אביך ועבדהו בלב שלם, כי כל ענין ידיעה והשגה אפילו בענינים היותר עמוקים, צריך לבוא בעבודה, היינו פעולת דבר בבירור וזיכוך המדות והתקשרות פנימית הנקרא בלשון החסידות עבודה.
hayomYom.clear:
It is written, “Know the G‑d of your father and serve Him with a whole heart” (Divrei HaYamim I 28:9).

All knowledge and understanding, even of the deepest subjects, must lead to avoda. That means it must actually do something: refine and purify your character traits, and create an inner bond [with G‑d]. This is what the language of Chassidus calls “avoda.”
translationNotes: אביך is singular, “your father.” Kehot’s “your fathers” is inaccurate.
פעולת דבר: it must “accomplish something” in practice.

hayomYom.english: To avert chibut hakever ("Purgatory of the grave") recite words of Torah, Tehillim, etc., for one sixth of the day. To merit purity of the soul that obviates kaf hakela ("the hollow of a sling"), spend as much of the day as possible in reciting Mishna, Tanya and Tehillim by heart.
hayomYom.hebrew: השעור להפטר מחבוט הקבר הוא, שחלק ששי מהמעת-לעת יאמר אותיות התורה, תהלים כו'. לזכות לזיכוך הנפש להפטר מכף הכלע הוא, ע"י [על ידי] חזרה כל היום, כמה שיש ביכולתו, משניות תניא תהלים בעל פה.
hayomYom.clear:
The measure to be spared from chibut hakever [the beating of the grave] is to say the letters of Torah, Tehillim and so on, for one sixth of the twenty-four hours.

To merit the refinement of the soul and be spared from kaf hakela [the hollow of the sling], review by heart, all day, as much as you are able: Mishnayos, Tanya, Tehillim.
translationNotes: מעת-לעת is a full 24-hour period, so one sixth is four hours. Kehot’s “day” is vague.
אותיות התורה: the actual letters, words of Torah said aloud.

hayomYom.english: The Tzemach Tzedek instructed all the tutors of his young grandchildren, that, in addition to regular studies, they should teach the simple meaning of the prayers. Once a month the children came to their grandfather to be tested in this subject.
hayomYom.hebrew: הצ"צ [הצמח צדק] ציוה את כל המלמדים שלמדו עם נכדיו הקטנים, אשר, מלבד למודים הרגילים, ילמדו עמהם פירוש המלות [פירוש הפשוט] של סדר התפלה. ופעם בחודש היו באים אל הצ"צ [הצמח צדק] להבחן בזה.
hayomYom.clear: The Tzemach Tzedek instructed all the melamdim who taught his young grandchildren that, besides the regular studies, they should teach them the meaning of the words of the davening [the simple translation]. Once a month the children would come to the Tzemach Tzedek to be tested on it.
translationNotes: פירוש המלות: the meaning of each word, the plain translation of the siddur.

hayomYom.english: Our custom in aleinu (Siddur Tehilat Hashem p. 84) is to say "for they bow to vanity and nothingness," and markedly not to say "and pray..." This wording is followed also in Musaf for Rosh Hashana and Yom Kippur. The expectorating is after these words; the reason is that speech stimulates saliva, and we do not wish to benefit from this saliva.
hayomYom.hebrew: נוהגין בנוסח 'עלינו' לומר: שהם משתחוים להבל ולריק. - וגם בתפילת מוסף דראש השנה אומרים כן - ומדייקים שלא לומר ומתפללים כו'. הרקיקה היא אחר האמירה. טעם הרקיקה, כי מדיבור מתהווה רוק, ואין רוצים ליהנות מרוק זה.
hayomYom.clear:
Our custom in Aleinu is to say: “for they bow to vanity and emptiness.” This is also said in Musaf of Rosh Hashana. We are careful not to say “and pray...”

The spitting is after saying these words. The reason for the spitting: speech produces saliva, and we do not want to benefit from this saliva.
translationNotes: The Hebrew mentions only Rosh Hashana Musaf. Kehot adds Yom Kippur.
מדייקים: we are careful, precise, not to say ומתפללים.

hayomYom.english: From the Tzemach Tzedek's answer at yechidus: It is written, "Let the wicked leave his path and the man of sin his thoughts etc." Aven (sin) is the same as on, meaning power and strength. Just as it is imperative that the "wicked leave his path," for without teshuva it is impossible to approach the Sacred, so must the "man of strength," one with unshakeable confidence in his reasoning, "leave his thoughts." He is not to insist, "I say so. This is what I think;" every "I", ego, is a source of evil, a cause of divisiveness.
hayomYom.hebrew: מענה הצ"צ [הצמח צדק] על יחידות: כתיב יעזוב רשע דרכו ואיש און מחשבותיו גו'. און הוא מלשון און בחולם, שפירושו כח ועוז. וכשם דיעזוב רשע דרכו זהו דבר המוכרח, אשר בלא תשובה אי אפשר לגשת אל הקדש, הנה כמו כן צריך האיש און, כלומר איש החזק בדעת עצמו, לעזוב מחשבותיו, ולא יאמר איך זאג אזוי, איך האלט אזוי, כי כל "איך" ומציאות הוא מקור הרע וגורם פירוד לבבות.
hayomYom.clear:
From the Tzemach Tzedek’s answer at yechidus:

It is written, “Let the wicked man leave his path, and the man of aven his thoughts” (Yeshayahu 55:7). Aven here is from the word on, with a cholam, which means power and strength.

Just as “let the wicked man leave his path” is a must, since without teshuva you cannot approach holiness, so too the “man of strength,” meaning a person who is strong in his own opinion, must leave his thoughts. He should not say “I say so, I think so.” Because every “I,” every sense of self, is the source of evil and causes separation between hearts.
translationNotes: איש החזק בדעת עצמו: a person firm in his own opinion. Kehot’s “unshakeable confidence in his reasoning” is close.
פירוד לבבות: “separation of hearts.” Kehot’s “divisiveness” loses the image.

hayomYom.english: Man's life is dependent on the air around him. Without air he cannot live and the quality of life is dependent on the quality of air. In an atmosphere of Torah and mitzvot there is healthy life. In a G‑dless environment life is diseased, and one is constantly threatened with the possibility of being stricken with contagious maladies. The first general step in healing is to purify the atmosphere. Purification of the air is the task of every person familiar with Torah and Torah-literature, and is effected through the letters of Torah. When reciting words of Torah while in the store or walking in the street or riding the subway, one cleans the air. Everyone knowledgeable in Torah must have some Torah memorized - Chumash, Tehillim, Mishna, Tanya, etc., so that at all times and in all places he will be able to think and utter the holy letters of Torah.
hayomYom.hebrew: דעם מענשענס לעבען איז תלוי אין דעם אויר וואו ער געפינט זיך. אהן אויר קען מען ניט לעבען, און אין וואס פאר א אויר מען לעבט אזא לעבען איז דאס. ווען מען לעבט אין א תורה ומצות אויר, איז דער לעבען א געזונטער. ווען מען לעבט אין כפירה-אויר, איז דאס א קראנקער לעבען, און מען איז כסדר אין געפאהר קראנק צו ווערען מיט אנשטעקענדע מחלות. די ערשטע אלגעמיינע רפואה איז צו מאכען ריין די לופט. די ארבעט פון טהרת האויר ליגט אויף די יודעי ספר און יודעי תורה. טהרת האויר איז דורך אותיות התורה. ווען מ'שטעהט אין סטאר, אדער ווען מען געהט אין גאס, אדער ווען מ'פאהרט אין סאבוויי און מען זאגט אותיות שבתורה, מאכט מען מיט דעם ריין דעם אויר. יעדער איינער פון די יודעי ספר און יודעי תורה מוז האבען עפעס אויסגעלערנט בעל פה: חומש, תהלים, משניות, תניא, אזוי, אז צו יעדער צייט און אין יעדען ארט, זאל ער קענען טראכטען און זאגען די הייליגע אותיות שבתורה.
hayomYom.clear:
A person’s life depends on the air where he is. Without air you cannot live, and the kind of air you live in is the kind of life you have.

When you live in an air of Torah and mitzvos, life is healthy. When you live in an air of heresy, life is sick, and you are constantly in danger of catching contagious diseases.

The first general cure is to purify the air. The work of purifying the air rests on those who know sefarim and know Torah. The air is purified through the letters of Torah. When you stand in a store, or walk in the street, or ride the subway, and say words of Torah, you purify the air.

Every one of those who know sefarim and Torah must have learned something by heart: Chumash, Tehillim, Mishnayos, Tanya. Then at any time and in any place, he can think and say the holy letters of Torah.
translationNotes: כפירה-אויר: an atmosphere of heresy, denial of G‑d. Stronger than Kehot’s “G‑dless.”
יודעי ספר: those who “know a book,” the learned. Kehot merges it into “familiar with Torah.”

hayomYom.english: In 5648 (1887) my father was elected gabai (an official) of the Chevra Kadisha. As was customary he was led on Simchat Torah in procession to the shul accompanied by a throng. At that time he said the maamar beginning "Ein H.B.H. ba bitrunya." The conclusion was: Even the great minds who are here must lay aside their intellects and not be ruled by their reason and knowledge, for they are susceptible to being misguided by their intellect to the point that their end may be a bitter one. The essential thing in these times of the "footsteps of Mashiach" is not to follow intellect and reason, but to fulfill Torah and mitzvot wholeheartedly, with simple faith in the G‑d of Israel.
hayomYom.hebrew: בשנת תרמ"ח נבחר אאמו"ר [אדני אבי מורי ורבי] לגבאי דחברה קדישא. וכפי המנהג, הובילו אותו בשמח"ת [בשמחת תורה] בלוית עם רב לביהכ"נ [לבית הכנסת]. אמר אז המאמר אין הקב"ה [הקדוש ברוך הוא] בא בטרוניא. וסיום דבריו: גם האנשים בעלי מוחין הנמצאים עתה צריכים להניח שכלם ולא לילך אחרי הטעם ודעת, כי יכולים להטות ע"פ [על פי] שכלם כו' עד כי ח"ו [חס ושלום] מרה תהיה באחרונה כו'. וזהו העיקר בזמן הזה בעקבות דמשיחא, שלא לילך אחר השכל וטו"ד [וטעם ודעת], כי אם לקיים התורה והמצות בתמימות ואמונה פשוטה באלקי ישראל.
hayomYom.clear:
In 5648 (1887) my father was elected gabbai of the Chevra Kadisha [burial society]. As was the custom, on Simchas Torah he was escorted to the shul by a large crowd. He then said the maamar Ein HaKadosh Baruch Hu ba bitrunya [“G‑d does not deal tyrannically with His creatures”].

He concluded: Even the people with great minds who are here now must set their intellect aside and not follow reason and knowledge. Because their intellect can lead them astray, until, G‑d forbid, it may end bitterly.

And this is the main thing in our times, ikvesa d’Meshicha [the era just before Mashiach]: not to follow intellect and reason, but to keep the Torah and mitzvos with temimus [simple sincerity] and simple faith in the G‑d of Israel.
translationNotes: מרה תהיה באחרונה: “it will be bitter in the end.” Echoes Shmuel II 2:26.
בתמימות: with simple wholeheartedness. Kehot’s “wholeheartedly” is close.

hayomYom.english: Where a lantern is placed, those who seek light gather around - for light attracts.
hayomYom.hebrew: כשמעמידים פנס - מתקבצים החפצים באור, כי אור ממשיך - ליכטיגקייט ציהט צו.
hayomYom.clear: When you set up a lantern, those who want light gather around it. Because light draws, light attracts.
translationNotes: אור ממשיך and the Yiddish ליכטיגקייט ציהט צו say the same thing twice: light pulls people in.

hayomYom.english: The Shpola Zeideh ("Grandfather of Shpola"), a disciple of the Maggid of Mezritch, was a man of intense fervor, far more than any of his colleagues - the Maggid's other disciples. When he visited the Alter Rebbe in Liadi in 5569 or 5570 (1809 or 1810) he related that when he was a child of three he saw the Baal Shem Tov. "He placed his holy hand on my heart and ever since I have felt warm." A gesture of a tzadik, certainly seeing him and hearing his voice, must make an impression never to be forgotten.
hayomYom.hebrew:
הסבא משפאלע - דער שפאלער זיידע - היה איש נלהב מאד, ביתר שאת ויתר עז על שאר חבריו תלמידי המגיד. בביקורו בליאדי אצל רבינו הזקן - שנת תקס"ט או תק"ע - סיפר, אשר בהיותו בן שלש שנים ראה את הבעש"ט [הבעל שם טוב] "און ער האט מיר ארויפגעלייגט די הייליגע האנט אויפ'ן הארצען און פון יעמאלט אן איז מיר ווארעם".

תנועת צדיק, ומכל שכן ראיה או שמיעת קול, צריך לפעול שלא ישכח לעד.
hayomYom.clear:
The Shpoler Zeide [“Grandfather of Shpola”] was a very fiery man, far more than his colleagues, the other students of the Maggid.

When he visited the Alter Rebbe in Liadi, in 5569 or 5570 (1809 or 1810), he told that when he was three years old he saw the Baal Shem Tov, “and he put his holy hand on my heart, and since then I have been warm.”

A gesture of a tzaddik, and all the more so seeing him or hearing his voice, should have an effect that is never forgotten.
translationNotes: נלהב מאד: intensely fervent, aflame.
צריך לפעול: it “should” have this effect. Not automatic, it is a demand on the person.

hayomYom.english: (An emendation of the text of Torah Or appears here, meaningful only in Hebrew. Translator) Hearken and hear Israel, this is the time marked for the redemption by Mashiach. The sufferings befalling us are the birth-pangs of Mashiach. Israel will be redeemed only through teshuva. Have no faith in the false prophets who assure you of glories and salvation after the War. Remember the word of G‑d, "Cursed is the man who puts his trust in man, who places his reliance for help in mortals, and turns his heart from G‑d" (Yirmiyahu 17:5). Return Israel unto the Eternal your G‑d; prepare yourself and your family to go forth and receive Mashiach, whose coming is imminent.
hayomYom.hebrew:
תו"א [תורה אור] ד"ה [דיבור המתחיל] אוסרי סעיף המתחיל והנה זהו, צ"ל [צריך להיות]: "והעלאת ניצוצות שנפלו אפילו הבהמות יתעלו כמו שהיה בתחילת".

הסכת ושמע ישראל, העת הזאת היא מועד הגאולה על ידי משיח צדקנו, והיסורים הבאים עלינו הם חבלי משיח, ואין ישראל נגאלין אלא בתשובה. אל תאמינו לנביאי השקר המבטיחים לכם ישועות ונחמות אחרי כלות המלחמה, זכרו דבר ה' [ירמיה יז, ה] ארור הגבר אשר יבטח באדם ושם בשר זרועו ומן ד' יסור לבו. שובה ישראל עד ד' אלקיך, והכן עצמך ובני ביתך לקבל פני משיח צדקנו הבא בקרוב ממש.
hayomYom.clear:
Torah Or, maamar Osri, section beginning V’hinei zehu, should read: “and the raising of the sparks that fell; even the animals will be elevated, as it was at the beginning.”

“Listen and hear, Israel” (Devarim 27:9): this is the time set for the redemption through Mashiach Tzidkeinu. The sufferings coming upon us are the birth pangs of Mashiach, and Israel is redeemed only through teshuva.

Do not believe the false prophets who promise you salvation and comfort after the war ends. Remember the word of G‑d: “Cursed is the man who trusts in man, who makes flesh his strength, and whose heart turns away from G‑d” (Yirmiyahu 17:5).

Return, Israel, to G‑d your G‑d. Prepare yourself and your household to greet Mashiach Tzidkeinu, who is coming very soon.
translationNotes: The old English skips the Torah Or correction. It is translated here from the Hebrew.
הבא בקרוב ממש: “coming truly soon,” literally imminent.
ישועות ונחמות: salvation and consolation. Kehot’s “glories” is loose.

hayomYom.english: The Tzemach Tzedek told Reb Hendel at yechidus: "Study of Zohar exalts the soul; study of Midrash arouses the heart; Tehillim with tears scours the vessel.
hayomYom.hebrew: דער צ"צ [צמח צדק] האט געזאגט ר' הענדל'ן אויף יחידות: זוהר איז מרומם דעם נפש, מדרש איז מעורר דאס הארץ, און תהלים מיט טרערען וואשט אויס די כלי.
hayomYom.clear: The Tzemach Tzedek told R. Hendel at yechidus: Zohar uplifts the soul. Midrash awakens the heart. And Tehillim with tears washes out the vessel.
translationNotes: וואשט אויס די כלי: “washes out the vessel.” Kehot’s “scours” is right.

hayomYom.english: The reason for not studying Torah on nittel-night, I heard from my father, is to avoid adding vitality. My father once said: Those diligent students who begrudge those eight hours and cannot tear themselves away from study - I am not fond of them. This (abstaining from study) applies only until midnight.
hayomYom.hebrew:
מה שנוהגים שלא ללמוד בניתל, שמעתי מאאמו"ר [מאדוני אבי מורי ורבי] הטעם, שהוא כדי שלא להוסיף חיות.
פעם אמר אאמו"ר [אדוני אבי מורי ורבי]: די מתמידים וואס די אכט שעה איז זיי נוגע בנפש, האב איך ניט האלט.
והוא רק עד חצות לילה.
hayomYom.clear:
The custom of not studying Torah on Nittel [Christmas eve]: I heard the reason from my father. It is so as not to add vitality.

My father once said: The diligent students who are pained to lose these eight hours, I am not fond of them.

This applies only until midnight.
translationNotes: חיות: vitality, energy given to the unholy side of the day.
איז זיי נוגע בנפש: it “touches their soul,” they are upset by it. Kehot’s “begrudge” is close.
האב איך ניט האלט: “I don’t care for them,” a mild Yiddish disapproval.

hayomYom.english: The one called for the last aliya (concluding each Book of the Chumash), also says chazak chazak venit'chazeik (as does the congregation). In saying viyhi noam (p. 116) on Saturday night, repeat the verse orech yamim...; but not at Shacharit (of Shabbat, p. 154). When the Tzemach Tzedek was a boy and learned the passage, "Yaakov lived in the land of Egypt seventeen years," his teacher translated according to the Baal Haturim commentary: "Our father Yaakov lived his seventeen best years in Egypt." When he returned home from Cheder he asked his grandfather, the Alter Rebbe: How can it be that our father Yaakov, the elect of the Patriarchs, should have as the best years of his life the seventeen that he lived in Egypt, the land of corruption? The Alter Rebbe answered: It is written, "And Yehuda he sent before him to Yosef to give instructions for Goshen." The Midrash states, and Rashi quotes this, R. Nechemya said - to establish a house of study so Torah would be there and the tribes would study Torah. "To give instructions for Goshen" means (in a deeper sense), when one learns Torah he comes closer to The Al-mighty, may He be blessed, so even in Egypt it was true to say vay'chi - he lived.
hayomYom.hebrew:
גם העולה לתורה אומר חזק חו"נ [חזק ונתחזק].

באמירת ויהי נועם במוצש"ק [במוצאי שבת קודש] כופלים פסוק אורך ימים גו', אבל לא בתפלת שחרית.

בהיות הצ"צ [הצמח צדק] ילד ולמד את הכתוב ויחי יעקב בארץ מצרים שבע עשרה שנה, תירגם לו מורו - ע"פ [על פי] פירוש בעה"ט [בעל הטורים] - יעקב אבינו האט געלעבט די זיבעצעהן בעסטע יאהרען אין מצרים. כשבא הביתה מהחדר שאל את זקנו אדמו"ר הזקן: היתכן שיעקב אבינו, בחיר האבות, יהיו מבחר שנות חייו יז שנה שגר בארץ מצרים ערות הארץ.

ויענהו אדמוה"ז [אדמו"ר הזקן]: כתיב ואת יהודה שלח לפניו אל יוסף להורות לפניו גשנה, ואיתא במדרש מובא ברש"י - א"ר [אמר רבי] נחמיה להתקין לו בית תלמוד, שתהא שם תורה ושיהיו השבטים הוגים בתורה. להורות לפניו גשנה, אז מען לערענט תורה ווערט מען נעהנטער צום אויבערשטען ב"ה [ברוך הוא], און אויך אין מצרים איז געווען ויחי געלעבט.
hayomYom.clear:
The one called up to the Torah [for the last aliya of a book of Chumash] also says Chazak chazak v’nis’chazeik.

When saying Vihi no’am on Motzaei Shabbos, the verse Orech yamim [“With long life”] is repeated. But not at Shacharis.

When the Tzemach Tzedek was a boy, he learned the verse “Yaakov lived in the land of Egypt seventeen years.” His teacher translated it for him according to the Baal HaTurim: “Yaakov our father lived the seventeen best years in Egypt.”

When he came home from cheder he asked his grandfather, the Alter Rebbe: How can it be that Yaakov our father, the chosen of the Avos, had the best years of his life in the seventeen years he lived in Egypt, “the nakedness of the land”?

The Alter Rebbe answered him: It is written, “He sent Yehuda ahead of him to Yosef, to prepare the way before him to Goshen” (Bereishis 46:28). The Midrash, quoted by Rashi, says: R. Nechemya said, to set up a house of study for him, so that there would be Torah there and the tribes would study Torah. “To prepare the way before him to Goshen” means: when you learn Torah you come closer to G‑d, blessed be He. And so even in Egypt there was vayechi, he truly lived.
translationNotes: ערות הארץ (“the nakedness of the land,” Bereishis 42:9) is Yosef’s phrase for Egypt’s moral corruption. Kehot’s “land of corruption” drops the quote.
להורות is read as “to teach, show the way.” Torah is what brings life even in Egypt.

hayomYom.english: Chabad chassidim have a tradition from generations, instituted by the Alter Rebbe, that every day we study a parsha of Chumash of that week's sedra with Rashi. This was done by the Rebbe'im, too.
hayomYom.hebrew: ביי חסידי חב"ד איז מקובל מדור דור, דעם אלטען רבי'ס א תקנה, אז אלע טאג זאל מען לערנען א פרשה חומש מיט פירש"י [פירוש רש"י] פון דער וואך סדרה. אזוי האבען זיך אויך נוהג געווען די רביים נשיאי חסידי חב"ד.
hayomYom.clear: Among Chabad chassidim there is a tradition from generation to generation, an institution of the Alter Rebbe: every day you study a section of Chumash with Rashi from that week’s sedra. The Rebbes, the leaders of Chabad chassidim, also did this.
translationNotes: תקנה: a formal enactment of the Alter Rebbe, not just a custom.

hayomYom.english: The Mitteler Rebbe answered someone at yechidus: When two discuss a subject in avoda and they study together, there are two Divine souls against one natural soul.
hayomYom.hebrew: דער מיטעלער רבי האט געענטפערט איינעם אויף א יחידות: אז איינער רעדט מיט דעם אנדערען בעניני עבודה און זיי לערנען צוזאמען, איז דאס צוויי נפש האלקית אויף איין נפש הטבעית.
hayomYom.clear: The Mitteler Rebbe answered someone at yechidus: When one person talks with another about avoda and they study together, it is two G‑dly souls against one animal soul.
translationNotes: נפש הטבעית: the “natural” soul, i.e. the animal soul. Kehot keeps “natural soul.”

hayomYom.english: The Rebbe, R. Yosef Yitzchak, once met a watercarrier carrying full buckets and remarked: When one encounters water there is an appropriate maxim of the Baal Shem Tov that he should say, namely: "When encountering water one should say that the Baal Shem says that it is a sign of blessing."
hayomYom.hebrew: (כבוד קדושת אדמו"ר [אדוננו מורנו ורבנו] שליט"א [שיחיה לימים טובים ארוכים] פגע בנושא דליים מלאים מים. ויאמר:) אז מ'באגעגענט וואסער זאגט דער בעש"ט [בעל שם טוב]: אז מ'באגעגענט וואסער זאל מען זאגען, אז דער בעל שם זאגט, אז דאס איז א סימן ברכה.
hayomYom.clear: (The Rebbe shlita [the Rebbe Rayatz] once met someone carrying buckets full of water, and said:) When you meet water, the Baal Shem Tov says: when you meet water you should say that the Baal Shem says it is a sign of blessing.
translationNotes: The Hebrew has the Baal Shem Tov telling you to say “the Baal Shem says” it is a blessing. The circular wording is the point.
כבוד קדושת אדמו"ר שליט"א is the Rebbe Rayatz, then living.

hayomYom.english: My father proclaimed at a farbrengen: Just as wearing tefillin every day is a Mitzva commanded by the Torah to every individual regardless of his standing in Torah, whether deeply learned or simple, so too is it an absolute duty for every person to spend a half hour every day thinking about the Torah-education of children, and to do everything in his power - and beyond his power - to inspire children to follow the path along which they are being guided.
hayomYom.hebrew: הכרזת אאמו"ר [אדוני אבי מורי ורבי] באחת ההתועדות: אט אזוי ווי הנחת תפילין בכל יום איז א מצוה דאורייתא אויף יעדען אידען, אהן א חילוק צי א גדול בתורה, צי א איש פשוט, אזוי איז א חוב גמור אויף יעדען אידען צו טראכטען יעדען טאג א האלבע שעה וועגן דעם חנוך פון קינדער, און טאן אלץ, וואס עס איז בכוחו צו טאן און יתר מכפי כחו, זעהן פועל זיין ביי די קינדער, אז זיי זאלען געהן אין דעם דרך וואס מען איז זיי מדריך.
hayomYom.clear:
My father announced at a farbrengen: Just as putting on tefillin every day is a Torah mitzva for every Jew, with no difference between a great Torah scholar and a simple person, so it is an absolute duty for every Jew to think every day for half an hour about the education of children.

And to do everything that is in his power to do, and more than his power, to make sure the children go in the path they are being guided in.
translationNotes: הכרזה: a public proclamation, more forceful than “said.”
יתר מכפי כחו: “beyond his strength.” Kehot keeps this.

hayomYom.english: (Here appears an emendation to the text of Torah Or, relevant only in Hebrew. Translator). Groaning by itself won't do a bit of good. A groan is only a key to open the heart and eyes, so as not to sit there with folded arms, but to plan orderly work and activity, each person wherever he can be effective, to campaign for bolstering Torah, spreading Torah and the observance of Mitzvot. One person might do this through his writing, another with his oratory, another with his wealth.
hayomYom.hebrew:
תו"א [תורה אור] ד"ה [דיבור המתחיל] מי שם פה סעיף המתחיל והנמשל יובן: "כי יש בחינת מעלה" צ"ל צריך להיות "וכן יש מעלה".

באנחות לבד לא נושע. האנחה היא רק כפת המנעול לפתוח את הלב ולפקוח את העינים שלא לשבת בחבוק ידים, רק לסדר עבודה ופועל, איש איש באשר יוכל לפעול ולעשות בתעמולה לחיזוק התורה הרבצת התורה ושמירת המצות, זה בכתבו וזה בנאומו וזה בכספו.
hayomYom.clear:
Torah Or, maamar Mi sam peh, section beginning V’hanimshal yuvan: “for there is a level of advantage” should read “and so there is an advantage.”

Groaning alone will not save us. A groan is only the key to the lock: to open the heart and open the eyes, so you won’t sit with folded arms, but organize work and action. Each person wherever he can be effective and act, to campaign for strengthening Torah, spreading Torah and keeping the mitzvos. One with his pen, one with his speeches, one with his money.
translationNotes: The old English skips the Torah Or correction. It is translated here from the Hebrew.
לא נושע: “we will not be saved.” Kehot’s “won’t do a bit of good” is weaker.
כפת המנעול: the handle or key of the lock.

hayomYom.english: On this day the Alter Rebbe passed away in the village Piena on Saturday night of parshat Sh'mot 5573 (1812). He is interred in the city of Haditz. My grandfather (R. Shmuel) asked the Tzemach Tzedek: What did Grandfather (the Alter Rebbe) intend with the "ways of Chassidus" and what did he intend with Chassidus? The Tzemach Tzedek answered: The "ways of Chassidus" are that all Chassidim are to be like one family, with affection, as Torah teaches. Chassidus is vitality. Chassidus is to bring life and illumination into everything, to shed light even on the undesirable - to become aware of one's own evil exactly as it is, in order to correct it.
hayomYom.hebrew:
הסתלקות אדמו"ר הזקן בכפר פיענא במוצאי שבת קדש פרשת שמות תקע"ג. ומ"כ [ומנוחתו כבוד] בעיר האדיץ.
אאזמו"ר [אדוני אבי זקני מורי ורבי] שאל את הצ"צ [הצמח צדק]: וואס האט דער זיידע געוואלט מיט דרכי החסידות, און וואס האט ער געוואלט מיט חסידות. ויענהו הצ"צ: דרכי החסידות איז, אז אלע חסידים זאלען זיין ווי איין משפחה ע"פ [על פי] התורה באהבה. חסידות איז חיות. אריינטראגען א חיות און באלייכטען אלץ, אויך דעם לא טוב, מען זאל וויסען פון דעם אייגענעם רע ווי ער איז, אויף מתקן זיין עס.
hayomYom.clear:
The passing of the Alter Rebbe, in the village of Piena, on Motzaei Shabbos of parshas Shemos, 5573 (1812). He is buried in the town of Haditch.

My grandfather [the Rebbe Maharash] asked the Tzemach Tzedek: What did Grandfather [the Alter Rebbe] want with the “ways of Chassidus,” and what did he want with Chassidus?

The Tzemach Tzedek answered him: The ways of Chassidus are that all chassidim should be like one family, with love, according to the Torah. Chassidus is vitality. It is to bring vitality and light into everything, even into the not good: you should know your own evil as it really is, in order to correct it.
translationNotes: אאזמו"ר is the Rebbe Maharash.
לא טוב: “the not good.” Kehot’s “undesirable” loses the plain phrasing.

hayomYom.english: Bless Rosh Chodesh Sh'vat. Say the entire Tehillim in the early morning. Day of farbrengen. Haftora: Haba'im yashreish. From my father's sichot: Exodus from Egypt means leaving limitations and bounds, and Chassidus is to enable man to leave the restrictions of the material world. There is a difference: The Egyptian Exodus means shattering and then departure, which is why they went away from Egypt. The Chassidic exodus means purification and correction, stepping out of worldly limitations and bounds while remaining in the world. This means, while functioning within the world we must transcend its limitations. We are to remove the limitations and bounds, and perceive the truth - that the world per se is truly good, since, after all, the natural world is what G‑d intended. This is attained through the avoda of Chassidus.
hayomYom.hebrew: מברכים ר"ח שבט, אמירת כל התהלים בהשכמה, יום התוועדות.
hayomYom.clear:
From my father’s talks: Leaving Egypt means leaving limitations and boundaries, and Chassidus is to bring a person out of the limitations of the material world.

There is a difference. The Exodus from Egypt was breaking and then leaving, which is why they left Egypt. The exodus of Chassidus is refining and correcting: going out of the world’s limitations and boundaries while staying in the world. While working within the world, you rise above its limitations.

You remove the limitations and boundaries and see the truth: the world itself is truly good, because the natural world is what G‑d intended. This is reached through the avoda of Chassidus.
translationNotes: The Hebrew field holds only the calendar line. The talk is translated from the Kehot English.

calendar.original5703: Bless Rosh Chodesh Shevat. Say the entire Tehillim early in the morning. Day of farbrengen. Haftorah: Haba’im yashreish.

hayomYom.dataFlag: Hebrew contains only the calendar line (מברכים ר"ח שבט...); the haftorah line and the talk exist only in the English. Translation based on the English.

hayomYom.english: In the b'racha V'lamalshinim (p. 55, "Let thee..." in English), pause slightly between ut'mageir ("crush") and v'tachnia ("and subdue"), in consonance with the kavana that t'akeir ut'shabeir ut'mageir ("uproot, break, crush") refer to the three kelipot that must be completely eradicated. V'tachnia ("subdue") refers to kelipat noga that must be subdued, but can be purified.
hayomYom.hebrew: בברכת ולמלשינים מפסיקים קצת בין "ותמגר" לתיבת "ותכניע", מתאים להכוונה, אשר "תעקר ותשבר ותמגר" הם נגד ג' קליפות שצריכים העברה לגמרי, "ותכניע" - לנגד קליפת נוגה שצריכה הכנעה ויש בה ברור.
hayomYom.clear: In the blessing V’lamalshinim, pause slightly between “us’mageir” [“and crush”] and the word “v’sachnia” [“and subdue”]. This fits the intention: “uproot, break and crush” are against the three [completely impure] kelipos, which must be removed entirely. “And subdue” is against kelipas noga, which needs to be subdued, and can be refined.
translationNotes: יש בה ברור: kelipas noga contains good that can be extracted and refined.
Kehot’s siddur page numbers are not in the original and are left out.

hayomYom.english: The Alter Rebbe said: Jewish physical matter is spiritual. G‑d gives us material bounty for us to transform into something spiritual. When occasionally it is not so at the moment (G‑d has not provided the material wealth), then we must give G‑d whatever we can, even a "pauper's offering," and then He gives generously.
hayomYom.hebrew: רבינו הזקן אמר: אידישע גשמיות איז רוחניות, דער אויבערשטער גיט אונז גשמיות, מיר זאלן דערפון מאכען רוחניות. אמאל אז עס איז לרגע ניט אזוי, דארפען געבען דעם אויבערשטען אפילו מנחת עני גיט ער א פולע.
hayomYom.clear:
The Alter Rebbe said: Jewish material things are spiritual. G‑d gives us material things so we will make spirituality out of them.

Sometimes, for a moment, it is not so. Then you need to give G‑d even a pauper’s offering, and He gives in full.
translationNotes: אידישע גשמיות איז רוחניות: “Jewish physicality is spirituality,” a flat statement.
גיט ער א פולע: “He gives a full one,” a full measure in return.

hayomYom.english: The published version of Sefer Hachakira (Derech Emuna) of the Tzemach Tzedek lacks many glosses. He composed it in connection with his trips to Petersburg where he had to answer many questions on those subjects.
hayomYom.hebrew: בספר החקירה (דרך אמונה) להצ"צ [להצמח צדק] הנדפס - חסרים הרבה הגהות. הצ"צ [הצמח צדק] חברו ביחס עם נסיעותיו לפטרבורג, ששם היה צריך לענות על כמה שאלות בענינים אלו.
hayomYom.clear: In the printed Sefer HaChakira (Derech Emuna) of the Tzemach Tzedek, many glosses are missing. The Tzemach Tzedek wrote it in connection with his trips to Petersburg, where he had to answer a number of questions on these subjects.
translationNotes: Matches the original. No meaning lost.

hayomYom.english: We are "day workers." Day means light. Our work is to illuminate, to enlighten the world with the light of the Torah. Besides the necessity of maintaining our own selves properly, with G‑d's help - being what we ought to be - our whole avoda is to be privileged to develop pupils who are firmly based people, devoted with heart and mind to the inner kavana, the intention or purpose of our existence. Our pupils must know that it is not sufficient to study the Revealed Torah and to cherish the Sacred by observing mitzvot; there must also be avoda sheb'leiv, the service of the heart, davening.
hayomYom.hebrew: אנן פועלי דיממא אנן. יום הוא אור, עבודתנו היא עבודת האור, מאכען ליכטיג די וועלט באור תורה. ומלבד כי צריכים לעמוד במעמד ומצב טוב בעז"ה [בעזרת ה'] בעצמו - אליין דארף מען זיין ווי עס דארף צו זיין - הנה כל העבודה היא לזכות להעמיד תלמידים גרונטיקע מענשען, אשר יהיו מסורים בלבם ודעתם אל הכוונה הפנימית. שאינו מספיק למוד תורה הנגלית וחבוב הקודש בשמירת המצות, כי אם צריכים גם עבודה שבלב.
hayomYom.clear:
We are day workers. Day is light. Our work is the work of light: to make the world bright with the light of Torah.

Besides the need to be, with G‑d’s help, in a good position and state yourself, since you yourself must be what you should be, the whole avoda is to merit raising students who are solid people. People who will be devoted in their heart and mind to the inner intention. Because it is not enough to study the revealed Torah and to cherish holiness by keeping the mitzvos. You also need avoda shebalev [service of the heart, davening].
translationNotes: אנן פועלי דיממא אנן is Aramaic, “we are day workers.”
גרונטיקע מענשען: “solid, grounded people.” Kehot’s “firmly based” is close.
הכוונה הפנימית: the inner intention, the purpose behind it all.

hayomYom.english: The daily recital of Tehillim after davening applies equally to Chabad chassidic shuls and to those who follow the Ashkenazic or Polish nusach - may G‑d be with them. On account of ahavat Yisrael, love of our fellow...and especially in view of the importance and inner purpose of saying Tehillim with a minyan, which literally affects all of Israel, materially in "children, life and sustenance," and spiritually ...we must endeavor with every means possible that it become an established practice in every shul of every nusach.
hayomYom.hebrew: אמירת תהלים האמור (בכל יום אחר התפלה) אין בזה שום הפרש בין בתי כנסיות של אנשי שלומינו שי' או מתפללי נוסח אשכנז או נוסח פולין, ד' עליהם יחיו. ומצד אהבת ישראל... ובפרט לגודל הענין של אמירת תהלים בצבור וכוונתה הפנימית, הנוגע לכלל ישראל ממש בגשמיות, בבני חיי ומזונא, וברוחניות... עלינו להשתדל בכל מיני השתדלות אשר יוקבע בכל בית הכנסת מאיזה נוסח שיהיה.
hayomYom.clear:
As for the saying of Tehillim mentioned above (every day after davening), there is no difference at all between the shuls of anash [our chassidim] and those who daven in Nusach Ashkenaz or Nusach Poland, may G‑d be with them.

Because of ahavas Yisrael... and especially because of the great importance of saying Tehillim with a congregation, and its inner purpose, which literally affects all of Israel, materially in children, life and sustenance, and spiritually... we must make every possible effort that it be established in every shul, of whatever nusach.
translationNotes: אנשי שלומינו: “people of our circle,” Chabad chassidim.
בני חיי ומזונא: the classic triad of children, life and livelihood (Moed Katan 28a).

hayomYom.english: My father related: The maamar Va'eira...ushmi Hashem, discussing the idea that "none of them will be repelled" - (not the maamar with this title which is printed in Torah Or) acquired the name, "the frum - ('G‑d-fearing') Va'eira." The Alter Rebbe would repeat it every three years, each time almost verbatim. The Tzemach Tzedek said, "Each time there was a new light." "My father commented: Or, light, is always the same, but maor, luminary, is always like something new.
hayomYom.hebrew: אאמו"ר [אדוני אבי מורי ורבי] סיפר: הדרוש וארא גו' ושמי ד' גו' המדבר בענין כי לא ידח ממנו נדח (אינו הנדפס בתו"א [בתורה אור]), קנה לו שם "דער פרומער וארא", והיה רגיל רבינו הזקן לחזור אותו אחת לשלש שנים, ובכל פעם ופעם כמעט שהיה אומר אותו כלשונו. ואמר הצ"צ [הצמח צדק]: יעדער מאל איז געווען א אור חדש. האט דער טאטע געזאגט: א אור איז אלע מאל גלייך, אבער מאור איז אלעמאל ווי א דבר חדש.
hayomYom.clear:
My father related: The maamar Va’eira... ushmi Hashem [“I appeared... and My name Hashem”], which discusses the idea “so that no one is banished from Him” (Shmuel II 14:14) (not the one printed in Torah Or), got the name “the frum Va’eira.” The Alter Rebbe used to repeat it once every three years, and each time he said it almost word for word.

The Tzemach Tzedek said: “Each time it was a new light.”

My father commented: Or, light, is always the same. But a ma’or, a source of light, is always like something new.
translationNotes: כמעט שהיה אומר אותו כלשונו: almost in the very same words, yet felt new each time.
מאור is the source, the luminary, which keeps generating new light.

hayomYom.english: Torah Or was first printed in 5597 (1837) in Kopust (without supplements). The Tzemach Tzedek, in his letter of Sh'vat 3 that year, wrote:   Before the second part could be printed, informers had the government close a number of Hebrew printshops in Russia, including the one in Kopust where the Torah Or was printed. In 5608 (1848) the second part was printed in Zhitomir with a different title, Likutei Torah.
hayomYom.hebrew:
תורה אור נדפס לראשונה בשנת תקצ"ז בקאפוסט (בלי ההוספות). הצ"צ [הצמח צדק] במכתבו מיום ג' שבט תקצ"ז כותב: ספר תורה אור הנדפס עתה... בו מאמרים רוב הדרושים שמשנת תקנ"ו עד סוף תקע"ב, אשר הרבה מהם שם רבינו ז"ל [זכרונו לברכה] בעצמו עין עיונו עליהם והגיהם, והסכימה דעתו הקדושה להביאם לבית הדפוס. והספר כולל שני חלקים, חלק הראשון על שני חומשי התורה וחנוכה ופורים גם כמה דרושים לחג השבועות זמן מ"ת [מתן תורה] בפ'[רשת] יתרו וקצת לפסח בפ'[רשת] ויקהל. וחלק השני אי"ה [אם ירצה ה'] על ג' חומשי התורה ושה"ש [ושיר השירים] ומועדים ור"ה [וראש השנה] ויוכ"פ [ויום כפור]... ושם המחבר נאה לו שניאור כמו ואהבת בגימט'[ריא] ב"פ [ב' פעמים] אור... עכ"ל [עד כאן לשונו].

לא הספיקו להדפיס רק חלק הראשון, כי ע"י [על ידי] מלשינות סגרה הממשלה כמה מבתי הדפוס העברים ברוסיה, וביניהם גם ביה"ד [בית הדפוס] בקאפוסט אשר שם הדפיסו התו"א [התורה אור]. בשנת תר"ח נדפס ח"ב [חלק ב'] בזיטאמיר ובשינוי השם "לקוטי תורה".
hayomYom.clear:
Torah Or was first printed in 5597 (1837) in Kopust (without the additions). The Tzemach Tzedek, in his letter of 3 Shevat 5597, writes:

“The book Torah Or, now printed... contains most of the maamarim from 5556 to the end of 5572. Our master [the Alter Rebbe] himself reviewed many of them and edited them, and his holy mind agreed to have them printed. The book has two parts. The first part is on two books of the Torah, and Chanuka and Purim, and also several maamarim for Shavuos, the time of the Giving of the Torah, in parshas Yisro, and some for Pesach in parshas Vayakhel. The second part, G‑d willing, is on three books of the Torah, Shir HaShirim, the festivals, Rosh Hashana and Yom Kippur... And the author’s name fits it: Shneur [read as shnei or, “two lights”], just as v’ahavta in gematria is twice or [light]...” End of quote.

They managed to print only the first part. Because of informers, the government closed a number of Hebrew printing houses in Russia, among them the press in Kopust where Torah Or was printed. In 5608 (1848) the second part was printed in Zhitomir, under a different name: Likutei Torah.
translationNotes: The Kehot English leaves the letter blank. The quote is translated here from the Hebrew.
שניאור כמו ואהבת בגימטריא ב"פ אור: the name Shneur suggests “two lights,” just as ואהבת (414) equals twice אור (207).
hayomYom.dataFlag: English is truncated: the Tzemach Tzedek's letter is missing (blank after 'wrote:'). Letter translated from the Hebrew.

hayomYom.english: Mitzrayim (Egypt) expresses constriction, limitation. The spiritual Egyptian exile is the animal soul's restricting and concealing the G‑dly soul so severely that the G‑dly soul is compressed to the degree that it is diminished and obscured. "Exodus from Egypt" is the removal of the constriction and bounds; i.e. the intellect in the brain illuminates the heart, bringing about fine character traits translated into actual practice.
hayomYom.hebrew: מצרים הוא לשון מיצר וגבול. גלות מצרים ברוחניות הוא מה שנפש הבהמית מגבלת ומסתרת על הנפש האלקית, עד שנפה"א [שנפש האלוקית] מתצמצמת כל כך שנעשה בקטנות והעלם. ויציאת מצרים הוא הסרת המיצר והגבול. והיינו דהשכל שבמוח מאיר בלב במדות טובות בפועל ממש.
hayomYom.clear:
Mitzrayim [Egypt] means constriction and limitation. The spiritual exile of Egypt is when the animal soul limits and hides the G‑dly soul, until the G‑dly soul is so contracted that it becomes small and hidden.

Leaving Egypt is removing the constriction and limitation. That is: the intellect in the mind shines into the heart, in good character traits, in actual practice.
translationNotes: קטנות והעלם: “smallness and concealment,” the state of mochin d’katnus.
בפועל ממש: in actual deed. The light of the mind has to show in behavior.

hayomYom.english: One must recite words of Torah copiously, saying Tehillim or verbally reviewing Mishna whenever and wherever possible, in order to bolster the existence of Creation, to be saved from chibut hakever and kaf hakela,1 and to merit all the highest revelations.
hayomYom.hebrew: א מענטש דארף מרבה זיין אין זאגען אותיות התורה (זאגען תהלים, חזר'ן משניות) ווען און וואו ער קען, בכדי צו שטארקען דעם קיום העולם, בכדי מציל צו זיין זיך פון חיבוט הקבר און כף הקלע, און זוכה זיין צו אלע העכסטע גילוים.
hayomYom.clear: A person should say many words of Torah (say Tehillim, review Mishnayos) whenever and wherever he can. This strengthens the existence of the world, saves him from chibut hakever and kaf hakela [the afterlife purifications], and earns him all the highest revelations.
translationNotes: קיום העולם: the continued existence of the world itself. Kehot’s “Creation” is the same idea.

hayomYom.english: My father wrote that he heard in the name of the Alter Rebbe that all rabbinic authors until and including the Taz and Shach, composed their works with ruach hakodesh, the Divine Spirit. An individual's ruach hakodesh, as explained by Korban Ha'eida in Tractate Sh'kalim (Talmud Yerushalmi), end of ch. 3, means that the mysteries of Torah are revealed to him. This comes from the aspect of chochma in its pre-revelation state.
hayomYom.hebrew: אאמו"ר [אדוני אבי מורי ורבי] כותב ששמע בשם רבינו הזקן, שכל המחברים עד הט"ז והש"ך, והם בכלל, עשו החבורים שלהם ברוח הקודש, וענין רוה"ק [רוח הקודש] איתא בקרבן העדה ספ"ג [סוף פרק ג'] דשקלים שזהו שמגלים לו רזי תורה, שזהו מבחי'[נת] העלם דחכמה.
hayomYom.clear:
My father [the Rebbe Rashab] wrote that he heard in the name of the Alter Rebbe: All the authors of halachic works, up to and including the Taz and the Shach, wrote their works with ruach hakodesh [Divine inspiration].

What is ruach hakodesh? The Korban HaEidah (on Yerushalmi Shekalim, end of ch. 3) explains: it means the secrets of the Torah are revealed to the person. This comes from the hidden level of Chochma.
translationNotes: המחברים is “the authors” of halachic works. Kehot’s “rabbinic authors” is fine.
והם בכלל: the Taz and Shach themselves are included.
העלם דחכמה is Chochma in its concealed state, before it is revealed.

hayomYom.english: When the Alter Rebbe was nine he studied geometry and astronomy. At ten he composed a calendar for fifteen years. When he was twelve years old, it happened that he lectured publicly on Rambam's laws of kidush hachodesh. The preeminent Torah-scholars who were present at that time in the study-hall were utterly overwhelmed.
hayomYom.clear: When the Alter Rebbe was nine, he studied geometry and astronomy. At ten, he drew up a calendar for fifteen years. When he was twelve, he once gave a public lecture on the Rambam’s laws of Kiddush HaChodesh [sanctifying the new month]. The leading Torah scholars who were in the study hall at the time were completely astounded.
translationNotes: No Hebrew text available to compare. Based on the English.
hayomYom.dataFlag: Hebrew field is empty. Translation based on Kehot English only.

hayomYom.english: In these days especially, when by G‑d's kindness we stand at the threshold of redemption, we must make every conceivable effort to strengthen every facet of our religion. Mitzvot must be observed b'hidur, with "beauty," beyond minimal requirements. Customs must be kept scrupulously, nothing compromised. It is a Mitzva and duty of every Rabbi in Israel to inform his congregation that the current tribulations and agonies are the "birth-pangs of Mashiach." G‑d is demanding that we return to Torah and mitzvot, that we not hinder the imminent coming of our righteous Mashiach.
hayomYom.hebrew: בפרט בזמן הזה אשר בחסדי השי"ת [השם יתברך] אנו עומדים על סף הגאולה, עלינו להתאמץ בכל מיני אימוץ, לחזק כל עניני הדת בהידור מצוה, ולשמור את כל המנהגים מבלי לוותר אף כל שהוא, ומצוה וחובה על כל רב בישראל, להודיע לקהל עדתו כי הצרות והיסורים חבלי משיח המה, וה"א [וה' אלקנו] דורש מאתנו תשובה לתומ"צ [לתורה ומצות], שלא נעכב ביאת משיח צדקנו בקרוב ממש.
hayomYom.clear:
Especially now, when by G‑d’s kindness we stand at the threshold of the Redemption, we must make every possible effort to strengthen every part of our religion, keeping mitzvos with hiddur [beyond the minimum], and keeping every custom without giving up even the slightest bit.

It is a mitzva and a duty for every rav in Israel to tell his congregation: these troubles and sufferings are the birth pangs of Mashiach. G‑d our G‑d is asking us to return to Torah and mitzvos, so that we do not hold back the coming of our righteous Mashiach, very soon, truly.
translationNotes: בקרוב ממש: “very soon, truly.” Kehot’s “imminent” softens ממש.
דורש מאתנו תשובה: G‑d asks for teshuva, a return. Kehot has this.

hayomYom.english: When my father concluded the entire Talmud for the third time he said a maamar on the subject of the meaning of a hadran. During the year of mourning for his mother, my father concluded the entire Mishna at the end of eleven months, and the entire Talmud at her Yahrzeit.
hayomYom.hebrew:
כשסיים אאמו"ר [אדוני אבי מורי ורבי] הש"ס בפעם השלישית אמר מאמר דא"ח [דברי אלוקים חיים], ותוכנו מהו הדרן.
בשנת האבילות אחרי אמו סיים אאמו"ר [אדוני אבי מורי ורבי] ש"ס [ששה סדרי] משנה לסוף י"א חדש, וליום היא"צ [היארצייט] - כל הש"ס.
hayomYom.clear:
When my father [the Rebbe Rashab] finished the entire Talmud for the third time, he said a maamar of Chassidus whose theme was: what is a hadran [the completion of a tractate]?

During the year of mourning for his mother, my father finished all six orders of Mishna at the end of eleven months, and the entire Talmud on her yahrzeit.
translationNotes: מהו הדרן: the maamar asked what “hadran” itself means.
ש"ס משנה is all six orders of Mishna.

hayomYom.english: (At this point in the Hebrew text appears an emendation of a passage in Torah Or, relevant only in Hebrew. Translator). When my grandmother, Rebbetzin Rivka, was eighteen (in 5611, 1851) she fell ill and the physician ordered her to eat immediately upon awakening. She, however, did not wish to eat before davening; so she davened very early, then ate breakfast. When her father-in-law, the Tzemach Tzedek, learned of this he said to her: "A Jew must be healthy and strong. The Torah says about mitzvot, 'Live in them,' meaning bring vitality into the mitzvot. To be able to infuse mitzvot with vitality, one must be strong and joyful." Then he concluded: "You should not be without food. Better to eat for the sake of davening rather than to daven for the sake of eating;" he then blessed her with long life. [She was born in 5593 (1833) and passed away on Sh'vat 10, 5674 (1914)]. My father told this teaching of the Tzemach Tzedek to someone at yechidus, adding: "And this must be done with joy."
hayomYom.hebrew:
