תו"א [תורה אור] ד"ה [דבור המתחיל] למען תהי'[ה] סוף סעיף המתחיל אמנם, "לא ישבות יומם מלראות" צ"ל [צריך להיות] "לא ישבות יומם ולילה מלרצות".

אמי זקנתי (הרבנית מרת רבקה נ"ע )[נשמתה עדן] בהיותה כבת שמונה עשרה שנה - בשנת תרי"א - חלתה, וציוה הרופא אשר תאכל תיכף בקומה משנתה, אמנם היא לא חפצה לטעום קודם התפלה, והיתה מתפללת בהשכמה, ואחר התפלה היתה אוכלת פת שחרית. כשנודע הדבר לחותנה אדמו"ר [אדננו מורנו ורבנו] הצ"צ [הצמח צדק], אמר לה: א איד דארף זיין געזונד און א בעל כח. אויף מצות שטייט וחי בהם, איז דער טייטש וחי בהם, מען דארף אריינבריינגען א חיות אין מצות. בכדי אז מען זאל קענען אריינבריינגען א חיות אין מצות, מוז מען זיין א בעל כח און זיין בשמחה. וסיים: דו דארפסט ניט זיין קיין ניכטערע. בעסער עסען צוליב דאווענען ווי דאווענען צוליב עסען. ובירכה באריכות ימים, - (נולדה בשנת תקצ"ג ונפטרה י' שבט תרע"ד).-
מאמר זה אמר אאמו"ר [אדוני אבי מורי ורבי] לאחד על יחידות, והוסיף: און מען דארף עס טאן בשמחה.
hayomYom.clear:
Torah Or, maamar L’maan tihyeh, end of the section beginning Amnam: “he will not cease day from seeing” should read “he will not cease day and night from desiring.”

My grandmother, Rebbetzin Rivka, fell ill when she was about eighteen, in 5611 [1851]. The doctor ordered her to eat as soon as she woke up. But she did not want to taste anything before davening, so she would daven very early and eat breakfast after davening.

When her father-in-law, the Tzemach Tzedek, heard about this, he told her: “A Jew has to be healthy and strong. About mitzvos it says, ‘and live by them’ (Vayikra 18:5). The meaning of ‘and live by them’ is: you have to bring life into the mitzvos. To be able to bring life into the mitzvos, you have to be strong and joyful.”

He concluded: “You must not go without eating. Better to eat for the sake of davening than to daven for the sake of eating.” And he blessed her with long life. (She was born in 5593 [1833] and passed away on 10 Shevat 5674 [1914].)

My father told this teaching to someone at yechidus [private audience], and added: “And you have to do it with joy.”
translationNotes: The Kehot English skips the Torah Or correction. Translated here from the Hebrew.
ניכטערע: “fasting,” on an empty stomach. Kehot’s “without food” is close.
בעל כח: a strong, able person.

hayomYom.english: The routine of the day begins with saying modeh ani (Siddur Tehilat HaShem p. 6, "I acknowledge before You, living and eternal King etc..."). This is said before the morning laving of the hands, even while the hands are "impure." The reason is that all the impurites in the world do not defile a Jew's "I acknowledge." He might lack one thing or another, but his modeh ani remains intact.
hayomYom.hebrew: דער סדר פון טאג הויבט זיך אן מיט מודה אני, און דאס זאגט מען פאר נעגעל וואסער אפילו בידים טמאות, ווארום כל הטומאות שבעולם זיינען ניט מטמא דעם מודה אני פון א אידען. ער קען זיין א חסר בזה או בזה, אבער דער מודה אני בלייבט גאנץ.
hayomYom.clear: The order of the day begins with Modeh ani. You say it before negel vasser [the morning hand-washing], even with impure hands. The reason: all the impurities in the world cannot make a Jew’s Modeh ani impure. He may be lacking in this or that, but his Modeh ani stays whole.
translationNotes: גאנץ: “whole, intact.” Kehot has this.
The Siddur page reference and the text of Modeh ani are Kehot additions, not in the original. Left out.

hayomYom.english: Intellect and excitement are two separate worlds. Intellect - a world cold and settled; excitement - a world seething and impetuous. Man's avoda is to combine them, unite them. The impetuousness then becomes transformed into a longing, and the intellect into the guide in a life of avoda and action.
hayomYom.hebrew: השכל וההתפעלות שני עולמות הם: עולם קר ומיושב, ועולם רותח ומבוהל. וזאת היא עבודת האדם לחברם להיות לאחדים. ואז הבהלה נהפכת לשאיפה, והשכל - למורה דרך בחיים של עבודה ופועל.
hayomYom.clear: Intellect and emotional excitement are two separate worlds. One is a cold, settled world. The other is a boiling, agitated world. Our avoda is to join them together until they are one. Then the agitation turns into aspiration, and the intellect becomes the guide in a life of avoda and action.
translationNotes: שאיפה: “aspiration,” a reaching toward. Kehot’s “longing” is close.
להיות לאחדים: to become truly one, not just “combined.”

hayomYom.english: Yahrzeit is observed on the anniversary of the day of death even the first year, and even if the day of burial was much later than the day of death. When my grandfather (R. Shmuel) was seven, his father (the Tzemach Tzedek) once answered him: The kindness and special quality in G‑d's making man upright, to walk erectly, is that though he walks on the earth he sees the Heavens; not so with beasts that go on all fours; they see only the earth.
hayomYom.hebrew:
יא"צ [יאר צייט] - ביום המיתה אפילו בשנה ראשונה, ואפילו כשיום הקבורה רחוק מיום המיתה.
מענה הצ"צ [הצמח צדק] לאאזמו"ר [לאדוני אבי זקני מורי ורבי] בהיותו כבן שבע: החסד ויתרון המעלה אשר האלקים עשה את האדם ישר להיות הולך בקומה זקופה הוא, דהגם שהולך על הארץ, מכל מקום הוא רואה את השמים, לא כן בהולך על ארבע דאינו רואה אלא את הארץ.
hayomYom.clear:
A yahrzeit is kept on the day of death, even in the first year, and even when the burial was long after the day of death.

The Tzemach Tzedek’s answer to my grandfather [the Rebbe Maharash] when he was about seven: The kindness and special quality in G‑d making man upright, walking erect, is this: even though he walks on the earth, he still sees the heavens. Not so with an animal that walks on all fours. It sees only the earth.
translationNotes: מענה: an “answer,” meaning a reply to the child’s question.
אשר האלקים עשה את האדם ישר echoes Koheles 7:29.

hayomYom.english: Tachanun (p. 103) is not said at Mincha. Our Holy forebears, the Rebbe'im through the generations, appealed to G‑d and evoked Divine compassion toward their Chassidim, those bound to them. This was not all; they also had an avoda of bringing their Chassidim to mind, inwardly, pondering their affection and attachment to the Rebbe, reciprocating that affection and attachment. Bringing someone to mind has the effect of arousing that person's innermost powers. We see that when one looks deeply and intently at another he will turn around and return the glance, because the penetrating gaze awakens the core of the soul. Thought has the same effect.
hayomYom.hebrew:
במנחה אין אומרים תחנון.
בא כ"ק [כבוד קדושת] אבותינו רבותינו הקדושים, איז, לבד דער ענין פון התעוררות רחמים אויף די מקושרים, געווען א עבודה פון דערמאנען בינו לבין עצמו די מקושרים, און אריינטראכטן בענין אהבתם והתקשרותם כמים הפנים, וואס דאס איז מעורר די כחות פנימים פון דעם וואס מ'טראכט וועגען עם, ווי מיר זעהען במוחש, אז מ'קוקט שטארק אויף איינעם מוז ער א קוק טאן, ווייל די הבטה פנימית איז מעורר דעם עצם הנפש, און אזוי איז אויך אין דעם כח המחשבה.
hayomYom.clear:
Our holy forefathers, our Rebbeim: besides arousing Divine mercy for their mekusharim [those bound to them], they had a further avoda. Privately, on their own, they would bring their mekusharim to mind and think deeply about their love and attachment, “as water reflects a face to a face” (Mishlei 27:19).

This stirs up the inner powers of the one being thought about. You can see this plainly: when you look hard at someone, he has to turn and look back, because an inner gaze awakens the very core of the soul. The power of thought works the same way.
translationNotes: כמים הפנים: the love reflects back, like a face in water. Kehot’s “reciprocating” loses the image.
בינו לבין עצמו: privately, alone with himself.
מוז ער א קוק טאן: he “has to” look back. It is compelled, not optional.

calendar.original5703: No tachanun at Mincha.

hayomYom.english: When the second part of Torah Or was about to be printed, Chassidim knew that the Tzemach Tzedek had written glosses and commentaries on the maamarim. They pleaded with him to publish these with the maamarim, but he refused. He then dreamt that his grandfather, the Alter Rebbe, visited him and asked him to publish them, but he revealed this to no one. Only after three of his sons had the same dream and reported this to him did he agree to have his glosses and commentary printed with the second part of Torah Or, which they now entitled "Likutei Torah."
hayomYom.hebrew: אין אומרים תחנון.
hayomYom.clear:
When the second part of Torah Or was about to be printed, the chassidim knew that the Tzemach Tzedek had written notes and explanations on the maamarim. They begged him to print these together with the maamarim, but he refused.

Then he dreamed that his grandfather, the Alter Rebbe, came to him and asked him to print them. He told no one. Only after three of his sons had the same dream and told him did he agree to print his notes and explanations with the second part of Torah Or. That part was then named Likutei Torah.
translationNotes: No Hebrew text for the content to compare. Based on the English.

calendar.original5703: No tachanun.

hayomYom.dataFlag: Hebrew field holds only the calendar line (no tachanun). Translation based on Kehot English only.

hayomYom.english: My father said: Coldness and heresy are separated by so slender a barrier! It is said, "For the Eternal your G‑d is a consuming fire." G‑dliness is a flame of fire. Learning Torah and davening must be with a blazing heart, that "all my bones may utter" the words of G‑d in Torah and prayer.
hayomYom.hebrew: אאמו"ר [אדוני אבי מורי ורבי] אמר: צווישען קעלט און כפירה איז גאר א דינע מחיצה. עס שטעהט כי ה' אלקיך אש אוכלה הוא, אלקות איז פלאם פייער, לערנען און דאווענען בעדארף מען מיט התלהבות הלב, אז כל עצמותי תאמרנה די דברי ה' אין תורה ותפלה.
hayomYom.clear:
My father [the Rebbe Rashab] said: Between coldness and heresy there is only a very thin wall.

It says, “For G‑d your G‑d is a consuming fire” (Devarim 4:24). G‑dliness is a flame of fire. You have to learn and daven with a heart on fire, so that “all my bones will say” (Tehillim 35:10) the words of G‑d in Torah and in prayer.
translationNotes: גאר א דינע מחיצה: “a very thin partition.” A plain statement, not an exclamation as in Kehot.
התלהבות הלב: a heart aflame.

hayomYom.english: There is a custom of eating black buckwheat on this Shabbat. On Shabbat B'shalach 5621 (1861) the Tzemach Tzedek said the maamar R'u ki Hashem printed in Likutei Torah. Shortly afterward he said to his son, my grandfather: On Shabbat B'shalach 5565 (1805) my grandfather said this maamar. Afterwards he sent for me and told me that in 5529 (1769) when he was in Mezritch the Maggid had summoned him to his room and had said:   Then the Maggid repeated the maamar to the Alter Rebbe, adding an interpretation of "River Ginai, part for me," which is similar to k'riat yam suf, the splitting of the Red Sea. The Tzemach Tzedek concluded: Today the Baal Shem Tov, the Maggid and the Alter Rebbe came to me, each repeating the maamar in his own style. Several hours later the Tzemach Tzedek called my grandfather again and told him an interpretation of the maamar.
hayomYom.hebrew:
עס איז א מנהג צו עסן שווארצע קאשע.

שבת בשלח שנת תרכ"א אמר הצ"צ [הצמח צדק] המאמר ראו כי ה' הנדפס בלקו"ת [בלקוטי תורה]. וסיפר אח"כ [אחר כך] לבנו אאזמו"ר [אדוני אבי זקני מורי ורבי]: שבת בשלח שנת תקס"ה אמר אאזמו"ר [אדוני אבי זקני מורי ורבי] זה המאמר. אח"כ [אחר כך] קרא אותי וסיפר לי, אשר בשנת תקכ"ט בהיותו במעזריטש, קרא אותו הה"מ [הרב המגיד] לחדרו וא"ל [ואמר לו]: שבת בשלח שנת תקט"ז אמר הבעש"ט [הבעל שם טוב] מאמר ע"פ [על פסוק] וישב הים לפנות בוקר לאיתנו, לתנאו כמארז"ל [כמאמר רבותינו זכרונם לברכה]. בשנת תקכ"א (שנה אחרי הסתלקות הבעש"ט [הבעל שם טוב]) הי' אצלי - המשיך דבריו הה"מ [הרב המגיד] - רבי (הבעש"ט [הבעל שם טוב]) ואמר המאמר והוסיף ביאור בענין עושין רצונו - ולא דברו - של מקום. והיום הי' אצלי מורי לחזור המאמר. ואמר הה"מ [הרב המגיד] המאמר לפני אדמוה"ז [אדננו מורנו ורבנו הזקן], והוסיף ביאור בענין גנאי נהרא שזהו כענין קריעת ים סוף.

וסיים הצ"צ [הצמח צדק]: היום היו אצלי הבעש"ט [הבעל שם טוב] הה"מ [הרב המגיד] ואאזמו"ר [ואדוני אבי זקני מורי ורבי], וכל אחד אמר לי המאמר בסגנונו. - כעבור איזה שעות קרא הצ"צ [צמח צדק] את אאזמו"ר [אדוני אבי זקני מורי ורבי] עוד הפעם ואמר לפניו ביאור על המאמר.
hayomYom.clear:
There is a custom to eat black kasha [buckwheat].

On Shabbos Beshalach 5621 [1861], the Tzemach Tzedek said the maamar R’u ki Hashem, printed in Likutei Torah. Afterwards he told his son, my grandfather [the Rebbe Maharash]:

On Shabbos Beshalach 5565 [1805], my grandfather [the Alter Rebbe] said this maamar. Afterwards he called me and told me: In 5529 [1769], when I was in Mezritch, the Maggid called me to his room and said to me: “On Shabbos Beshalach 5516 [1756], the Baal Shem Tov said a maamar on the verse ‘And the sea returned at morning to its strength’ (Shemos 14:27), l’eisano, meaning ‘to its condition,’ as our Sages say. In 5521 [1761], a year after the Baal Shem Tov’s passing,” the Maggid went on, “my Rebbe, the Baal Shem Tov, came to me and said the maamar again, and added an explanation of ‘doing the will’ (and not ‘the word’) of the Omnipresent. And today my teacher came to me to repeat the maamar.” Then the Maggid said the maamar to the Alter Rebbe, and added an explanation of the River Ginai [which split for R. Pinchas ben Yair], which is like the splitting of the Sea.

The Tzemach Tzedek concluded: Today the Baal Shem Tov, the Maggid and my grandfather came to me, and each one said the maamar to me in his own style.

A few hours later the Tzemach Tzedek called my grandfather again and said an explanation of the maamar to him.
translationNotes: The Kehot English drops the Maggid’s words about the Baal Shem Tov’s 5516 maamar and his 5521 visit. Restored from the Hebrew.
עושין רצונו, ולא דברו, של מקום: the added point was “His will,” not “His word.”
לאיתנו לתנאו: the Sages read “to its strength” as “to its condition” (stipulation made at Creation).
hayomYom.dataFlag: Kehot English has a gap where the Maggid’s words should be (text missing after “had said:”). Translated in full from the Hebrew.

hayomYom.english: The Tzemach Tzedek told his son, my grandfather, that the maamar Umareihem uma'asseihem in Torah Or, Yitro, is the first discourse the Maggid delivered when he assumed leadership of the chassidim, on Shavuot 5521 (1761). The Alter Rebbe heard the maamar from R. Mendel Horodoker, author of Pri Haaretz, who had been present that Shavuot in 5521. However, the Alter Rebbe expounded the maamar in his own style.
hayomYom.hebrew: הצ"צ [הצמח צדק] ספר לבנו אאזמו"ר [אדוני אבי זקני מורי ורבי], אשר הדרוש ומראיהם ומעשיהם - תורה אור פ'[רשת] יתרו - הוא דרוש הראשון שאמר הרב המגיד ממעזריטש בשעת קבלו את הנשיאות - חג השבועות תקכ"א, - כפי אשר שמעו רבינו הזקן מפי הרמ"מ [הרב ר' מנחם מענדל] מהאראדאק - בעל פרי הארץ - שהי' באותו מעמד, רק שרבינו ביאר הדרוש ע"פ [על פי] סגנונו.
hayomYom.clear:
The Tzemach Tzedek told his son, my grandfather [the Rebbe Maharash]: The maamar Umareihem uma’aseihem (Torah Or, Yisro) is the first maamar the Maggid of Mezritch said when he took on the leadership, on Shavuos 5521 [1761].

The Alter Rebbe heard it from R. Menachem Mendel of Horodok, author of Pri HaAretz, who was present at that gathering. But the Alter Rebbe explained the maamar in his own style.
translationNotes: קבלו את הנשיאות: accepting the nesius [leadership]. Kehot has “leadership of the chassidim.”
Matches the original. No meaning lost otherwise.

hayomYom.english: The first positive mitzva is, in the words of Rambam, "To know that there is a First Being, who caused the existence of all beings...The knowledge of this principle is a positive command, as it is said, I am the Eternal your G‑d." This is a Mitzva relating to mind and intellect. True, every one of Israel believes in G‑d with a simple faith, and his heart is whole with G‑d; still it is the duty of the mind and intellect to bring this faith to a level of knowledge and comprehension. This is the meaning of "To know that there is a First Being;" the Mitzva specifies comprehension and intellectual grasp, as written in Torah: "Know the G‑d of your father and serve Him with a whole heart" and it is also written, "know this day etc."
hayomYom.hebrew: מצות עשה הראשונה, ובל'[שון] הרמב"ם "לידע שיש שם מצוי ראשון ממציא כל נמצא כו' וידיעת דבר זה מ"ע [מצות עשה] וכמ"ש [וכמו שכתוב] אנכי ה"א [ה' אלוקיך]", היא מצות המוח והשכל, והיינו דהגם דכל אחד ואחד מישראל הוא מאמין בה' באמונה פשוטה ולבבו תמים עם ה', חובת המוח והשכל להביא אמונה זו בידיעה והשגה, וזהו "לידע שיש שם מצוי ראשון", ער זאל דאס וויסען בהשגה והבנה דוקא, וכמ"ש [וכמו שכתוב] דע את אלקי אביך ועבדהו בלב שלם, וכתיב וידעת היום גו'.
hayomYom.clear:
The first positive mitzva, in the Rambam’s words, is “to know that there is a First Being who brings into existence all that exists... and knowing this is a positive mitzva, as it says, ‘I am G‑d your G‑d.’”

This is a mitzva of the mind and intellect. Every single Jew believes in G‑d with simple faith, and his heart is whole with G‑d. Still, the duty of the mind and intellect is to bring this faith into knowledge and understanding.

That is the meaning of “to know that there is a First Being”: he should know it specifically through comprehension and understanding. As it says, “Know the G‑d of your father and serve Him with a whole heart” (Divrei HaYamim I 28:9), and it says, “Know this day...” (Devarim 4:39).
translationNotes: דוקא: “specifically” through comprehension, not faith alone.
The Rambam quote is Hilchos Yesodei HaTorah 1:1.

hayomYom.english: My father wrote in one of his letters: According to the glosses of Ashri, when laving the hands for a meal, pour water over each hand three times consecutively; this was the practice of my father (R. Shmuel). He would leave a little water from the third pouring cupped in the palm of his left hand and, with this water, rub his hands together.
hayomYom.hebrew: אאמו"ר [אדוני אבי מורי ורבי [כותב באחד ממכתביו: על פי הגהות אשר"י נטילת ידים לסעודה ג' פעמים רצופות, כן היה עושה אאמו"ר [אדוני אבי מורי ורבי] - (מהר"ש נ"ע [נשמתו עדן]) - ומניח משפיכה הג' מעט מים בכף יד השמאלית ובזה משפשף שתי ידיו.
hayomYom.clear: My father [the Rebbe Rashab] wrote in one of his letters: According to the glosses of the Ashri, washing hands for a meal is three pourings in a row. This is what my father [the Rebbe Maharash] did. He would leave a little water from the third pouring in the palm of his left hand, and with it rub both hands together.
translationNotes: רצופות: three times “in a row,” on each hand, without a break.
Here “my father” is the Rebbe Rashab speaking of the Rebbe Maharash.

hayomYom.english: It is the duty of Chassidic wives and daughters (may they live and be well) to stand in the first rank of every activity dedicated to strengthening religion and Judaism in general, particularly concerning taharat hamishpacha. They must organize a Society of Chassidic Daughters to reinforce all the chassidic practices concerning upbringing and education of children - as prevalent from time immemorial in chassidic homes.
hayomYom.hebrew: חובת נשי ובנות החסידים יחיו לעמוד בשורה ראשונה בכל מפעל של חזוק הדת והיהדות בכלל, ובפרט בענין טהרת המשפחה. ועליהם לארגן חברת בנות החסידים לחזק כל דרכי החסידים בעניני הדרכה וחינוך כמו שהיה בבתי החסידים מאז ומקדם.
hayomYom.clear:
It is the duty of the wives and daughters of chassidim, may they live, to stand in the front line of every effort to strengthen religion and Yiddishkeit in general, and taharas hamishpacha [family purity] in particular.

They should organize a society of chassidic daughters to strengthen all the chassidic ways of guidance and education, as it was in chassidic homes from long ago.
translationNotes: הדרכה וחינוך: “guidance and education.” Kehot adds “of children,” which is implied but not stated.

hayomYom.english: There are two sorts of statutes: a) statutes that create life, and b) statutes created by life. Human laws are created by life so they vary from land to land according to circumstances. The A-lmighty's Torah is a G‑dly law that creates life. G‑d's Torah is the Torah of truth, the same in all places, at all times. Torah is eternal.
hayomYom.hebrew: עס זיינען דא צווייערליי חוקים: א) א געזעץ וועלכער שאפט לעבען ב) א געזעץ וועלכער ווערט באשאפען פון לעבען. מענשליכע געזעצען זיינען געשאפען פון לעבען, דערפאר זיינען זיי אין יעדער לאנד פארשידען, לויט די תנאים פון לאנד. תורת ה', איז דער ג-טליכער געזעץ וועלכער שאפט א לעבען. תורת ה' איז תורת אמת, די תורה איז אין אלע ערטער און אין אלע צייטען גלייך, תורה איז נצחית.
hayomYom.clear:
There are two kinds of laws: a law that creates life, and a law that is created by life.

Human laws are created by life. That is why they differ from country to country, according to each country’s conditions.

G‑d’s Torah is the Divine law that creates life. G‑d’s Torah is the Torah of truth. The Torah is the same in every place and at every time. The Torah is eternal.
translationNotes: Matches the original. No meaning lost.

hayomYom.english: Once, as the Alter Rebbe stepped out of his room, he overheard his wife remarking to several women, "Mine says..." The Rebbe said: "With one mitzva I am yours; with how many are we G‑d's!" With these words he fell onto the doorpost in dveikut. On "awakening" from the dveikut he said: "Go out and see" - to step out of self and perceive the Divine, comes from (the following words in that verse) "daughters of Zion," Malchut arousing z'a. The Future will bring the fulfillment of "A valorous woman is her husband's crown."
hayomYom.hebrew:
אמאל ארויסגייענדיק פון זיין חדר, האט דער אלטער רבי אנגעטראפען, ווי די רביצין זאגט צו עטליכע פרויען: "מיינער זאגט".

האט דער רבי געזאגט: מיט איין מצוה בין איך דיינער, מיט מצות וויפל איז מען דעם אויבערשטען'ס. און איז געפאלען אויף דער פריטעלקע און האט זיך פארדבק'עט. אויפכאפענדיג זיך פון דבקות, האט ער געזאגט: צאינה וראינה - אויף ארויסגיין פון זיך און זעהן אלקות, ווערט דאס פון - בנות ציון, מלכות מעוררת ז"א [ זעיר אנפין], לעתיד לבוא וועט זיין אשת חיל עטרת בעלה.
hayomYom.clear:
Once, as he was coming out of his room, the Alter Rebbe heard the Rebbetzin saying to a few women: “Mine says...”

The Rebbe said: “With one mitzva I am yours. With how many mitzvos do we belong to G‑d!” He fell against the doorpost and became absorbed in dveikus [cleaving to G‑d].

When he came out of the dveikus, he said: “Go out and see” (Shir HaShirim 3:11). To go out of yourself and see G‑dliness comes from “daughters of Zion”: Malchus arouses Z’eir Anpin. In the Time to Come, “a woman of valor is her husband’s crown” (Mishlei 12:4) will be fulfilled.
translationNotes: מיינער: “mine,” as a wife refers to her husband. The Rebbe answers in kind: דיינער, “yours.”
צאינה וראינה: “go out and see,” read as going out of yourself.

hayomYom.english:
During the reading of the Ten Commandments, stand facing the Sefer-Torah.
Haftora: Bishnat...matzavta.
Bless Rosh Chodesh Adar I. Say the entire Tehillim in the early morning.
Day of farbrengen.

"The people saw and moved." Simply perceiving G‑dhood caused the people to move, a movement showing vitality, life. * * * If you only knew - The Tzemach Tzedek said - the power of verses of Tehillim and their effect in the highest Heavens, you would recite them constantly. Know that the chapters of Tehillim shatter all barriers, they ascend higher and still higher with no interference; they prostrate themselves in supplication before the Master of all worlds, and they effect and accomplish with kindness and compassion.
hayomYom.hebrew:
וירא העם וינועו, אז זיי האבען דערזעהן ג-טליכקייט איז שוין וינועו, עס איז געווארען א תנועת חיים.

אלו ידעתם - אמר אדמו"ר [אדננו מורנו ורבנו] הצמח צדק - כחם של פסוקי תהלים ופעולתם בשמי רום, הייתם אומרים אותם בכל עת. תדעו שמזמורי תהלים שוברים כל המחיצות, ועולים בעילוי אחר עילוי בלי שום הפרעה, ומשתטחים לפני אדון עולמים ופועלים פעולתם בחסד וברחמים.
hayomYom.clear:
“The people saw and trembled” (Shemos 20:15). As soon as they saw G‑dliness, they trembled. A movement of life was born.

“If you only knew,” said the Tzemach Tzedek, “the power of verses of Tehillim and what they accomplish in the highest heavens, you would say them all the time. Know that chapters of Tehillim break through all barriers. They rise higher and higher with nothing stopping them. They prostrate themselves before the Master of the worlds, and they accomplish what they do with kindness and mercy.”
translationNotes: וינועו: they “moved, trembled.” The point is that seeing alone set them in motion.
תנועת חיים: a movement of life, of vitality.

hayomYom.english: Studying a parsha of Chumash with Rashi every day (Sunday until Sheini, Monday until Shlishi, etc.), saying Tehillim every day and the entire Tehillim on Shabbat m'varchim - be scrupulous about all of these. It is crucial for you, for your children and your children's children.
hayomYom.hebrew: לערנען בכל יום א פרשה חומש מיט פירש"י [פירוש רש"י] (זונטאג ביז שני, מאנטאג ביז שלישי וכו'), אמירת תהלים בכל יום, גומר זיין דעם תהלים שבת מברכים - דאס דארף מען אפהיטען, דאס איז נוגע איהם, זיינע קינדער און קינד'ס קינדער.
hayomYom.clear: Learn a section of Chumash with Rashi every day (Sunday up to Sheini, Monday up to Shlishi, and so on). Say Tehillim every day, and finish the whole Tehillim on Shabbos Mevarchim. You have to guard these carefully. This affects you, your children and your children’s children.
translationNotes: אפהיטען: “guard, keep carefully.”
נוגע: it “touches, affects” him and his descendants.

hayomYom.english: Ahava, affection, is the breath of life in the Avoda of Chassidus. It is the thread that binds chassidim to each other, that binds Rebbe to chassidim and chassidim to Rebbe. Ahava works in a direct way (initiated affection) and also in a reflective way (responding to the other's affection). It knows no barriers and transcends the limits of time and place.
hayomYom.hebrew: אהבה איז דער רוח החיים אין עבודת החסידות, דער חוט המקשר חסידים איינעם מיט דעם אנדערען, און דער חוט המקשר רבי מיט חסידים און חסידים מיט רבי'ן. עס איז הן בדרך אור ישר הן בדרך אור חוזר, האט קיינע מחיצות ניט, און עס איז העכער פון דער הגבלה פון מקום וזמן.
hayomYom.clear:
Ahava [love] is the breath of life in the avoda of Chassidus. It is the thread that binds chassidim to one another, and the thread that binds the Rebbe to the chassidim and the chassidim to the Rebbe.

It works both as or yashar [direct light, love that goes out] and as or chozer [reflected light, love that returns]. It has no barriers, and it is above the limits of place and time.
translationNotes: אור ישר / אור חוזר: Kabbalistic terms “direct light” and “reflected light.” Kehot paraphrases them away.

hayomYom.english: My father writes in one of his maamarim: Early chassidim resolved in their souls to refrain from anything that is permissible (by Torah law) but for which they felt a desire and urge. This breaks the passion.
hayomYom.hebrew: אאמו"ר [אדוני אבי מורי ורבי] כותב באחד ממאמריו: חסידים הקודמים עשו הסכם בנפשם שכל דבר המותר, אך שיש לו איזה רצון וחמדת הלב לזה לא יעשנו, ועל ידי זה נעשה שבירת התאוה.
hayomYom.clear: My father [the Rebbe Rashab] writes in one of his maamarim: The early chassidim made a firm resolve in their souls: anything that is permitted, but which they had some desire and craving for, they would not do. Through this, desire is broken.
translationNotes: חמדת הלב: a craving of the heart.
Matches the original. No meaning lost.

hayomYom.english: One of the Baal Shem Tov's teachings: "When you see chamor, a donkey" - when you carefully examine your chomer ("materiality"), your body, you will see... ..."your enemy" - meaning, that your chomer hates your Divine soul that longs for G‑dliness and the spiritual, and furthermore, you will see that it is... ..."lying under its burden" placed upon it - (the body) by G‑d, namely, that it should become refined through Torah and mitzvot; but the body is lazy to fulfill them. It may then occur to you that... ..."you will refrain from helping it" - to enable it to fulfill its mission, and instead you will follow the path of mortification of the flesh to break down the body's crass materiality. However, not in this approach will the light of Torah reside. Rather... ..."you must aid it" - purify the body, refine it, but do not break it by mortification.
hayomYom.hebrew:
אחת מתורות הבעל שם טוב:
כי תראה חמור - כאשר תסתכל בעיון טוב בהחומר שלך שהוא הגוף, תראה - שונאך - שהוא שונא את הנשמה המתגעגעת לאלקות ורוחניות, ועוד תראה שהוא - רובץ תחת משאו - שנתן הקב"ה [הקדוש ברוך הוא] להגוף שיזדכך ע"י [על ידי] תומ"צ [תורה ומצות] והגוף מתעצל בקיומם. ואולי יעלה בלבבך - וחדלת מעזוב לו - שיוכל לקיים שליחותו, כי אם תתחיל בסיגופים לשבור את החומריות, הנה לא בזו הדרך ישכון אור התורה, כי אם - עזוב תעזוב עמו - לברר את הגוף ולזככו ולא לשברו בסיגופים.
hayomYom.clear:
One of the Baal Shem Tov’s teachings, on the verse “When you see the donkey of your enemy lying under its burden... you shall surely help with him” (Shemos 23:5):

“When you see a chamor [donkey]”: when you look carefully at your chomer [materiality], which is your body, you will see “your enemy.” It hates the soul, which longs for G‑dliness and spirituality. You will also see that it is “lying under its burden,” the burden G‑d gave the body: to become refined through Torah and mitzvos. And the body is lazy about keeping them.

You might think: “Would you refrain from helping it” to carry out its mission? So you start afflicting yourself to break your materiality. But the light of Torah will not dwell in this way. Rather, “you shall surely help with him”: refine the body and purify it, and do not break it with self-affliction.
translationNotes: לברר את הגוף ולזככו: refine and purify the body, the opposite of breaking it.
סיגופים: ascetic self-affliction.

hayomYom.english: The Alter Rebbe once said:
hayomYom.hebrew: דער אלטער רבי האט אמאל געזאגט: פירש"י [פירוש רש"י] אויף חומש איז יינה של תורה, פותח הלב ומגלה אהבה ויראה עצמיות, פירש"י [פירוש רש"י] אויף גמרא איז פותח המוח ומגלה שכל עצמי.
hayomYom.clear: The Alter Rebbe once said: Rashi on Chumash is the wine of the Torah. It opens the heart and reveals essential love and fear [of G‑d]. Rashi on Gemara opens the mind and reveals essential intellect.
translationNotes: יינה של תורה: “the wine of the Torah.”
עצמיות / עצמי: “essential,” coming from the core of the soul.
hayomYom.dataFlag: Kehot English is cut off after “The Alter Rebbe once said:”. Translated from the Hebrew.

hayomYom.english: Many Chassidim considered the day they arrived in Lubavitch to be their "birthday." My teacher, R. Shmuel Betzalel, arrived in Lubavitch the first time on Thursday evening parshat Mishpatim 5608 (1848). Every year after that, he stayed awake all that night and took pains to put on his tefillin at the exact time he had entered the Tzemach Tzedek's chamber for yechidus the first time.
hayomYom.hebrew: כמה וכמה חסידים חשבו יום בואם לליובאוויטש ליום הולדת שלהם. מורי הרשב"ץ בא בפעם הראשונה לליובאוויטש אור ליום ששי פ'[רשת] משפטים שנת תר"ח, ובכל שנה ושנה היה ער כל אותו הלילה, ומכוון להניח תפילין בה בשעה אשר נכנס להצ"צ [להצמח צדק] בפעם הראשונה.
hayomYom.clear:
Many chassidim counted the day they arrived in Lubavitch as their birthday.

My teacher, R. Shmuel Betzalel [the Rashbatz], first came to Lubavitch on Thursday night of the week of parshas Mishpatim, 5608 [1848]. Every year he stayed awake that whole night, and made a point of putting on tefillin at the same hour that he had first entered the Tzemach Tzedek’s room.
translationNotes: אור ליום ששי: the night before Friday, i.e., Thursday night.
נכנס להצ"צ: entered to the Tzemach Tzedek. Kehot adds “for yechidus,” which is implied.

hayomYom.english: (Here there appears an interpretation of an abbreviation in Torah Or, relevant only in Hebrew. Translator). It is written: "Man goes out to his work and to his labor (avoda) until evening." Every soul in its descent into this material world has general and personal tasks. This, then, is the meaning of the verse: Man goes out to his work - the soul "goes out" from its position in the trove of souls, in the highest heavens, and descends from plane to plane until it comes to be invested in a body and in the natural and animal souls. The purpose of this descent is "man to his work" - to his general task of achieving dominance of "form over matter" (meaning, the spiritual over the material), to illuminate the world with the light of Torah and the candle of Mitzva. ...to his labor refers to each individual's particular mission, for every soul has its unique Avoda in intellect and emotions according to its nature and character. ...until evening - while there is still time to accomplish, as it is written, "Today, to perform them (the mitzvot)." On a more profound level the verse may be explained as follows: The verse refers to the ascent of the soul in general, achieved by its prior descent (Man goes out) into the material world: When the soul ascends from its being enclothed in the body in this material world, then... ...to his work - the soul's occupation in the World To Come is commensurate with its occupation in the material world. If he had studied Torah regularly, there too (in the World To Come) the soul is ushered into the "Tents of Torah"; ...to his labor - if he performed his avoda properly then his ascent goes on... ...until erev ("evening") - higher and higher until he attains the ultimate delight and areivut ("sweetness") of the Essence of the En Sof, may He be blessed.
hayomYom.hebrew:
תו"א [תורה אור] ד"ה [דבור המתחיל] לא תהי' משכלה סעיף המתחיל והנה אחר: "במסירת נפש בפ"ע [בפני עצמו]" פירוש הר"ת [הראשי תיבות] הוא "בפנימית עצמותו".

כתיב: יצא אדם לפעלו ולעבדתו עדי ערב. הנה כל נשמה בירידתה למטה, יש לה מלאכות כלליות ופרטיות. וזהו יצא אדם לפעלו, דיציאת הנשמה מעמידתה בשמי רום באוצר הנשמות, וירידתה מדרגא לדרגא עד בואה להתלבש בגוף ונה"ט [ונפש הטבעית] והבהמית, הוא בשביל אדם לפעלו במלאכות הכלליות להגביר הצורה על החומר, להאיר את העולם באור תורה ונר מצוה. ולעבודתו שהיא מלאכה הפרטית, דכל נשמה יש לה עבודה פרטית במוחין ובמדות כפי טבעה וענינה.. עדי ערב בעוד יש זמן לעשות כמ"ש [כמו שכתוב] היום לעשותם. ובעומק הענין ביאור הכתוב.. דקאי על כללות ענין העליה שנעשה ע"י [על ידי] ירידת הנשמה למטה דיצא אדם, דבעלות הנשמה מהיותה למטה מלובשת בגוף, לפעלו היא עוסקת בעוה"ב [בעולם הבא] באופן התעסקותה בעוה"ז [בעולם הזה], ואם היה קובע עתים לתורה, גם שם מכניסים אותו באהלי תורה, ולעבודתו, אם עסק בעבודתו כראוי אז הנה עליתו עדי ערב שעולה בעילוי אחר עילוי עד הנועם והעריבות דעצמות אין סוף ברוך הוא.
hayomYom.clear:
Torah Or, maamar Lo sihyeh meshakeila, section beginning V’hinei achar: in “b’mesirus nefesh b’f"a,” the abbreviation means “b’pnimiyus atzmuso” [in the innermost of his essence].

It says: “Man goes out to his work and to his labor until evening” (Tehillim 104:23). Every soul, in its descent below, has general tasks and particular tasks.

This is “man goes out to his work.” The soul goes out from its place in the highest heavens, in the treasury of souls, and descends level after level until it is clothed in a body and in the natural and animal soul. This is so that “man [goes] to his work,” his general tasks: to make form prevail over matter, and to light up the world with the light of Torah and the candle of mitzva.

“And to his labor”: this is his particular task. Every soul has its own particular avoda, in its mind and its emotions, according to its nature and character.

“Until evening”: while there is still time to do it, as it says, “today, to do them” (Devarim 7:11).

At a deeper level, the verse refers to the whole ascent that comes about through the soul’s descent below, “man goes out.” When the soul rises from being clothed in a body below:

“To his work”: in the World to Come it is occupied the same way it was occupied in this world. If he set fixed times for Torah, there too they bring him into the tents of Torah.

“And to his labor”: if he did his avoda properly, then his ascent goes “until evening [erev]”: he rises higher and higher until the pleasantness and sweetness [arevus] of the Essence of the Ein Sof, blessed be He.
translationNotes: The Kehot English skips the Torah Or abbreviation note. Translated here: בפ"ע means בפנימית עצמותו, not בפני עצמו.
עדי ערב / העריבות: wordplay, erev (evening) and arevus (sweetness).
Kehot’s “(meaning, the spiritual over the material)” is an added gloss. Left out.

hayomYom.english: Rabeinu Haggadol the Alter Rebbe, set forth a program for Chassidim of striving (avoda) with the mind and seeking truth, to critically examine one's every move to be certain it conforms strictly with truth and comes through avoda, effort. This avoda does not imply - as some think, altogether erroneously - that one must pulverize mountains and shatter boulders, turn the world upside down. The absolute truth is that any avoda, any act, whatever it may be, is perfectly satisfactory when performed with true kavana, intent: A b'racha pronounced with kavana; a word of davening as it should be, with a prepared heart and an awareness of "before Whom you stand"; a passage in Chumash said with an awareness that it is the word of G‑d; a verse of Tehillim; a beneficent trait of character expressed in befriending another with affection and love. The truth of the matter is, that to achieve this calls for great and intense effort, meaning simply to study a great deal of Torah and to comprehend it - each according to his ability - and then G‑d will help him be what truth demands.
hayomYom.hebrew:
רבינו הגדול - הזקן - סידר לפני אנ"ש [אנשי שלומינו] העבודה במוח ולחפש את האמת, לבקר כל תנועה, שתהיה רק כפי האמת ובאה ע"י [על ידי] עבודה.

ועבודה זו אינה כמו שטועים בזה טעות גמור לחשוב שצריך לפרק הרים ולשבר סלעים, איבערקערען די וועלט. האמת הגמור הוא, אשר כל עבודה ופועל, איזה שיהיו, בכוונה אמיתית די ומספיק: א ברכה בכוונה, דעם ווארט אין דאוונען כדבעי בהכנת הלב ובידיעה לפני מי אתה עומד, א פסוק חומש בידיעה שהוא דבר ה', א פסוק תהלים, ומדה טובה לקרב לבו של חברו באהבה וחבה.

אמת הדבר, אשר בכדי להגיע לזה צריכים יגיעת רבה ועצומה, פשוט לערנען א רבוי און פארשטיין - כל אחד לפי ערכו - ואז ה' בעזרו שיהי'[ה] כפי האמת.
hayomYom.clear:
Our great Rebbe, the Alter Rebbe, laid out for our chassidim an avoda of the mind: to search for the truth, and to examine every move you make, so that it is only according to the truth and comes through avoda.

This avoda is not, as some completely mistakenly think, about smashing mountains and shattering rocks, turning the world upside down. The full truth is: any avoda or act, whatever it is, done with true kavana, is enough. A blessing said with kavana. A word of davening said properly, with a prepared heart and with awareness of “before Whom you stand.” A verse of Chumash, knowing it is the word of G‑d. A verse of Tehillim. And the good trait of drawing a friend’s heart close with love and affection.

It is true that to reach this takes great and intense effort: simply, to learn a lot and understand it, each according to his level. Then G‑d will help him, so that it will be according to the truth.
translationNotes: די ומספיק: “enough and sufficient.” Kehot’s “perfectly satisfactory” is close.
לקרב לבו של חברו: “to draw a friend’s heart close,” kiruv. Kehot’s “befriending” loses it.

hayomYom.english: The Alter Rebbe said: The mitzva of ahavat yisrael extends to anyone born into the people of Israel, even if you have never met him. How much more so does it extend to every member - man or woman of the Jewish community where you live, who belongs to your own community.
hayomYom.hebrew: רבינו הזקן אמר: מצות אהבת ישראל הוא ליליד עם ישראל אשר מעולם לא ראה אותו, ומכל שכן לחבר עדת ישראל אשר במקום מגורו, שהוא בן או בת עדתו.
hayomYom.clear: The Alter Rebbe said: The mitzva of ahavas Yisrael [loving a fellow Jew] applies to anyone born of the Jewish people, even someone you have never seen. All the more so it applies to a member of the Jewish community where you live, who is a son or daughter of your own community.
translationNotes: Matches the original. No meaning lost.

hayomYom.english: The initial preparations for delving into deep intellectual concepts, especially concepts of G‑dliness, are (a) a strenuous effort of the body to be rid of one's delight in worldly matters, and (b) a strenuous effort of the soul to stimulate delight in intellectual pursuit in general, and in G‑dly matters in particular.
hayomYom.hebrew: ראשית ההכנה להתעסקות בשכלים עיונים, ובשכל אלקי בפרט, הוא א) יגיעת בשר להסיר הטוב טעם מעניני עולם ב) יגיעת נפש לעורר הטוב טעם במושכלות בכלל, ובעניני אלקות בפרט.
hayomYom.clear:
The first preparation for delving into deep intellectual ideas, and especially G‑dly ideas, is:

1. Effort of the body: to remove the taste for worldly things.
2. Effort of the soul: to awaken a taste for intellectual ideas in general, and for G‑dly matters in particular.
translationNotes: יגיעת בשר / יגיעת נפש: effort of the flesh and effort of the soul.
טוב טעם: “good taste,” relish.

hayomYom.english: There is not the vaguest shadow of doubt that, wherever our feet tread, it is all in order to cleanse and purify the world with words of Torah and tefilla (prayer). We, all of Israel, are emissaries of G‑d, each of us as Divine Providence has decreed for us. None of us is free from this sacred task placed on our shoulders.
hayomYom.hebrew: בלי שום צל ספק וספק ספיקא, הנה בכל מקום מדרך כף רגלינו, הכל הוא לזכות ולטהר את הארץ באותיות התורה והתפלה, ואנחנו כל ישראל שלוחי דרחמנא אנו, איש איש כאשר גזרה עליו השגחה העליונה, אין חפשי מעבודת הקדש, אשר הועמסה על שכמנו.
hayomYom.clear: Without the slightest shadow of a doubt, or even a doubt of a doubt: wherever our feet tread, it is all in order to bring merit to the land and purify it with the letters of Torah and tefilla. All of us, all Israel, are emissaries of the Merciful One, each one as Divine Providence decreed for him. No one is free of the holy work that has been loaded onto our shoulders.
translationNotes: ספק ספיקא: “a doubt of a doubt.” Kehot drops it.
לזכות: to bring merit to, refine. Kehot’s “cleanse” is close.
שלוחי דרחמנא: emissaries of the Merciful One.

hayomYom.english: From my father's sichot: It is a magnificent gift of G‑d to merit an innate sense - a "feel" - for doing kindness to another, to derive deep pleasure from it. This can develop to the point that one cherishes the other more than oneself. He may find many explanations as to why he deserves his own tribulations, G‑d forbid, but to do so with regard to another's suffering - is absolutely impossible.
hayomYom.hebrew: משיחות אאמו"ר [אדוני אבי מורי ורבי]: עס איז א מעלה נפלאה, וואס דער אויבערשטער ב"ה [ברוך הוא] איז מזכה און מען קריגט א חוש מיט א געשמאק א אידען א טובה טאן, ביז אז יענער ווערט בא אים טייערער ווי ער בא זיך, ווארום אויף זיך קען ער געפינען כמה טעמים פאר וואס עס קומט אים זאל, ח"ו [חס ושלום], זיין ניט גוט, אבער אויף דעם אנדערען איז דאס ניט שייך כלל.
hayomYom.clear: From my father’s [the Rebbe Rashab’s] sichos: It is a wonderful quality when G‑d grants you the merit of a real feel and a taste for doing a favor for a fellow Jew, to the point that the other person becomes dearer to you than you are to yourself. Because about yourself, you can find many reasons why it should be, G‑d forbid, not good for you. But about another person, that does not apply at all.
translationNotes: חוש מיט א געשמאק: a sense with relish, real enjoyment.
טייערער: “dearer, more precious,” than oneself.

hayomYom.english: It is imperative that every Jew know that he is an emissary of the Master of all, charged with the mission - wherever he may be of bringing into reality G‑d's will and intention in creating the universe, namely, to illuminate the world with the light of Torah and avoda. This is done through performing practical mitzvot and implanting in oneself fine character traits.
hayomYom.hebrew: כל איש בישראל עליו לדעת, כי הוא שליח אדון כל, למען הביא לפועל - בכל מקום שהוא - רצונו ית' [יתברך] וכוונתו בבריאת העולם, שהם להאיר את העולם באור תורה ועבודה, והוא ע"י [על ידי] קיום מצות מעשיות והשרשת מדות טובות.
hayomYom.clear: Every Jew must know that he is an emissary of the Master of all, to bring about, wherever he is, G‑d’s will and His intention in creating the world: to light up the world with the light of Torah and avoda. This is done by keeping the practical mitzvos and rooting good character traits in yourself.
translationNotes: השרשת מדות טובות: “rooting” good traits deep in oneself. Kehot has “implanting.”

hayomYom.english: The Alter Rebbe once summoned a young disciple of the Maggid and said to him in his customary chant: I have the mitzva of "teach them to your children." You have the mitzva of sustaining and providing for your family. Let us make an exchange. I will give you what you need to fulfill your mitzva and you will teach my son (who was later the Mitteler Rebbe). Then the Rebbe explained the method of instruction: The first thing is to teach the letters, alef, beit and so on. What is an alef? A dot above, a dot below, and a line between this is an alef. A child must know that the alef of Torah is a yud above, a yud below, and a line of faith that joins them. Another version: A yud above - this is the soul; a yid (Jew) below - this is the body; a line of yir'at Shamayim (fear of Heaven) in the center.
hayomYom.hebrew: דער אלטער רבי האט אמאל אריינגערופען א יונגערמאן פון דעם מגיד'ס תלמידים, און האט איהם געזאגט - מיט א ניגון, כדרכו -: "איך האב א מצוה פון ולמדתם אותם את בניכם, דו האסט א מצוה פון זן ומפרנס בני ביתו, לאמיר זיך בייטען: איך וועל דיר געבען דו זאלסט קענען מקיים זיין דיין מצוה, און דו לערען מיט מיין זון - דאס איז געווען דער מיטעלער רבי -. און האט איהם מבאר געווען סדר הלימוד: דאס ערשטע לערענט מען אותיות א. ב... וואס איז אן אלף - א פינטעלע פון אויבען, א פינטעלע פון אונטען, א קו באמצע - דאס איז אן אלף. א קינד מוז וויסען, אז דער אלף פון תורה איז דער יוד פון אויבען דער יוד פון אונטען מיט דעם קו פון אמונה וואס באהעפט זיי. נאך א נוסחא איז דא: "א יוד למעלה דאס איז די נשמה, א איד למטה דאס איז דער גוף און א קו של יראת שמים באמצע".
hayomYom.clear:
The Alter Rebbe once called in a young man, one of the Maggid’s students, and said to him with a melody, as was his way: “I have the mitzva of ‘and you shall teach them to your children’ (Devarim 11:19). You have the mitzva of feeding and supporting your family. Let’s trade. I will give you what you need to keep your mitzva, and you will learn with my son.” (This was the Mitteler Rebbe.)

Then he explained to him the order of teaching: First you teach the letters, alef, beis... What is an alef? A dot above, a dot below, and a line in the middle. That is an alef. A child must know that the alef of Torah is the yud above, the yud below, and the line of faith that joins them.

There is another version: “A yud above, that is the soul. A Yid [Jew] below, that is the body. And a line of yiras Shamayim [fear of Heaven] in the middle.”
translationNotes: פינטעלע: a little dot, the yud shape.
יוד / איד: wordplay, yud above and Yid below.

hayomYom.english: When someone walks the street and thinks words of Mishna or Tanya, or sits in his store with a Chumash or Tehillim - that is more valued today than it was when the streets were bright with the light of Torah. We must not go about in the street with a vacant heart. We must have some Torah memorized, to take with us into the street.
hayomYom.hebrew: אז מען געהט אין גאס און מען טראכט משניות תניא, און מ'זיצט אין קראם (סטאר) מיט א חומש, א תהלים, איז איצט איז דאס טייערער, ווי אין דער צייט, ווען אין גאס (סטריט) איז געווען ליכטיג באור תורה. מ'טאר ניט געהן אין גאס אליבא רקניא, מען דארף האבען תורה, מיט וואס צו געהן אין גאס.
hayomYom.clear: When you walk in the street and think words of Mishna or Tanya, or sit in your store with a Chumash or a Tehillim, that is more precious now than in the days when the street was bright with the light of Torah. You must not walk in the street with an empty heart. You need to have Torah with you to walk in the street with.
translationNotes: טייערער: “more precious, dearer.”
אליבא רקניא: Aramaic, “with an empty heart.” Kehot adds “memorized,” which is implied.

hayomYom.english: At birkat hamazon, before washing the fingers, say al naharot bavel, lamnatzei'ach bin'ginot, avarcha, zeh cheilek (p. 88). When tachanun is not said, say shir hamaalot b'shuv, livnei korach, avarcha, zeh cheilek. After washing the fingers say vay'dabeir eilai (p. 89).
hayomYom.hebrew:
בברכת המזון קודם מים אחרונים אומרים על נהרות בבל, למנצח בנגינות, אברכה, זה חלק.
ביום שא"א [שאין אומרים] בו תחנון: שה"מ [שיר המעלות] בשוב, לבני קרח, אברכה, זה חלק.
אחר מים אחרונים וידבר אלי.
hayomYom.clear:
In Birkas HaMazon, before mayim acharonim [washing the fingers], we say Al naharos Bavel, Lamnatzei’ach binginos, Avarcha, and Zeh chelek.

On a day when tachanun is not said: Shir hamaalos b’shuv, Livnei Korach, Avarcha, Zeh chelek.

After mayim acharonim: Vaydabeir eilai.
translationNotes: Matches the original. No meaning lost.
Siddur page numbers are Kehot additions. Left out.

hayomYom.english: The following is well-known and is a tradition, regarding the kavanot (mystical "intentions") in davening: For those intellectually incapable of meditating on those kavanot (either because they lack knowledge, or because they cannot remember the specific kavanot during prayer) it is sufficient that they keep one general kavana in mind: That his prayer be heard by G‑d, with all the kavanot described in the Kabala literature.
hayomYom.hebrew: ידוע ומקובל בענין הכוונות שבתפלה, אשר אלו שאין דעתם יפה לכוון, מפני העדר הידיעה או מפני שאין בכחם לזכור כוונות הפרטיות בעת התפלה, מספיק שיכוונו כוונה כללית: להיות תפלתו נשמעת לפניו יתברך עם כל הכוונות המבוארות בספרי קבלה.
hayomYom.clear: It is known and handed down about the kavanos [mystical intentions] in davening: those who are not able to have these kavanos in mind, because they lack the knowledge or because they cannot remember the detailed kavanos during davening, it is enough for them to have one general intention: that their prayer be heard before G‑d, with all the kavanos explained in the books of Kabbalah.
translationNotes: ומקובל: “accepted, a tradition.” Matches Kehot.
Matches the original. No meaning lost.

hayomYom.english: It is written: "The gift of man makes room for him and leads him before the great." Some are renowned for their wisdom or wealth. But "the gift of man" - when an individual gives his "man," i.e., devotes himself to an undertaking to strengthen Judaism, then not only will he "make room for himself" (releasing him from constrictions and bounds), but it "leads him before the great" (his position will be superior to the great).
hayomYom.hebrew: כתיב מתן אדם ירחיב לו ולפני גדולים ינחנו. יש לך אנשים שהם גדולי השם בחכמתם או בעשרם, אבל מתן אדם, כשהאדם נותן את האדם שלו באיזה התעסקות בהחזקת הדת, הנה לא זו בלבד כי ירחיב לו, אלא עוד זאת כי לפני גדולים ינחנו.
hayomYom.clear:
It says: “A man’s gift makes room for him and brings him before the great” (Mishlei 18:16).

There are people who are famous for their wisdom or their wealth. But “a man’s gift”: when a person gives his own self, “his man,” to some work of strengthening Judaism, then not only does it “make room for him,” it also “brings him before the great.”
translationNotes: נותן את האדם שלו: he gives “his man,” his very self.
Kehot’s bracketed glosses (“releasing him from constrictions,” “superior to the great”) are not in the original. Left out.

hayomYom.english: Tachanun is not said at Mincha. My father said: I am certain that when a chassid is in the beit hamidrash teaching or reciting a maamar of Chassidus to others, my forebears are filled with joy; and their joy is adequate to provide that Chassid, and his children and children's children, with an abundance of blessing, materially and spiritually.
hayomYom.hebrew:
במנחה א"א [אין אומרים] תחנון.
אאמו"ר [אדוני אבי מורי ורבי] אמר: בא מיר איז ברור, אז א חסידישער איד זיצט אין בית המדרש, און לערענט אדער חזר'ט א חסידות ברבים, איז א שמחה בא די זיידעס, און זייער שמחה איז מספיק פאר איהם, קינדער און קינד'ס קינדער רוב טוב בגשמיות וברוחניות.
hayomYom.clear: My father [the Rebbe Rashab] said: To me it is clear that when a chassidic Jew sits in the beis midrash and learns or repeats Chassidus in public, there is joy among the zeides [our grandfathers, the Rebbeim]. Their joy is enough to bring him, his children and his children’s children an abundance of good, materially and spiritually.
translationNotes: די זיידעס: “the grandfathers,” a warm Yiddish term for the previous Rebbeim.
ברבים: in public, to a group.

calendar.original5703: No tachanun at Mincha.

hayomYom.english: My grandfather told my father: "My father (the Tzemach Tzedek) selected the maamarim printed in Likutei Torah from among 2,000 maamarim.
hayomYom.hebrew: אאזמו"ר [אדוני אבי זקני מורי ורבי] סיפר לאאמו"ר [לאדוני אבי מורי ורבי]: די מאמרים וואס זיינען געדרוקט אין לקוטי תורה, האט דער טאטע (הצמח צדק) אויסגעקליבען פון צוויי טויזענט מאמרים.
hayomYom.clear: My grandfather [the Rebbe Maharash] told my father [the Rebbe Rashab]: The maamarim printed in Likutei Torah were chosen by Father (the Tzemach Tzedek) out of two thousand maamarim.
translationNotes: דער טאטע: “Father,” a familiar Yiddish term.
Matches the original. No meaning lost.

hayomYom.english: Before pronouncing the b'racha hamotzi, a scratch is made on the bread with the knife, but we are careful not to cut into it. Even when saying kiddush over bread, we still say savri maranan (p. 141). It is said of the Time To Come: "A stone in the wall will cry out and a beam from the tree will respond." At present, inert creations are mute; though trodden upon, they remain silent. But there will come a time when the revelation of the Future becomes a reality, that the inert will begin to speak, relate and demand: "If a man was walking along without thinking or speaking words of Torah, why did he trample upon me?" The earth trodden upon has been waiting for millenia, ever since the Six Days of Creation. All kinds of living creatures have been treading upon it all this time, but it is waiting for a Jew (or two Jews) to walk on it while discussing Torah. But if they do not say words of Torah, the earth will protest: "You too are just like an animal!"
hayomYom.hebrew:
רושמים על הלחם קודם ברכת המוציא, אבל נזהרים שלא לחתוך.

גם בקדוש על הפת אומרים סברי מרנן.

אויף לעתיד לבוא שטעהט: אבן מקיר תזעק וכפיס מעץ יעננה. איצטער שווייגט דער דומם, מ'טרעט אויף איהם און ער שווייגט. אבער עס וועט קומען א צייט אין דעם גילוי פון לעתיד, וואס דער דומם וועט אנהויבען ריידען, דערציילען, און ער וועט מאנען, אויב מען האט גייענדיג ניט געטראכט אדער גערעדט דברי תורה, פארוואס האט מען אויף אים געטראטען.

די ערד וואס מען טרעט אויף איהר, ווארט טויזענטער יאהרען, פון ששת ימי בראשית, און עס טרעטען אויף איהר דערווייל כמה ברואים בעלי חיים כו', ביז עס וועט דארט טרעטען א איד, צוויי אידען, און וועלען ריידען א דבר תורה. ובאם לאו - זאגט זי: דו ביזט דאך אויך ווי א בהמה.
hayomYom.clear:
Before the blessing of Hamotzi, we mark the bread [with the knife], but we are careful not to cut it.

Even at Kiddush over bread, we say Savri maranan.

About the Time to Come it says: “A stone will cry out from the wall, and a beam from the wood will answer it” (Chavakuk 2:11). Now, the inanimate is silent. People step on it and it says nothing. But a time will come, with the revelation of the Future, when the inanimate will begin to speak and tell, and it will demand: if you walked without thinking or speaking words of Torah, why did you step on me?

The earth that is walked on has been waiting thousands of years, since the Six Days of Creation. Meanwhile, all kinds of creatures and animals walk on it, until a Jew, or two Jews, will walk there and speak words of Torah. And if not, it says: “You are just like an animal too!”
translationNotes: רושמים: “mark,” make a sign on the bread.
מאנען: “demand,” as in calling in a debt.

hayomYom.english: The Alter Rebbe said: The offerings for the Sanctuary included gold, silver and copper, but nothing sparkled except for the mirrors presented by the women. From these mirrors were fashioned the washbasin and its base. These were the last of the Sanctuary articles to be made, but were used at the start of every Sanctuary service (for laving by the kohanim) - for their beginning is implanted in their end.
hayomYom.hebrew: רבינו הזקן אמר: בתרומת המשכן היו זהב וכסף ונחושת. ולא היה דבר המבריק זולת מראות הצובאות שמהן נעשו הכיור וכנו. הכיור וכנו הם הבאים באחרונה מכל כלי המשכן, ותשמישו הוא בראש כל עבודות המשכן, כי נעוץ תחלתן בסופן.
hayomYom.clear:
The Alter Rebbe said: The contributions to the Mishkan [Sanctuary] included gold, silver and copper. But nothing there sparkled except the mirrors of the women who gathered (Shemos 38:8). From those mirrors the kiyor [washbasin] and its base were made.

The kiyor and its base were the last of all the Mishkan’s vessels to be made. Yet its use comes first, at the start of all the services in the Mishkan [the kohanim washed from it before serving]. For “their beginning is wedged in their end” (Sefer Yetzirah 1:7).
translationNotes: מראות הצובאות: the mirrors of the women “who gathered” at the Tent of Meeting, the phrase from the verse.
תשמישו הוא בראש כל עבודות המשכן: its use comes at the head of all the services. Kehot’s “laving by the kohanim” is an added explanation, kept here in brackets.

hayomYom.english: Many years before the Alter Rebbe's imprisonment in Petersburg in 5559 (1798), he once came out of his private quarters to where the Chassidim were gathered and said: "In gan eden they sense the preciousness of this lowly world. Not only the Ministering Angels, but even the earliest Emanations would forego everything for one amein y'hei sh'mei raba said by a Jew 'with all his power,' meaning with full concentration, i.e., being totally immersed and involved with these words." This was all he said. The effect was that he kindled such a flame and such a burning enthusiasm in all who heard, that for a full year their amein y'hei sh'mei raba was fiery.
hayomYom.hebrew:
א סך יאהרען נאך פאר פעטערבורג (המאסר שם בשנת תקנ"ט), איז דער אלטער רבי אמאל ארויס צום עולם און האט געזאגט: אין גן עדן דערהערט מען די טייערקייט פון עולם הזה. לא מיבעי מלאכי השרת, אפילו נאצלים הראשונים וואלטען אלץ אוועק געגעבען פאר א אמן יהא שמי'ה רבא פון א אידען, אז ער זאגט בכל כחו כפירושו בכל כוונתו, היינו אז ער איז אינגאנצען אין דעם.

דאס איז געווען דער גאנצער מאמר, און ער האט געפועלט אזא התלהבות והתלהטות בא די הערער, אז א גאנץ יאהר האט מען געזאגט איש"ר [אמן יהא שמי'ה רבא] מיט א ברען.
hayomYom.clear:
Many years before Petersburg [the Alter Rebbe’s arrest there in 5559 (1798)], the Alter Rebbe once came out to the chassidim and said:

In Gan Eden they sense how precious this world is. Not only the ministering angels, but even the first emanated beings, would give up everything for one “Amen, yehei shmei raba” said by a Jew “with all his strength” (Shabbos 119b). That means, as its plain meaning, with all his concentration: he is completely in it.

That was the entire teaching. And it stirred such excitement and fire in those who heard it that for a whole year they said “Amen, yehei shmei raba” with a burning flame.
translationNotes: דאס איז געווען דער גאנצער מאמר: that was the whole saying. A few words were enough.
התלהבות והתלהטות: two words for fire, “enthusiasm and blazing.”
מיט א ברען: literally “with a burn,” a fiery intensity.

hayomYom.english: After drinking wine and eating one of the seven fruits (p. 96), the concluding b'racha ends: v'al pri hagafen v'al hapeirot, baruch...al pri hagafen v'hapeirot (not v'al hapeirot).
hayomYom.hebrew: בברכה מעין שלש אם שתה יין ואכל פירות מז' המינים, חותם: ועל פרי הגפן ועל הפירות, בא"י [ברוך אתה ה'] על פרי הגפן והפירות (ולא "ועל" הפירות).
hayomYom.clear: In the after-blessing Me’ein Shalosh: if you drank wine and also ate fruit of the seven species, you close with: “v’al pri hagafen v’al hapeiros. Baruch Atah Hashem, al pri hagafen v’hapeiros” (not “v’al hapeiros”).
translationNotes: ברכה מעין שלש: the three-faceted after-blessing (Al hamichya). Kehot calls it only “the concluding b’racha.”
Kehot’s Siddur page number is not in the original and is left out.

hayomYom.english: Even ordinary Chassidim were lucid in their knowledge of Tanach. They had a customary procedure: After davening Shacharit they studied Mishna; then while folding tallit and tefillin they would recite a certain set portion of Tanach, so apportioned that they concluded Tanach every three months.
hayomYom.hebrew: החסידים, אפילו הבינונים, היו בקיאים בתנ"ך [בתורה נביאים וכתובים]. ומנהג מסודר היה אצלם, אשר אחר לימוד שיעור משניות שאחרי תפלת שחרית, בשעת קפילת הטו"ת [הטלית ותפילין] היו אומרים שיעור בתנ"ך [בתורה נביאים וכתובים], באופן אשר במשך שלשה חדשים היו גומרים את התנ"ך [התורה נביאים וכתובים].
hayomYom.clear: Chassidim, even the average ones, knew Tanach [Torah, Prophets and Writings] thoroughly. They had a set custom: after the daily portion of Mishnah studied after Shacharis, while folding their tallis and tefillin, they would recite a set portion of Tanach. It was arranged so that they finished all of Tanach every three months.
translationNotes: הבינונים: the “average” chassidim, not the great ones. Kehot’s “ordinary” is close.
בקיאים: thoroughly fluent. Kehot’s “lucid” is vague.

hayomYom.english: Avoda (translated as "service" and "striving") is not the striving that avoda (service) itself be true; rather, truth itself is an avoda, that the "fingernails" be true. Why does that surprise you? "He saw the attribute of Truth," the Talmud declares, "and he prostrated himself."
hayomYom.hebrew: ניט עבודה איז אז עבודה זאל זיין באמת, נאר אמת אליין איז אן עבודה, אז די נעגעל זיינען אמת. וואס ווערסטו נתפעל? מדת האמת ראה (סנהדרין קיא. א) ונפל על פניו.
hayomYom.clear:
Avoda is not just that your avoda should be done with truth. Truth itself is an avoda: that even your fingernails are true.

Why does that surprise you? “He saw the attribute of truth, and fell on his face” (Sanhedrin 111a).
translationNotes: די נעגעל זיינען אמת: even your fingernails, the outermost and least feeling part of you, are truthful. Truth must reach every extremity.
וואס ווערסטו נתפעל: “why are you so taken aback?” The original does not say “the Talmud declares” but gives the source.

hayomYom.english: The term "chassid" is an ancient one that the Sages had even applied to Adam. It describes perfection and excellence in intellect or in emotive character-traits, or in both. However, in Chabad Chassidic doctrine the appellation "Chassid" refers to one who recognizes his own essence-character and his standing in the knowledge and study of Torah, as well as his situation in observing mitzvot. He knows what he lacks and he is concerned and takes pains to fill that void. He is diligent in obedience in the manner of "accepting the yoke."
hayomYom.hebrew: שם חסיד הוא שם קדום הנמצא בדרז"ל [בדברי רבותינו זכרונם לברכה] גם על אדם הראשון (עירובין יח ב), והוא תואר השלימות וההפלגה אם בשכל או במדות או בשניהם יחדיו. אמנם בתורת חסידות חב"ד תואר חסיד הוא, מי שמכיר מהותו העצמי ומעמדו בידיעת התורה ולימודה ומצבו בקיום המצות. יודע הוא מה שחסר לו ונותן לב ודואג למלאות את החסר, ומרבה במשמעת בדרך קבלת עול.
hayomYom.clear:
The name “chassid” is an ancient title. It appears in the words of our Sages even for Adam, the first man (Eruvin 18b). It is a title of completeness and excellence, in intellect, or in character traits, or in both together.

But in the teaching of Chabad Chassidus, a chassid is someone who recognizes what he truly is, and where he stands in knowing and studying Torah and in keeping mitzvos. He knows what he lacks. He pays attention and worries about filling that lack. And he is very obedient, in the way of kabbalas ol [accepting the yoke of Heaven].
translationNotes: מהותו העצמי: his own true essence. Kehot’s “essence-character” is clumsy.
נותן לב ודואג: he pays attention and worries, two separate actions.

hayomYom.english: My father writes in one of his maamarim: "Regarding s'uda shlishit (the third Shabbat meal): The allusion to the verse, today you will not find it (the manna, i.e., Shabbat bread) etc., means only that bread is not required at that meal, but we must partake of some food. R. Yosi did say, may my lot be with those who partake of three Shabbat meals. * * * The Alter Rebbe taught, shortly after he came to Lyozna: One must always (l'olam) be scrupulous (zahir) about the Mincha davening. The special quality of Mincha over Shacharit and Maariv is that it comes in the middle of the day, when people are occupied and busy with their personal affairs, yet they interrupt to daven Mincha. Therefore, l'olam ("always," or more literally: "for the world"), man's avodain This World is... ...y'hei adam (lit. "man must be," but the Hebrew words also imply "be a man" i.e. that) his intellect illuminate and affect his emotions. ...zahir (lit. "scrupulous," but also:) "luminous," i.e., that form (the spiritual) "illuminate" or have dominance over the material. This becomes evident through the Mincha davening.
hayomYom.hebrew:
אאמו"ר [אדוני אבי מורי ורבי] כותב באחד ממאמריו: הא דסעודה שלישית היום לא גו', היינו שא"צ [שאין צריך] פת, אבל צריך לטעום איזה דבר, וא"ר [ואמר רבי] יוסי יהא חלקי מאוכלי ג' סעודות.

תורת רבינו הזקן בתחלת בואו לליאזנא: לעולם יהא אדם זהיר בתפלת המנחה. יתרון תפלת המנחה על התפלות דשחרית וערבית הוא בזה, שהיא באמצע היום, בשעה שבני אדם עסוקים וטרודים בעניניהם, ומפסיקים לתפלת מנחה. וזהו: לעולם, עבודת האדם בעולם היא, שיהא אדם, שכל המאיר ופועל במידות, זהיר יאיר, היינו התגברות הצורה על החומר, וזה ניכר בענין תפלת המנחה.
hayomYom.clear:
My father [the Rebbe Rashab] writes in one of his maamarim: About seudah shlishis [the third Shabbos meal], the hint from the verse “today you will not find it” (Shemos 16:25) means that bread is not required. But you do need to taste something. And R. Yosi said: “May my portion be with those who eat three meals on Shabbos” (Shabbos 118b).

A teaching of the Alter Rebbe, from when he first came to Lyozna: “A person should always be careful with the Minchah prayer” (Berachos 6b).

What makes Minchah greater than Shacharis and Maariv is that it comes in the middle of the day, when people are busy and absorbed in their affairs, and they stop for Minchah.

So this is the meaning:
“Always” (l’olam, also “in the world”): a person’s avoda in the world is,
“a person should be” (yehei adam): that his intellect shines and acts on his emotions,
“careful” (zahir, also “shining”): that form [the spiritual] prevails over matter.
And this shows in the Minchah prayer.
translationNotes: עבודת האדם בעולם: לעולם is read as בעולם, “in the world.”
זהיר יאיר: zahir, “careful,” is read as “will shine,” from זוהר.
שכל המאיר ופועל במידות: “a person” (אדם) means the intellect that lights up and affects the emotions.

hayomYom.english: Rabbis and scholars are called the "eyes of the community" and "heads of the thousands of Israel," and when the head is healthy, the body is then also healthy.
hayomYom.hebrew: הרבנים ובעלי תורה נקראים עיני העדה וראשי אלפי ישראל, וכשהראש הוא בריא אזי גם הגוף בריא.
hayomYom.clear: Rabbis and Torah scholars are called “the eyes of the congregation” (Bamidbar 15:24) and “the heads of the thousands of Israel” (Bamidbar 1:16). And when the head is healthy, the body is healthy too.
translationNotes: Matches the original. No meaning lost.

hayomYom.english: To R. Hillel Paritcher's question whether to review Chassidus even in towns where the people have no conception of Chassidus, the Mitteler Rebbe responded: "The soul hears words of Chassidus." It is written, "Flowing from Lebanon." Lebanon is spelled (in Hebrew) l'b nu'n. "Lebanon" thus represents chochma and bina of the soul. When the soul hears, from there issues a "flow", a "stream of droplets" into that "radiance" or ha'ara of the soul which vitalizes the body; this results in a strengthening of "do good" expressed in the 248 positive mitzvot, and of "turn from evil" expressed in the 365 prohibitions.
hayomYom.hebrew: אדמו"ר [אדוננו מורנו ורבינו] האמצעי ענה לר"ה [לרבי הלל] פאריטשער על שאלתו, אם יחזור חסידות גם בעיירות שאנשיהם אין להם מושג בחסידות: דברי חסידות הערט די נשמה. וכתיב ונוזלים מן לבנון, לבנון ל"ב נו"ן, חכמה ובינה שבנשמה. און אז די נשמה הערט, איז נוזל ונוטף אין דער הארת הנשמה וואס איז מחיה דעם גוף, און עס ווערט א חזוק אין דעם ועשה טוב פון רמ"ח מ"ע [מצות עשה] און אין דעם סור מרע פון שס"ה מל"ת [מצות לא תעשה].
hayomYom.clear:
R. Hillel of Paritch asked the Mitteler Rebbe whether he should review Chassidus even in towns where the people have no idea what Chassidus is. The Mitteler Rebbe answered:

The soul hears words of Chassidus. It is written, “Flowing from Levanon” (Shir HaShirim 4:15). Levanon is lamed-beis nun [32 and 50: the 32 paths of chochmah and the 50 gates of binah], meaning the chochmah and binah of the soul.

And when the soul hears, it flows and drips down into the glow of the soul that gives life to the body. This strengthens the “do good” of the 248 positive mitzvos, and the “turn away from evil” of the 365 prohibitions.
translationNotes: ל"ב נו"ן: the numbers 32 and 50, which Kehot leaves unexplained.
נוזל ונוטף: flows and drips, the image from the verse.

hayomYom.english: Hoshi'einu (p. 76) is said after the Song of the Day on weekdays, Shabbat, Festivals, Rosh Hashana and Yom Kippur.
hayomYom.hebrew: הושיענו אחר שיר של יום אומרים הן בחול הן בשבת, יו"ט [יום טוב], ר"ה [ראש השנה] ויהכ"פ [ויום הכיפורים].
hayomYom.clear: Hoshi’einu is said after the Song of the Day on weekdays and on Shabbos, Yom Tov, Rosh Hashanah and Yom Kippur.
translationNotes: Kehot’s Siddur page number is not in the original and is left out.

hayomYom.english: With three instruments of service - love of G‑d, love of Torah and love of Israel - must young students of Torah approach their Avoda in the vineyard of the L-rd of Hosts, to bring the hearts of their brothers closer to observing practical mitzvot and to designating regular time for Torah study. They must do this without paying any attention to the affliction of factions. The absolute truth is that the heart of Israel is a wellspring, a source of living waters, and there is a "covenant" with effort and publicity - that they shall never be fruitless.
hayomYom.hebrew: בשלשה כלי שרת - אהבת ה', אהבת התורה, אהבת ישראל - צריכים צעירים בני תורה לגשת לעבוד בכרם ה' צבאות, לקרב לב אחיהם לקיום מצות מעשיות וקביעות עתים לתורה - מבלי התחשב עם מחלת המפלגות. והאמת הגמור הוא, אשר לב ישראל הוא מעין מקור מים חיים, וברית כרותה לעבודה ותעמולה שאינן חוזרות ריקם.
hayomYom.clear:
Young Torah students must go to work in “the vineyard of the L‑rd of Hosts” (Yeshayahu 5:7) with three sacred vessels: love of G‑d, love of Torah, and love of Israel. Their task: to bring the hearts of their brothers closer to keeping practical mitzvos and to setting regular times for Torah study. And they must do it without taking into account the disease of party factions.

The absolute truth is that the heart of a Jew is a spring, a source of living water. And there is a covenant made with work and outreach: they never come back empty.
translationNotes: כלי שרת: “sacred vessels,” the vessels of the Temple service, not just “instruments.”
מחלת המפלגות: the “disease” of political parties and factions.
תעמולה: outreach, active campaigning. Kehot’s “publicity” is too weak.

hayomYom.english: My father said: Truth is the middle path. An inclination to the right, to be overly stringent with oneself and find faults or sins not in accord with the truth, or an inclination to the left, to be overly indulgent, covering one's faults or being lenient in demands of avoda out of self-love - both these ways are false.
hayomYom.hebrew: אאמו"ר [אדוני אבי מורי ורבי] אמר: אמת איז דרך המיצוע, א נטי'ה לימין אויף מחמיר זיין אויף זיך און געפינען אין זיך חסרונות, אדער עניני עבירות, וואס ניט ווי דער אמת איז, אדער א נטי'[ה] לשמאל, מקיל זיין זיך, מכסה זיין אייגענע חסרונות, אדער מקיל זיין אין עניני עבודה מצד אהבת עצמו, זיינען ביידע פאלשע דרכים.
hayomYom.clear:
My father [the Rebbe Rashab] said: Truth is the middle path.

Leaning to the right means being strict with yourself and finding in yourself faults, or even sins, that are not really there. Leaning to the left means going easy on yourself, covering up your own faults, or being lenient in matters of avoda out of self-love. Both are false paths.
translationNotes: וואס ניט ווי דער אמת איז: faults that are not the way the truth is, imagined ones.
מצד אהבת עצמו: the reason for leniency is self-love.

hayomYom.english: In the sh'ma before retiring (p. 118): On Shabbat and Festivals we do not say Ribono shel olam or lam'natzei'ach (p. 122). But we do say them on other days that tachanun is not said. After the three paragraphs of sh'ma (p. 120), add the word "emet." Ya'alzu is said once. Hinei and y'varech'cha are said three times. In tikun chatzot do not say lam'natzei'ach...b'vo on days tachanun is omitted.
hayomYom.hebrew: בקריאת שמע שעל המטה רבוש"ע [רבונו של עולם] הריני מוחל וכן למנצח גו' בבוא - א"א [אין אומרים] בשויו"ט [בשבת ויום טוב], אבל צ"ל [צריך לומר] בשאר ימים שא"א [שאין אומרים] בהם תחנון. בסיום הג' פרשיות אומרים תיבת "אמת". יעלזו חסידים - פעם אחת, הנה מטתו - ג"פ [ג' פעמים], יברכך - ג"פ [ג' פעמים]. בתקון חצות א"א [אין אומרים] למנצח גו' בבוא בימים שא"א [שאין אומרים] בהם תחנון.
hayomYom.clear:
In the Shema at bedtime: “Ribono shel olam, hareini mochel” and also “Lamnatzei’ach… bevo” are not said on Shabbos and Yom Tov. But they are said on the other days when Tachanun is not said.

At the end of the three paragraphs of the Shema, add the word “emes.”

“Yaalzu chassidim” is said once. “Hinei mitaso” three times. “Yevarechecha” three times.

In Tikkun Chatzos, “Lamnatzei’ach… bevo” is not said on days when Tachanun is not said.
translationNotes: הריני מוחל: the full opening words of the prayer, which Kehot shortens.
יעלזו חסידים... הנה מטתו: the original lists each verse by its opening words. Kehot’s page numbers are not in the original and are left out.

hayomYom.english:
Haftora: Vayichrot Y'hoyada...Add the first and last verses of the haftora for Machar Chodesh.
Bless Rosh Chodesh Adar Sheini; say the entire Tehillim in the early morning.

In responding to l'chayim there are two versions: (a.) L'chayim tovim ul'shalom, "for good life, and for peace." The reason for this blessing is that the first time drinking wine is mentioned in the Torah, there were undesirable results. "Noach began etc." also, the Tree of Knowledge was a grapevine. Therefore we extend the blessing that this wine be for a good life. (b.) The Maggid of Mezritch used to respond l'chayim velivracha. Once at a farbrengen, the Alter Rebbe responded l'chayim velivracha. After the farbrengen Chassidim discussed this expression, which they heard then for the first time. One chassid proposed: Since "When wine enters, the secret comes out," which in avoda signifies that the emotions are revealed, we need a b'racha for this; the expression is l'chayim velivracha, and "livracha" may be read, leiv racha, a sensitive heart. The Tzemach Tzedek commented: Such an interpretation could be proposed only by a chassid who has davened and labored in avoda for thirty years.
hayomYom.hebrew:
באמירת לחיים יש שתי נוסחאות: א) לחיים טובים ולשלום, וטעם הברכה - להיות כי בשתית היין הנזכרת בפעם הראשונה בתורה היו תוצאות לא טובים - ויחל נח גו', ועץ הדעת גפן היה, ולכן מברכים שיין זה יהיה לחיים טובים.

ב) הרב המגיד ממעזריטש היה עונה לחיים ולברכה. פעם בהתועדות שהיה נוכח רבינו הזקן, ענה רבינו הזקן: לחיים ולברכה. אחרי ההתועדות שוחחו החסידים בטעם נוסח זה, ששמעהו אז פעם הראשונה. אחד החסידים אמר, אשר להיות כי נכנס יין יצא סוד, ובעבודה הוא התגלות המדות, לכן זקוקים לברכה. והנוסח הוא "לחיים ולברכה" - אותיות לב-רכה. הצ"צ [הצמח צדק] אמר ע"ז [על זה]: דאס קען זאגען א חסיד, וואס האט געדאווענט און געטאן אין עבודה דרייסיג יאהר.
hayomYom.clear:
When saying l’chaim there are two versions:

1. L’chaim tovim ul’shalom [for a good life and for peace]. The reason for this blessing: the first time drinking wine is mentioned in the Torah, the results were not good. “Noach began…” (Bereishis 9:20). Also, the Tree of Knowledge was a grapevine. So we bless that this wine should be for a good life.

2. The Maggid of Mezritch used to answer l’chaim velivrachah [for life and for blessing]. Once, at a farbrengen where the Alter Rebbe was present, the Alter Rebbe answered: l’chaim velivrachah. After the farbrengen the chassidim discussed the reason for this version, which they were hearing for the first time.

One of the chassidim said: “When wine goes in, the secret comes out” (Eruvin 65a). In avoda this means the emotions are revealed. That is why a blessing is needed. And the version is “l’chaim velivrachah,” whose letters spell lev rakah [a soft heart].

The Tzemach Tzedek said about this: That is something only a chassid can say who has davened and worked in avoda for thirty years.
translationNotes: נוכח: the Alter Rebbe was “present” at that farbrengen. Kehot leaves this out.
לב-רכה: a soft, tender heart. Kehot’s “sensitive” is close.
דאס קען זאגען א חסיד: Kehot’s “could be proposed only by” adds “only,” which fits the tone.

hayomYom.english: My father said: A chassid creates an environment. If he does not, he had better check his own baggage carefully, to see whether his own affairs are in order. The very fact that he fails to create an environment should make him as broken as a splinter. He must demand of himself: What am I doing in this world?
hayomYom.hebrew: אאמו"ר [אדוני אבי מורי ורבי] אמר: א חסיד מאכט א סביבה. אויב ניט, דארף ער גוט א טאפ טאן בא זיך אין פעקל, וואס טוט זיך מיט איהם אליין. און דאס אליין וואס ער מאכט ניט קיין סביבה - דארף איהם צוברעכען ווי א קינעלע (קיסם). און ער דארף פרעגען בא זיך אליין: וואס טו איך אויף דער וועלט?
hayomYom.clear:
My father [the Rebbe Rashab] said: A chassid makes an environment. If he doesn’t, he has to feel around well in his own bundle, to see what is going on with himself.

And the very fact that he does not make an environment should break him like a splinter. He has to ask himself: What am I doing in this world?
translationNotes: א טאפ טאן אין פעקל: to feel around in your own pack, a hands-on self-check.
צוברעכען ווי א קינעלע (קיסם): snap like a thin chip of wood.

hayomYom.english: In Yaaleh v'yavo (p. 57) zachreinu...bo, ufakdeinu vo
hayomYom.hebrew: ביעלה ויבוא: זכרנו ה"א [ה' אלוקינו] בו - בית דגושה - ופקדנו בו - בית רפוי'.
hayomYom.clear: In Yaaleh v’yavo: “Zachreinu Hashem Elokeinu bo” with a hard beis [bo], and “ufokdeinu vo” with a soft beis [vo].
translationNotes: בית דגושה... בית רפוי': the dagesh and rafeh rule, which explains the bo/vo difference that Kehot only implies.
hayomYom.dataFlag: English is truncated (ends mid-phrase, no explanation of the dagesh rule). Translation completed from the Hebrew.

hayomYom.english: A b'racha must have a hold in something, just as rain benefits only the plowed and sown field, and early and later heavy rains benefit the crops of field or vine. But a waste field, unplowed and unsown, will benefit from neither soft rain, nor the early or later heavy rains.
hayomYom.hebrew: הברכה צריכה לאיזה דבר שתאחז בו, וכמו המטר על שדה חרושה וזרועה, או היורה ומלקוש על תבואת השדה והכרם. אבל בשדה בור לא חרושה ולא זרועה, אין המטר יורה ומלקוש מביאים תועלת.
hayomYom.clear: A blessing needs something to take hold of. It is like rain on a field that has been plowed and sown, or the early and late rains on the crops of the field and the vineyard. But on a wild field, not plowed and not sown, neither rain nor the early and late rains do any good.
translationNotes: שדה בור: an untended, wild field.
Kehot adds “soft” and “heavy” to the rains. The Hebrew just says “rain,” “early rain” and “late rain.”

hayomYom.english: The Tzemach Tzedek told a chassid who had mastered the entire Talmud and related works and had a profound grasp of Chassidus: Kabalat ol transforms one's being. When a simple servant serves out of kabalat ol you can see that he bears the yoke of service even when he sleeps. When a pre-eminent savant and brilliant scholar acquires this sort of kabalat ol, even he can attain the height and value of the simple, sincere person who has mesirat nefesh - total devotion, self-sacrifice.
