hayomYom.hebrew: מענה הצ"צ [הצמח צדק] לחסיד בקי בש"ס כו' ומשכיל גדול בחסידות: קבלת עול איז משנה דעם מהות. דורך קבלת עול פון א עבד פשוט, וואס בשעת ער שלאפט איז אויך ניכר דער עול העבדות זיינער, קען אפילו א למדן און א גאון אויך קומען צו דער מעלה און חשיבות פון א פראסט - תמימות'דיקער מסירת-נפש איד.
hayomYom.clear:
The Tzemach Tzedek answered a chassid who knew all of Shas [the Talmud] and more, and who had deep understanding of Chassidus:

Kabbalas ol changes a person’s very essence. Take the kabbalas ol of a simple servant: even while he sleeps, you can see the yoke of his servitude. Through that kind of kabbalas ol, even a scholar and a gaon can reach the level and worth of a plain, sincere Jew who has mesirus nefesh.
translationNotes: פראסט - תמימות'דיקער: a plain, wholehearted Jew. The point is that the gaon can reach the simple Jew’s level, not the other way around.
משנה דעם מהות: changes the essence, not just behavior.

hayomYom.english: When the Mitteler Rebbe would say Chassidus, there was a perfect hush. Still he would intersperse the Chassidus with, "Sha, sha!" My father explained that this was to still the gushing of his intellect. With this he explained the expression in Zohar: The venerable sage whose mind is concealed, for it is still and tranquil.
hayomYom.hebrew:
צו חסידות ביים מיטעלען רבי'ן, איז געווען זייער שטיל, דאך פלעגט ער בשעת חסידות זאגען: שא, שא.
דער טאטע האט עס ערקלערט, אז דאס איז געווען אויף להשקיט נביעת המוחין. און האט מיט דעם מבאר געווען דעם מאמר הזהר סבא דעתוהי סתים דשקיט ושכיך.
hayomYom.clear:
When the Mitteler Rebbe said Chassidus, it was very quiet. Still, while saying Chassidus he would say: “Sha, sha!” [Hush, hush!]

My father explained that this was to calm the gushing of his intellect. And with this he explained the saying of the Zohar: “The Elder whose mind is hidden, for it is still and quiet.”
translationNotes: להשקיט נביעת המוחין: to quiet the flow welling up in his mind. The “sha” was directed at himself, not at the listeners.
דער טאטע: Yiddish for “my father” [the Rebbe Rashab].

hayomYom.english: Studying Talmud and related works, studying Chassidus, and actual avoda, are all imperative. Not only can there be no thought of one superseding or being superseded by the other, on the contrary, their relationship is symbiotic, mutually enriching: An ignorant person cannot be a chassid, so the study of Talmud and halacha is an absolute necessity. Who is a chassid? He who conducts himself with piety toward his Creator, so there must be the study of Chassidus, and the ultimate purpose of all study is, after all, actual avoda.
hayomYom.hebrew: לימוד הנגלה לימוד החסידות ועבודה בפועל, כולם כאחד מוכרחים המה. ולא זו בלבד דאינו שייך לומר שהאחד ידחה או יודחה מפני חברו, אלא אדרבא הם מסייעים זה לזה, וכמאמר ולא עם הארץ חסיד - שצריך להיות לימוד הנגלה. איזהו חסיד המתחסד עם קונו - שצריך להיות לימוד החסידות, ותכלית הלימוד הלא הוא העבודה בפועל.
hayomYom.clear:
Studying the revealed Torah [Talmud and halacha], studying Chassidus, and actual avoda: all three are equally essential.

Not only can you not say that one pushes aside the other or is pushed aside by it. On the contrary, they help each other.

As it is said: “An ignorant person cannot be a chassid” (Avos 2:5). So there must be study of the revealed Torah.
“Who is a chassid? One who acts with kindness toward his Maker.” So there must be study of Chassidus.
And the purpose of study is, after all, actual avoda.
translationNotes: מסייעים זה לזה: they help each other. Kehot’s “symbiotic” is more than the Hebrew says.
המתחסד עם קונו: going beyond the letter of the law for his Maker. Kehot’s “piety” loses the sense of kindness.

hayomYom.english: It is a tradition among the elders of anash that the Tanya is a compilation of words of counsel given by the Alter Rebbe to anash at yechidus during the years 5540-5550 (1780-1790). In the summer of 5552 (1792) he began arranging the Tanya in the form it now has. A year later, there were already numerous copies, and in time, there were corruptions of the text and even falsifications. For that reason the Rebbe then moved quickly to have it printed. Another version: For twenty years the Rebbe wrote his work, the Tanya, painstakingly examining every last word. By the year 5555 (1795) the text was pure and clarified and he granted permission to copy it. When copies became numerous and corrupted he had it printed. The Tzemach Tzedek related that on the first Rosh Hashana of his life (in 5550, 1789) the Alter Rebbe spoke on the statement in the Talmud, He is administered an oath, Be a tzadik... This discourse is in fact the first three chapters of Tanya.
hayomYom.hebrew:
מקובל אצל זקני אנ"ש [אנשי שלומינו]: ספר התניא הוא לקוטי עצות מה שענה רבינו הגדול לאנ"ש [לאנשי שלומינו] על יחידות בשנות תק"מ-תק"ן. בקיץ תקנ"ב התחיל לסדר את ספר התניא בצורתו כמו שהוא עתה לפנינו. תקנ"ג כבר היו העתקות רבות ממנו, ובמשך הזמן נשתבשו, וגם התחילו לזייפו. ומהאי טעמא נזדרז רבינו למסרו לדפוס. יש נ"א [נוסח אחר]: עשרים שנה כתב רבינו את ספרו התניא, ודייק בכל תיבה ותיבה. בשנת תקנ"ה כבר היה צרוף וזקוק, ואז נתן רשות להעתיקו, וכשרבו ההעתקות ונשתבשו מסרו לדפוס.

הצ"צ [הצמח צדק] סיפר אשר, בראש השנה הראשונה לחייו - שנת תק"ן - אמר רבינו הגדול דרוש משביעין אותו תהי צדיק וכו', והוא הוא שלשת פרקים הראשונים של ספר התניא.
hayomYom.clear:
It is a tradition among the elders of Anash [our chassidic community]: the Tanya is a collection of the advice that the Alter Rebbe gave to Anash in yechidus during the years 5540 to 5550 (1780 to 1790).

In the summer of 5552 (1792) he began arranging the Tanya in the form we have now. By 5553 (1793) there were already many copies of it. Over time the copies became corrupted, and people even began to forge it. That is why the Alter Rebbe hurried to have it printed.

Another version: The Alter Rebbe wrote his Tanya for twenty years, weighing every single word. By 5555 (1795) it was refined and pure, and then he gave permission to copy it. When the copies multiplied and became corrupted, he had it printed.

The Tzemach Tzedek related: On the first Rosh Hashanah of his [the Tzemach Tzedek’s] life, in 5550, the Alter Rebbe said the discourse on “He is made to swear: Be a tzaddik…” (Niddah 30b). That discourse is the first three chapters of Tanya.
translationNotes: תקנ"ג: the Hebrew gives the year 5553. Kehot says “a year later.”
לחייו: the Tzemach Tzedek’s own life (he was born in 5549). Kehot leaves “his” unclear.
צרוף וזקוק: refined and purified, like metal.

hayomYom.english: Walking in the street one must think words of Torah. Whether to actually pronounce the words depends on the place, if one is permitted - according to Torah law - to utter words of Torah there. But when someone goes about not occupied with Torah words, then the stone he treads on exclaims: "Bulach! ('clod', in Russian) How dare you trample me! How are you any higher than I am?"
hayomYom.hebrew: אז מען געהט אין גאס דארף מען טראכטען דברי תורה צי אין מחשבה צי אין דבור, דאס ווענדט זיך, צי מען מעג ע"פ [על פי] דין ריידען דארטען דברי תורה. אבער אז ער געהט און איז ניט פארנומען אין דברי תורה, זאגט אים דער שטיין אויף וועמען ער טרעט: בולאך (גולם) וואס טרעטסטו אויף מיר? מיט וואס ביסטו העכער פאר מיר?
hayomYom.clear:
When you walk in the street you must think words of Torah, whether in thought or in speech. That depends on whether, by halacha, you are allowed to speak words of Torah there.

But if you walk and are not occupied with words of Torah, the stone you step on says to you: “Bulach! [clod, dummy] Why are you stepping on me? How are you any higher than me?”
translationNotes: צי אין מחשבה צי אין דבור: “whether in thought or in speech.” Kehot reorders this.
בולאך (גולם): a lump, a dummy. The original glosses it as golem.

hayomYom.english: My father writes in one of his letters: A single act is better than a thousand groans. Our G‑d lives, and Torah and mitzvot are eternal; quit the groaning and work hard in actual avoda, and G‑d will be gracious to you.
hayomYom.hebrew: אאמו"ר [אדוני אבי מורי ורבי] כותב באחד ממכתביו: טובה פעולה אחת מאלף אנחות. אלקינו חי ותורה ומצות נצחיים המה, עזוב את האנחה ושקוד בעבודה בפועל ויחנך האלקים.
hayomYom.clear: My father [the Rebbe Rashab] writes in one of his letters: One action is better than a thousand sighs. Our G‑d is alive, and Torah and mitzvos are eternal. Stop sighing, work hard in actual avoda, and G‑d will be gracious to you.
translationNotes: אנחות: sighs. Kehot’s “groans” is a bit heavier than the original.

hayomYom.english: In the b'racha Borei nefashot (p. 95), say al kol ma shebarata, "kol" with a cholam, not a kamatz. The intense longing to be bound closely (to a Rebbe) can be satisfied only by learning maamarim of Chassidus which the Rebbe delivers as oral discourses and writes down; simply seeing him is not enough.
hayomYom.hebrew:
בברכת בורא נפשות אומרים על כל מה שבראת - הכ"ף בחולם ולא בקמץ.

גודל התשוקה להתקשרות, יכול להשביע רק כאשר ילמוד מאמרי החסידות שאומר הרב וכותב, כי בראית פנים בלבד לא סגי.
hayomYom.clear:
In the blessing Borei nefashos, say “al kol mah shebarasa,” the kaf with a cholam, not a kamatz.

The great longing for hiskashrus [being bound to the Rebbe] can be satisfied only by studying the maamarim of Chassidus that the Rebbe says and writes. Just seeing his face is not enough.
translationNotes: התקשרות: the bond with the Rebbe. Kehot says “longing to be bound closely (to a Rebbe).”
ראית פנים: seeing the Rebbe’s face in person.

hayomYom.english: Before embarking on a journey from your place of residence, arrange a Chassidic farbrengen and receive a parting blessing from your good friends, and as the familiar expression goes: Chassidim never say farewell, for they never depart from each other. Wherever they are, they are one family.
hayomYom.hebrew: טרם הנסיעה ממקום מדורו יסדר א חסידישען פארבריינגען, ויקבל ברכת הפרידה מחבריו הטובים, וכמאמר הידוע: חסידים זעגענען זיך ניט, ווייל מען פאהרט זיך קיינמאל ניט פאנאנדער, וואו מ'איז - איז מען איין משפחה.
hayomYom.clear: Before you travel away from your hometown, arrange a chassidishe farbrengen and receive a parting blessing from your good friends. As the well-known saying goes: Chassidim don’t say goodbye, because they never part from each other. Wherever they are, they are one family.
translationNotes: זעגענען זיך ניט: chassidim don’t take leave of each other. מ'פאהרט זיך ניט פאנאנדער: they never really drive apart.

hayomYom.english: Chassidus contains two fundamental principles: (a) Understanding every halacha (Torah law) on its spiritual plane, in its root and ultimate source, namely in the Sefirot and planes in every World according to that World's character, as explained in Chassidus. (b) Comprehending the subject of every halacha in avoda; meaning, although the halacha is an expression of G‑dly wisdom and intelligence and is a law in Torah, nevertheless one must discover in it an avoda - concept to guide man's conduct in his life here in This World.
hayomYom.hebrew: חסידות כוללת שני ענינים עקרים: א) הבנת כל הלכה בשרשה ומקורה העצמי ברוחניות, היינו בספירות ומדריגות בכל עולם ועולם לפי ענינו כמבואר בדא"ח [בדברי אלקים חיים]. ב) הבנת ענין כל הלכה בעבודה, היינו שהגם שהיא חכמה ושכל אלקי ודין התורה, מ"מ [מכל מקום] צריך למצוא בזה ענין בעבודה בהנהגת האדם בחיי עולם זה.
hayomYom.clear:
Chassidus includes two main things:

1. Understanding every halacha in its root and true source in the spiritual: in the sefiros and levels of each world, according to that world’s nature, as explained in Chassidus.

2. Understanding what every halacha means in avoda. That is, even though the halacha is G‑dly wisdom and intellect and a law of the Torah, you still have to find in it a lesson in avoda, for how a person conducts himself in his life in this world.
translationNotes: דא"ח: Divrei Elokim Chayim [words of the living G‑d], a name for Chassidus.
מקורה העצמי: its own essential source.

hayomYom.english: The Torah portion dealing with altar offerings begins: "A man who offers (yakriv) of you an offering to G‑d." The logical order of the words should be, "A man of you who offers, etc." The Alter Rebbe answers: "A man who offers" - in order that a man become closer to G‑d - "of you an offering to G‑d" - he must bring the offering of himself. He must sacrifice his personal "animal," the desire for evil that is called the animal soul.
hayomYom.hebrew: דער אנהויב פון פרשת הקרבנות איז: אדם כי יקריב מכם קרבן לה'. עס האט דאך געדארפט שטיין אדם מכם כי יקריב גו', זאגט דער אלטער רבי: אדם כי יקריב, בכדי א מענטש זאל ווערען נעהנטער צו השי"ת [השם יתברך] איז מכם קרבן לה', פון אייך אליין דארף זיין דער קרבן, מקריב זיין זיין אייגענע בהמה, דעם יצר הרע וואס ווערט אנגערופען נפש הבהמית.
hayomYom.clear:
The section of the offerings begins: “Adam ki yakriv mikem korban la’Shem,” “A man who brings near of you an offering to G‑d” (Vayikra 1:2). It should have said, “A man of you who brings…”

The Alter Rebbe says: “A man who brings near” means: for a person to come closer to G‑d, “of you an offering to G‑d,” the offering must come from yourself. You must offer up your own animal: the yetzer hara, which is called the animal soul.
translationNotes: יקריב: “brings near,” from the same root as קרוב, close. That is the basis of the Alter Rebbe’s reading.
פון אייך אליין: “from you yourselves.” The sacrifice is the self.

hayomYom.english: "Amalek came forth and fought with Israel at Refidim." "Refidim" implies "weakness of hands," Israel's neglect of Torah. When Jews become weak in Torah - and Torah study is directed to fulfillment - then Amalek comes and cools the Jew's ardor. "Amalek fought with Israel." The word "Israel" is an acronym in Hebrew for "there are 600,000 letters in the Torah"; (Every Jew has a letter in the Torah, and this is the reason for the universal Jewish custom of each person writing a letter in a Torah scroll.) Amalek cools this sanctity of Torah. The antidote for this is (Moshe's command to Yehoshua) "Choose men for us" - Moshe's men, and "In every generation there is an extension of Moshe," for in every generation there are the "heads of the thousands of Israel." "And go forth and fight Amalek." Note the verbs in singular form (addressing each individual), for Torah is eternal, equally relevant in every generation in every time and place.
hayomYom.hebrew: ויבוא עמלק וילחם עם ישראל ברפידים, שרפו ידיהם מדברי תורה. אז מ'ווערט שוואך אין תורה, וואס דער לימוד התורה איז דאך על מנת לעשות ולקיים, קומט עמלק און קיהלט אפ דעם אידען, וילחם עם ישראל, ר"ת [ראשי תיבות] יש ששים רבוא אותיות לתורה, - דכל אחד מישראל יש לו אות אחת בתורה, ולכן נהגו כל ישראל לכתוב אות בתורה, - און עמלק מאכט קאלט קדושת התורה. והעצה לזה בחר לנו אנשים, אנשי משה, ואתפשטותא דמשה בכל דרא, שבכל דור יש ראשי אלפי ישראל. וצא הלחם בעמלק ל' [לשון] יחיד, לפי שהתורה היא נצחית בכל דור ובכל זמן ובכל מקום בשוה.
hayomYom.clear:
“Amalek came and fought with Israel in Refidim” (Shemos 17:8). Refidim: because they weakened their hands from words of Torah [rafu yedeihem].

When you become weak in Torah, and Torah study is meant to lead to doing and keeping, then Amalek comes and cools the Jew down.

“And fought with Israel”: Yisrael is an acronym for “there are 600,000 letters in the Torah.” (Every Jew has one letter in the Torah. That is why all Jews have the custom of writing a letter in a Torah scroll.) And Amalek makes the holiness of Torah cold.

The answer to this is “Choose men for us” (Shemos 17:9): men of Moshe. There is an extension of Moshe in every generation, since in every generation there are “heads of the thousands of Israel.”

“And go out and fight Amalek”: in the singular. Because the Torah is eternal, equally in every generation, every time and every place.
translationNotes: רפו ידיהם מדברי תורה: the name Refidim is read as “their hands went slack from Torah.”
קיהלט אפ: cools the Jew off. Amalek’s attack is coldness, not open opposition.
ל' יחיד: singular form. Kehot adds “addressing each individual”; the original’s reason is that Torah is eternal for every generation.

hayomYom.english: In reading the Megilla, we read (8:11); laharog ul'abeid, v'laharog ul'abeid. In 9:2, v'ish lo amad bifneihem, v'ish lo amad lifneihem. When saying ha'igeret hazot and igeret ha'Purim hazot hasheinit, we rustle the Megilla. In Shoshanat Yaakov (p. 340): bruchim kol hatzadikim. Shehecheyanu is said before the daytime Megilla-reading too. In the Megilla my grandfather wrote, he did not place the ten sons of Haman in a separate column-page, nor did he begin each column-page with the word hamelech ("the king"). (In the Hebrew text at this point, there appear textual emendations in Torah Or, meaningful only in Hebrew. Translator).
hayomYom.hebrew:
במגלה שכתב אאזמו"ר [אדוני אבי זקני מורי ורבי] לא נכתבו עשרת בני המן בעמוד בפ"ע [בפני עצמו]. וכן לא כל העמודים מתחילים בתיבת "המלך".
בתו"א [בתורה אור] ביאור ד"ה [דבור המתחיל] יביאו לבוש סעיף המתחיל והנה בחי' [בחינת] לבוש, צ"ל [צריך להיות]: "והיא בחי' [בחינת] פני וזו היא המסתתרת.. שהיא בחי' [בחינת] עתיק בחי' [בחינת] סדכ"ס [סתימא דכל סתימין]". ויש נ"א [נוסח אחר]: "והנה בחי' [בחינת] ביום ההוא הוא בחי' [בחינת] בינה אימא עילאה המקננת בבריאה בכורסיא אכן מל'[מלכות] דאצילות נעשה עתיק לבריאה שנעתק וגבוה מבריאה ואינה באה בהתגלות בעולם הבריאה שאפילו מבחי' [מבחינת] ביום ההוא הוא בבחי' [בבחינת] העלם והסתר. ומה שנאמר אסתיר פני שכן נקרא מל' [מלכות] דאצי'[לות] לפי שמקבלת מכל הי"ס [היו"ד ספירות] ממל'[כות] דכתר דאצילות נעשה כתר מלכות וממל'[כות] שבחכ' [שבחכמה] נעשה חכ' [חכמה] שבמל' [שבמלכות] כו'".
hayomYom.clear:
When reading the Megillah, read (8:11) “laharog ul’abeid” and also “v’laharog ul’abeid.” In 9:2, read “v’ish lo amad bifneihem” and also “v’ish lo amad lifneihem.” When saying “ha’igeres hazos” and “igeres haPurim hazos hasheinis,” shake the Megillah.

In Shoshanas Yaakov: “beruchim kol hatzaddikim.” Shehecheyanu is said before the daytime Megillah reading too.

In the Megillah my grandfather [the Rebbe Maharash] wrote, the ten sons of Haman were not written in a column by themselves. Also, not all the columns begin with the word “HaMelech” [the King].

In Torah Or, the explanation of the maamar “Yavi’u levush,” in the section beginning “Vehinei bechinas levush,” it should read: “And this is the level of ‘My face,’ and this is what is hidden… which is the level of Atik, the level of Setima dechol setimin [the most hidden of all hidden].”

Another version: “And behold, the level of ‘on that day’ is the level of Binah, Imma Ila’ah [the supernal mother], which nests in Beriah, in the Throne. But Malchus of Atzilus becomes Atik for Beriah: it is removed from and higher than Beriah and is not revealed in the world of Beriah, so that even from the level of ‘on that day’ it is in a state of hiddenness and concealment. And when it says ‘I will hide My face’ (Devarim 31:18), it is because Malchus of Atzilus is called that, since it receives from all ten sefiros. From the Malchus of Kesser of Atzilus it becomes Kesser of Malchus, and from the Malchus of Chochmah it becomes Chochmah of Malchus, and so on.”
translationNotes: Kehot skips the Torah Or corrections as “meaningful only in Hebrew.” They are translated here directly.
עמוד בפ"ע: a column by itself. In most Megillos, Haman’s sons get their own column and each column begins with המלך.
hayomYom.dataFlag: Hebrew is missing the first part of the English (Megillah readings laharog ul’abeid, v’ish lo amad, rustling the Megillah, Shoshanas Yaakov, Shehecheyanu by day). That part is translated from the English; the rest from the Hebrew. Check source for the missing opening lines.

hayomYom.english: My grandfather said that the Mitteler Rebbe wrote specific maamarim and a special book for every different kind of maskil and oveid in the Chassidic community. Shaar Hayichud and Shaarei Ora, however, are general, written for all chassidim. Shaar Hayichud is the key to the teachings of Chassidus; Shaarei Ora is the alef-beit of Chassidus.
hayomYom.hebrew: אאזמו"ר [אדוני אבי זקני מורי ורבי] אמר, אשר אדמו"ר [אדוננו מורנו ורבינו] האמצעי כתב בשביל כל סוג וסוג מהמשכילים והעובדים אשר בעדת החסידים מאמרים וספר מיוחד, לבד שער היחוד ושערי אורה שהם כלליים, ונכתבו עבור כל החסידים: שער היחוד הוא המפתח דתורת החסידות, ושערי אורה - אלף-בית דתורת החסידות.
hayomYom.clear:
My grandfather [the Rebbe Maharash] said: The Mitteler Rebbe wrote maamarim and a special book for each type of maskil [one who serves through understanding] and oved [one who serves through prayer and work on himself] among the chassidim. The exceptions are Shaar HaYichud and Shaarei Orah, which are general, written for all chassidim.

Shaar HaYichud is the key to the teaching of Chassidus. Shaarei Orah is the alef-beis of the teaching of Chassidus.
translationNotes: המשכילים והעובדים: the two types of chassidim, the contemplative and the worker. Glossed here.

hayomYom.english: Avoda for the businessman includes arousing within himself the faith and perfect trust in the One Who feeds and sustains all flesh, that He will provide him with an ample livelihood. He must be truly happy and cheerful, as though all his livelihood were already in hand.
hayomYom.hebrew: מעבודת בעל עסק: לעורר בעצמו האמונה ובטחון גמור בהזן ומפרנס לכל בשר, כי הוא ית' [יתברך] יתן לו פרנסתו בריוח, וצריך להיות בשמחה וטוב לבב באמת כאלו פרנסתו כבר מזומנת לפניו.
hayomYom.clear: Part of the avoda of a businessman: to awaken in himself faith and complete trust in the One who feeds and sustains all flesh, that He will give him his livelihood generously. And he must be truly happy and in good spirits, as if his livelihood were already set out before him.
translationNotes: בריוח: with ease and abundance.
באמת: “truly” happy. Real joy, not acted.

hayomYom.english: In the Tehillim of this day (87:7), say kol maayanei boch (kol with a kamatz). In Birkat hamazon, say kol (in the same verse) with a cholam.
hayomYom.hebrew: באמירת תהלים (פז. ז) אומרים כל מעיני הכ"ף בקמץ, בסדר ברכת המזון - הכ"ף בחולם.
hayomYom.clear: When saying Tehillim, in 87:7, say “kol maayanai bach” with the kaf with a kamatz. In the order of Birkas Hamazon, the kaf is with a cholam.
translationNotes: Kehot’s “the Tehillim of this day” and “in the same verse” are not in the Hebrew. The Hebrew just contrasts Tehillim with Birkas Hamazon.

hayomYom.english: My grandfather wrote in one of his maamarim: It is necessary to study some of the Written Torah daily with Rashi, for his commentaries are the t'rumot - the select - of the interpretations of our Sages. ...and at the very least everyone must study a tractate of Talmud each year.
hayomYom.hebrew: אאזמו"ר [אדוני אבי זקני מורי ורבי] כותב באחד ממאמריו: צריכים ללמוד בכל יום תושב"כ [תורה שבכתב] עם פירש"י [פירוש רש"י] שזהו תרומות מדרשי רז"ל [רבותינו זכרונם לברכה]... ולכל הפחות צריך כל אחד ללמוד מסכת גמרא בשנה.
hayomYom.clear: My grandfather [the Rebbe Maharash] writes in one of his maamarim: You must study the Written Torah every day with Rashi’s commentary, for it is the terumah [the choice portion] of the Midrashim of our Sages… And at the very least, everyone must study one tractate of Gemara a year.
translationNotes: תרומות מדרשי רז"ל: Rashi is the choice selection of the Sages’ Midrashim, like terumah taken from the crop.
בכל יום: every day. Kehot’s “some of” is not in the Hebrew.

hayomYom.english: R. Moshe Meisels related: The (Alter) Rebbe taught us that the alef of Chassidus is to use our natural traits and instincts in avoda. The beginning of avoda is to employ the natural characteristics of man's powers, for example the natural dominion of mind over heart.
hayomYom.hebrew: ר' משה מייזליש סיפר: דער רבי (רבינו הזקן) האט אונז געלערענט, אז דער אלף פון חסידות איז, אויסצוניצען די טבעיות אין עבודה. און ראשית העבודה זאל זיין אויסצוניצען די טבע הכחות, ווי למשל די טבע פון מוח שליט על הלב.
hayomYom.clear: R. Moshe Meisels related: The Rebbe [the Alter Rebbe] taught us that the alef of Chassidus is to use your nature in avoda. The beginning of avoda should be to use the natural qualities of your faculties, for example, the natural rule of the mind over the heart.
translationNotes: אויסצוניצען: to make use of, to harness. Nature is a tool, not an obstacle.
מוח שליט על הלב: the mind rules the heart by nature.

hayomYom.english: Haftora: Va'y'hi dvar Hashem...dibarti v'assissi. Say Av harachamim. The Alter Rebbe related: Among the teachings my Rebbe (the Maggid) told me at yechidus, there was one on the verse, "A constant fire shall be kept burning on the altar; it shall not be extinguished." The Maggid taught: Though fire descends from Above, spontaneously, it is a mitzva to bring from the 'ordinary,' by man. (Man's action is) an awakening from below which engenders an awakening Above. (For the nature of spirit is that) 'spirit elicits (another, responding) spirit and in turn calls forth another, yet higher spirit.' The spirit from below elicits the spirit from Above, calling forth spirit from higher and still higher. It is a positive mitzva to kindle fire on the altar. 'Altar' refers to the 'man who offers of you.' The offering itself is insufficient. Man must kindle a fire on the offering that is 'of you.' This fire, lo tichbeh (literally, 'it shall not be extinguished'), shall extinguish (tichbeh) the lo (the 'no,' the negative). My Master told me this teaching ten times to engrave it in the ten powers of my soul. "You, my pupil," he said to me, "are in need of this constant fire, for yours is the duty of extinguishing the great lo (of the opponents of Chassidus). You shall extinguish the lo, and G‑d will transform the lo to hein ('yes'; assent, the positive).
hayomYom.hebrew:
רבינו הזקן סיפר: מהתורות שאמר מורי (הרב המגיד) לפני ביחידות, היתה תורה על הפסוק אש תמיד תוקד על המזבח לא תכבה, דהגם שהאש יורד מלמעלה באתערותא דלעילא, מצוה להביא מן ההדיוט, כי באתערותא דלתתא אתערותא דלעילא, כי רוח אייתי רוח ואמשיך רוח, רוח מלמטה אייתי רוח מלעילא, ואמשיך רוח מלעילא ולעילא. ומצות עשה להבעיר אש על המזבח, מזבח הוא אדם כי יקריב מכם, וההקרבה עצמה אינה מספקת, וצריכים להבעיר אש על הקרבן אשר מכם, ואש זה לא תכבה, שהיא מכבה את ה"לא".

את התורה הזאת אמר מורי לפני עשר פעמים - כדי לחקקה בעשר כחות נפשי - ויאמר לי, אתה תלמידי הנך נצרך להאש תמיד, לפי שעליך הוטל לכבות לא (של המנגדים) גדול. אתה תכבה את הלא והשי"ת [והשם יתברך] יהפוך את הלא להן.
hayomYom.clear:
The Alter Rebbe related: One of the teachings my Rebbe [the Maggid] told me in yechidus was on the verse, “A constant fire shall burn on the altar; it shall not go out” (Vayikra 6:6).

Even though fire comes down from Above, as an arousal from Above, it is a mitzvah to bring fire from the ordinary [from man]. Because an arousal from below brings an arousal from Above. For “spirit brings spirit, and draws more spirit”: spirit from below brings spirit from Above, and draws spirit from higher and higher still.

It is a positive mitzvah to light a fire on the altar. The altar is “a man who brings of you an offering.” The offering itself is not enough. You have to light a fire on the offering that is “of you.” And this fire, lo tichbeh, “will not go out,” is the one that puts out the “lo” [the “no”].

My Rebbe told me this teaching ten times, to engrave it in the ten powers of my soul. And he said to me: You, my student, need this constant fire, because you have been given the task of putting out a great “no” [of the opponents of Chassidus]. You will put out the “no,” and G‑d will turn the “no” into a “yes.”
translationNotes: לא תכבה: read as “it puts out the לא.” The fire extinguishes the “no.”
מן ההדיוט: from an ordinary source, from people.
רוח אייתי רוח ואמשיך רוח: the chain of spirit drawing spirit.

calendar.original5703: Haftorah: Vayehi dvar Hashem… dibarti ve’asisi. Say Av Harachamim.

hayomYom.dataFlag: Hebrew lacks the haftorah/Av Harachamim calendar line; cal taken from the English.

hayomYom.english: The Tzemach Tzedek said at the conclusion of the preceding narrative (20 Adar II): "My grandfather, the Alter Rebbe, is the Moshe Rabeinu of Chassidus Chabad. Our sages say that the Torah was given to Moshe but he acted generously (sharing it with Israel). The G‑dly "constant fire" related to the teachings of Chabad Chassidus was given by the Maggid to my grandfather; my grandfather acted generously and gave it to anyone who occupies himself with the study of Chassidus. I am absolutely certain that whoever teaches another and arouses in him that G‑dly "constant fire" is assured of his reward, that this merit of his will never be extinguished.
hayomYom.hebrew: הצ"צ [הצמח צדק] אמר בסיום ספור הנ"ל [הנזכר לעיל] (כ' אד"ש [אדר שני]): זקני - רבינו הזקן - הוא משה רבינו דתורת חסידות חב"ד. במשה אמרז"ל [אמרו רבותינו זכרונם לברכה] שהתורה ניתנה לו, אלא שנהג בה טוב עין. אש תמיד האלקי הנוגע לתורת חסידות חב"ד נתן הה"מ [הרב המגיד] לזקני, וזקני נהג בה טוב עין ויתנה לכל העוסקים בתורת החסידות. ברור לי אשר כל הלומד עם חברו ומעורר בו את האש תמיד האלקי, הנה שכרו אתו אשר זכותו זה לא תכבה לעד.
hayomYom.clear:
At the end of that story (20 Adar II), the Tzemach Tzedek said:

My grandfather, the Alter Rebbe, is the Moshe Rabbeinu of Chabad Chassidus. About Moshe our Sages said that the Torah was given to him, but he was generous with it [and shared it with Israel] (Nedarim 38a).

The G‑dly constant fire of the teaching of Chabad Chassidus, the Maggid gave to my grandfather. My grandfather was generous with it and gave it to everyone who studies Chassidus.

I am certain that anyone who studies with a friend and awakens in him the G‑dly constant fire will have his reward with him: this merit of his will never go out.
translationNotes: נהג בה טוב עין: “had a good eye with it,” he was generous and shared it.
הלומד עם חברו: one who studies together with a friend. Kehot’s “teaches another” changes the picture slightly.

hayomYom.english: Birkat kohanim (p. 268) elicits Divine Intellect. The "raising of the hands" (by the kohanim) is the elevation of the emotive attributes (midot). Their blessing of Israel, "children of kings," signifies malchut. Thus we have the full configuration of the Ten Sefirot.
hayomYom.hebrew: ברכת כהנים הוא המשכת המוחין, הגבהת הידים הוא העלאת המדות, ומברכים לישראל שהם בני מלכים מל' [מלכות], הרי פרצוף שלם של עשר ספירות.
hayomYom.clear: Birkas Kohanim draws down the mochin [intellect]. Raising the hands is the elevation of the middos [emotions]. And they bless Israel, who are children of kings: malchus. So here is a complete structure of all ten sefiros.
translationNotes: פרצוף שלם: a complete partzuf [configuration]. Kehot renders it well.

hayomYom.english: My father once said to a Rav, who labored in avoda and was an especially diligent scholar: A Rav must remember at all times and at every moment that he always stands on the threshold between being one of those who bring merit to the public and, G‑d forbid, one of those who cause the public to sin - the threshold between the loftiest of heights and the most abysmal depth. All issues must touch him at the innermost core of his soul, literally, because his very soul is at stake.
hayomYom.hebrew: אאמו"ר [אדוני אבי מורי ורבי] אמר לרב אחד - בעל עבודה ומתמיד בלימודו: א רב בעדארף בכל עת ובכל רגע געדיינקען, אז תמיד שטייט ער אויף דעם שוועל וואס צווישען מזכי הרבים און ח"ו [חס ושלום] מחטיאי הרבים, אויף דעם שוועל פון עומק רום און עומק תחת, און אלע ענינים בעדארף נוגע זיין אין פנימית נקודת הנפש ממש, ווייל בנפשו הוא.
hayomYom.clear:
My father [the Rebbe Rashab] said to a certain Rav, a man of avoda who was devoted to his learning:

A Rav must remember at every moment that he always stands on the threshold between those who bring merit to the public and, G‑d forbid, those who lead the public to sin. On the threshold between the depth of the heights and the depth of the lowest depths.

And every matter must touch the innermost point of his soul, literally. Because his soul is at stake.
translationNotes: עומק רום ועומק תחת: from Sefer Yetzirah 1:5, the farthest height and the farthest depth.
בנפשו הוא: his very life and soul depend on it.

hayomYom.english: When saying Ana b'choach (p. 22), look at - or picture in thought - the sheimot (Divine Names) formed by the acronyms of the words, but do not pronounce them.
hayomYom.hebrew: באמירת אנא בכח צריך לראות - או לצייר במחשבה - השמות, שהם הר"ת [הראשי תיבות], אבל לא לאמרם.
hayomYom.clear: When saying Ana bechoach, you should look at, or picture in your mind, the Divine Names formed by the first letters of the words. But do not say them.
translationNotes: Matches the original. No meaning lost.

hayomYom.english: The chassid, R. Mordechai Horodoker, related: The first aphorism we heard from the Alter Rebbe when we arrived in Lyozna was: What is forbidden is forbidden, and what is permitted is unnecessary. For some three or four years we labored with this until we integrated this manner (of service) into the various aspects of our lives. Only then did we enter into yechidus, to ask for a path in avoda.
hayomYom.hebrew: החסיד ר' מרדכי האראדאקער סיפר: פתגם הראשון ששמענו מרבינו הזקן כשבאנו לליאזנא הי': וואס מען טאר ניט טאר מען ניט, און וואס מען מעג דארף מען ניט. - כשלש ארבע שנים עבדנו בזה עד שהבאנו אופן זה בעניני חיינו, ורק אז נכנסנו ליחידות לשאול דרך בעבודה.
hayomYom.clear:
The chassid R. Mordechai of Horodok related: The first saying we heard from the Alter Rebbe when we came to Lyozna was: What is forbidden is forbidden. And what is permitted is not necessary.

For about three or four years we worked on this, until we brought this way into the details of our lives. Only then did we go in to yechidus to ask for a path in avoda.
translationNotes: וואס מען מעג דארף מען ניט: what is permitted, you don’t need. Not forbidden, just unnecessary.
עבדנו בזה: “we worked on this,” as avoda.

hayomYom.english: All that is sacred to the nation of the G‑d of Avraham and is fundamental to the house of Israel - in establishing and rearing an upright generation, kashrut of food, the sublime pure holiness of Shabbat, was entrusted by awesome and revered G‑d - for preservation and development - to the woman of Israel. The woman who fulfills her obligation and destiny in the life of the family, in conducting the home, and in seeing that the education be according to Torah, this woman is the subject of the verse, "The wisdom of women constructed her home."
hayomYom.hebrew:
כל הקדוש בעם אלקי אברהם ויסוד בית ישראל, בהעמדת דור ישרים וחנוכם, בכשרות האוכל, ואצילות טוהר קדושת השבת, מסר ונתן השם הנכבד והנורא על ידי נשי ישראל לשמרם ולעבדם.
האשה אשר תמלא חובתה ותעודתה בחיי המשפחה, בהנהגת הבית ובחנוך על פי התורה, עליה הכתוב אומר חכמות נשים בנתה ביתה.
hayomYom.clear:
Everything holy to the people of the G‑d of Avraham, and the foundation of the house of Israel, was handed over by the glorious and awesome G‑d to the women of Israel, to guard it and to cultivate it: raising an upright generation and educating them, the kashrus of the food, and the refined, pure holiness of Shabbos.

The woman who fulfills her duty and her calling in family life, in running the home, and in an education according to Torah, is the one the verse speaks of: “The wise among women, each builds her home” (Mishlei 14:1).
translationNotes: לשמרם ולעבדם is “to guard them and to work them,” echoing Adam’s charge in Eden. Kehot’s “preservation and development” hides the echo.
חובתה ותעודתה: her duty and her destiny or calling, two separate words.

hayomYom.english: Bless Rosh Chodesh Nissan; say the entire Tehillim in the early morning. Day of farbrengen. Haftora: Ko amar...olat tamid. From my father's sichot: The sin of Aharon's sons was "...when they drew close before G‑d and died." This was ratzo without shov, return. The truth is that when coming "before G‑d" there must be tit'haru, one must be clean and pure, and (the closeness) must be evident in actual deeds. That which is on the very highest planes descends to the very lowest depths; hence ratzo without shov is death. Continuing, G‑d commands Moshe (Vayikra 16:2) to speak to Aharon. The letters in the name Aharon are those in the word nir'eh, "visible," which in terms of the powers of the soul refers to intellect. Moshe is to tell Aharon that in order to enter the sacred (area), even "within the curtain" - meaning the state prior to tzimtzum - he must know that... ...upon the ark (ha'aron - the letters of this word spelling nir'eh, "visible" - i.e. intellect) there is a kaporet, a covering, an inner intent and purpose of a concealment, expressed in the words, "the face of (or "the inner aspect of") the kaporet." For this reason one "should not die," i.e. he should not stop with ratzo, the entering alone - for "...in a cloud will I appear on the kaporet;" the inner intent and purpose of the First tzimtzum is revelation. The introductory word to all this is v'al, "he shall not (enter)." This expression of negation indicates total nullification of self, bitul, doing what Chassidus demands, not what his intelligence dictates. Then "he shall enter the sacred (area)."
hayomYom.hebrew: משיחת אאמו"ר [אדוני אבי מורי ורבי]: חטא בני אהרן הי' בקרבתם לפני ה' וימותו, רצוא בלי שוב. דער אמת איז אז מ'קומט לפני ה' דארף זיין תטהרו, ריין און קלאהר, עס מוז זיך דערהערען אין מעשה בפועל, כל הגבוה גבוה ביותר יורד למטה מטה ביותר, ורצוא בלי שוב, היא מיתה. ועל זה בא ציווי ה' אל משה (ויקרא טז ב) שיאמר לאהרן, אותיות נראה, ובכחות הנפש הוא השכלה, לאמר, בשביל לבוא אל הקדש גם מבית לפרוכת שהוא לפני הצמצום, דארף מען וויסען אז על הארן, אותיות נראה, השכלה, איז פאראן א כפורת, א כוונה פון א פארשטעל, וואס דאס איז דער פני הכפורת, אשר על כן ולא ימות, זאל מען ניט בלייבען באם רצוא אליין, כי בענן אראה על הכפורת, דער צמצום הראשון איז כוונתו הגילוי, און דער מבוא צו דעם איז דער ואל, ביטול עצמי, טאן וואס חסידות הייסט, ניט דאס וואס דער שכל זאגט, דאן איז יבוא אל הקדש.
hayomYom.clear:
From a sicha of my father [the Rebbe Rashab]:

The sin of Aharon’s sons was “when they came close before G‑d, and they died” (Vayikra 16:1). This was ratzo without shov [running toward G‑d without returning].

The truth is that when you come “before G‑d,” there must be “you shall be purified” (Vayikra 16:30): clean and clear. It has to be felt in actual deeds. Whatever is highest of all descends lowest of all. So ratzo without shov is death.

On this came G‑d’s command to Moshe (Vayikra 16:2) to speak to Aharon. The letters of אהרן [Aharon] are the letters of נראה [“visible”], which among the soul’s powers is intellect. He was to tell him: To enter the sanctuary, even “within the curtain,” which is the level before the tzimtzum [G‑d’s contraction of His light], you must know this. “Upon the ark” (ארן, again the letters of נראה, intellect) there is a kapores, a cover: an intended concealment. This is “the face of the kapores.”

Therefore, “so that he shall not die”: do not stop at ratzo alone. For “in a cloud I will appear upon the kapores”: the purpose of the first tzimtzum is revelation.

The entrance to all this is the word “ve’al” [“let him not”]: bittul atzmi [nullifying yourself], doing what Chassidus says, not what your intellect says. Then “he may enter the sanctuary.”
translationNotes: עס מוז זיך דערהערען אין מעשה בפועל: it must be felt, show itself, in actual deeds.
א כוונה פון א פארשטעל: a purposeful screen or concealment. The covering itself has a purpose.
ביטול עצמי: self-nullification, the opening into everything that follows.

calendar.original5703: Shabbos Mevarchim Nissan. Say the whole Tehillim early in the morning. A day of farbrengen. Haftorah: Ko amar... olas tamid.

hayomYom.english: We do recite the Harachaman of brit mila (p. 95). (From a sicha at a brit mila repast): At a brit mila we say, "Just as he has entered into the Covenant so may he enter into Torah, into marriage and into good deeds" (p. 141). It is our custom to make an advance payment on tuition fees for the boy's studies. (Here the Rebbe gave a sum of money and said): This is for the Yeshiva.
hayomYom.hebrew:
הרחמן דברית מילה - אומרים.
(משיחה בסעודת ברית מילה): בברית מילה אומרים כשם שנכנס לברית כן יכנס לתורה ולחופה ולמעשים טובים. ונוהגים אצלנו, אז מען גיט דמי קדימה אז דער אינגעל זאל לערנען - (ונתן כ"ק [כבוד קדושת] אדמו"ר [אדוננו מורנו ורבינו] שליט"א [שיחיה לימים טובים ארוכים] סכום מסוים באמרו): - דאס איז פאר דער ישיבה.
hayomYom.clear:
The Harachaman for a bris mila [added in Birkas HaMazon]: we do say it.

(From a sicha at a bris mila meal:) At a bris we say, “Just as he has entered the covenant, so may he enter into Torah, the chuppah and good deeds.” Our custom is to give an advance payment so the boy will learn Torah.

(The Rebbe [Rayatz] shlita then gave a certain sum of money, saying:) This is for the yeshiva.
translationNotes: דמי קדימה: money paid in advance, so the child’s learning is “paid for” from the start.
Kehot’s siddur page numbers are not in the original. Left out.

hayomYom.english: My father said at a farbrengen: G‑d created the universe and all physical objects yeish mei'ayin, something from nothing. Jews must transform the "something" into "nothing," transform the material into spiritual. The avoda of turning the physical into spiritual and making the physical into an instrument for the spiritual, is a personal obligation. Every single person, individually, is required to do this.
hayomYom.hebrew: באחת ההתועדות אמר אאמו"ר [אדוני אבי מורי ורבי]: הקב"ה [הקדוש ברוך הוא] ברא את העולם וכל הדברים הגשמיים מאין ליש, און אידען דארפען מאכען מיש לאין, פון די גשמיות מאכען רוחניות. די עבודה מאכן פון גשמיות רוחניות און דעם גשמי מאכען א כלי פאר רוחניות, דאס איז א חובת גברא, אין דעם איז מחויב כל אחד ואחד בפרט.
hayomYom.clear:
At one farbrengen my father [the Rebbe Rashab] said:

G‑d created the world and all physical things from nothing into something. Jews have to make the something into nothing: to make spirituality out of physicality.

The avoda of making the physical into spiritual, and making the physical into a vessel for the spiritual, is a chovas gavra [a personal duty]. Each and every person is obligated in it individually.
translationNotes: מאין ליש / מיש לאין: “from nothing to something” and back again. Kept the mirror image.
חובת גברא: a duty on the person himself, not something that can be delegated.

hayomYom.english: We do not say tachanun all month. After saying the nassi (p. 368), we say the Yehi ratzon (p. 371) which is printed in Torah Or Siddur. Kohanin and levi'im also say it. My father instructed his brother-in-law, R. Moshe Horenstein, a kohein, to say Yehi ratzon after the nassi, noting that even a kohein or leivi must say it, for it is related to ibur.
hayomYom.hebrew: אאמו"ר [אדוני אבי מורי ורבי] ציוה לגיסו הרב משה הארענשטיין הכהן לאמר היהי רצון שאחר הנשיא, ואמר לו כי אפילו כהן ולוי צריך לאמרו, כי זה שייך לעיבור.
hayomYom.clear: My father [the Rebbe Rashab] told his brother-in-law, R. Moshe Horenstein, a kohen, to say the Yehi ratzon after the nasi [the daily reading of the tribal prince’s offering, said in Nissan]. He told him that even a kohen or a Levi must say it, because it relates to ibur [the soul of that tribe’s nasi coming to assist].
translationNotes: שייך לעיבור: ibur is a soul “joining” another to help it. Kehot leaves the term unexplained.

calendar.original5703: No tachanun all month. After the nasi, say the Yehi ratzon printed in Siddur Torah Or. Kohanim and Levi’im say it too.

hayomYom.english: Yahrzeit of my father the Rebbe, (R. Sholom Dovber) who passed away on Saturday night, 2 Nissan 5680 (1920), in Rostov, and is interred there. The first maamar he (R. Sholom Dovber) delivered after the passing of his father (the Rebbe Maharash) was on the second day of Chol Hamoed Sukot 5643 (1882), beginning Keter yitnu l'cha etc. The last public maamar in his lifetime was delivered at the Purim repast 5680, beginning Reishit goyim Amalek...keitz sam lachoshech.
hayomYom.hebrew:
הילולא של כ"ק [כבוד קדשת] אאמו"ר [אדוני אבי מורי ורבי]. נסתלק אור ליום א' ב' ניסן שנת תר"ף בראסטאב. ושם מ"כ [מנוחתו כבוד.].
מאמר הראשון אשר אמרו ברבים, אחרי הסתלקות אביו: ביום השני דחה"ס [דחג הסוכות] תרמ"ג, ומתחיל כתר יתנו לך כו'. מאמר - ברבים - האחרון בהיותו בעלמא דין: בסעודת פורים תר"ף, ומתחיל ראשית גוים עמלק גו' קץ שם לחשך.
hayomYom.clear:
The yahrzeit of my father, the Rebbe [Rashab]. He passed away on Saturday night, 2 Nissan 5680 [1920], in Rostov, and is buried there.

The first maamar he said publicly after his father’s [the Rebbe Maharash’s] passing was on the second day of Sukkos 5643 [1882]. It begins Keser yitnu lecha.

The last maamar he said publicly while in this world was at the Purim meal of 5680. It begins Reishis goyim Amalek... keitz sam lachoshech.
translationNotes: ביום השני דחה״ס is “the second day of Sukkos.” Kehot says “the second day of Chol Hamoed.”
אור ליום א׳: the night before Sunday, i.e. Saturday night.

hayomYom.english: Among my father's regular Torah-study sessions: A parsha of Chumash with Rashi daily; reciting Tanach by heart - a chapter each of Torah, Nevi'im and Ketuvim; a chapter of Mishnayot; a regular session in profound study of Gemara - two folio pages weekly, another in rapid study of Gemara - three pages daily; a session of study of the Jerusalem Talmud; a regular period for Codes, but not daily. During the course of the year he would conclude the entire Midrash Raba, "borrowing" from the long sedrot and "repaying" on the shorter ones.
hayomYom.hebrew: משיעורי אאמו"ר [אדוני אבי מורי ורבי]: בכל יום פרשה חומש עם פירש"י [פירוש רש"י]. אמירת תנ"ך [תורה נביאים כתובים] בעל פה: קאפ' [קאפיטל] אחד מתורה וכן מנביאים וכן מכתובים. פרק אחד משניות. שיעור גמרא לעיוני ב' דפים לשבוע, שיעור למיגרס ג' דפים ליום. שיעור בירושלמי. גם שיעור - לא בכ"י [בכל יום] - בפוסקים. במשך השנה הי' [היה] מסיים כל המד"ר [המדרש רבה]: לווה בסדרות הארוכות ופורע בקצרות.
hayomYom.clear:
Among my father’s [the Rebbe Rashab’s] regular study sessions:

Every day: a parsha of Chumash with Rashi. Tanach by heart: one chapter of Torah, one of Nevi’im and one of Kesuvim. One chapter of Mishnayos.

Gemara in depth: two pages a week. Gemara for quick, broad review: three pages a day.

A session in Talmud Yerushalmi. Also a session, not every day, in the poskim [halachic codes].

Over the course of the year he finished all of Midrash Rabbah. He “borrowed” on the long parshiyos and “repaid” on the short ones.
translationNotes: לעיונא / למיגרס: deep analysis versus fast, wide reading. Kehot’s “profound” and “rapid” is close.
לווה ... ופורע: borrowing and repaying. On long parshiyos he fell behind and caught up on short ones.

hayomYom.english: The avoda of laymen has two categories: 1) Avoda with self: When actually at work, in a free moment in his store, for example, he should study a Mishna or two, or a chapter of Tanya. He should commit some Torah to memory - for example, Chumash, Mishna, Tehillim, Tanya, so that he will be able to review these while in the marketplace, the street or wherever. 2) Avoda with another: When discussing business, he should turn the conversation towards introducing a story with content, and seek some reason or opportunity to stimulate the other to study Torah, or to do similar activities.
hayomYom.hebrew:
עבודת בעלי עסקים מתחלקת לשני סעיפים עיקרים:
א) העבודה עם עצמו. בעת עסקו ממש בשעה הפנוי'[ה], בישבו בחנות וכדומה, ילמוד משנה משניות פרק תניא, ויהי לו איזה דברי תורה, כמו חומש משניות תניא, שיהי'[ה] בקי בהם בעל פה, למען שיוכל לחזור עליהם בהלכו ברחוב, בשוק וכדומה.
ב) העבודה עם זולתו. בעת הדבור בעניני עסק יסבב הדבור לספר איזה ספור תוכני, ולמצוא עילה וסיבה לעורר ע"ד [על דבר] למוד וכיוצא בזה.
hayomYom.clear:
The avoda of businesspeople divides into two main parts:

1. Avoda with yourself. While you are actually at work, in a free moment, sitting in the store and the like, learn a mishna or a few, or a chapter of Tanya. Have some Torah that you know well by heart, like Chumash, Mishnayos or Tanya, so you can review it while walking in the street, in the market and so on.

2. Avoda with others. When talking business, steer the conversation toward telling a story with real content. Find a reason and an opening to stir the other person about learning, and the like.
translationNotes: בקי בהם בעל פה: know it fluently by heart.
The Hebrew list is Chumash, Mishnayos, Tanya. Kehot adds Tehillim, which is not in the original.
ספור תוכני: a story with substance, not just small talk.

hayomYom.english: In Birkat Hamazon, in Retzei (p. 91), say baal hayeshuot ("b" in the first word) u'vaal hanechamot ("v" in the second word). My grandfather commented on the saying, "The place of man does not honor him; rather man honors his place." The term, kavod, "honor," has two implications. One is kaveid, "liver," as the Torah says, "Pharaoh's heart is kaveid ("heavy"), and the Sages comment, "His heart became like a liver," (cold, insensitive). The other meaning is kavod, "honor," signifying the revelation of a supernal encompassing illumination. "The place of man does not honor him": Place (and circumstances) do not make him cold and insensitive. Rather, "Man honors his place," man has the capacity and the power to illuminate his environment ("place") with the light of Torah and avoda. When the soul descends into the body, it is administered an oath to be a tzadik, This oath, sh'vua, implies sova, "satiety"; the person is generously endowed with eminent powers to be able to fulfill G‑d's intention in having the soul descend (into the material world). And just as it is with the soul's descent, so is it also with every person, in whatever place he may be.
hayomYom.hebrew:
ברצה דברהמ"ז [דברכת המזון] אומרים "בעל הישועות" - בית דגושה "ובעל הנחמות" - בית רפוי'[ה].
אאזמו"ר [אדוני אבי זקני מורי ורבי] אמר במרז"ל [במאמר רבותינו זכרונם לברכה] לא מקומו של אדם מכבדו אלא אדם מכבד את מקומו, כבוד יש בו שני פירושים: לשון כבדא כמרז"ל [כמאמר רבותינו זכרונם לברכה] כבד לב פרעה נעשה לבו ככבד. ולשון כבוד, גילוי אור מקיף נעלה. וזהו: לא מקומו של אדם מכבדו כלומר מקררו, אלא אדם מכבד את מקומו, שניתן לו כח ועוז להאיר את מקומו באור תורה ועבודה. כשם דבירידת הנשמה בגוף משביעים אותו תהא צדיק, דשבועה זו הוא ענין השובע בכחות נעלים שתוכל להשלים כונת ירידתה, הנה כן הוא בכל אדם ואדם במקום שהוא.
hayomYom.clear:
In Retzei of Birkas HaMazon, say “ba’al hayeshuos” with a hard b, and “uva’al hanechamos” with a soft v.

My grandfather [the Rebbe Maharash] said about the Sages’ teaching, “It is not a man’s place that honors him, but the man who honors his place” (Taanis 21b):

Kavod has two meanings. One is from kaved, “liver,” as the Sages said on “Pharaoh’s heart was heavy [kaved]”: his heart became like a liver. The other is kavod, “honor”: a revelation of a lofty, encompassing light.

So: “It is not a man’s place that kaveds him,” meaning, it does not make him cold. “Rather, the man kaveds his place”: he was given the power and strength to light up his place with the light of Torah and avoda.

When the soul descends into the body, it is made to swear, “Be a tzaddik” (Niddah 30b). This oath, shevua, is about sova, being filled with lofty powers so the soul can complete the purpose of its descent. And just as it is with the soul’s descent, so it is with every person, in whatever place he is.
translationNotes: מקררו: “cools him.” The liver image means cold and unfeeling.
שובע בכחות נעלים: satisfied, filled to the full with lofty powers.

hayomYom.english: Experience has shown that with less speculation, but working with orderliness and firmness, in accord with the "pleasantness" of Torah (with the "right hand bringing close and the left hand rejecting") one is certain to achieve results, especially in matters concerning the fundamentals of our religion.
hayomYom.hebrew: הנסיון הראה, אשר כשממעטים בחקירות, ועובדים בסדר ובתוקף, על פי הנעימות של תורה, ימין מקרבת ושמאל דוחה, אזי פועלים בודאי, ובפרט בענינים העיקרים מעקרי הדת.
hayomYom.clear: Experience has shown: when you cut down on speculation and work with order and firmness, following the pleasantness of the Torah, “the right hand draws close and the left pushes away” (Sotah 47a), you will certainly accomplish. Especially in matters that are among the fundamentals of the faith.
translationNotes: ממעטים בחקירות: doing less theorizing and deliberating. Less talk, more work.
בתוקף: with firmness, alongside the pleasantness, not instead of it.

hayomYom.english: Text of Vay'hi binsoa (p. 185, par. Al): v'chirtzon kol amcha beit yisrael. The Alter Rebbe's family name was Baruchovitch. The Mitteler Rebbe's family name was Schneuri. The Tzemach Tzedek's family name was Schneersohn.
hayomYom.hebrew:
נוסח ויהי בנסוע: וכרצון כל עמך בית ישראל.
כינוי משפחה של רבינו הזקן: ברוכאוויטש.
כינוי משפחה של בנו אדמו"ר [אדוננו מורנו ורבינו] האמצעי: שניאורי.
כינוי משפחה של הצ"צ [הצמח צדק]: שניאורסאהן.
hayomYom.clear:
The text of Vayehi binso’a: “vechirtzon kol amcha beis Yisrael.”

The family name of the Alter Rebbe: Baruchovitch.
The family name of his son, the Mitteler Rebbe: Schneuri.
The family name of the Tzemach Tzedek: Schneersohn.
translationNotes: וכרצון: “and as the will,” with the vav. That is the point of the nusach note.

hayomYom.english: Every soul has its particular avoda, in the areas of intellect and emotions, in accordance with that soul's nature and character. It is written: "From my foes have You given me wisdom"; from the evil tendencies one detects in his natural traits, he can become wise and know how to handle the correction of these traits, and how to subordinate his powers, in the service of G‑d.
hayomYom.hebrew: כל נשמה יש לה עבודה פרטית במוחין ומדות כפי טבעה וענינה. וכתיב מאויבי תחכמני, מההטיות הרעות שמרגיש במדותיו הטבעיות, מזה מתחכם ויודע איך לכלכל תקון מדותיו ושעבוד הכחות שלו בעבודת השי"ת [השם יתברך].
hayomYom.clear:
Every soul has its own particular avoda, in mind and emotions, according to its nature and makeup.

It is written, “From my enemies You make me wise” (Tehillim 119:98). From the bad leanings you feel in your natural traits, you become wise. You learn how to manage the correction of your traits and how to bring your powers into the service of G‑d.
translationNotes: ההטיות הרעות: bad leanings or tilts, not full-blown evil.
שעבוד הכחות: harnessing, subjugating your powers to serve G‑d.

hayomYom.english: Jewish wealth is not houses and gold. The everlasting Jewish wealth is: Being Jews who keep Torah and Mitzvot, and bringing into the world children and grandchildren who keep Torah and Mitzvot.
hayomYom.hebrew: ניט הייזער און געלד איז דער אידישער רייכטום. דער אידישער אייביקער רייכטום איז, אז מען איז אידען וואס היטען אפ תורה און מצות און מ'בריינגט אויף דער וועלט קינדער און אייניקלאך וואס היטען אפ תורה און מצות.
hayomYom.clear: Houses and money are not Jewish wealth. The eternal Jewish wealth is this: to be Jews who keep Torah and mitzvos, and to bring into the world children and grandchildren who keep Torah and mitzvos.
translationNotes: Matches the original. No meaning lost.

hayomYom.english: On the subject of the campaign to popularize the observance of taharat hamishpacha in your community, ponder this deeply: Let us imagine that G‑d were to give you the opportunity to save a Jewish community from extinction (G‑d forbid), you would certainly be willing to risk your life for this and you would thank and praise Him for His great kindness in offering you an opportunity of such enormous merit. The same then holds true to an even greater degree with regard to the campaign for taharat hamishpacha; it is an endeavor which literally saves lives.
hayomYom.hebrew: בדבר התעמולה בענין טהרת המשפחה במושבו, יתבונן בזה: אילו יצוייר, אשר ה' אנה לידו להציל מושב יהודים מכליון, ר"ל [רחמנא לצלן], הנה בטח הי'[ה] מוסר נפשו על זה, והי'[ה] מהלל ומשבח את השי"ת [השם יתברך], על גודל החסד לזכותו בזכות גדול כזה. כן ויותר מכן היא תעמולה זו, שהיא הצלת נפשות ממש.
hayomYom.clear:
About the campaign for taharas hamishpacha [the laws of family purity] in your town, think about this:

Imagine G‑d gave you the chance to save a Jewish community from destruction, G‑d forbid. You would surely give your life for it. And you would praise and thank G‑d for His great kindness in giving you such a great merit.

This campaign is the same, and even more so. It is literally saving lives.
translationNotes: אנה לידו: G‑d “brought it into his hands,” placed the opportunity before him.
מוסר נפשו: give over his life, mesirus nefesh. Kehot’s “risk your life” is softer.

hayomYom.english: On his birthday, one should spend time in seclusion. He should recall his experiences and think deeply into them. He should then repent and correct those (of his past deeds) that need correction and repentance.
hayomYom.hebrew: ביום ההולדת, על האדם להתבודד, ולהעלות זכרונותיו ולהתבונן בהם, והצריכים תקון ותשובה ישוב ויתקנם.
hayomYom.clear: On your birthday, spend time alone. Bring up your memories and think them over. Whatever needs correcting and teshuva, do teshuva and correct it.
translationNotes: להתבודד: to seclude yourself, a set time alone with your thoughts.

hayomYom.english: From the time of the exodus from Egypt the Jewish people are called the "Army of G‑d." They are also called "servants." The difference is this: A servant performs his master's service which may be on many different levels; he may work at the delicate craft of threading pearls, he may do other kinds of expert work or he may perform simple tasks. His service involves great toil and labor, but this does not constitute mesirat nefesh - a willingness to sacrifice self, to lay down one's life. Soldiers are servants who serve with great toil and labor and with self sacrifice, in wars of defense or attack. The soldiers stand at their posts with the highest degree of stalwart determination, undeterred by the opposing enemy; their service is not one of comprehension, for they act according to the orders of their commander. The Jews in Egypt were utterly degraded under their severe and bitter affliction. Yet, despite it all, they did not change their names, their language, or their distinctive clothing. With absolute determination they stood at their posts, for they knew that G‑d had promised to redeem them. Whoever behaves as they did under such circumstances is a soldier in the Army of G‑d, and the Al-mighty will come to his assistance in a manner that manifests itself in nature - yet transcends nature.
hayomYom.hebrew: מזמן יציאת מצרים נקראו בני ישראל צבאות ה'. ההפרש בין עבדים - שנקראו כן בנ"י [בני ישראל] - וצבאות הוא: עבד עושה עבודת רבו - ובזה כמה דרגות נוקב מרגליות, עושה שאר מלאכות, עושה מלאכות פשוטות - ויש בזה יגיעה ועמל רב, אבל אין זה ענין של מסירת נפש. צבא הם עבדים שעובדים ביגיעה רבה ועמל ובמסירת נפש, הן במלחמת הגנה והן במלחמת תנופה, ועומדים על משמרתם בתכלית התוקף מבלי התפעל מהמנגד ושונא, ועבודתם זו אינה ענין של השגה, כי הם מתנהגים ע"פ [על פי] הוראת מצביאם. והנה נש"י [נשמות ישראל] במצרים היו בתכלית השפלות בעינוים קשים ומרים, ועם זה לא שינו שמם ולשונם ולבושיהם, ועמדו על משמרתם בתכלית החוזק, כי ידעו שהקדוש ברוך הוא הבטיח לגאול אותם, והמתנהג כזה במצב זה הוא מצבא ה', דה' עוזרו בדרך מלמעלה מן הטבע בטבע.
hayomYom.clear:
From the time of the Exodus, the Jewish people are called “the hosts of G‑d.” They are also called servants. The difference between servants and soldiers:

A servant does his master’s work. There are levels in this: drilling pearls, other skilled work, simple tasks. It takes effort and a lot of toil, but it is not mesirus nefesh.

Soldiers are servants who serve with great effort and toil, and with mesirus nefesh, in defensive and offensive war. They hold their posts with total firmness, unshaken by the opponent and the enemy. Their service is not a matter of understanding: they act on their commander’s orders.

The Jewish souls in Egypt were at the lowest point, under hard and bitter suffering. Even so, they did not change their names, their language or their clothing. They held their posts with total strength, because they knew G‑d had promised to redeem them.

Whoever acts this way in such a situation is one of G‑d’s hosts. G‑d helps him in a way that is above nature, within nature.
translationNotes: נוקב מרגליות: drilling pearls, a delicate skill. Kehot says “threading.”
מבלי התפעל מהמנגד: not being affected at all by the opposition.
מלמעלה מן הטבע בטבע: help beyond nature, dressed in nature.

hayomYom.english: Yahrzeit of the Rebbe Tzemach Tzedek. He passed away in the year 5626 (1866) in Lubavitch and was interred there. My grandfather related: At the age of 12 the Tzemach Tzedek began to write scholarly dissertations in the field of Talmud and halacha as well as in chassidic philosophy.
hayomYom.hebrew:
הילולא של כ"ק [כבוד קדושת] הצ"צ [הצמח צדק]. נסתלק שנת תרכ"ו בליובאוויטש, ושם מ"כ [מנוחתו כבוד].
מספורי אאזמו"ר [אדוני אבי זקני מורי ורבי]: הצ"צ [הצמח צדק] התחיל לכתוב נגלה ודא"ח [ודברי אלקים חיים] בהיותו בן שתים עשרה שנה.
hayomYom.clear:
The yahrzeit of the Tzemach Tzedek. He passed away in 5626 [1866] in Lubavitch, and is buried there.

From my grandfather’s [the Rebbe Maharash’s] stories: The Tzemach Tzedek began writing nigleh [Talmud and halacha] and Chassidus when he was twelve.
translationNotes: נגלה ודא״ח: the revealed Torah and Chassidus. Kehot’s “scholarly dissertations” is more than the Hebrew says.

hayomYom.english: With regard to selling the chametz it is the custom in the Rebbe's family not to designate the rabbi as an agent (empowered to sell the chametz to the non-Jew) but to sell the chametz outright to the rabbi with an areiv kablan, a third party guarantor. My father would personally supervise the baking of the sh'mura matza on erev Pesach afternoon. He, too, would recite the hallel, but he would interrupt - even in the middle of a chapter - to give instructions regarding the kneading, baking and so forth.
hayomYom.hebrew:
בבית רבינו נוהגים שלא לעשות את הרב למורשה, אלא למכור לו את החמץ ובערב קבלן.

באפית השמורה ערב פסח אחר חצות, הי'[ה] אאמו"ר [אדוני אבי מורי ורבי] נוכח, ואומר ג"כ [גם כן] הלל, והיה מפסיק - גם באמצע פרק - להורות בהנוגע להלýישה, אפי'[ה] וכה"ג [וכהאי גוונא].
hayomYom.clear:
In the Rebbe’s household the custom is not to appoint the rav as an agent [to sell the chametz], but to sell the chametz to him directly, with an arev kablan [a guarantor].

At the baking of the shmura matza on Erev Pesach after midday, my father [the Rebbe Rashab] was present. He also said Hallel, and he would stop, even in the middle of a chapter, to give instructions about the kneading, the baking and the like.
translationNotes: למורשה: an agent with power of attorney. The point is a direct sale, not agency.

hayomYom.english: At the first seder my father would be brief, in order to eat the afikoman before midnight. On the second night, however, he would expound at length; he began the seder before 9 p.m. and ended at about 3 or 4 in the morning, dwelling at length on the explanation of the Haggada. The Alter Rebbe declared: The matza of the first evening of Pesach is called the Food of Faith; the matza of the second evening is called the Food of Healing. When healing brings faith ("Thank you, G‑d, for healing me") then clearly there has been illness. When faith brings healing, there is no illness to start with.
hayomYom.hebrew:
בסדר הראשון הי'[ה] אאמו"ר [אדוני אבי מורי ורבי] מקצר בכדי לאכול האפיקומן לפני חצות, אבל בשני היה מאריך. מתחיל לפני שעה ט וגומרו בשעה ג-ד אחר חצות, והי'[ה] מאריך בביאור ההגדה.

אדמו"ר הזקן אמר: מיכלא דמהימנותא - לילה הראשון. מיכלא דאסותא - לילה השני. אז די רפואה בריינגט די אמונה, וואס ער זאגט א דאנק דיר ג-ט פאר מיין רפואה, איז ער דאך געווען קראנק. אבער אז די אמונה בריינגט די רפואה, איז מען לכתחילה ניט קראנק.
hayomYom.clear:
At the first Seder my father [the Rebbe Rashab] kept it short, so as to eat the afikoman before midnight. At the second he went at length. He began before 9 and finished at 3 or 4 after midnight, explaining the Haggadah at length.

The Alter Rebbe said: The first night is “the food of faith.” The second night is “the food of healing.” If the healing brings the faith, so that you say, “Thank You, G‑d, for my healing,” then you were sick. But if the faith brings the healing, you are not sick to begin with.
translationNotes: מיכלא דמהימנותא / מיכלא דאסותא: the Zohar’s names for matza, food of faith and food of healing.

hayomYom.english: Even one who is, G‑d forbid, orphaned from his father, declares before beginning the ma nishtana, "tateh ich vell ba dir freggen feer kashess" ("Father, I am going to ask you four questions"). In a similar vein, even one whose mother and father are, G‑d forbid, no longer alive, nonetheless says in birkat hamazon (grace after meals) "May the Merciful One bless my father my teacher, etc., my mother my teacher, etc." (p. 93).
hayomYom.hebrew: גם מי שאין לו אב, ר"ל [רחמנא לצלן], אומר לפני מה נשתנה "טאטע איך וועל בא דיר פרעגען פיר קשיות", וסמוכות לזה, שגם מי שאין לו אב ואם, ר"ל [רחמנא לצלן], צ"ל [צריך לומר] בברכת המזון: הרחמן הוא יברך את אבי מורי כו' אמי מורתי כו'.
hayomYom.clear:
Even someone whose father is no longer alive, G‑d forbid, says before Ma Nishtana, “Tatte, ich vel ba dir fregn fir kashyes” [“Father, I will ask you four questions”].

There is support for this: even someone whose father and mother are no longer alive, G‑d forbid, says in Birkas HaMazon, “May the Merciful One bless my father, my teacher... my mother, my teacher...”
translationNotes: Matches the original. No meaning lost.

hayomYom.english: "Whoever expands on the narrative of the exodus from Egypt, this person (harei zeh) is to be praised" (Haggada). The Hebrew word zeh ("this") indicates a state of holiness, as in the phrase, "Here, this (zeh) is our G‑d" (p. 336). Whoever expands on the narrative of the exodus, his zeh, his element of holiness, is enriched.
hayomYom.hebrew: הרי זה משובח - זה, מורה על מדריגה דקדושה, הנה אלקינו זה - וכל המרבה כו' זה שלו הוא משובח.
hayomYom.clear: “Whoever tells more [about the Exodus], harei zeh, this one is praiseworthy.” The word zeh [“this”] points to a level of holiness, as in “Behold, this [zeh] is our G‑d” (Yeshaya 25:9). Whoever tells more: his zeh is praiseworthy.
translationNotes: משובח means both “praised” and “improved.” His own level of holiness becomes better. Kehot’s “enriched” captures the second sense.

hayomYom.english: Patach Eliyahu is said before Mincha, but not Hodu (p. 124/125). In 5608 (1848) the Tzemach Tzedek delivered a maamar on the verse "If you lend money..." The Hebrew word kessef ("money") connotes the soul, because the soul has a desire and longing (kossef) to rise to the heights. This is expressed in the passage, "It is the spirit of man which rises upward to the supernal heights." "Man" (adam in this verse) refers to the souls of Israel, as in the statement, "You (Israel) are called adam." The soul is "on loan" to man, and it is written "Days are formed", i.e. there is a fixed number of days that each man shall live, and if one day is missing - one garment is missing.
hayomYom.hebrew:
במנחה אין אומרים הודו, אבל אומרים פתח אלי'[הו].
שנת תר"ח אמר הצמח צדק מאמר על פסוק אם כסף תלוה גו', כסף הוא הנשמה, על שם שהיא תמיד בכוסף ותשוקה לעלות למעלה, וכדכתיב רוח האדם היא העולה למעלה, דאדם הם נש"י [נשמות ישראל], אתם קרוים אדם, והנשמה נתונה בהלואה להאדם, וכתיב ימים יוצרו גו', דיש מספר קבוע כו', וחסר יומא חדא חסר לבושא חדא.
hayomYom.clear:
In 5608 [1848] the Tzemach Tzedek said a maamar on the verse, “If you lend money” (Shemos 22:24).

Kesef [“money”] is the soul, because it always yearns, kosef, and longs to rise upward. As it is written, “The spirit of man, it rises upward” (Koheles 3:21). “Man” is the souls of Israel: “You are called adam [man]” (Yevamos 61a).

The soul is given to the person as a loan. And it is written, “Days were formed” (Tehillim 139:16): there is a fixed number of days. If one day is missing, one garment is missing.
translationNotes: כוסף: yearning, the root of כסף. The wordplay carries the teaching.
חסר לבושא חדא: each day of life weaves one garment for the soul.

calendar.original5703: At Mincha, Hodu is not said, but Pasach Eliyahu is said.

hayomYom.english: In L'cha dodi substitute besimcha, and say gam besimcha uv'tzahala (p. 132). The following prayers are to be said in an undertone this Shabbat: Shalom aleichem, Eishet chayil, Mizmor l'David, Da hi s'udata (pages 144-146). Also V'yitein l'cha (p. 235). My father once expanded on Ma nishtana (the "four questions" at the Seder): How is this night, i.e. this present, final exile of Israel (exile being analogous to night) different from all other nights, i.e. all earlier exiles? 1) On all other nights we do not dip (the Hebrew word matbilin is used for immersion in a mikva for purification), expressing scouring, cleansing, purifying... ...even once; i.e. the cleansing was not completed in the earlier exiles, for they were followed by yet another exile; but tonight we dip twice, this final exile will bring about the scouring of the body and the revelation of the soul. 2) On all other nights we eat chametz or matza. Following each of the earlier exiles our avoda involved our G‑dly soul (indicated by matza, a metaphor for nullification of self) and also our animal soul (indicated by chametz, a metaphor for ego, self-awareness); But this night, following this final exile... ...we eat only matza, for the spirit of impurity will be abolished. 3) On all other nights we eat various greens. The face of a jealous person turns green, that color symbolizing envy. During the earlier exiles there were various forms of envy; for example, the competitive envy among Torah-scholars; But on this night, after the final exile... ...only maror, bitter greens, the most intense sort of envy, similar to a statement in the Talmud that in the Hereafter "each tzadik will be scorched by the 'canopy' of his fellow." 4) On all other nights we eat either sitting or reclining... "Eating" indicates the spiritual delight, ta'anug, in the revelations that ensue from exile. There is the extension or manifest ta'anug, and there is (higher yet) the essence of ta'anug. Some through their avoda attain the extension of ta'anug, while others attain the essence of ta'anug. ...but tonight we all recline. After this final exile, all Israel will attain the quintessential ta'anug.
hayomYom.hebrew:
פעם פירש אאזמו"ר [אדוני אבי זקני מורי ורבי]: מה נשתנה הלילה - גלות שנמשל ללילה - הזה - האחרון - מכל הלילות - גליות שקדמוהו.

שבכל הלילות אין אנו מטבילין - לשון מרוק נקיון וטהרה - אפילו פעם אחת - לא נגמר המירוק בהם, כי הרי הי'[ה] אחריהם עוד גלות - הלילה הזה שתי פעמים - מירוק גוף וגילוי הנפש.

שבכל הלילות אנו אוכלים חמץ או מצה - היינו כי גם אחר הגלות, העבודה היא מצד נפש האלקית, מצה ביטול, ומצד נפה"ב [נפש הבהמית], חמץ ישות. - הלילה הזה - אחר גלות האחרון - כולו מצה - שיועבר רוח הטומאה.

שבכל הלילות אנו אוכלין שאר ירקות - כל המקנא פניו מוריקות, ובכל הגליות הרבה בחינות בקנאה: קנאת סופרים והדומה - הלילה הזה - אחר גלות האחרון - כולו מרור - קנאה היותר גדולה, על דרך מאמר רבותינו זכרונם לברכה כל צדיק נכוה מחופתו של חברו.

שבכל הלילות אנו אוכלין בין יושבין בין מסובין - כל הגילוים שעל ידי הגליות - אוכלין - בחינת התענוג, ויש התפשטות התענוג ותענוג העצמי ויש מי שמגיע בעבודתו להתפשטות התענוג ויש לתענוג העצמי - הלילה הזה - אחר גלות האחרון - כולנו מסובין - שכל ישראל יגיעו לבחינת תענוג העצמי.
hayomYom.clear:
My grandfather [the Rebbe Maharash] once explained Ma Nishtana:

“Why is this night,” the exile, which is compared to night, “this” last one, “different from all the nights,” the exiles before it?

1. “On all other nights we do not dip,” a term for scouring, cleaning and purifying, “even once”: the scouring was not finished in them, since another exile came after them. “This night, twice”: the scouring of the body and the revealing of the soul.

2. “On all other nights we eat chametz or matza”: even after those exiles, avoda came from the G‑dly soul, matza, which is bittul, and also from the animal soul, chametz, which is ego. “This night,” after the last exile, “only matza”: the spirit of impurity will be removed.

3. “On all other nights we eat other vegetables”: whoever is jealous, his face turns green. In all the exiles there were many kinds of jealousy, like the jealousy among scholars and the like. “This night,” after the last exile, “only maror”: the greatest jealousy, like the Sages’ saying, “Each tzaddik is burned by the canopy of his fellow.”

4. “On all other nights we eat sitting or reclining”: all the revelations that come through the exiles. “Eating” is ta’anug [delight]. There is the outward spread of delight, and there is the essential delight. Some reach the spread of delight through their avoda, and some reach the essential delight. “This night,” after the last exile, “we all recline”: all of Israel will reach essential delight.
translationNotes: The Hebrew says אאזמו״ר (my grandfather, the Rebbe Maharash). Kehot says “my father.” Followed the Hebrew.
התפשטות התענוג / תענוג העצמי: delight as it spreads out into things versus delight in its essence.

calendar.original5703: In Lecha dodi say “besimcha” and “gam besimcha uvetzahala.” This Shabbos say quietly: Shalom aleichem, Eishes chayil, Mizmor leDovid, Da hi seudasa. Also Veyiten lecha.

hayomYom.dataFlag: Hebrew says אאזמו״ר (my grandfather), Kehot says “my father.” Translation follows the Hebrew; verify against a print edition.

hayomYom.english: One Pesach, Reb Chayim Avraham (the Alter Rebbe's son) went to his brother (the Mitteler Rebbe) to wish him gut yom-tov. Reb Chayim Avraham related on that occasion that the Alter Rebbe had said, "On Pesach one does not offer a guest food and drink, but the guest may help himself."
hayomYom.hebrew: פעם נכנס כבוד קדשת הר' חיים אברהם (בן רבינו הזקן) אל אדמו"ר האמצעי בחג הפסח לאמר גוט יום טוב. וסיפר אז - הר' חיים אברהם - שרבינו הזקן אמר: פסח דארף איינער דעם אנדערען ניט מכבד זיין באכילה ושתיה, אבער נעמען אליין מעג מען.
hayomYom.clear: One Pesach, R. Chaim Avraham (the Alter Rebbe’s son) came in to the Mitteler Rebbe to wish him Gut Yom Tov. He told then that the Alter Rebbe had said: On Pesach, one should not urge another person to eat and drink. But taking by yourself is allowed.
translationNotes: מכבד זיין באכילה ושתיה: to offer or press food on a guest. Because of kashrus stringencies, each person takes for himself.

hayomYom.english: It was the custom in Lubavitch to stay awake on the night of the Seventh of Pesach as well as on Shavuot and on Hosha'ana Raba. By the age of nine I did not go to sleep on the Seventh of Pesach. One should study Torah the whole night.
hayomYom.hebrew: אין ליובאוויטש פלעגט מען זיין אויף שביעי של פסח - אויך שבועות און הושענא רבה. אז איך בין אלט געווען ניין יאהר האב איך זיך שוין ניט געלייגט שלאפען שביעי של פסח - מ'דארף לערנען א גאנצע נאכט.
hayomYom.clear: In Lubavitch they used to stay up all night on Shvi’i shel Pesach, and also on Shavuos and Hoshana Rabba. By the time I was nine, I no longer went to sleep on Shvi’i shel Pesach. You need to learn the whole night.
translationNotes: מ׳דארף לערנען: “one must learn.” Staying up is for learning, not just for being awake.

hayomYom.english: By day we take care to follow this order: Make Kiddush, then daven Mincha, and after that eat the festive yom tov meal. The Baal Shem Tov used to eat three festival meals on Acharon Shel Pesach. The Baal Shem Tov called the (third) meal of this day Mashiach's s'uda (the "festival meal of Mashiach"). Acharon Shel Pesach is the day for Mashiach's s'uda because on this day the radiance of the light of Mashiach shines openly. In 5666 (1906) a new procedure was adopted for Pesach in the Yeshiva Tomchei T'mimim in Lubavitch: The students ate the Pesach meals all together, in the study hall. There were 310 students present seated at eighteen tables. My father the Rebbe ate the festive meal of Acharon Shel Pesach with the yeshiva students. He ordered that four cups of wine be given each student, and then declared, "this is Mashiach's s'uda."
hayomYom.hebrew:
ביום מהדרים: לקדש, אחר כך מתפללים תפלת המנחה, ואחר זה סעודת יום טוב.

הבעל שם טוב היה אוכל ג' סעודות באחרון של פסח.

סעודת אחרון של פסח היתה נקראת - אצל הבעל שם טוב - משיח'ס סעודה. אחרון של פסח איז משיח'ס סעודה, ווייל אחרון של פסח איז מאיר גילוי הארת המשיח.

בשנת תרס"ו התחיל הסדר, אשר תלמידי תומכי תמימים יאכלו יחד בחג הפסח בהיכל הלימוד. והיה אז ש"י תלמידים וח"י שלחנות. סעודת אחרון של פסח אכל אאמו"ר [אדוני אבי מורי ורבי] ביחד עם התלמידים, וציווה לתת לכל תלמיד ד' כוסות. ואמר אז: דאס איז סעודת משיח.
hayomYom.clear:
In the daytime, the preferred practice is: make Kiddush, then daven Mincha, and after that the Yom Tov meal.

The Baal Shem Tov ate three meals on Acharon shel Pesach.

The Baal Shem Tov called the meal of Acharon shel Pesach “Moshiach’s seuda.” Acharon shel Pesach is Moshiach’s seuda because on Acharon shel Pesach the revealed light of Moshiach shines.

In 5666 [1906] a new practice began: the students of Tomchei Temimim ate together on Pesach, in the study hall. There were 310 students and 18 tables. My father [the Rebbe Rashab] ate the meal of Acharon shel Pesach together with the students. He had each student given four cups. And he said then: This is Moshiach’s seuda.
translationNotes: מהדרים: the meticulous, preferred practice, not a strict obligation.

hayomYom.english: The presence of Mashiach is revealed on Acharon Shel Pesach, and this revelation has relevance to all Israel: Pesach is medaleg, "skipping over" (rather than orderly progress), and leil shimurim, the "protected night." In general the mood of Pesach is one of liberty. Then Pesach ends, and we find ourselves tumbling headlong into the outside world. This is where Mashiach's revealed presence comes into play - imbuing us with a powerful resoluteness that enables us to maintain ourselves in the world.
hayomYom.hebrew: עס איז פאראן דער ענין וואס אחרון של פסח איז דער גילוי פון משיח, וואס איז שייך לכל ישראל. פסח איז דאך דער מדלג און ליל שמורים, און בכלל הערט זיך חרות'דיק, און נאכדעם פאלט מען אריין אין וועלט, איז דאס איז דער גילוי פון משיח, דער תוקף וואס עס גיט אז מ'זאל קענען געהן אין וועלט.
hayomYom.clear:
There is this idea that Acharon shel Pesach is the revelation of Moshiach, and it belongs to all of Israel.

Pesach is “skipping over” and “the night of protection.” In general, you feel free. And afterward you fall into the world. So this is the revelation of Moshiach: the strength it gives you, so that you can go out into the world.
translationNotes: הערט זיך חרות׳דיק: you feel a sense of freedom.
אז מ׳זאל קענען געהן אין וועלט: “so you can go into the world.” Kehot’s “maintain ourselves” shifts the image.

hayomYom.english: It is customary not to recite the b'racha she'he'che'yanu during the days of the omer count. We all possess an element of "non-good." Why, the scapegoat (representing evil, banished to Azazeil) was actually a service in the Beit hamikdash! A physical created being inevitably has a negative element, but we must banish that evil to a "desolate land."
hayomYom.hebrew:
נוהגים שאין מברכים שהחיינו בימי ספירת העומר.

לא טוב האבען מיר אלע. שעיר לעזאזל איז געווען אן עבודה אין בית המקדש. ווי באלד א נברא איז דא לא טוב, דארף מען עס אוועקשיקען אין ארץ גזרה.
hayomYom.clear:
The custom is not to say Shehecheyanu during the days of Sefiras HaOmer.

We all have “not good.” The goat sent to Azazel was an avoda in the Beis HaMikdash. As soon as there is a created being, there is “not good.” You have to send it away to a “desolate land” (Vayikra 16:22).
translationNotes: לא טוב: “not good,” the same term as in the Baal Shem Tov’s saying. Not “evil.”

hayomYom.english: The individual's avoda must be commensurate with his character and innate qualities. There may be one who can drill pearls or polish gems but works at baking bread (the analogy in the realm of avoda may be easily understood). Though baking bread is a most necessary craft and occupation, this person is considered to have committed a "sin."
hayomYom.hebrew: העבודה היא בכל אדם לפי מהותו ומעלתו. מי שיש בידו לנקוב מרגליות או ללטוש אבנים טובות ועוסק בעבודת מלאכת אפית לחם, - ומובן דוגמת כ"ז [כל זה] בעבודה - הגם שהיא עבודה ומלאכה הנצרכת במאד, בכל זה לחטא יחשב לאיש ההוא.
hayomYom.clear: Each person’s avoda is according to who he is and his level.
