If someone is able to drill pearls or polish gems, and he works at baking bread (the parallel in avoda is clear), then even though it is work and a craft that is very much needed, it is still counted as a sin for that person.
translationNotes: לחטא יחשב: it is “counted as a sin,” strong language for wasted potential.

hayomYom.english: Bless Rosh Chodesh iyyar; say the entire Tehillim in the early morning. Day of farbrengen. Haftora: Halo kivnei kushi'im. From a sicha of my father: Chassidus demands that one "...wash his flesh (Hebrew, et b'ssaro) with water, and clothe himself in them (the priestly robes)." The intellectual element of Chassidus must thoroughly cleanse the flesh and rinse away the habits of the flesh. The habits are alluded to by the word et ("and") in the quoted verse, signifying "that which is incidental to the flesh," the habits developed by the body. Only then can one clothe himself in the "sacred garments." Pondering Chassidus, discussing Chassidus, and the practice of Chassidim to meditate before davening - these are "sacred garments," garments that were given from the heights of sanctity. But it is the person himself who must "wash his flesh with water..." The garments of the soul are given to the individual from On High. But washing away unwholesome "incidentals" that arise from bodily nature and making the body itself "flesh of sanctity," this is achieved solely by man's own efforts. This is what Chassidus demands; it is for this ideal that our great teacher (the Alter Rebbe) devoted himself totally and selflessly. He opened the channel of total devotion, sacrifice, for serving G‑d through prayer, to be bound up with the Essence of the En Sof, infinite G‑d. Chassidus places a chassid face to face with the Essence of the En Sof.
hayomYom.hebrew: משיחת אאמו"ר [אדוני אבי מורי ורבי]: חסידות מאנט אז ורחץ את בשרו במים ולבשם. ד.ה. [דאס הייסט] די השכלה פון חסידות מוז אויסוואשען דעם בשר, און אראפשוויינקען דעם את בשרו, את הטפל לבשרו, די אלע רגילות'ן, וועלכע בשר מאכט, און דאן קען מען ערשט אנטאן די בגדי קדש. מחשבת ודבýור חסידות והנהגתם של חסידים בהתבוננות קודם התפלה בגדי קדש הם, דאס איז בגדים וועלכע מען האט געגעבען מן הקדש, אבער דער ורחץ במים את בשרו דאס דארף מען אליין. לבושי הנפש דאס גיט מען מלמעלה, אבער אפוואשען דעם טפל וואס ווערט פון בשריות און דעם בשר אליין מאכען פאר א בשר קדש, דאס איז נאר בכח עצמו. און דאס מאנט חסידות, און אויף דעם האט רבינו הגדול געהאט מסירת נפש. ער האט געעפענט דעם צנור פון מס"נ [מסירת נפש] אויף עבודת ה' בתפלה, זיין צוגעבונדען צו עצמות א"ס [אין סוף], חסידות שטעלט אוועק א חסיד פנים אל פנים צו עצמות א"ס [אין סוף].
hayomYom.clear:
From a sicha of my father [the Rebbe Rashab]:

Chassidus demands “he shall wash his flesh in water and put them on” (Vayikra 16:4). That is: the intellect of Chassidus must wash out the flesh and rinse away es besaro, “with his flesh,” what is secondary to the flesh: all the habits the flesh creates. Only then can you put on the holy garments.

Thinking and speaking Chassidus, and the practice of chassidim to meditate before davening, are holy garments. These are garments given from holiness. But the “washing his flesh in water,” that you must do yourself.

The soul’s garments are given from Above. But washing away what is secondary, what comes from physicality, and making the flesh itself into holy flesh, is only through your own strength.

This is what Chassidus demands. And for this, our great Rebbe [the Alter Rebbe] had mesirus nefesh. He opened the channel of mesirus nefesh for serving G‑d in prayer, to be bound to the Essence of the Ein Sof. Chassidus places a chassid face to face with the Essence of the Ein Sof.
translationNotes: מאנט: “demands,” as in demanding payment. Chassidus makes a claim on you.
את הטפל לבשרו: the word את read as “what accompanies” the flesh, its habits.

calendar.original5703: Shabbos Mevarchim Iyar. Say the whole Tehillim early in the morning. A day of farbrengen. Haftorah: Halo kivnei Kushiyim.

hayomYom.english: The permissible, when done for one's pleasure, is completely evil, as the Alter Rebbe writes in Tanya, Chapter 7, for we are commanded, "sanctify yourself with what is permitted to you." One must introduce sanctity into those matters that are permissible so that they serve the purpose of enhancing one's Torah, mitzvot, fear-of-G‑d and good character traits.
hayomYom.hebrew: דברים המותרים אם עושה אותם להנאתו הם רע גמור כמ"ש [כמו שכתב] רבינו נ"ע [נשמתו עדן] [תניא פ"ז [פרק ז']]. לפי דקדש עצמך במותר לך. צריך להכניס קדושה בדברים המותרים שיהי'[ה] בהם תכלית של תורה ומצות יראת שמים ומדות טובות.
hayomYom.clear:
Permitted things, when you do them for your own pleasure, are complete evil, as the Alter Rebbe writes (Tanya, ch. 7). This is because of “Sanctify yourself in what is permitted to you” (Yevamos 20a).

You must bring holiness into permitted things, so that they have a purpose of Torah and mitzvos, yiras Shamayim and good character.
translationNotes: רע גמור: “complete evil,” stated bluntly in the original.

hayomYom.english: Chassidim asked the Alter Rebbe: "Which is the superior avoda, love of G‑d or love of Israel?" He replied: "Both love of G‑d and love of Israel are equally engraved in every Jew's neshama, ruach, and nefesh. Scripture is explicit: 'I have loved you, says the L-rd.' It follows that love of Israel is superior - for you love whom your beloved loves."
hayomYom.hebrew: החסידים שאלו את אדמו"ר הזקן: איזה עבודה נעלית יותר, אהבת ה' או אהבת ישראל. ויען: אהבת ה' ואהבת ישראל שתיהן כאחת חקוקות בנשמתו רוחו ונפשו של כל אחד מישראל. ומקרא מלא דיבר הכתוב אהבתי אתכם אמר ה', הרי דגדולה אהבת ישראל, דאוהב מה שהאהוב אוהב.
hayomYom.clear:
The chassidim asked the Alter Rebbe: Which avoda is higher, love of G‑d or love of Israel?

He answered: Love of G‑d and love of Israel are both engraved together in the neshama, ruach and nefesh of every Jew. And the verse says it outright: “I have loved you, says G‑d” (Malachi 1:2). So love of Israel is greater: you love what your beloved loves.
translationNotes: שתיהן כאחת: the two together, as one, engraved side by side.
מקרא מלא: an explicit verse, said outright.

hayomYom.english: The Introduction to "Likutei Torah On Three Parshiot" is the maamar which begins, "To understand the matter of the G‑dly soul; it is written, You shall not eat ...". This maamar was originally said by the Alter Rebbe to the Tzemach Tzedek. The Tzemach Tzedek repeated the maamar in the Alter Rebbe's presence, who then said to him, "Nu, and the flavoring?" The Tzemach Tzedek then wrote a transcript of the maamar with parenthetical notes. The Alter Rebbe reviewed and corrected the transcript and ordered that the parenthetical notes be entered as part of the body of the maamar text. At my father's suggestion this maamar was selected to serve as an introduction to the "Likutei Torah (On Three Parshiot," of the Rebbe Maharash).
hayomYom.hebrew: הקדמת הלקו"ת [הלקוטי תורה] על ג"פ [ג' פרשיות] "להבין ענין נה"א [נפש האלקית], הנה כתיב לא תאכלו" הוא מאמר שאמרו רבינו הזקן לפני הצ"צ [הצמח צדק], וחזרו הצ"צ [הצמח צדק] לפניו, ויאמר רבינו הזקן: נו, הטעמה? ויכתוב הצ"צ [הצמח צדק] הנחה עם הגהות במוקף. רבינו הגיה ההנחה, ויצוו להכניס ההגהות בפנים המאמר. ע"פ [על פי] הצעת אאמו"ר [אדוני אבי מורי ורבי] בחרו במאמר זה בתור הקדמה להלקו"ת [להלקוטי תורה].
hayomYom.clear:
The introduction to Likkutei Torah on Three Parshiyos, “To understand the G‑dly soul: it is written, ‘You shall not eat,’” is a maamar the Alter Rebbe said before the Tzemach Tzedek.

The Tzemach Tzedek repeated it before him. The Alter Rebbe said, “Nu, and the explanation?” So the Tzemach Tzedek wrote a transcript with notes in brackets. The Alter Rebbe corrected the transcript and ordered the notes to be put into the body of the maamar.

At my father’s [the Rebbe Rashab’s] suggestion, this maamar was chosen as the introduction to the Likkutei Torah.
translationNotes: הטעמה: making it understood, giving the reasons. Kehot’s “flavoring” is literal and unclear.
Kehot adds that this Likkutei Torah is “of the Rebbe Maharash.” The Hebrew does not say so. Left out.

hayomYom.english: The following farbrengens should take place in shul: The farbrengen of s'uda shlishit, of Shabbat m'varchim, and of holidays (such as Rosh Chodesh and festive days of anash) The farbrengen of melava malka should be held in the private homes of anash.
hayomYom.hebrew: ההתועדות דסעודה שלישית, שבת מברכים, ויומי דפגרא - בראשי חדשים ומועדי אנ"ש [אנשי שלומינו] - צריכים להתקיים בביהכ"נ [בבית הכנסת]. ההתוועדות דמלוה מלכה - אצל אנ"ש [אנשי שלומינו] שי' [שיחיו] בבתיהם הפרטים.
hayomYom.clear: The farbrengens of seuda shlishis, Shabbos Mevarchim and days of celebration, Rosh Chodesh and the festive days of anash [our chassidic community], should be held in shul. The farbrengen of melave malka should be held in the private homes of anash.
translationNotes: יומי דפגרא: “days off,” days of celebration.

hayomYom.english: At a farbrengen during the days of sefira (at some time in the years 5651-5653, 1891-1893) someone said to my father, "The Alter Rebbe's chassidim were always keeping count." My father took a great liking to the saying, and he commented: "That idea characterizes man's avoda. The hours must be 'counted hours,' then the days will be 'counted days.' When a day passes one should know what he has accomplished and what remains yet to be done... In general, one should always see to it that tomorrow should be much better than today."
hayomYom.hebrew: מען האט געזאגט אמאל פאר'ן טאטען - אין א פארבריינגען ספירה-צייט אין די יאהרען תרנ"א-נ"ג: דעם אלטען רבין'ס חסידים פלעגען אלעמאל ציילען. דער ווארט איז דעם טאטען זייער געפעלען געווארען. ואמר: אזוי איז דער ענין העבודה. די שעות דארפען זיין געציילטע, דאן זיינען די טעג געציילטע. אז עס גייט אוועק א טאג, דארף מען וויסען וואס מ'האט אויפגעטאן און וואס מ'דארף ווייטער טאן... בכלל דארף מען זעהן אז דער מארגען זאל זיין א סך שענער ווי דער היינט.
hayomYom.clear:
Once, at a farbrengen during Sefira in the years 5651 to 5653 [1891 to 1893], someone said to my father [the Rebbe Rashab]: “The Alter Rebbe’s chassidim were always counting.”

My father liked this saying very much, and said: That is what avoda is. The hours have to be counted hours. Then the days are counted days. When a day goes by, you have to know what you accomplished and what still has to be done...

In general, you have to see to it that tomorrow will be much better than today.
translationNotes: א סך שענער: “much nicer,” finer. Not just more productive.

hayomYom.english: My grandfather (the Rebbe Maharash) was born on this day in 5593 (1833). When he was seven years old he was once tested in his studies by his father, the Tzemach Tzedek. My grandfather did so well in the test that his teacher was enormously impressed. Unable to restrain himself he said to the Tzemach Tzedek, "Well, what do you say? Hasn't he done marvelously?" The Tzemach Tzedek responded: "What is there to be surprised about when tiferet-within-tiferet does well?"
hayomYom.hebrew:
יום הולדת את אאזמו"ר [אדוני אבי זקני מורי ורבי] - בשנת תקצ"ג.

צו זיבען יאהר האט עם אמאל דער צ"צ [צמח צדק] פארהערט. דער זיידע האט געמאכט אזוי גוט, אז זיין מלמד איז זייער נתפעל געווארען, האט זיך ניט געקענט איינהאלטען און געזאגט דעם צ"צ [צמח צדק]: הא, וואס זאגט איהר, ער מאכט גוט. דער צ"צ [צמח צדק] האט איהם געענטפערט: וואס איז די התפעלות, אז תפארת שבתפארת מאכט גוט.
hayomYom.clear:
The birthday of my grandfather [the Rebbe Maharash], in 5593 [1833].

When he was seven, the Tzemach Tzedek once tested him. He did so well that his melamed [teacher] was deeply impressed. He couldn’t hold himself back and said to the Tzemach Tzedek, “Well, what do you say? He does well!”

The Tzemach Tzedek answered him, “Why get excited when tiferes shebetiferes [beauty within beauty] does well?”
translationNotes: וואס איז די התפעלות: “what is there to get excited about,” said dryly.

hayomYom.english: One should not drink water before havdala. It is possible to utilize for G‑d's service, according to Torah, all behavior-traits. This includes those traits that are unwholesome, and even those that are evil, as their names and descriptions indicate. For example, the tzadik Rabbi Meshulam Zusya of Anipoli, of blessed memory, learned a number of methods of serving G‑d - from a thief: a) He works quietly without others knowing. b) He is ready to place himself in danger. c) The smallest detail is of great importance to him. d) He labors with great toil. e) Alacrity. f) He is confident and optimistic. g) If he did not succeed the first time, he tries again and again.
hayomYom.hebrew:
אין שותים מים קודם הבדלה.

כל המדות, אף גם המדות הלא טובות, או גם רעות על פי תוארם ושמותיהם, אפשר להשתמש בהם לעבודת ה' ע"פ [על פי] התורה. וכמו שהרה"צ [שהרב הצדיק] ר' משולם זוסיא זצ"ל [זכר צדיק לברכה] מהאניפאליא למד כמה דרכים בדרכי העבודה מגנב: א) הצנע לכת ב) מעמיד עצמו בסכנה ג) דבר היותר קטן חשוב כדבר גדול ד) עמל בטרחא גדולה ה) זריזות ו) בוטח ומקוה ז) אם לא הצליח בפעם הראשונה חוזר הרבה פעמים.
hayomYom.clear:
We do not drink water before Havdala.

All the traits, even ones that are not good, or even ones that are evil by their description and name, can be used for the service of G‑d according to Torah.

For example, the tzaddik R. Meshulam Zusya of Anipoli learned several ways of avoda from a thief:
1. He works quietly.
2. He puts himself in danger.
3. The smallest thing matters to him as much as a big one.
4. He works with great effort.
5. Speed.
6. He is confident and hopeful.
7. If he did not succeed the first time, he tries again many times.
translationNotes: הצנע לכת: discreetly, out of sight.
דבר היותר קטן חשוב כדבר גדול: the smallest thing is as important to him as a big thing.

hayomYom.english: It is a Jewish custom not to shave or cut a baby boy's hair until his third birthday. The first haircutting or opsherenish of a baby boy is a Jewish custom of great importance. The essence of the custom is the educational act of leaving (uncut) the peyot (sidelocks). From the day of the haircutting and leaving the peyot it is the custom to take particular care in accustoming the little boy to wear a tallit katan, to recite the early-morning b'rachot, the grace after meals (birkat hamazon p. 89) and the bedtime sh'ma (p. 118).
hayomYom.hebrew:
מנהג ישראל שלא לגלח ושלא לספר שערות ראש תינוק עד מלאת לו שלש שנים.

גזיזת השערות - אפשערענעש [של תינוק] - הוא דבר גדול במנהגי ישראל. ועיקרו הוא בהחינוך דהשארת פיאות הראש. ומיום הגזיזה והנחת פיאות הראש נהגו להדר להרגיל את התינוק בענין נשיאת ט"ק [טלית קטן] וברכות השחר וברהמ"ז [וברכת המזון] וק"ש [וקריאת שמע] שעל המטה.
hayomYom.clear:
It is a Jewish custom not to shave or cut a child’s hair until he turns three.

The haircutting, the upsherenish, is a great thing among Jewish customs. Its main point is the education of leaving the peyos.

From the day of the haircut and leaving the peyos, the custom is to take care to train the child in wearing a tallis katan, and in saying the morning blessings, Birkas HaMazon and the bedtime Shema.
translationNotes: Matches the original. No meaning lost.

hayomYom.english: The Alter Rebbe received the following teaching from the tzadik Reb Mordechai, who had heard it from the Baal Shem Tov: A soul may descend to this world and live seventy or eighty years, in order to do a Jew a material favor, and certainly a spiritual one.
hayomYom.hebrew: רבינו הזקן קבל מר'[בי] מרדכי הצדיק ששמע מהבעש"ט [מהבעל שם טוב]: עס קומט אראפ א נשמה אויף דער וועלט און לעבט אפ זיבעציג אכציג יאהר, צוליב טאן א אידען א טובה בגשמיות ובפרט אין רוחניות.
hayomYom.clear: The Alter Rebbe received this from R. Mordechai the tzaddik, who heard it from the Baal Shem Tov: A soul comes down to the world and lives seventy or eighty years just to do a Jew a favor in material things, and especially in spiritual things.
translationNotes: ובפרט: “and especially,” not Kehot’s “certainly.”
צוליב: “just for the sake of.” A whole life for one favor.

hayomYom.english: Our sages said: "One should not take leave of his friend other than with a parting word of Torah-law, a d'var halacha." Our forefathers, the saintly Rebbes, explained: The parting word should be the kind of Torah-teaching that transforms the listener into a mehaleich. "Progress," hiluch, means to rise from level to level, with one ascent after another. Such progression embodies the superiority of the human soul over the angels, for this ascent is greatest through an act of goodness - extending a favor to another, a material favor in general, a spiritual favor in particular.
hayomYom.hebrew: אמרז"ל [אמרו רבותינו זכרונם לברכה]: אל יפטר אדם מחברו אלא מתוך דבר הלכה, ופירשו הוד כ"ק [כבוד קדושת] אבותינו רבותינו הקדושים, אזא דבר תורה וואס מאכט איהם - דעם הערער - פאר א מהלך. ענין ההילוך הוא לעלות מדרגא לדרגא בעילוי אחר עילוי, מעלת הנשמות על מעלת המלאכים, דעלי'[ה] זו היא ביותר ע"י [על ידי] עבודה בפועל טוב, טאן א טובה א אידען בגשמיות בכלל וברוחניות בפרט.
hayomYom.clear:
The Sages said: “A person should not part from his friend except with a word of halacha” (Berachos 31a). Our holy fathers, our Rebbes, explained: such a word of Torah that makes him, the listener, into a mehalech [one who moves forward].

Moving forward means rising from level to level, one ascent after another. This is the advantage of souls over angels. And this ascent comes most of all through avoda in actual good deeds: doing a Jew a favor, in material things in general, and in spiritual things especially.
translationNotes: מהלך: one who walks, keeps progressing, as opposed to angels who “stand.”
עבודה בפועל טוב: actual good deeds. Kehot’s “act of goodness” is close.

hayomYom.english: When one enwraps himself with the tallit gadol (large tallit) it is unnecessary to cover his head and face down to his mouth; this is indicated in the laws of tzitzit in the siddur (p. 11). It is our custom, however, to cover the eyes with the upper part of the tallit. During the days of sefira it is customary to study tractate Sota, one page each day - in addition to one's regular study sessions.
hayomYom.hebrew:
בעטיפת ט"ג [טלית גדול] אין צריך לכסות ראשו עד פיו, וכמ"ש [וכמו שכתוב] בהלכות ציצית אשר בסידור. אבל נוהגין לכסות בחלקו העליון של הט"ג [הטלית גדול] גם העינים.

נוהגים ללמוד בימי הספירה מס' [מסכת] סוטה - נוסף על שיעורים הקבועים - דף ליום דף ליום.
hayomYom.clear:
When you wrap yourself in the tallis gadol [the large tallis], you do not need to cover your head down to your mouth, as written in the laws of tzitzis in the Siddur. But our custom is to cover the eyes too, with the upper part of the tallis.

During the days of Sefiras HaOmer, the custom is to study tractate Sotah, one page a day, in addition to your fixed study sessions.
translationNotes: The Hebrew says only "in the Siddur." The page number (p. 11) is Kehot's addition. Left out.
גם העינים: "the eyes too." The point is that the custom goes further than the minimum.

hayomYom.english: An emissary is one with his sender. This concept is similar to that of an angel acting as a Divine emissary, when he is actually called by G‑d's name. If this is so with an angel it is certainly true of the soul; in fact with the soul the quality of this oneness is of a higher order, as explained elsewhere. Now chassidim are emissaries of the Rebbe, the Alter Rebbe. So if the chassid actively discharges his mission, he is bound up with his Rebbe, bound up in his entire being - there walks a chassid, there eats a chassid, there sleeps a chassid.
hayomYom.hebrew:
א שליח איז דאך איין זאך מיט דעם משלח, - ע"ד [על דרך] המבואר בענין שהמלאך נקרא בשם ה' ממש כשהוא שליח מלמעלה, ומכל שכן נשמות, ומבואר שבנשמות הוא עוד במעלה יתרה. -

והנה חסידים זיינען שלוחים פון רבי'ן, פון אלטען רבýי'ן, איז אז מ'טוט, איז מען מקושר, איז דאמאלט איז ער אין אלץ מקושר: עס געהט א חסיד, עסט א חסיד, שלאפט א חסיד.
hayomYom.clear:
An emissary is one with the one who sent him. This is like what is explained about an angel: when it is sent from Above, it is actually called by G‑d's Name. All the more so with souls, and it is explained that with souls this oneness is of an even higher order.

Now, chassidim are emissaries of the Rebbe, of the Alter Rebbe. When you act [carry out the mission], you are connected. And then you are connected in everything: a chassid walks, a chassid eats, a chassid sleeps.
translationNotes: אז מ'טוט, איז מען מקושר: "when you act, you are connected." The bond depends on doing.
אין אלץ מקושר: connected "in everything," every ordinary act. Kehot's "entire being" is close.

hayomYom.english: Our teacher the Baal Shem Tov said: Every single thing one sees or hears is an instruction for his conduct in the service of G‑d. This is the idea of avoda, service, to comprehend and discern in all things a way in which to serve G‑d.
hayomYom.hebrew: מורנו הבעש"ט [הבעל שם טוב] אמר: כל דבר ודבר אשר האדם רואה או שומע, הוא הוראת הנהגה בעבודת השם. וזהו ענין העבודה, להבין ולהשכיל מכל דרך בעבודת השם.
hayomYom.clear:
Our teacher the Baal Shem Tov said: Every single thing you see or hear is a lesson in how to conduct yourself in serving G‑d.

This is what avoda [serving G‑d] means: to understand and learn, from everything, a way to serve G‑d.
translationNotes: הוראת הנהגה: a practical "instruction for conduct," not just a general idea.

hayomYom.english: It is our custom to dip the piece of bread (for hamotzi) into salt three times, not to sprinkle the salt on the bread. At the festive meal on the second day of Shavuot 5621 (1861), the Tzemach Tzedek related as follows: At the festive meal on the second day of Shavuot 5555 (1795) my grandfather (the Alter Rebbe) said: At the festive meal on the second day of Shavuot 5528 (1768) my saintly master and teacher (the Maggid of Mezritch) said: "You shall count for yourselves," us'fartem lachem. The word us'fartem, - you shall count - has the root of sapirut, - brilliance and brightness. Us'fartem lachem, your lachem, selves, must be bright. The Tzemach Tzedek continued his narrative: My grandfather (the Alter Rebbe) then leaned his head on his hands and sang the Niggun (melody) Of Four Stanzas with profound d'veikut. Afterward he raised his head and said in a questioning tone, "And with what does one brighten the lachem?" - and without a pause he continued in a tone of response, "with the seven complete weeks (more literally, "...seven...Sabbaths"), that is, through refining one's seven emotion-traits, each trait in turn to be sub-incorporated with all seven. The seven attributes themselves are to become 'seven Sabbaths,' Shabbat needing no refinement."
hayomYom.hebrew:
נהגינן להטביל פרוסת המוציא שלש פעמים במלח ולא לזרוק המלח על הפרוסה.

יום ב' דחה"ש [דחג השבועות] תרכ"א בסעודה סיפר הצ"צ [הצמח צדק]: יום ב' דחה"ש [דחג השבועות] תקנ"ה בסעודה אמר אאזמו"ר [אדוני אבי זקני מורי ורבי] [רבינו הזקן]: ביום ב' דחה"ש [דחג השבועות] תקכ"ח בסעודה אמר כ"ק [כבוד קדושת] מו"ר [מורי ורבי] [המגיד ממעזריטש] וספרתם לכם, וספרתם הוא מלשון ספירות ובהירות. וספרתם לכם, צריכים לעשות שיהי'[ה] הלכם בהיר. וישען כ"ק [כבוד קדושת] אאזמו"ר [אדוני אבי זקני מורי ורבי] על זרועות קדשו וישורר את הניגון של ד' בבות בדבקות גדולה. אח"כ [אחר כך] הגביה את ראשו הק' [הקדוש] ויאמר - בניגון של שאלה: ובמה מספרים את הלכם? ותוך כדי דיבור אמר - בניגון של תשובה: בשבע שבתות תמימות, בבירור שבע המדות, שכל מדה ומדה תהי'[ה] כלולה משבע, ושבע המדות עצמם יהיו שבע שבתות, דשבת אינה צריכה בירור.
hayomYom.clear:
Our custom is to dip the piece of bread for HaMotzi into salt three times, and not to sprinkle the salt on the bread.

On the second day of Shavuos 5621 [1861], at the meal, the Tzemach Tzedek related: On the second day of Shavuos 5555 [1795], at the meal, my grandfather [the Alter Rebbe] said: On the second day of Shavuos 5528 [1768], at the meal, my master and teacher [the Maggid of Mezritch] said:

"U'sefartem lachem, you shall count for yourselves" (Vayikra 23:15). U'sefartem comes from the word sapirus, brightness and radiance. U'sefartem lachem: you must make your lachem [your own self] bright.

My grandfather [the Alter Rebbe] then leaned on his holy arms and sang the Niggun of Four Stanzas with great d'veikus [deep attachment to G‑d]. Afterward he raised his holy head and asked, in the tune of a question: "And with what does one make the lachem bright?" And in the same breath he answered, in the tune of an answer: "With seven complete weeks [literally, seven complete Shabbosos]. By refining the seven middos [emotional traits], so that each trait includes all seven. And the seven traits themselves are to become 'seven Shabbosos,' since Shabbos needs no refining."
translationNotes: ספירות ובהירות: the root is "sapir" (sapphire), brilliance. "Sefirah" counting and shining are one word here.
בניגון של שאלה / בניגון של תשובה: the question and answer were sung in tunes, as in Talmud study.
ותוך כדי דיבור: "in the same breath," with no pause at all.

hayomYom.english: The following are the correct readings in the siddur: V'chain (sh'nei ch'tuvim), with a tsayreh vowel, not a patach. ("When two Biblical passages..."; Page 26). Chiyitani (miyyardi vor) with a kamatz vowel, not a patach. ("You have kept me alive"; Page 30). Zecher (rav tuv'cha), with a segol vowel, not a tsayreh. ("They will express the remembrance..."; Page 33). Mashlich karcho (k'fitim) with a patach vowel, not a kamatz. ("He hurls His ice like morsels..." Page 35). Umalchuto ve'emunato la'ad kayemet. ("...and His sovereignty and His truth abide forever." Page 48).
hayomYom.hebrew:
אומרים בתפלה: וכן - בצירי ולא בפתח - שני כתובים.

חייתני - בקמץ ולא בפתח - מירדי בור.

זכר - זיין בסגול ולא בצירי - רב טובך.

משליך קרחו - בפתח ולא בקמץ - כפתים.

ומלכותו ואמונתו לעד קימת.
hayomYom.clear:
In davening we say:

V'chein (shnei chesuvim): with a tzeirei, not a patach.

Chiyisani (miyordi vor): with a kamatz, not a patach.

Zecher (rav tuvcha): the zayin with a segol, not a tzeirei.

Mashlich karcho (ch'fitim): with a patach, not a kamatz.

U'malchuso ve'emunaso la'ad kayemes.
translationNotes: The page numbers and English glosses of each phrase are Kehot's additions. Not in the Hebrew.
זכר - זיין בסגול: the vowel note is specifically on the letter zayin.

hayomYom.english: The following are the correct readings in the siddur: Menu ma'amar with a kamatz vowel. K'yom...ne'emar, with a patach. ("to our supplication...and there it is said:" Page 62). Zachur (ki afar anachnu) with a m'lupam vowel. ("He is mindful that we are but dust...". Page 68). Un'tal'tani with the vowels patach, sh'va, patach. ("And a wind lifted me..."; Page 72). Ve'ahavatecha lo tassur, not al tassir. ("May Your love never depart..."; Page 107).
hayomYom.hebrew:
אומרים בתפלה: מנו מאמר - מ"ם שלישית קמוצה. כיום כו' נאמר - מם פתוחה.

זכור - במלאופם - כי עפר אנחנו.

ונטלתני - טי"ת פתוחה, למד בשבא, תיו דגושה פתוחה.

ואהבתך לא תסור - ולא אל תסיר -.
hayomYom.clear:
In davening we say:

Mnu ma'amar: the third mem with a kamatz. K'yom ... ne'emar: the mem with a patach.

Zachur (ki afar anachnu): with a melupam [shuruk].

U'n'tal'tani: the tes with a patach, the lamed with a sheva, the tav with a dagesh and a patach.

V'ahavas'cha lo sasur, not al tasir.
translationNotes: מ"ם שלישית קמוצה: the note is on the third mem. Kehot's "with a kamatz vowel" does not say which letter.
תיו דגושה: Kehot drops that the tav has a dagesh.

hayomYom.english: At Mincha, tachanun is said. The Alter Rebbe once said (during those years that he would say short maamarim): "Know what is above you." Know that everything "above" in the supernal sefirot and partzufim (Divine emanations and configurations), all derives "from you"; it all depends on man's service.
hayomYom.hebrew:
במנחה אומרים תחנון.

רבינו הזקן - באותם השנים שהי'[ה] אומר מאמרים קצרים - אמר: דע מה למעלה ממך, דע כי כל מה שיש למעלה בפרצופים וספירות העליונות, הכל הוא ממך, שתלוי בעבודת האדם.
hayomYom.clear:
The Alter Rebbe, in the years when he used to say short maamarim [Chassidic discourses], said:

"Know what is above you" (Avos 2:1). Know that everything that exists Above, in the supernal partzufim and sefiros [Divine configurations and emanations], all of it is "from you." It all depends on a person's avoda.
translationNotes: דע מה למעלה ממך is read as "know that what is Above is from you." Kehot keeps this.

calendar.original5703: At Mincha, tachanun is said.

hayomYom.english: The theme of Pesach Sheini is that it is never too late. It is always possible to put things right. Even if one was tamei (ritually impure), or one was far away, and even in a case of lachem, when this (impurity etc.) was deliberate - nonetheless he can correct it.
hayomYom.hebrew: פסח שני ענינו איז - עס איז ניטא קיין "פארפאלען", מען קען אלע מאל פאריכטען. אפילו מי שהי-ה טמא, מי שהי'[ה] בדרך רחוקה. אוýן אפילו "לכם", אז דאס איז געווען ברצונו, פונדעסטוועגען קען מען מתקן זיין.
hayomYom.clear:
What Pesach Sheni is about: nothing is ever lost for good. You can always set things right.

Even someone who was impure, even someone who was "on a distant road." And even "lachem" ["you yourselves"], when it was by his own choice: even so, he can fix it.
translationNotes: פארפאלען: "lost, gone for good." Stronger than Kehot's "too late."
לכם is from Bamidbar 9:10. It is read as hinting the person was far off deliberately, ברצונו.

hayomYom.english: In the days of the Alter Rebbe the Chassidim had a familiar saying: "The piece of bread that I have is yours just as it is mine." And they would say the word "yours" first, "...yours just as it is mine."
hayomYom.hebrew: בימי רבינו הזקן הי'[ה] שגור בפי החסידים הפתגם: דער שטיקעל ברויט וואס איך האב, איז ער דיינער ווי מיינער. והיו מקדימים מלת "דיינער" - דיינער ווי מיינער.
hayomYom.clear:
In the Alter Rebbe's time, chassidim had a saying always on their lips: "The piece of bread I have is yours as much as mine."

And they would say "yours" first: "yours as much as mine."
translationNotes: שגור בפי: a saying "constantly on their lips," not just familiar.

hayomYom.english: After my father pared his nails, he would place a small piece of wood among them before burning them. In terms of scholarship and aptitude the Chassid Reb Elyeh Abeler was a simple man. Once, when he came into yechidus, my grandfather said to him: "Elyeh, I envy you. You travel to various fairs, you meet many people. Sometimes, in the middle of a business transaction, you get into a warm discussion about a Jewish saying, a saying from the Ein Yakov etc., and you arouse the other fellow's interest in studying nigleh (Talmud, halacha etc.) and Chassidus. This causes joy On High, and the A-lmighty rewards such "trade" with the blessings of children, health and sustenance; the larger the fair the more work there is and the greater is the livelihood earned."
hayomYom.hebrew:
אאמו"ר [אדוני אבי מורי ורבי] כשהי'[ה] נוטל צפרניו, הי'[ה] מערב עמהם קיסם, קודם השריפה.

אאזמו"ר [אדוני אבי זקני מורי ורבי] אמר להחסיד ר' אלי' אבעלער - איש פשוט מצד כשרונותיו וידיעותיו - כשנכנס אליו ליחידות: אלי' איך בין דיר מקנא. פאהרסט אויף מערק זעהסט א סך מענשען, איז ווען אינמיטען עסק רעדט מען זיך מיט יענעם פאנאנדער אין א אידישען ווארט א עין יעקב ווארט, און מ'איז מעורר אויף לערנען נגלה און חסידות, פון דעם ווערט שמחה למעלה. און די מעקלעריי צאהלט דער אויבערשטער אפ בבני חיי ומזוני. און וואס גרעסער דער מארק מעהר ארבעט, איז גרעסער די פרנסה.
hayomYom.clear:
My father [the Rebbe Rashab], when he cut his nails, would mix a splinter of wood in with them before burning them.

The chassid R. Elya Abeler was a simple man in his abilities and knowledge. Once, when he came in for yechidus [a private meeting], my grandfather [the Rebbe Maharash] said to him:

"Elya, I envy you. You travel to the fairs and see lots of people. In the middle of business you get into a conversation with someone about a Jewish teaching, a saying from Ein Yaakov, and you inspire him to study nigleh [revealed Torah: Talmud and halacha] and Chassidus. This makes joy Above. And G‑d pays you for this 'brokering' with children, life and sustenance. And the bigger the fair, the more work, and the bigger the livelihood."
translationNotes: מעקלעריי: "brokerage," the broker's fee. G‑d pays him a commission for the deal he brokered.
בבני חיי ומזוני: "children, life and sustenance." Kehot's "health" softens חיי, life itself.
קיסם: a small splinter of wood.

hayomYom.english: Tzidkat'cha (p. 209) is not said. Some recite the sh'ma in the morning, before services, to fulfill their obligation of reciting the sh'ma in its proper time; they should repeat (as usual in a non-communal sh'ma reading) the three words ani Hashem Elokeichem (p. 48), and conclude with the word emet. When reciting the sh'ma with the tefillin of Rabeinu Tam or Shimusha Raba, the three words are not repeated, but one does conclude with emet. On Lag Ba'Omer, about 5604 (1844), the Tzemach Tzedek related this teaching of the Baal Shem Tov: It is written, "For you (Israel) shall be a land of desire, says the L-rd of Hosts". Just as the greatest scientists will never discover the limits of the enormous natural resources which the A-lmighty has sunk into the land ("everything came from the earth"), neither will anyone ever find the limits of the great treasures which lie within Israel - G‑d's "land of desire." The Baal Shem Tov concluded: I want to make Israel yield the kind of produce which the A-lmighty's "land of desire" is capable of yielding.
hayomYom.hebrew:
א"א [אין אומרים] צדקתך.

בק"ש [בקריאת שמע] שיש אומרים בבוקר - קודם התפלה - כדי לצאת חובת ק"ש [קריאת שמע] בזמנה, ג"כ [גם כן] כופלים ג' התיבות, ומסיימים בתיבת "אמת". בק"ש [בקריאת שמע] דתפילין דר"ת [דרבינו תם] ושמ"ר [ושמושא רבה] אין כופלים, אבל אומרים "אמת".

ל"ג בעומר שנת תר"ד - לערך - סיפר הצ"צ [הצמח צדק] תורת הבעש"ט [הבעל שם טוב]: עס שטעהט כי תהיו אתם ארץ חפץ אמר ה' צבאות. אט אזוי ווי די גרעסטע חכמים וועלען אייביג ניט דערגיין די גרויסע, טבעיות'דיגע אוצרות, וועלכע השי"ת [השם יתברך] האט טובע געווען בארץ, אז הכל הי'[ה] מן העפר, אט אזוי קען קיינער ניט דערגיין די גרויסע אוצרות וואס ליגען אין אידען, וואס זיי זיינען דעם אויבערשטענס ב"ה [ברוך הוא] ארץ חפץ. וסיים הבעש"ט [הבעל שם טוב]: איך וויל מאכען פון אידען, אז זיי זאלען געבען דעם יבול, וואס דעם אויבערשטענס ב"ה [ברוך הוא] א ארץ חפץ קען געבען.
hayomYom.clear:
In the Shema that some say in the morning before davening, to fulfill the mitzva of saying Shema at its proper time: here too you repeat the three words [Ani Hashem Elokeichem], and finish with the word "emes." In the Shema said with the tefillin of Rabbeinu Tam and of Shimusha Rabba, you do not repeat them, but you do say "emes."

On Lag BaOmer of about 5604 [1844], the Tzemach Tzedek related a teaching of the Baal Shem Tov:

It is written, "For you shall be a land of desire, says G‑d of Hosts" (Malachi 3:12). The greatest scientists will never reach the end of the great natural treasures that G‑d sank into the earth, for "all came from the earth" (Koheles 3:20). In the same way, no one can ever reach the end of the great treasures that lie within Jews, who are G‑d's "land of desire."

The Baal Shem Tov concluded: I want to make Jews yield the produce that G‑d's "land of desire" can yield.
translationNotes: דערגיין: "get to the bottom of," reach the end of. Same verb for the earth's treasures and the Jew's.
יבול is produce of the land, continuing the metaphor.

calendar.original5703: Tzidkas'cha is not said.

hayomYom.english: Lag Ba'Omer was one of the Mitteler Rebbe's particularly noteworthy festivals. He and the Chassidim would go out to the fields that day, and although he did not wash and break bread, he did partake of mashkeh (strong drink), which he was not allowed to do for health reasons. Many wonders were seen at that time, most of them involving the blessing of children for childless couples - and all year long people waited for Lag Ba'Omer.
hayomYom.hebrew:
אצל אדמו"ר [אדוננו מורנו ורבינו] האמצעי הי'[ה] לג בעומר מיו"ט [מימים טובים] המצויינים. מען פלעגט ארויסגעהן אויפ'ן פעלד, ער פלעגט זיך ניט וואשען, אבער נעהמען משקה, וואס מצד הבריאות האט ער עס ניט געטארט. מען האט דעמאלט געזעהן א סך מופתים. דאס רוב מופתים איז געווען בנוגע קינדער. און א גאנץ יאהר האט מען געווארט אויף לג בעומר.

.
hayomYom.clear:
For the Mitteler Rebbe, Lag BaOmer was one of the outstanding festive days. They would go out to the field. He would not wash [for bread], but he would take mashke [strong drink], which, for health reasons, he was not allowed to do.

Many wonders were seen then. Most of the wonders had to do with children. And all year long, people waited for Lag BaOmer.
translationNotes: מיו"ט המצויינים: one of the "outstanding" festive days.
בנוגע קינדער: "regarding children." Kehot's "for childless couples" is a fair reading but narrower than the original.

hayomYom.english: Chassidus is Divine intelligence, an understanding which shows man how small he is, and how great he can become.
hayomYom.hebrew:
חסידות איז א ג-טליכער פארשטאנד, דער פארשטאנד וואס ווייזט דעם מענטשן ווי קליין ער איז, און ווי גרויס ער קען זיך דערהויבן.

.
hayomYom.clear: Chassidus is a G‑dly understanding. It is the understanding that shows a person how small he is, and how high he can raise himself.
translationNotes: זיך דערהויבן: "raise himself up." It is his own effort, not only "become."

hayomYom.english: There is no one for whom to pride oneself. We must toil strenuously. With patience and friendliness we can prevail in all things, with G‑d's help. With a denigrating attitude toward others and inflating our own importance we lose everything, G‑d forbid.
hayomYom.hebrew: ניטא בא וועמען איבערנעמען זיך. מען בעדארף הארעווען, מיט סבלנות און קירוב הדעת קען מען, בעזה"י [בעזרת השם יתברך], אלס דורכזעצען, מיט ביטול הזולת והגבהת עצמו ווערט מען חלילה אלץ אן.
hayomYom.clear:
There is no one to be haughty over. You have to work hard.

With patience and warmth toward others, with G‑d's help, you can push everything through. By belittling others and puffing yourself up, you lose everything, G‑d forbid.
translationNotes: הארעווען: hard, grinding labor, stronger than "toil."
קירוב הדעת: closeness and warmth toward people. "Friendliness" is close.
דורכזעצען: "push through," accomplish in spite of resistance.

hayomYom.english: Every person must know that G‑d, through His individual Providence, gives each person the ability to bring G‑d's supernal Will from the potential state to the actual. This is done through fulfilling the mitzvot and strengthening Judaism and our holy Torah at all times in every place. All depends solely upon one's avoda.
hayomYom.hebrew: על כל אחד ואחד לדעת, כי הוא ית' [יתברך] בהשגחתו הפרטית נותן לכל אדם האפשרות להביא רצון העליון ית' [יתברך] מן הכח אל הפועל, בקיום המצות ובחיזוק היהדות ותורתנו הקדושה בכל עת ובכל מקום שהוא, ואין הדבר תלוי אלא בעבודתו.
hayomYom.clear:
Each and every person must know: G‑d, by His individual Providence, gives every person the ability to bring the supreme Will of G‑d from potential into actual. This is done by keeping the mitzvos and by strengthening Yiddishkeit and our holy Torah, at every time and in every place you are.

And it depends only on your avoda.
translationNotes: אין הדבר תלוי אלא בעבודתו: "it depends only on his own avoda." Kehot's "one's avoda" is right.

hayomYom.english: Several of the early chassidim had a farbrengen sometime between 5544-47 (1784-87) and the core of the discussion was this: The Rebbe (the Alter Rebbe) had accomplished something novel - that we are not alone. At one time, the Master - Rosh Yeshiva or Talmudic sage - was "alone" and his disciples were "alone." The chassidic way instituted by the Rebbe is a tremendous Divine achievement, that the Rebbe is not alone, nor are the chassidim alone.
hayomYom.hebrew: פעם אחת התוועדו חסידים הראשונים - בשנת תקמ"ד-ז - ותוכן שיחתם הי'[ה]: דער רבי - רבינו הזקן - האט אויפגעטאן וואס מען איז ניט עלענט. אמאל, איז דער רבי - דער ר"מ [ראש מתיבתא] און גאון - געווען עלענט, און די תלמידים זיינען געווען עלענט. דער דרך החסידות וואס דער רבי האט מייסד געווען איז דער גרויסער ג-טליכער אויפטו, וואס דער רבי איז ניט עלענט און חסידים זיינען ניט עלענט.
hayomYom.clear:
Once, in the years 5544 to 5547 [1784 to 1787], the early chassidim held a farbrengen [Chassidic gathering]. The gist of their talk was:

The Rebbe, the Alter Rebbe, accomplished that we are not alone. In the past, the Rebbe, the Rosh Yeshiva and Gaon, was alone, and the students were alone.

The path of Chassidus that the Rebbe founded is the great G‑dly achievement: the Rebbe is not alone, and chassidim are not alone.
translationNotes: עלענט: Yiddish for "alone" and "lonely." Both senses are meant: isolated, without real bond.

hayomYom.english: The beginning of one's decline, G‑d save us, is the lack of avoda in davening. Everything becomes dry and cold. Even a mitzva performed by habit becomes burdensome. Everything is rushed. One loses the sense of pleasure in Torah-study. The atmosphere itself becomes crass. Needless to say, one is totally incapable of influencing others.
hayomYom.hebrew: ראשית הירידה, ר"ל [רחמנא לצלן], הוא העדר העבודה בתפלה, עס ווערט אלץ טרוקען און קאלט, די מצות אנשים מלוýמדה ווערט שוין אויך שווער, מען איילט, מען ווערט אן דעם געשמאק אין תורה, והאויר מתגשם, ומובן הדבר שאינו שייך כלל לפעול על הזולת.
hayomYom.clear:
The start of the decline, G‑d spare us, is the lack of avoda in davening.

Everything turns dry and cold. Even a mitzva done by rote becomes hard. You rush. You lose the taste in Torah. The air itself turns coarse. And clearly, you are in no position at all to influence anyone else.
translationNotes: מצות אנשים מלומדה (Yeshaya 29:13): a mitzva done out of rote habit.
געשמאק: "taste," delight. Kehot's "pleasure" is close.

hayomYom.english:
Bless Rosh Chodesh Sivan; say the entire Tehillim in the early morning.
Day of farbrengen.

"If you go in My statutes." Our Sages interpret the word "if" as a plea, in the sense of "if only you would go in My statutes." G‑d's pleading (as it were) with Israel to keep the Torah, in itself aids man and gives him the ability to remain steadfast in his choice of the good. Moreover, "...you go in My statutes" - the soul then becomes a mehaleich, it progresses. * * * With the advent of Mashiach, there will be revealed the superior quality of the traits of simplicity and wholeheartedness found in the avoda of simple folk who daven and recite Tehillim with simple sincerity.
hayomYom.hebrew:
אם בחוקותי תלכו, אם זה הוא לשון תחנונים כמרז"ל [כמאמר רבותינו זכרונם לברכה], שכוונתו הלואי בחוקותי תלכו. וזה שהקב"ה [שהקדוש ברוך הוא] כביכול, מתחנן לפניהם שישמרו את התורה, זה עצמו מסייע ונותן כח לאדם שיעמוד בבחירתו הטובה. ועוד זאת אשר בחוקותי תלכו דנעשית הנשמה מהלך.

------------------------

בביאת המשיח תתגלה מעלת הפשיטות והתמימות שיש בעבודתם של אנשים פשוטים שמתפללים ואומרים תהלים בתמימות.
hayomYom.clear:
"If you walk in My statutes" (Vayikra 26:3). "If" here is a word of pleading, as our Sages say (Avoda Zara 5a). It means: if only you would walk in My statutes!

And the very fact that G‑d, so to speak, pleads with them to keep the Torah, itself helps a person and gives him strength to hold firm in choosing good.

And further: "you walk in My statutes" means the soul becomes a mehalech, one who walks and moves forward.

The coming of Mashiach will reveal the special quality of the simplicity and wholeheartedness in the avoda of simple people, who daven and say Tehillim with simple sincerity.
translationNotes: מהלך: "one who walks," moving forward.
פשיטות והתמימות: simplicity and wholeheartedness, two distinct qualities.

hayomYom.english: Among the Alter Rebbe's maamarim of 5555 (1795) in Lyozna: "The reward of a mitzva is the mitzva." The mitzva in its ultimate essence - state is the reward. The revelation of this essence will take place in the Time to Come. This is the "enduring principal of the mitzva." However, man also "eats of its fruits in This World," each mitzva according to its particular nature; i.e. when man has that particular need, he is answered.
hayomYom.hebrew: ממאמרי רבינו הזקן בשנת תקנ"ה בליאזנא: שכר מצוה מצוה, המצוה בעצם עצמותה היא השכר והתגלות העצמות תהי'[ה] לעתיד, אבל זהו הקרן קיימת של המצוה, אמנם פירותי'[ה] אדם אוכל בעולם הזה, והוא בכל מצוה ומצוה בענינה, דכאשר צריך לאותו דבר הוא נענה.
hayomYom.clear:
From the Alter Rebbe's maamarim of 5555 [1795] in Liozna:

"The reward of a mitzva is the mitzva" (Avos 4:2). The mitzva in its very essence is the reward, and the revelation of that essence will come in the Time to Come. This is the lasting principal of the mitzva.

But a person also eats its fruits in this world (Pe'ah 1:1). This is in every mitzva according to its own nature: when you need that particular thing, you are answered.
translationNotes: הקרן קיימת: "the principal remains," the mishna's language (Pe'ah 1:1) for the lasting essence.

hayomYom.english: The command "You shall rebuke" is preceded by the words "You shall not hate your brother," for this is a precondition for the rebuke. The Torah continues, "...and you shall not ascribe sin to him," for if the rebuke was ineffectual, you are certainly the one responsible, for yours were not words coming from the heart.
hayomYom.hebrew: קודם ציווי הוכח תוכיח, כתיב ולא תשנא את אחיך, כי זהו תנאי מוקדם להוכחה. ואח"ז [ואחר זה] כתיב ולא תשא עליו חטא, שאם לא פעלה ההוכחה, בודאי אתה האשם, שלא היו דברים היוצאים מן הלב.
hayomYom.clear:
Before the command "You shall surely rebuke" (Vayikra 19:17), it is written, "You shall not hate your brother," because that is a precondition for rebuke.

And after it is written, "and you shall not bear sin on his account." Because if the rebuke did not work, you are surely the one at fault: your words did not come from the heart.
translationNotes: ולא תשא עליו חטא: read here as "do not lay the sin on him." The failure is yours.
דברים היוצאים מן הלב: echoes "words from the heart enter the heart."

hayomYom.english: My father related that he heard from his father quoting his father (the Tzemach Tzedek), who heard the Alter Rebbe refer to himself as the son of the Maggid (his Rebbe), and as the grandson of the Baal Shem Tov.
hayomYom.hebrew: אאמו"ר [אדוני אבי מורי ורבי] סיפר ששמע מאביו בשם הצ"צ [הצמח צדק] ששמע מרבינו הזקן שהי'[ה] קורא את עצמו בשם בן להרב המגיד ובשם נכד להבעש"ט [להבעל שם טוב].
hayomYom.clear: My father [the Rebbe Rashab] related that he heard from his father [the Rebbe Maharash], in the name of the Tzemach Tzedek, who heard it from the Alter Rebbe: The Alter Rebbe would call himself a son of the Maggid and a grandson of the Baal Shem Tov.
translationNotes: Matches the original. No meaning lost.

hayomYom.english: In one of the nocturnal visions in which the Tzemach Tzedek saw the Alter Rebbe (his grandfather), during the Thirty Days of Mourning for the Alter Rebbe, the latter recited for him the maamar, Al shlosha dvarim. After the maamar the Alter Rebbe said, "If the man emits seed first, she bears a female" - that is your mother; "if the woman emits seed first, she bears a male" - that is you.
hayomYom.hebrew: באחד החזיונות לילה שראה הצ"צ [הצמח צדק] את רבינו הזקן, בתוך שלשים להסתלקותו, אמר לפניו המאמר על שלשה דברים העולם עומד. אחרי המאמר א"ל [אמר לו]: איש מזריע תחלה יולדת נקבה - זהו אמך. אשה מזרעת תחלה יולדת זכר - זהו אתה.
hayomYom.clear:
In one of the night visions in which the Tzemach Tzedek saw the Alter Rebbe, within thirty days of his passing, the Alter Rebbe said the maamar "Al shelosha devarim ha'olam omed" ["The world stands on three things"] (Avos 1:2) before him.

After the maamar, he said to him: "'If the man emits seed first, she bears a female' (Niddah 31a): that is your mother. 'If the woman emits seed first, she bears a male': that is you."
translationNotes: The Hebrew gives the full name of the maamar, על שלשה דברים העולם עומד. Kehot shortens it.

hayomYom.english: The ascent of the soul occurs three times daily, during the three times of davening. This is particularly true of the souls of tzadikim who "go from strength to strength." It is certain that at all times and in every sacred place they may be, they offer invocation and prayer on behalf of those who are bound to them and to their instructions, and who observe their instructions. They offer prayer in particular for their disciples and disciples' disciples, that G‑d be their aid, materially and spiritually.
hayomYom.hebrew: עלית הנשמה היא שלש פעמים בכל יום בהג' תפלות, ובפרט נשמת הצדיקים דילכו מחיל אל חיל, ודבר ודאי, אשר בכל עת ובכל מקום קדוש היותם, נושאים רנה ותפלה בעד המקושרים אליהם ואל פקודתם ושומרים פקודיהם, ובפרט בעד תלמידיהם ותלמידי תלמידיהם, להושע בגשמיות וברוחניות.
hayomYom.clear:
The soul ascends three times every day, during the three prayers. This is especially so for the souls of tzaddikim, who "go from strength to strength" (Tehillim 84:8).

It is certain that at every time, and in every holy place where they are, they raise up song and prayer on behalf of those who are bound to them and to their instructions and who keep their instructions. Especially for their students and their students' students: that they be helped, materially and spiritually.
translationNotes: נושאים רנה ותפלה: "raise song and prayer," joyful as well as pleading.
המקושרים אליהם ואל פקודתם: bound both to the tzaddik and to his directives.

hayomYom.english: "Throw a stick into the air; it will fall back on ikrei, its root-side." Our fathers, the holy Rebbes, bequeathed a boundless heritage to the first chassidim, that their sons' children and their daughters' children throughout the generations, in whatever country and environment they may be, will have that "root" - which is the attraction of their "inwardness of heart" to the rock from which they were hewn. At times this element is covered and concealed in a number of garbs. This, then, is the avoda of whoever desires life - to remove these coverings, to establish for himself periods for the study of Chassidus, and to conduct himself in the manner of the Chassidic community.
hayomYom.hebrew:
עד י"ב בחדש - ועד בכלל - א"א [אין אומרים] תחנון.

זרוק חוטרא לאוירא אעיקרי'[ה] קאי. נחלה בלי מצרים הנחילו אבותינו רבותינו הקדושים לכבוד חסידים הראשונים, אשר בני בניהם ובני בנותיהם לדורותיהם, באיזה מדינה וסביבה שיהיו, יהי'[ה] אצלם אותו ה"עיקרי'[ה]", והוא המשכת פנימיות הלב אל צור מחצבתו. לפעמים העיקרי'[ה] מכוסה ונעלם בכמה לבושים, וזאת היא עבודת החפץ בחיים להסיר את הכיסוים ולקבוע לו זמני למוד בתורת החסידות ולנהוג במנהגי עדת החסידים.
hayomYom.clear:
"Throw a stick into the air, it lands on its root."

Our fathers, our holy Rebbes, left the early chassidim an inheritance without limits: that their sons' sons and daughters' sons, for all generations, in whatever country and surroundings they may be, will have that "root." That root is the pull of the innermost heart toward the rock from which it was hewn.

Sometimes the root is covered and hidden under many layers. So this is the avoda of anyone who wants life: to remove the coverings, to set himself fixed times for studying Chassidus, and to follow the customs of the chassidic community.
translationNotes: נחלה בלי מצרים: "an inheritance without boundaries," a phrase from Shabbos 118a about Yaakov.
החפץ בחיים (Tehillim 34:13): "whoever desires life."

calendar.original5703: Until the 12th of the month, inclusive, tachanun is not said.

hayomYom.english: Ana B'choach at Kabalat Shabbat (p. 131) is said in an undertone. Ufros aleinu... at Kabalat Shabbat (p. 138) is said standing. In the year 5589 (1829) the Shabbat of Parshat Bamidbar was on 5 Sivan. Before the kindling of the Shabbat candles, the Tzemach Tzedek delivered the maamar, S'u et rosh...avotam. Following the commentary of Ibn Ezra, he interpreted the word S'u in the sense of elevation, as in "Ki tisa et rosh," (lit. "When you take up the head.") The implication is that through avoda of the radiance of the soul within the body, an elevation is effected in the head (rosh) and essence of the soul as it is Above. In this vein he then explained a number of Torah-verses and statements in Zohar and Midrash. At noon on Shabbat the Rebbe delivered the maamar V'eirastich and its elaboration as printed in Likutei Torah. The next day, the first day of Shavuot, he delivered the maamar Us'fartem and its elaboration as printed in Likutei Torah. During the festival meal of the second day of Shavuot, the Rebbe delivered the maamar V'hachachma mei'ayin timatzei which is the second elaboration on the subject of tisp'ru chamishim yom printed in Likutei Torah.
hayomYom.hebrew:
א"א [אין אומרים] צדקתך.

אנא בכח - דקבלת שבת - אומרים בלחש.

ופרוש עלינו כו' - בקבלת שבת - בעמידה.

בשנת תקפ"ט חל ש"פ [שבת פרשת] במדבר ה' בסיון. קודם הדלקת נרות של שבת אמר הצ"צ [הצמח צדק] מאמר שאו את ראש גו' אבותם. פי' [פירוש] שאו כפירוש הראב"ע [הרב אברהם בן עזרא] מענין כי תשא את ראש. וביאור הענין שע"י [שעל ידי] עבודת הארת הנשמה שבגוף, נעשה עלי'[ה] בראש ועצם הנשמה כמו שהיא למעלה והסביר כמה פסוקים ומאמרי זהר ומדרש. בשבת בצהרים אמר רבינו הדרוש וארשתיך לי לעולם וביאורו שנדפסו בלקו"ת [בליקוטי תורה]. ביום א דחה"ש [דחג השבועות] אמר רבינו את הדרוש וספרתם לכם וביאורו - שנדפסו בלקו"ת [בליקוטי תורה] ביום השני דחה"ש [דחג השבועות] בסעודת יו"ט [יום טוב] אמר רבינו את הדרוש והחכמה מאין תמצא, והוא ביאור השני בענין תספרו חמשים יום הנדפס בלקו"ת [בליקוטי תורה].
hayomYom.clear:
Ana B'choach in Kabbalas Shabbos is said quietly.

U'fros aleinu in Kabbalas Shabbos is said standing.

In 5589 [1829], Shabbos Parshas Bamidbar fell on the 5th of Sivan. Before candle lighting for Shabbos, the Tzemach Tzedek said the maamar "Se'u es rosh ... avosam." He explained "se'u" following Ibn Ezra, in the sense of "Ki sisa es rosh" ["when you lift up the head"]. The idea: through the avoda of the soul's light that is in the body, the head and essence of the soul, as it is Above, is lifted up. He explained several verses and statements of the Zohar and Midrash this way.

On Shabbos at midday, the Rebbe [the Tzemach Tzedek] said the discourse "V'eirastich li l'olam" and its explanation, printed in Likkutei Torah. On the first day of Shavuos he said the discourse "U'sefartem lachem" and its explanation, printed in Likkutei Torah. On the second day of Shavuos, at the festive meal, he said the discourse "V'hachochma mei'ayin timatzei," which is the second explanation on the subject of "tispru chamishim yom" printed in Likkutei Torah.
translationNotes: רבינו here is the Tzemach Tzedek. Kehot's "the Rebbe" could be misread.
Kehot's page numbers are not in the Hebrew. Left out.

calendar.original5703: Tzidkas'cha is not said.

hayomYom.english: Haircutting during the Three Days of Preparation, before Erev Shavuot, was displeasing to my father. Whoever ponders the approach of Tosafot in his comment beginning "Torah etc..." (Shabbat 89a) will understand that the festival of Shavuot is an auspicious time Above. On that day G‑d confounds the "supernal accuser" of Israel, similar to His confounding the accuser during Shofar-sounding on Rosh Hashana and on the holy day of the Fast of Yom Kippur.
hayomYom.hebrew:
כשהסתפרו בימי הגבלה, קודם עחה"ש [ערב חג השבועות], לא היתה רוח אאמו"ר [אדוני אבי מורי ורבי] נוחה מזה.

המעיין בשיטת תוד"ה [תוספות דבור המתחיל] תורה [שבת פט. א] יבין, שחה"ש [שחג השבועות] הוא זמן עת רצון למעלה, והשי"ת [והשם יתברך] מטריד את המקטרג על עם ישראל, כדוגמת הטרדתו בשעת התקיעות בר"ה [בראש השנה] ויום הקדוש דצום כפורים.
hayomYom.clear:
When people got haircuts during the Days of Setting Bounds [the three days before Shavuos], before Erev Shavuos, my father [the Rebbe Rashab] was not pleased.

Whoever looks into Tosafos, starting "Torah" (Shabbos 89a), will understand: Shavuos is a time of Divine favor Above. G‑d confounds the accuser of the Jewish people, just as He confounds him during the shofar blowing on Rosh Hashana and on the holy day of the fast of Yom Kippur.
translationNotes: ימי הגבלה: "the days of setting bounds" around Mount Sinai (Shemos 19:12).
לא היתה רוח ... נוחה: "was not at ease with it," a mild but clear disapproval.
עת רצון: "a time of favor," not just "auspicious."

hayomYom.english: Shavuot is an opportune time to achieve everything in improving Torah-study and avoda marked by fear (awe) of G‑d, and also to strive in teshuva concerning Torah-study, without interference by the accusing Satan - just like the time of Shofar-sounding on Rosh Hashana and the holy day of the Fast of Yom Kippur.
hayomYom.hebrew: חה"ש [חג השבועות] הוא זמן המוכשר לעשות הכל לטובת לימוד התורה והעבודה ביראת שמים, וכן להתעסק בתשובה בהנוגע לתורה באין מפריע משטן המקטרג, כדוגמת זמן התקיעות בר"ה [בראש השנה] ויום הקדוש דצום הכפורים.
hayomYom.clear: Shavuos is the right time to do everything for the sake of Torah study and avoda with fear of Heaven. It is also the time to work on teshuva regarding Torah, with no interference from the accusing Satan. It is like the time of the shofar blowing on Rosh Hashana and the holy day of the fast of Yom Kippur.
translationNotes: ביראת שמים: "with fear of Heaven." Kehot's "marked by fear (awe)" is the same.
להתעסק בתשובה בהנוגע לתורה: teshuva specifically for lapses in Torah study.

hayomYom.english: On the eve of Shavuot 5557 (1797) the Alter Rebbe taught: Sanctify them today and tomorrow and they shall cleanse their garments. "Sanctify them today and tomorrow," is done from Above, but "they shall cleanse their garments" - one must do himself. This was the entire teaching. The Tzemach Tzedek elaborated: "Sanctify them" was said by G‑d to Moshe. The extension of Moshe is in every generation and they are able to sanctify the "today" and the "tomorrow"; but for this is needed "..and they shall cleanse their garments" - the garments of thought, speech and deed. This must be done by each person on his own.
hayomYom.hebrew: ערב חג השבועות תקנ"ז אמר רבינו הזקן תורה: וקדשתם היום ומחר גו' וקדשתם היום ומחר זהו מלמעלה, אבל וכבסו שמלותם דאס דארף מען אליין. דאס איז געווען די גאנצע תורה. דער צ"צ [צמח צדק] האט מבאר געווען: וקדשתם איז געזאגט געווארן צו משה'ן, און אתפשטותא דמשה בכל דרא ודרא, וואס זיי קענען הייליג מאכען דעם היינט און דעם מארגען, אבער מ'דארף דערצו וכבסו שמלותם - לבושי מחשבה דבור ומעשה, וואס דאס דארף מען אליין.
hayomYom.clear:
On Erev Shavuos 5557 [1797], the Alter Rebbe said a teaching: "Sanctify them today and tomorrow, and they shall wash their garments" (Shemos 19:10). "Sanctify them today and tomorrow": that comes from Above. But "they shall wash their garments": that you have to do yourself. That was the whole teaching.

The Tzemach Tzedek explained: "Sanctify them" was said to Moshe. And there is an extension of Moshe in every generation, and they can make the "today" and the "tomorrow" holy. But for that you need "they shall wash their garments": the garments of thought, speech and action. That you have to do yourself.
translationNotes: אתפשטותא דמשה בכל דרא ודרא: the Zohar's "extension of Moshe in every generation," the leader of each generation.
דאס דארף מען אליין: "you must do it yourself," said twice, deliberately.

hayomYom.english: The Baal Shem Tov passed away on Wednesday, the first day of Shavuot, 5520 (1760) and is interred in Mezibuz. The Alter Rebbe Commented (on Wednesday, the 20th of Kislev 5559 (1798) in Petersburg): "On the fourth day the luminaries were taken away."
hayomYom.hebrew:
בשעת קריאת עשה"ד [עשרת הדברות] עומדים ופניהם אל הס"ת [הספר תורה], אין אומרים אקדמות.

הסתלקות הבעש"ט [הבעל שם טוב] - ביום הרביעי א דחה"ש [דחג השבועות] תק"ך ומ"כ [ומנוחתו כבוד] במעזיבוש. אדמו"ר [אדוננו מורנו ורבנו] הזקן אמר ע"ז [על זה] - יום ד כ בכסלו תקנ"ט בפעטערבורג - ביום הרביעי נטלו המאורות.
hayomYom.clear:
During the reading of the Ten Commandments, we stand facing the Torah scroll. Akdamus is not said.

The Baal Shem Tov passed away on Wednesday, the first day of Shavuos, 5520 [1760], and is buried in Mezhibuzh. The Alter Rebbe said about this, on Wednesday, the 20th of Kislev 5559 [1798], in Petersburg: "On the fourth day, the luminaries were taken away."
translationNotes: Kehot drops the opening custom: standing facing the Sefer Torah for the Ten Commandments and not saying Akdamus. Translated here.
ביום הרביעי נטלו המאורות: the luminaries were hung on the fourth day of Creation. Here, "taken away."

hayomYom.english: Procedure for the congregant during the blessing by the kohanim (p. 268): When the kohanim say yevarech'cha, face forward; When kohanim say Hashem, turn head to right (which is the left of the kohein pronouncing the blessing). When the kohanim say v'yishm'recha, face forward. While kohanim say ya'eir, turn head to left (which is to the right of the kohein pronouncing the blessing), etc. At shalom face forward. Say Ribono shel olam only while the kohanim sing (the wordless accompanying melody); but when they pronounce the words, one must listen. When the kohanim sing the wordless melody prior to saying v'yaseim, say Ribono until hatzadik. During the similar choral introduction to l'cha, say from v'im until Elisha. Likewise before shalom say from Uch'sheim until l'tova. As the kohanim finish pronouncing the word shalom, say v'tishm'reini u't'chaneini vetirtseini. Adir bamarom is said after responding amein, while face is still covered by the tallit.
hayomYom.hebrew: נשיאות כפים: כשאומרים תיבת יברכך - המתברך ראשו באמצע. ה' - מיסב ראשו לימינו, שהיא שמאל המברך. וישמרך - באמצע. יאר - לשמאלו שהיא ימין המברך וכו'. שלום - ראשו באמצע. אמירת רבש"ע [רבונו של עולם] - בשעה שהכהנים מנגנים דוקא, אבל כשאומרים התיבות צריך לשמוע. כשמנגנים ל"וישם" אומרים רבוש"ע [רבונו של עולם]... הצדיק. כשמנגנים לתיבת "לך" - ואם... אלישע. ל"שלום" - וכשם... לטובה. כשאומרים "שלום" - אומרים "ותשמרני ותחנני ותרצני". אדיר במרום אומרים אחר ענית אמן כשעדיין הטלית על פניו.
hayomYom.clear:
Birkas Kohanim [the priestly blessing]:

When they say "yevarech'cha," the one being blessed holds his head straight. "Hashem": he turns his head to his right, which is the left of the one blessing. "V'yishm'recha": straight. "Ya'eir": to his left, which is the right of the one blessing, and so on. "Shalom": head straight.

Say Ribono shel Olam only while the kohanim are singing the tune. When they say the words, you have to listen.

When they sing before "v'yaseim," say Ribono shel Olam ... hatzaddik. When they sing before the word "lecha": v'im ... Elisha. Before "shalom": u'chshem ... l'tova. When they say "shalom," say "v'sishm'reini v'sechaneini v'sirtzeini."

Adir bamarom is said after answering Amen, while the tallis is still over your face.
translationNotes: באמצע: "in the middle," head straight, not necessarily "face forward."
דוקא: only while they sing. The stress is in the Hebrew.

hayomYom.english: The physical universe is a mixture. It is a meeting-place where G‑d meets together (as it were) with man, the select of all creatures; yet it is also ginat egoz, "a garden of nuts," the word egoz having the numerical equivalent of cheit, "sin." G‑d gives man the capacity to choose freely, that man may choose for himself a path in life.
hayomYom.hebrew: דער עולם הזה הגשמי איז א געמיש פון גינוניא של הקב"ה [הקדוש ברוך הוא] [א צוזאמענקונפט וואו השי"ת [ה' יתברך] כביכול קומט זיך צוזאמען מיט דעם אדם בחיר הנבראים] און גנת אגוז [בגימטריא חטא]. און השי"ת [ה' יתברך] גיט א בחירה חפשית צום מענשען, אז דער מענש קען זיך אליין אויסקלייבען א וועג אין לעבען.
hayomYom.clear:
This physical world is a mixture. It is a mix of G‑d's ginunya [garden], meaning a meeting place where G‑d, so to speak, comes together with man, the choicest of creatures, and of ginas egoz, "a garden of nuts" [egoz has the numerical value of chet, sin].

And G‑d gives man free choice, so that a person can choose a path in life for himself.
translationNotes: גינוניא של הקב"ה: "G‑d's garden" (Bamidbar Rabba 13:2). Kehot drops the garden image, so the contrast of two gardens is lost.
אדם בחיר הנבראים: man, "the choicest of creatures."

hayomYom.english: The world is in need of a purified atmosphere. Purified air comes only through words of Torah. Words of Torah offer protection in general and for each individual in particular. The division of the Six Orders of Mishna for memorization is intended for "when you walk on the road." The Mishna or two recited from memory wherever one may be, in whatever sort of place he may be, will illuminate the bond between Israel and G‑d. The letters MiSHNaH are the same as NeSHaMaH (soul). It is extremely difficult to find the words to express the tremendous benefit, with G‑d's help, in the general and individual protection that constant repetition of Mishna will bring. And there are no words to describe the tremendous gratification one thereby gives the Creator, may He be blessed.
hayomYom.hebrew: די וועלט דארף האבען טהרת האויר. טהרת האויר איז נאר דורך אותיות התורה. די אותיות שבתורה זיינען א שמירה כללית און א שמירה פרטית. חלוקת השתא סדרי משנה [בעל-פה] איז א "ובלכתך בדרך"'דיקער. די משנה משניות וואס מען וועט חזר'ן וואו מען וועט זיין, אין וואס פאר א פלאץ מען וועט זיין, וועט באלייכטען די פארבינדונג פון ישראל מיט קוב"ה [קודשא בריך הוא]. משנה איז אותיות נשמה. עס איז זייער שווער צו געפינען די ווערטער אויסצודריקען דעם גרעסטען תועלת בעזה"י [בעזרת ה' יתברך] אין דער שמירה כללית און דער שמירה פרטית, וואס דער כסדר'דיגער חזר'ן משניות וועט בעזה"י [בעזרת ה' יתברך] בריינגען. און עס פעלען אויס די ווערטער צו באשרייבען דעם גרויסען נחת רוח, וואס מען וועט פארשאפען דעם בורא עולם ב"ה [ברוך הוא].
hayomYom.clear:
The world needs pure air. Pure air comes only through the letters of Torah. The letters of Torah are a general protection and a personal protection.

The division of the Six Orders of Mishna [to be learned by heart] is a "when you walk on the road" (Devarim 6:7) kind of thing. The mishna or mishnayos that you review wherever you are, in whatever kind of place you are, will light up the bond between Israel and the Holy One, blessed be He. Mishna has the same letters as neshama [soul].

It is very hard to find the words to express the great benefit, with G‑d's help, in general and personal protection, that steady review of mishnayos will bring, with G‑d's help. And there are no words to describe the great nachas [satisfaction] it will give the Creator of the world, blessed be He.
translationNotes: אותיות התורה: "letters of Torah." Kehot's "words" loses the point that the letters themselves protect.
חזר'ן: to review over and over, by heart.

hayomYom.english: The Alter Rebbe responded to an individual at yechidus: "...The Jewish people are called neirot, lamps. A lamp comprises a vessel, wick, oil and flame. But one must kindle the flame - and then it sheds light. You have a good lamp, but you lack the igniter. By sharply striking the stone of the animal soul, a spark of fire flies out and kindles the G‑dly fire."
hayomYom.hebrew: רבינו הזקן ענה לאחד בהכנסו ליחידות: ...בני ישראל ווערען אנגערופען נרות. א נר איז כלול פון כלי פתילה שמן ואש. מען מוז אבער אנצינדען דעם אש און דעמאלט איז דאס מאיר. בא דיר איז א גוטער נר, אבער עס פעלט דיר דער אנצינדער. דורך הכאה בכח אין דעם אבן של נפש הבהמית, געהט ארויס א ניצוץ אש, וועלכער צינדט אן דעם אש אלקי.
hayomYom.clear:
The Alter Rebbe answered someone who came in for yechidus:

"... The Jewish people are called lamps. A lamp is made of a vessel, a wick, oil and fire. But you have to light the fire, and then it gives light.

You have a good lamp, but you are missing the lighter. By striking hard on the stone of the animal soul, a spark of fire flies out, and it lights the G‑dly fire."
translationNotes: Matches the original. No meaning lost.

hayomYom.english: From my father's talks: "The avoda of serving G‑d according to Chassidus comprises all kinds of levels... The level of "corpse" does not need much elaboration; but, thank G‑d, there is also "revival of the dead" in spiritual avoda. A corpse is cold; there is nothing as frigid as natural intellect, human intellect. When one's natural intelligence comprehends a G‑dly concept, and the emotions latent in intellect are enthused and moved by the pleasure-within-intellect - that is true revival of the dead.
hayomYom.hebrew: משיחות אאמו"ר [אדוני אבי מורי ורבי]: אין דער עבודה פון עבודת ה' ע"ד [על דרך] החסידות, זיינען פאראן אלע מדריגות... די דרגא פון מת באדארף קיין סך הסבר ניט האבען. עס איז אבער אויך פאראן - ת"ל [תודה לא-ל] - תחית המתים אין עבודה רוחנית. א מת איז קאלט, עס איז ניטא אזא קאלטע זאך ווי שכל הטבעי און שכל אנושי, און ווען דער שכל הטבעי פארשטעהט א השגה אלקית און די מדות שבשכל ווערען נתפעל און גערירט פון דעם געשמאק שכלי, איז דאס דער אמת'ער תחית המתים.
hayomYom.clear:
From my father's [the Rebbe Rashab's] talks:

In serving G‑d the way of Chassidus, there are all levels ... The level of "dead" does not need much explaining. But, thank G‑d, there is also resurrection of the dead in spiritual avoda.

A dead body is cold. Nothing is as cold as natural intellect, human intellect. And when natural intellect grasps a G‑dly concept, and the emotions within the intellect are stirred and moved by the intellectual delight, that is true resurrection of the dead.
translationNotes: געשמאק שכלי: the "taste" or delight of understanding.

hayomYom.english: In the b'racha shehakol: The yud of nih'yoh has a kamatz vowel, not a segol vowel. My father wrote in a letter: Cherish criticism, for it will place you on the true heights.
hayomYom.hebrew:
בברכת שנ"ב [שהכל נהי'[ה] בדברו]: נהי'[ה] היו"ד בקמץ ולא בסגול.

אאמו"ר [אדוני אבי מורי ורבי] כותב באחד ממכתביו: אהוב את הבקורת, כי היא תעמידך על הגובה האמיתי.
hayomYom.clear:
In the blessing Shehakol nih'yah bidvaro: the yud in nih'yah has a kamatz, not a segol.

My father [the Rebbe Rashab] writes in one of his letters: Love criticism, because it will set you on your true height.
translationNotes: אהוב את הבקורת: "love" criticism. Kehot's "cherish" is close.
תעמידך על הגובה האמיתי: puts you on your "true height," your real level, not an inflated one.

hayomYom.english: The Tzemach Tzedek composed many melodies. He studied Torah aloud and with song. It would happen that he would interrupt his studies, or his writing Chassidus or responsa, and sing some melody. My grandfather related that from the sound of the Tzemach Tzedek's melody he could tell in what subject he was then occupied.
hayomYom.hebrew:
הצ"צ [הצמח צדק] חבר כמה נגונים, למודו היה בקול ונגון, ולפעמים היה מפסיק באמצע למודו, או כתיבתו דא"ח [דברי אלקים חיים] או שו"ת [שאלות ותשובות], ומנגן איזה ניגון.

אאזמו"ר [אדוני אבי זקני מורי ורבי] סיפר, אשר מקול ניגונו של הצ"צ [הצמח צדק] היה יודע במה הוא עסוק באותה שעה.
hayomYom.clear:
The Tzemach Tzedek composed many niggunim [melodies]. He studied out loud and with a tune. Sometimes he would stop in the middle of his studying, or of writing Chassidus or responsa, and sing some niggun.

My grandfather [the Rebbe Maharash] related that from the sound of the Tzemach Tzedek's niggun he could tell what he was busy with at that moment.
translationNotes: דא"ח, דברי אלקים חיים: "words of the living G‑d," the classic name for Chassidus.

hayomYom.english: In putting on the tallit-katan in the morning, with "clean" hands and in a place where a b'racha may be said, recite al mitzvat tzitzit; (L'hitateif b'tzitzit is only said for a large tallit that has the size for "enwrapment.") If one may not say a b'racha when putting on a tallit-katan, then before davening, hold the four tzitzit and say the b'racha then. However, if one is wearing a large tallit as well, no b'racha is said for the tallit-katan.
hayomYom.hebrew: בלבישת טלית קטן בבוקר בידים נקיות ובמקום שמותר לברך, מברכים "על מצות ציצית" - כיון שאין בט"ק [בטלית קטן] שלנו שיעור עיטוף. אם אסור לברך, אזי קודם התפלה - אם אינו לובש ט"ג [טלית גדול] - ימשמש בד' ציציותיו ויברך אז.
hayomYom.clear:
When you put on the tallis katan in the morning, with clean hands and in a place where you may say a blessing, say "al mitzvas tzitzis," because our tallis katan is not big enough to wrap yourself in.

If you may not say the blessing then, then before davening, if you are not putting on a tallis gadol, touch the four tzitzis and say the blessing then.
translationNotes: כיון שאין בט"ק שלנו שיעור עיטוף: the reason is "our tallis katan lacks the size for wrapping." Kehot rephrases.
אם אינו לובש ט"ג: the Hebrew says the later blessing applies only if you do not wear a tallis gadol. Kehot words it as a separate rule. Following the Hebrew.
hayomYom.dataFlag: Kehot English rearranges the halacha (adds L'hisateif line, splits the tallis gadol clause). Translated from the Hebrew.

hayomYom.english: At first the Alter Rebbe would deliver extremely brief expositions that aroused a storm within the listener's heart, and greatly inflamed his emotions. These were called d'rachim, "pathways." Later his talks were a little more extended, and these were called igrot, "missives." In the next stage of development, his talks were termed torot, "teachings," and these formed the basis for the maamarim in Torah Or and Likutei Torah. Later came somewhat longer teachings called k'tavim, "writings." These were expositions with comparatively broad intellectual elaboration.
hayomYom.hebrew: בתחילה היה רבינו הגדול אומר דרושים קצרים במאד, מרעישי הלב ומלהיבים מאד, ונקראו בשם "דרכים", אח"כ [אחר כך] נקראו "אגרות" והם ארוכים יותר. אח"כ [אחר כך] השתלשל שנקראו "תורות" והם שרשי הדרושים שבתורה אור ולקו"ת [ולקוטי תורה], אח"כ [אחר כך] ארוכים מעט יותר ונקראו "כתבים", והם בביאור בהשגה רחבה לפי ערך.
hayomYom.clear: At first, the Alter Rebbe would say very short discourses that shook the heart and set it on fire. These were called "drachim" [paths]. Later came "igros" [letters], which were longer. After that they developed into what were called "toros" [teachings], which are the roots of the discourses in Torah Or and Likkutei Torah. After that came somewhat longer ones, called "ksavim" [writings], which explained things with relatively broad understanding.
translationNotes: מרעישי הלב ומלהיבים מאד: "shaking the heart" and "greatly inflaming." Matches Kehot.
שרשי הדרושים: "the roots" of the Torah Or and Likkutei Torah discourses.

hayomYom.english: The early sages, who were like angels (may their merit protect us) have already determined that the healing of the soul is like the healing of the body: The crucial first step is to identify the location of the illness, whether it is caused by the crassness, grossness and corruption of his physical body or by a failing in his soul-powers, the person being inclined to undersirable traits like arrogance or falsehood and the like. Or, the source of the malady may be habit - inadequate rearing or unwholesome environment having brought on bad habits. Without ascertaining the specific site of the illness and the cause of infection, it is impossible to embark on a cure. One can only prescribe an orderly proper conduct in all matters, what to do and what to avoid. To "do good" in terms of observing mitzvot, designating times for Torah-study and acquiring good character traits - and also to "turn away from evil." Most urgent of all, however, is that the patient make himself aware of two things: a) to know that he is ill, and desire most fervently to be cured of his malady; b) to know that he can be cured, with hope and absolute trust that, with G‑d's help, he will indeed be cured of his sickness.
hayomYom.hebrew:
כבר החליטו הראשונים כמלאכים זי"ע [זכותם יגן עלינו], אשר רפואת הנפש היא כרפואת הגוף.

לכל לראש צריך לסמן מקום החולי: אם הוא מצד שחומר גופו עב גס ומושחת, או שהחסרון הוא בכחות נפשו, שיש לה נטיות לענינים רעים כמו גאוה, שקר וכדומה, או שמקור החולי הוא בהרגילות, שמפני רוע החינוך או רוע הסביבה בא לרגילות רעות.

עד אשר לא יתבררו פרטי מקום החולי וסיבת אחיזת המחלה אי אפשר להתחיל ברפואתו, כי אם לסדר אופן הנהגה ישרה בכל הדברים במה שיעשה ובמה שימנע את עצמו מהם: בועשה טוב בקיום המצות קביעות עתים לתורה קנין מדות טובות, ובסור מרע. אמנם מה שנחוץ ביותר הוא שיעורר החולה בעצמו שני ענינים: א) לידע שהוא חולה ויכסוף וישתוקק להתרפאות מחליו. ב) הידיעה שיכול להתרפאות, והתקוה ובטחון גמור כי בעזה"י [בעזרת השם יתברך] יתרפא מחליו.
hayomYom.clear:
The early sages, who were like angels, may their merit protect us, already concluded: healing the soul is like healing the body.

First of all, you have to mark where the illness is. Is it because his physical body is thick, coarse and corrupted? Or is the lack in the powers of his soul, which leans toward bad things like arrogance, falsehood and the like? Or is the source of the illness habit: bad upbringing or bad surroundings led to bad habits?

Until the details of where the illness is, and what made the disease take hold, are clear, it is impossible to begin treating it. All you can do is set up an upright way of conduct in everything: what to do and what to keep away from. In "do good": keeping mitzvos, fixed times for Torah, acquiring good middos. And in "turn from evil."

But what is most necessary is that the patient awaken in himself two things:
1. To know that he is sick, and to long and yearn to be healed of his illness.
2. To know that he can be healed, with hope and complete trust that, with G‑d's help, he will be healed of his illness.
translationNotes: יכסוף וישתוקק: two words, "long and yearn." Kehot's "desire most fervently" merges them.
סור מרע ועשה טוב is Tehillim 34:15.

hayomYom.english: Refraining from deriving pleasure - in the fullest sense - from this world, is only a fine preparation for avoda. Avoda itself is transforming the physical into a vehicle for G‑dliness.
hayomYom.hebrew: ניט הנאה האבען פון עולם הזה אין פולען זין, הוא רק הכנה טובה לעבודה. ענין העבודה הוא לעשות הגשמי כלי לאלקות.
hayomYom.clear: Not having pleasure from this world, in the full sense, is only a good preparation for avoda. Avoda itself is making the physical into a vessel for G‑dliness.
translationNotes: כלי לאלקות: "a vessel for G‑dliness." Kehot's "vehicle" is close but loses the term kli.

hayomYom.english: This is the actual time of the "footsteps of Mashiach." It is therefore imperative for every Jew to seek his fellow's welfare - whether old or young - to inspire the other to teshuva (return), so that he will not fall out - G‑d forbid - of the community of Israel who will shortly be privileged, with G‑d's help, to experience complete redemption.
hayomYom.hebrew: בזמן הזה בעקבתא דמשיחא ממש, החובה על כל אחד מישראל לדרוש בטובת זולתו, בין זקן בין צעיר, לעוררו לתשובה, למען שלא יצא ח"ו [חס ושלום] מכלל ישראל שיזכו בעזה"י [בעזרת השם יתברך], לגאולה שלימה.
hayomYom.clear: In this time, the very footsteps of Mashiach [the final moments before the Redemption], every Jew has a duty to seek the good of another, whether old or young. Stir him to teshuva [return to G‑d], so that he does not, G‑d forbid, fall out of the community of Israel who, with G‑d’s help, will merit the complete Redemption.
translationNotes: עקבתא דמשיחא ממש: “the very footsteps of Mashiach.” The Hebrew stresses ממש, that this is literally the time.
לדרוש בטובת זולתו: actively seek another’s good, not just ask after his welfare.
Kehot adds “shortly.” The Hebrew has no such word. Left out.

hayomYom.english: In the month of Marcheshvan 5613 (1852) the Tzemach Tzedek started an additional program of study with my grandfather, besides the Tzemach Tzedek's regular studies. This was for two and a half hours daily, starting at 10:00 p.m. winters, and at 4:00 a.m. summers. For two years they studied Kabala with chassidic interpretation. Thereafter, until Elul 5616 (1856), when this special program ceased, they studied the following philosophical works: Those of R. Saadya Gaon, and Moreh Nevuchim, Ikarim, Kuzari, etc. - according to Chassidic teachings.
hayomYom.hebrew: בחדש מרחשון תרי"ג קבע הצ"צ [הצמח צדק], מלבד השיעורים האחרים, שיעור למוד עם אאזמו"ר [אדוני אבי זקני מורי ורבי] בכל יום שתי שעות ומחצה - בחורף מתחיל משעה העשירית לילה ובקיץ משעה הרביעית לפנות בוקר. - שתי שנים היה הלמוד: קבלה עם ביאורי חסידות. אחר זמן זה - עד אלול תרט"ז, שאז נפסק השיעור, למדו ספרי מחקר: הרס"ג [הרב סעדיה גאון] מורה נבוכים עיקרים כוזרי ועוד ע"פ [על פי] תורת החסידות.
hayomYom.clear:
In Marcheshvan 5613 [1852], the Tzemach Tzedek set up a study session with my grandfather [the Rebbe Maharash], on top of his other study sessions. It ran two and a half hours every day. In winter it began at ten at night; in summer, at four in the morning.
