For two years they studied Kabbala with Chassidic explanations. After that, until Elul 5616 [1856], when the session ended, they studied works of philosophy: R. Saadya Gaon, Moreh Nevuchim, Ikkarim, Kuzari and others, according to the teachings of Chassidus.
translationNotes: מלבד השיעורים האחרים: “besides the other sessions.” It is not clear these were the Tzemach Tzedek’s own studies, as Kehot implies; they may be other sessions with the Maharash.
ספרי מחקר: works of rational inquiry (philosophy).

hayomYom.english: Among my grandfather's aphorisms: The intellectual and emotional structure of the chassid is consonant with his first yechidus with his Rebbe. The first yechidus is in accordance with the essence-character of the chassid. The Rebbe prescribes an order of avoda appropriate to the nature of the chassid's essence-character.
hayomYom.hebrew: מפתגמי אאזמו"ר [אדוני אבי זקני מורי ורבי]: דער שכל און מדות געבוי פון א חסיד, איז לפי ערך זיין ערשטע יחידות בא זיין רבי'ן. די ערשטע יחידות איז לפי ערך מהות עצמו פון א חסיד, לפי אופן מהות עצמו אזא סדר עבודה גיט איהם דער רבי
hayomYom.clear:
One of my grandfather’s [the Rebbe Maharash’s] sayings:

A chassid’s structure of mind and emotions matches his first yechidus [private audience] with his Rebbe.

The first yechidus matches the chassid’s essential self. According to the kind of essential self he has, that is the order of avoda the Rebbe gives him.
translationNotes: געבוי is a “building” or structure: the whole edifice of mind and middos.
לפי ערך: “in proportion to.” The first yechidus sets the measure of what the chassid becomes.

hayomYom.english: The Alter Rebbe explains (in Tanya chapter 3) that the three faculties of intellect, chochma-bina-da'at, and the seven emotive powers, evolve from the ten supernal Sefirot. All this applies to nefesh, ruach, and neshama (three aspects of the soul) which are enclothed within the body of man. However, mesirat nefesh, the readiness for self-sacrifice for G‑d (that a Jew neither desires nor is capable of being - G‑d forbid - separated from G‑dhood) comes from the Essence of the En Sof (the Infinite One, may He be blessed) which transcends the Sefirot, the first of which is the Sefira of chochma.
hayomYom.hebrew: רבינו בספר של בינונים פ"ג [פרק ג'] אומר, כי ג' מוחין חב"ד וז' מדות הם השתלשלות מעשר ספירות העליונות, דכל זה הוא בנפש רוח ונשמה שהם המתלבשים בגוף האדם, אמנם ענין המסירת נפש על אלקות, וואס א איד ניט ער וויל און ניט ער קאן זיין ח"ו [חס ושלום] א נפרד מאלקות, זהו מעצמות א"ס [אין סוף] ב"ה [ברוך הוא], שלמעלה מענין הספירות דראשיתם היא ספירת החכמה.
hayomYom.clear:
The Alter Rebbe says in Tanya, chapter 3, that the three intellectual powers, chochma, bina and daas, and the seven middos [emotional attributes] come down from the ten supernal Sefiros. All of this applies to nefesh, ruach and neshama, the levels of the soul that are enclothed in the human body.

But mesirus nefesh [self-sacrifice] for G‑dliness, the fact that a Jew neither wants to nor can be, G‑d forbid, separated from G‑dliness, comes from the very Essence of the Ein Sof [the Infinite], blessed be He. That is higher than the whole realm of the Sefiros, the first of which is the Sefira of chochma.
translationNotes: ספר של בינונים is the Tanya’s own name. Kehot just says Tanya.
ניט ער וויל און ניט ער קאן: the Yiddish phrase “he neither wants to nor is able to” is a fixed Chabad expression.

hayomYom.english: In Ahavat olam (p. 44-5), at the words vehavi'einu leshalom, bring together the two front tzitzit. Then join to them the tzitzit of the left back corner, then the tzitzit of the right back corner, holding them together between the little finger and ring finger of the left hand. Kiss the tzitzit six times, at the words tzitzit, tzitzit, l'tzitzit, emet, kayemet and la'ad.
hayomYom.hebrew:
לאמירת והביאנו לשלום כו' מחברים תחלה ב' הציציות דלפניו, אח"כ [אחר כך] מצרפים ציצית כנף השמאלי דלאחוריו, אח"ז [אחר זה] ציצית דכנף הימין ואוחזים אותם בין קמיצה לזרת דיד שמאל.

נושקים הציציות שש פעמים היינו באמירת תיבות: ציצית, ציצית, לציצית, אמת, קימת, לעד.
hayomYom.clear:
When saying v’havi’einu l’shalom [“bring us in peace,” in the blessing before the Shema]: first bring together the two front tzitzis. Then add the tzitzis of the back left corner, and then the tzitzis of the back right corner. Hold them between the ring finger and the little finger of the left hand.

Kiss the tzitzis six times, at the words: tzitzis, tzitzis, l’tzitzis, emes, kayemes, la’ad.
translationNotes: Kehot adds “In Ahavas olam (p. 44‑5)” as a siddur reference. The Hebrew just says “when saying v’havi’einu l’shalom.”
Matches the original otherwise. No meaning lost.

hayomYom.english:
Bless Rosh Chodesh Tamuz. Say all the Tehillim in the early morning.
Day of Farbrengen.

In a reply to a yechidus query in the winter of 5635 (1874-75), my grandfather said to my father: The yetzer hara, (the evil impulse), is called "animal soul," not because it is necessarily a brute animal. At times it may be a fox, the most cunning of beasts, and great wisdom is needed to perceive its machinations. At other times it may clothe itself in the garb of an earnest, straightforward, humble tzadik, possessing fine traits of character. The animal soul manifests itself in each person according to his individual character. One person may suddenly experience a powerful longing to study Chassidus or to meditate deeply on some chassidic concept. The truth is, however, that this is nothing more than the yetzer hara's counsel and the animal soul's machinations to prevent him from engaging in the avoda of davening or a similar activity. Take this as a general principle and remember it always: Any matter that is effective towards or actually leads to active avoda, and is confronted with opposition of any sort, even the most noble, that opposition is the scheming of the animal soul. My father concluded: Until then I had not known that there can be a "pious" animal soul, let alone a "chassidic" animal soul.
hayomYom.hebrew:
מברכים ר"ח [ראש חודש] תמוז. אמירת כל התהלים בהשכמה.

יום התוועדות.

מענה אאזמו"ר [אדוני אבי זקני מורי ורבי] לאאמו"ר [לאדוני אבי מורי ורבי] ביחידות חורף תרל"ה: היצה"ר [היצר הרע] נקרא נה"ב [נפש הבהמית] לא מפני שהוא בהמה דוקא, כי לפעמים הוא שועל פקח שבחיות, וצריכים לחכמה מרובה להבין תחבולותיו. ולפעמים הוא מתלבש בלבוש צדיק תמים ענו ובעל מדות טובות.

בכל אחד ואחד הנה"ב [הנפש הבהמית] שלו היא לפי מהותו הפרטי. ויש אשר מתעורר חשק גדול ללמוד חסידות או להתבונן היטב באיזה השכלה, ובאמת הנה זהו רק עצת היצר ומתחבולות נה"ב [נפש הבהמית] למנוע מעבודת התפלה וכדומה.

ונקוט האי כללא בידך וזכור אותו תמיד, כי כל דבר המועיל או מביא לעבודה בפועל, הנה כל מניעה שתהי'[ה] לדבר זה - אפילו אם המניעה היא מדבר היותר נעלה - הוא רק מתחבולותיה של נה"ב [נפש הבהמית].

וסיים אאמו"ר [אדוני אבי מורי ורבי] נ"ע [נשמתו עדן]: עד אז לא ידעתי אז עס קען זיין א פרומער נה"ב [נפש הבהמית], ווער רעדט נאך א חסידישער נה"ב [נפש הבהמית].
hayomYom.clear:
In winter 5635 [1874‑75], at a yechidus, my grandfather [the Rebbe Maharash] answered my father [the Rebbe Rashab]:

The yetzer hara [evil inclination] is called the animal soul. Not because it is necessarily an animal. Sometimes it is a fox, the cleverest of beasts, and you need great wisdom to see through its tricks. And sometimes it dresses up as a tzaddik: earnest, humble, with fine character traits.

In each person, the animal soul fits his own particular nature. Sometimes a person feels a great urge to study Chassidus, or to think deeply about some concept. In truth, this is only the yetzer hara’s advice and one of the animal soul’s tricks, to keep him from the avoda of davening and the like.

Take this as a rule and always remember it: anything that helps or leads to actual avoda, any obstacle that comes up against it, even an obstacle from the loftiest thing, is just a trick of the animal soul.

My father concluded: Until then I did not know that there can be a pious animal soul, let alone a chassidic animal soul.
translationNotes: עבודה בפועל: avoda “in practice,” actually done. This is the test: whatever blocks real action is suspect.
שועל פקח שבחיות: “the cleverest of the beasts” (echoing Berachos 61b, where the fox is called the cleverest of animals).

calendar.original5703: Shabbos Mevarchim Tammuz. Say the whole Tehillim early in the morning. A day of farbrengen.

hayomYom.english: "You ask how can you be bound (m'kushar) to me when I do not know you personally..." "...The true bond is created by studying Torah. When you study my maamarim, read the sichot and associate with those dear to me - the chassidic community and the tmimim - in their studies and farbrengens, and you fulfill my request regarding saying Tehillim and observing Torah-study times - in this is the bond."
hayomYom.hebrew:
השואל במה היא ההתקשרות שלו אלי מאחר שאין אני מכירו פנים...

...ההתקשרות האמיתית היא ע"י [על ידי] לימוד התורה, כשהוא לומד המאמרי חסידות שלי, קורא את השיחות ומתחבר עם ידידי אנ"ש [אנשי שלומינו] ותלמידי התמימים יחיו בלימודם ובהתוועדותם, ומקיים בקשתי באמירת תהלים ובשמירת זמני הלימודים, הנה בזה היא ההתקשרות.
hayomYom.clear:
You ask how you can have a bond with me when I do not know you personally...

...The true bond is through Torah study. When you study my maamarim of Chassidus, read the sichos [talks], and join with my dear friends, the chassidim and the students of Tomchei Temimim, in their study and their farbrengens, and you fulfill my request about saying Tehillim and keeping set times for study: in this is the bond.
translationNotes: התקשרות: hiskashrus, the chassid’s bond with the Rebbe.
אין אני מכירו פנים: “I do not know him by face,” never met him.

hayomYom.english: "A care in a man's heart, yash'chena." Our sages offer two interpretations of that last word: "Remove the care from the mind" or "discuss it with others." The Tzemach Tzedek commented: "...with others" who are "others" only in the bodily sense, but are completely united with him, for they empathize with him.
hayomYom.hebrew:
דאגה בלב איש ישחנה ואמרז"ל [ואמרו רבותינו זכרונם לברכה] שני פירושים: יסיחנה מדעתו, ישיחנה לאחרים.

ופירש הצ"צ [הצמח צדק]: לאחרים רק בגוף, אבל מאוחדים אתו עמו, שמרגישים את ענינו.
hayomYom.clear:
“If there is worry in a man’s heart, yashchena” (Mishlei 12:25). Our Sages give two explanations of this word (Yoma 75a): put it out of your mind, or talk it over with others.

The Tzemach Tzedek explained: “Others” who are others only in body. In truth they are one with him, because they feel what he is going through.
translationNotes: שמרגישים את ענינו: they feel his situation as their own. Kehot’s “empathize” is close.
מאוחדים אתו עמו: doubled for emphasis, “truly united with him.”

hayomYom.english: "They went down to the pit alive" - even in the grave they think they are alive. There is a blessing contained in "They went down to the pit alive," as with "the sons of Korach did not die," - "a place was established for them and they repented." For teshuva, repentance, is effective only while one is still alive. This, then, is the blessing - that even in the pit they will live, and they will be able to effect teshuva.
hayomYom.hebrew:
וירדו חיים שאולה - שגם בשאול חושבים שהם חיים.

הברכה בוירדו חיים שאולה, כמו בני קרח לא מתו, מקום נתבצר להם ועשו תשובה, כי תשובה מועלת רק כל עוד שהוא חי, וזוהי הברכה, שגם בשאול יהיו חיים ויוכלו לעשות תשובה.
hayomYom.clear:
“They went down alive into the pit” (Bamidbar 16:33): even in the pit, they think they are alive.

There is a blessing in “they went down alive into the pit.” It is like “the sons of Korach did not die” (Bamidbar 26:11): a place was set apart for them there, and they did teshuva. For teshuva works only as long as a person is alive. So this is the blessing: even in the pit they will be alive, and they will be able to do teshuva.
translationNotes: שאול: Sheol, the pit or underworld.
מקום נתבצר להם: a place was “fortified” or set apart for them, from the Sages’ teaching on Korach’s sons.

hayomYom.english: "G‑d will bless you in whatever you do." Man needs but to make a receptacle for his livelihood and to endeavor with all his power that the receptacle be pure of any impurity or dross of cheating others and the like. This means that whatever he does conforms to Torah laws. Thus he becomes a "vessel" worthy of G‑d's blessing, in two ways: His livelihood will be ample and his earnings will be directed to desirable ends.
hayomYom.hebrew: כתיב וברכך ה"א [ה' אלקיך] בכל אשר תעשה. האדם עליו רק לעשות כלי לפרנסתו, ולהשתדל בכל כחו אשר הכלי יהיה טהור מכל סיג ופסולת דאונאה כו', היינו שיהי'[ה] הכל ע"פ [על פי] דיני התורה, אשר אז הוא כלי ראוי לברכה העליונה בשנים: פרנסה בריוח, ואשר הפרנסה תלך למקום הראוי.
hayomYom.clear:
It is written: “G‑d your G‑d will bless you in all that you do” (Devarim 15:18). All a person has to do is make a vessel for his livelihood. He must try with all his strength to keep that vessel pure of any dross and waste of cheating and the like. That means everything must follow the laws of the Torah.

Then he is a vessel fit for the blessing from Above, in two ways: an ample livelihood, and that his livelihood goes where it should.
translationNotes: סיג ופסולת דאונאה: “dross and waste of deceit,” metal imagery: a vessel must be clean.
תלך למקום הראוי: the money goes to its proper place. Kehot’s “desirable ends” is close.

hayomYom.english: The Tzemach Tzedek once told his son, my grandfather, an incident in his experience, and concluded: For helping someone in his livelihood, even to earn just 70 kopeks (a small, low-value Russian coin) on a calf, all the gates to the Heavenly Chambers are open for him. Years later my grandfather told this to my father and added: One should really know the route to the Heavenly Chambers, but actually it is not crucial. You only need the main thing - to help another wholeheartedly, with sensitivity, to take pleasure in doing a kindness to another.
hayomYom.hebrew:
הצ"צ [הצמח צדק] בספרו לבנו אאזמו"ר [אדוני אבי זקני מורי ורבי] מאורע מחייו, סיים: מיט דעם וואס מען העלפט א אידען אין פרנסה, אפילו פארדינען זיבעציג קאפיקעס [מטבע קטנה ברוסיא] אין א קעלבעל, איז אלע שערי היכלות העליונים זיינען פאר איהם אפען.

כעבור כמה שנים סיפר אאזמו"ר [אדוני אבי זקני מורי ורבי] כל הנ"ל [הנזכר לעיל] לאאמו"ר [לאדוני אבי מורי ורבי] והוסיף: מ'באדארף אפילו וויסען די וועג צו די היכלות העליונים, נאר דאס מאכט ניט אויס, עס דארף זיין דער עיקר, העלפען בלבב שלם מיט א געפיל, האבען א געשמאק אין א אידען טאן א טובה.
hayomYom.clear:
The Tzemach Tzedek once told his son, my grandfather [the Rebbe Maharash], about an event in his life, and ended: When you help a Jew earn a living, even if it is just earning seventy kopeks [a small Russian coin] on a calf, all the gates of the Heavenly Chambers are open for you.

Years later, my grandfather told all this to my father [the Rebbe Rashab], and added: You should also know the way to the Heavenly Chambers. But that is not what matters. The main thing has to be: help with a whole heart, with feeling, and take real pleasure in doing a Jew a favor.
translationNotes: האבען א געשמאק: “to have a geshmak,” to truly enjoy doing a kindness, not merely take pleasure.
דאס מאכט ניט אויס: “it doesn’t matter.” Kehot’s “not crucial” softens it a little.

hayomYom.english: Man's avoda according to Chassidus: To accustom himself to perceive individual Divine Providence (hashgacha p'ratit), how G‑d, in His goodness, renews the universe and all creatures every moment with His particular Divine Providence, which constitutes - to the exclusion of all else - the reality, life-force and sustained existence of all creatures.
hayomYom.hebrew: עבודת האדם ע"פ [על פי] תורת החסידות, להרגיל את עצמו לראות ענין השגחה פרטית, איך כי בטובו ית' [יתברך] מחדש את העולם והנבראים בכל רגע בהשגחתו הפרטית, אשר זה אך זה הוא מציאות הנבראים חיותם וקיומם.
hayomYom.clear: A person’s avoda according to Chassidus: train yourself to see hashgacha pratis [Divine Providence over every detail]. See how G‑d, in His goodness, renews the world and all creatures every moment with His individual Providence. That alone, and nothing else, is the existence, life and continued being of all creatures.
translationNotes: להרגיל את עצמו: “to accustom yourself,” it is a trained habit of seeing.
אשר זה אך זה: “this and only this.”

hayomYom.english: In reviewing the weekly parsha, twice the text and once the Targum Onkelos, we review verse by verse. We also review the haftora; two, in case of Shabbat-Rosh Chodesh or combined parshiot, etc. The Alter Rebbe's response to a young genius, famed for his intellectual gifts, at his first yechidus in 5555 (1795) in Lyozna: Spiritual and physical are antithetical in their very essence. A superior quality in the physical is a deficiency in the spiritual. In material matters, one who is "satisfied with his lot" is an individual of the highest quality. A person possessing this trait will, through avoda, attain the highest levels. In spiritual matters, however, to be satisfied with one's lot is the worst deficiency, and leads, G‑d forbid, to descent and falling.
hayomYom.hebrew:
העברת הפרשה שמו"ת [שנים מקרא ואחד תרגום] - פסוק פסוק. וקורין גם ההפטרה, או שתי ההפטרות אם הוא שבת ר"ח [ראש חודש], או פרשיות מחוברות וכיוצא בזה.

מענה רבינו הזקן לאברך עילוי מצוין ובעל כשרון מפורסם כשנכנס ליחידות שלו הראשונה - בשנת תקנ"ה בליאזנא: רוחניות וגשמיות זיינען הפכים בעצם מהותם. דאס וואס עס איז א מעלה אין גשמיות, איז א חסרון אין רוחניות.

אין גשמיות איז א שמח בחלקו דער גרעסטער בעל מעלה. און דורך עבודה וועט אזא איינער צוקומען צו די העכסטע מדריגות. אין רוחניות אבער איז א שמח בחלקו דער גרעסטער חסרון, און ער ווערט, ר"ל [רחמנא ליצלן], א יורד ונופל.
hayomYom.clear:
When reviewing the weekly parsha, twice the verse and once the Targum, go verse by verse. Also read the haftorah, or both haftoros when Shabbos is Rosh Chodesh, or when two parshiyos are joined, and the like.

The Alter Rebbe’s answer to a young prodigy, famous for his talents, at his first yechidus, in 5555 [1795] in Lyozna:

Spiritual and physical are opposites in their very essence. What is a virtue in the physical is a flaw in the spiritual.

In physical things, someone who is happy with his lot has the greatest virtue. Through avoda, such a person will reach the highest levels. But in spiritual things, being happy with your lot is the greatest flaw. Such a person, G‑d save us, goes down and falls.
translationNotes: שמח בחלקו: “happy with his lot” (Avos 4:1). The same trait is the highest virtue in one realm and the worst flaw in the other.
יורד ונופל: “goes down and falls,” a steady decline.

hayomYom.english: Mesirat nefesh (self-sacrifice) for Torah-scholars means, "When a man dies in a tent," as interpreted by our sages, to "put to death" all pleasure-taking in worldly matters - for even trivial wordly delights are obstacles to being thoroughly devoted and dedicated to the "tent" of Torah.
hayomYom.hebrew: מס"נ [מסירות נפש] הראויה לבני תורה הוא כדרז"ל [כדרשת רבותינו זכרונם לברכה] אדם כי ימות באהל, להמית את כל התענוגים בעניני עולם. כי אפילו דברים קלי הערך בתענוגי עולם, מונעים המה מלהיות מסור ונתון באהלה של תורה.
hayomYom.clear: The mesirus nefesh that fits a Torah scholar is what the Sages taught on “When a man dies in a tent” (Bamidbar 19:14; Berachos 63b): to put to death every pleasure in worldly matters. Because even small worldly pleasures keep you from being fully devoted and given over to the tent of Torah.
translationNotes: מסור ונתון: “devoted and given over,” a doubled phrase of total dedication.
Matches the original. No meaning lost.

hayomYom.english: The Alter Rebbe writes in his Siddur: It is proper to say before prayer, I hereby take upon myself to fulfill the mitzva - "Love your fellowman as yourself." This means that the precept of ahavat yisrael is the entry-gate through which man can pass to stand before G‑d to daven. By merit of that love the worshipper's prayer is accepted.
hayomYom.hebrew: רבינו הזקן כותב בסידורו: נכון לומר קודם התפלה הריני מקבל עלי מצות עשה של ואהבת לרעך כמוך. זאת אומרת, אשר מצות אהבת ישראל היא שער הכניסה, אשר דרך בו יכול האדם לבוא לעמוד לפני ה"א [ה' אלקינו] להתפלל, בזכותה תקובל תפלת המתפלל.
hayomYom.clear:
The Alter Rebbe writes in his Siddur: It is proper to say before davening, “I hereby take upon myself the positive mitzva of ‘Love your fellow as yourself’ (Vayikra 19:18).”

This means that the mitzva of ahavas Yisrael [love of a fellow Jew] is the entrance gate. Through it a person can come to stand before G‑d and daven. In its merit, the prayer is accepted.
translationNotes: מצות עשה: a positive commandment. Kehot drops “positive.”
שער הכניסה: the entrance gate, the way in.

hayomYom.english: My grandfather said: A Jewish groan which, G‑d forbid, arises from physical misfortune, is also a great teshuva; how much more so then, is a groan arising from spiritual distress a lofty and effective teshuva. The groan pulls him out of the depths of evil and places him on a firm footing in the realm of good.
hayomYom.hebrew: אאזמו"ר [אדוני אבי זקני מורי ורבי] אמר: א אידישער קרעכץ וואס קומט ח"ו [חס ושלום] בסבה פון א ניט גוט גשמי איז אויך א תשובה גדולה, בפרט א קרעכץ בסבה פון א ניט גוט רוחני איז אודאי און אודאי א תשובה מעליתא. דער קרעכץ שלעפט ארויס פון עומק רע, און שטעלט אנידער אין א מעמד טוב.
hayomYom.clear: My grandfather [the Rebbe Maharash] said: A Jewish groan that comes, G‑d forbid, because of something physically not good is also a great teshuva. All the more so, a groan because of something spiritually not good is certainly, certainly a lofty teshuva. The groan pulls you out of the depths of evil and sets you down in a place of good.
translationNotes: קרעכץ: a krechtz, a sigh or groan from the gut.
אודאי און אודאי: “certainly and certainly,” doubled for force. Kehot’s “how much more so” loses it.
שלעפט ארויס: “drags out.” Strong, physical verb.

hayomYom.english: One single chassid or student who devotes his heart, mind and soul to Torah and to bolstering Torah, effects wonders in a large city, in all that city's affairs - in a manner that transcends the natural order, by the merit of our Patriarchs, "Fathers of the World."
hayomYom.hebrew: חסיד אחד או תלמיד אחד כאשר נותן לבו דעתו ונפשו על התורה וחיזוקה, פועל ישועות בעיר גדולה בכל עניני העיר, והוא בדרך מלמעלה מדרך הטבע בזכות אבות העולם.
hayomYom.clear: One chassid or one student who gives his heart, mind and soul to Torah and to strengthening it brings about salvations in a large city, in all the city’s affairs. This happens beyond the natural order, in the merit of the Avos, the fathers of the world.
translationNotes: פועל ישועות: “brings salvations,” rescues. Kehot’s “effects wonders” blurs the idea of deliverance.

hayomYom.english: One of the Alter Rebbe's great and very close chassidim had yechidus, in the course of which the Rebbe inquired after his situation. The chassid complained bitterly that his financial situation had utterly deteriorated. The Rebbe responded: You are needed to illuminate your environment with Torah and avoda of the heart - (davening). Livelihood and what you need - that, G‑d must provide for you. You do what you must, and G‑d will do what He must.
hayomYom.hebrew: רבינו הזקן שאל את אחד החסידים הגדולים המקורבים ביותר בהיותו אצלו ביחידות, למצבו. ויתאונן החסיד כי ירד מנכסיו וכו'. ויענהו רבינו: דיך דארף מען - אז דו זאלסט מאכען ליכטיג דיין סביבה מיט תורה ועבודה שבלב. פרנסה און וואס דו דארפסט - דאס דארף דער אויבערשטער ב"ה [ברוך הוא] דיר געבען. טו וואס דו דארפסט, וועט השי"ת [השם יתברך] טאן וואס ער דארף.
hayomYom.clear:
The Alter Rebbe asked one of his great and closest chassidim, during a yechidus, how he was doing. The chassid complained that he had lost his wealth, and so on.

The Alter Rebbe answered: You are needed to light up your surroundings with Torah and with avoda of the heart [davening]. Livelihood and what you need: that, G‑d has to give you. You do what you have to do, and G‑d will do what He has to do.
translationNotes: דיך דארף מען: “you are needed.” The Rebbe turns it around: G‑d needs you for a task.
מאכען ליכטיג: “make bright,” fill with light.

hayomYom.english: (The effect of) each particular mitzva-act is called forth by (doing) those (other) mitzva-acts which are makif - general and all-encompassing in nature. The mitzva of tzedaka, for example, is one of those all-encompassing makif mitzvot, as evident from the reference to all mitzvot by the term "tzedaka." For this reason it is most appropriate to give a coin to tzedaka before performing any mitzva. This has the effect of bringing the general makif-aura into the p'nimi, the "inner aspect," (the particular mitzva). Nonetheless, this type of makif is a "close aura," whereas the makif of Torah is a "distant aura," whose effect is superior.
hayomYom.hebrew: המצות נמשכות ע"י [על ידי] המקיף שבמצות עצמם. מצות צדקה, עד"מ [על דרך משל], היא מצוה כוללת, אשר כל המצות נקראות בשם צדקה. ומהאי טעמא נכון במאד לתת קודם כל מצוה פרוטה לצדקה, שהוא המשכת המקיף בפנימי. ומ"מ [ומכל מקום] הוי מקיף הקרוב, משא"כ [מה שאין כן] תורה שהיא מקיף הרחוק ופעולתו נעלה יותר.
hayomYom.clear:
The mitzvos are drawn down by the makif [the encompassing aspect] that is within the mitzvos themselves.

Tzedaka, for example, is an all-inclusive mitzva, so much so that all the mitzvos are called by the name tzedaka. For this reason it is very proper to give a coin to tzedaka before every mitzva. This draws the makif into the pnimi [the inner aspect].

Still, this is a “near makif.” Torah, by contrast, is a “far makif,” and its effect is higher.
translationNotes: המקיף שבמצות עצמם: the makif within the mitzvos themselves. Kehot’s wording makes it sound like other mitzvos.
מקיף הקרוב / מקיף הרחוק: near and far encompassing lights. The far one is the higher one.

hayomYom.english: My father said: In Chassidus the "beginning is wedged into the end and the end is wedged into the beginning." This is the state of igulim, "circles," without beginning or end. Nonetheless, order and system are crucial. The Baal Shem Tov was systematic and orderly. The Maggid, his successor, insisted on order. And my great-grandfather - the Alter Rebbe - taught chassidim to be orderly. We see this in his maamarim, letters and melodies. Chassidim who had set times to come to the Rebbe in Lyozna - and later to Liadi - were not permitted to change this schedule without permission from the Rebbe. Any request for a change had to be justified with a reason. The Rebbe had a special committee headed by his brother, R. Yehuda Leib, charged with overseeing order among chassidim. Another committee, under the Miteler Rebbe, directed the younger chassidim.
hayomYom.hebrew:
אאמו"ר [אדוני אבי מורי ורבי] אמר: חסידות איז נעוץ תחלתן בסופן וסופן בתחילתן, די דרגא פון עיגולים מבלי אשר ימצא ראש וסוף, אבער אחר כל זה איז דער עיקר איז סדר.

דער בעש"ט [בעל שם טוב] איז געווען א מסודר, דער מעזריטשער האט מדקדק געווען אויף סדר, און דער עלטער זיידע - רבינו הזקן - האט געלערענט חסידים זיי זאלען זיין מסודרים, דאס זעהט מען אין זיינע מאמרים, בריף, ניגונים. די חסידים וואס האבען געהאט א זמן קבוע אויף קומען אין ליאזנא - דערנאך אין ליאדי - האבען ניט געהאט קיין רשות בייטען דעם זמן אן א רשיון פון רבי'ן, אויף באקומען א רשיון האט מען געדארפט זאגען א טעם.

באם רבי'ן איז געווען א ועד מיוחד אויף פיהרען סדר החסידים ובראשו מהרי"ל [מורנו הרב ר' יהודה לייב] אחי רבינו, און א באזונדער ועד אויף אנפירען מיט חסידישע יונגעלייט ובראשו אדמו"ר [אדוננו מורנו ורבנו] האמצעי.
hayomYom.clear:
My father [the Rebbe Rashab] said: In Chassidus, “the beginning is wedged in the end and the end in the beginning” (Sefer Yetzirah 1:7). This is the level of igulim [circles], where there is no head or end. But even so, the main thing is order.

The Baal Shem Tov was orderly. The Mezritcher [Maggid] was exacting about order. And my great-grandfather, the Alter Rebbe, taught chassidim to be orderly. You can see it in his maamarim, letters and niggunim.

Chassidim who had a set time to come to Lyozna, and later to Liadi, were not allowed to change it without the Rebbe’s permission. To get permission, you had to give a reason.

The Rebbe had a special committee to run the order of the chassidim, headed by his brother, R. Yehuda Leib. And there was a separate committee to lead the young married chassidim, headed by the Mitteler Rebbe.
translationNotes: דער עיקר איז סדר: “the main thing is order.” Kehot’s “crucial” is softer than עיקר.
יונגעלייט: young married men, not just “younger chassidim.”
עלטער זיידע: the Rebbe Rashab’s great-grandfather, the Alter Rebbe.

hayomYom.english: We find that G‑d's love for our father Avraham was mainly because "...he will command (yetzaveh) his children and his household." Yetzaveh here connotes "bring into a communion (with G‑d)." All of Avraham's towering avoda in the tests to which he was subjected, cannot be compared to his commanding others and bringing them into communion, i.e. to his bringing merit to others.
hayomYom.hebrew: מצינו דעיקר חבתו של הקב"ה [הקדוש ברוך הוא] לאברהם אע"ה [אבינו עליו השלום] הי'[ה] למען אשר יצוה - כפירושו יחבר - את בניו ואת ביתו. היינו דכל גודל עבודתו בהנסיונות אינו בערך לגבי הא דיצוה ויחבר אחרים, מה שיזכה אחרים.
hayomYom.clear:
We find that G‑d’s main fondness for our father Avraham was because “he will command his children and his household” (Bereishis 18:19). “Command” [yetzaveh] here means “join together” [with G‑d].

That is, all his great avoda in the tests he faced does not compare to commanding and joining others, bringing merit to others.
translationNotes: יצוה כפירושו יחבר: yetzaveh from tzavta, “joining.” Connects others to G‑d.
אינו בערך: “not in proportion,” beyond comparison.

hayomYom.english: The greatest guaranteed assurance (of Divine assistance) for all Jewish parents in need of special help and deliverance for their children is through their support of those who study Torah.
hayomYom.hebrew: אלע אידישע עלטערן וועלכע באדארפען האבען א ספעציעלע ישועה און הצלה פאר זייערע קינדער, איז דער זיכערסטער מיטעל צו שטיצען תורה לערנער.
hayomYom.clear: All Jewish parents who need a special salvation and rescue for their children: the surest means is to support those who learn Torah.
translationNotes: זיכערסטער מיטעל: “the surest means.” Kehot adds “guaranteed assurance (of Divine assistance)”; the Yiddish is simpler.
ישועה און הצלה: salvation and rescue.

hayomYom.english: In the early period of his leadership the Alter Rebbe taught: "The footsteps of man are directed by G‑d." When a Jew comes to a particular place it is for an (inner Divine) intent and purpose - to perform a mitzva, whether a mitzva between man and G‑d or a mitzva between man and his fellow-man. A Jew is G‑d's messenger. Wherever a messenger (shaliach) may be, he represents the power of the meshalei'ach, the one who sent him. The superior quality that souls possess, higher than the angels (who are also "messengers"), is that souls are messengers by virtue of Torah.
hayomYom.hebrew: רבינו הזקן בתחילת נשיאותו אמר תורה: מה' מצעדי גבר כוננו, אז א איד קומט אין א ארט, איז עס צוליב א כוונה טאן א מצוה, הן א מצוה שבין אדם למקום והן א מצוה שבין אדם לחבירו. א איד איז א שליח של מעלה, א שליח וואו ער איז, איז ער דער כח המשלח, דער יתרון המעלה אין נשמות לגבי מלאכים - וואס בא נשמות איז דאס על פי התורה.
hayomYom.clear:
Early in his leadership, the Alter Rebbe taught: “A man’s steps are set by G‑d” (Tehillim 37:23). When a Jew comes to a place, it is for a purpose: to do a mitzva, whether between man and G‑d or between man and his fellow.

A Jew is a messenger from Above. Wherever a messenger is, he is the power of the one who sent him. The advantage souls have over angels is that for souls, this is through the Torah.
translationNotes: אמר תורה: “said Torah,” delivered a teaching.
שליח וואו ער איז, איז ער דער כח המשלח: wherever the shliach is, he is the sender’s power, not just “represents” it.

hayomYom.english: In the Tanya edition published in Zolkvi in the year m'vasseir tov ("Herald of Good," numerically equivalent to 5559, or 1799), the first version of Igeret Hateshuva was printed. It was not divided into chapters and there are variances (from the present text) in content.
hayomYom.hebrew: בתניא דפוס זאלקווי שנת מבש"ר טו"ב, נדפסה אגרת התשובה מהדורא קמא, ולא נחלקה לפרקים, גם יש כמה שינוים בתוכן האגרת.
hayomYom.clear: In the Tanya printed in Zolkva in the year mevaser tov [“herald of good,” numerically 5559, 1799], the first edition of Iggeres HaTeshuva was printed. It was not divided into chapters, and there are several differences in the content of the Iggeres.
translationNotes: Matches the original. No meaning lost.

hayomYom.english: Birthday of the Rebbe, R. Yosef Yitzchak, in 5640 (1880). On this day, in 5687 (1927), he received the good tidings that he was freed from the exile imposed upon him after his arrest and imprisonment for his efforts in strengthening Torah and Judaism. From a letter of the Rebbe (R. Yosef Yitzchak): During the forthcoming two Days of Liberation 12 and 13 Tamuz, Chassidim are to farbreng, for material and spiritual good and blessing, as instituted by our first father, the Alter Rebbe (may the memory of this holy tzadik be a blessing for life in the Hereafter; his soul rests in the hidden exalted heights; may his merit protect us). During this farbrengen chassidim are to talk to one another in a spirit of brotherhood about strengthening fixed times for Torah study. I send them my blessing that G‑d favor them in body and spirit.
hayomYom.hebrew:
אין אומרים תחנון.

יום הולדת את כ"ק [כבוד קדושת] אדמו"ר [אדוננו מורנו ורבינו] שליט"א [שיחי'[ה] לימים טובים ארוכים] בשנת תר"ם. יום בו נתבשר - בשנת תרפ"ז - שהוא חפשי מגלותו אשר הגלה - אחרי שהיה תפוס במאסר - על עבודתו בחיזוק התורה והיהדות.

ממכתב כ"ק [כבוד קדושת] אדמו"ר [אדוננו מורנו ורבנו] שליט"א [שיחיה לימים טובים ארוכים]: בשני ימי הגאולה י"ב וי"ג תמוז הבע"ל [הבאים עלינו לטובה] יתועדו אנ"ש [אנשי שלומינו], לטובה ולברכה בגשמיות וברוחניות, כאשר הוקבע מאת אבינו הראשון הוד כ"ק [כבוד קדושת] אאזמו"ר [אדוני אבי זקני מורי ורבי] רבינו הזקן זצוקללה"ה [זכר צדיק וקדוש לברכה לחיי העולם הבא] נבג"מ [נשמתו בגנזי מרומים] זי"ע [זכותו יגן עלינו]. בהתועדות זו ידברו אנ"ש [אנשי שלומינו] שיחיו איש את רעהו בשבת אחים בחיזוק קביעות שיעורי הלמוד, והנני שולח להם את ברכתי כי ישא השם פניו אליהם בגו"ר [בגשמיות ורוחניות].
hayomYom.clear:
Birthday of the Rebbe shlita [the Rebbe Rayatz], in 5640 [1880]. On this day, in 5687 [1927], he received word that he was freed from the exile he had been sent to, after being imprisoned, for his work in strengthening Torah and Judaism.

From a letter of the Rebbe shlita:

On the two days of Redemption, 12 and 13 Tammuz, coming upon us for good, our fellow chassidim should farbreng, for good and for blessing in physical and spiritual matters, as established by our first father, my holy forebear the Alter Rebbe, may the memory of the holy tzaddik be for blessing in the World to Come, his soul is in the treasuries on high, may his merit protect us.

At this farbrengen, our fellow chassidim should speak with one another, as brothers sitting together, about strengthening fixed times for study. I send them my blessing that G‑d turn His face to them, in body and in spirit.
translationNotes: שבת אחים: “brothers sitting together” (Tehillim 133:1). Kehot’s “spirit of brotherhood” loses the verse.
ישא השם פניו: “may G‑d lift His face” toward them, from the Priestly Blessing.

calendar.original5703: No tachanun.

hayomYom.english: On this day the Rebbe (R. Yosef Yitzchak) was actually freed. The imprisonment began at 2:15 a.m. on Wednesday, Sivan 15, 5687 (June 15, 1927). He remained in exile - in the town of Kostrama - until one half-hour past mid-day, Wednesday, Tamuz 13, 5687 (July 13, 1927). From a letter of the Rebbe to mark the Festival of his Liberation: "I send you a maamar ...which is my participation - for their success - with my beloved friends the chassidim wherever they reside, (which is my way of) being united with you in your farbrengen for the purpose of strengthening the practices of Chassidus, in fixing and observing periods for studying Chassidus and to be stimulated to pragmatically implement those studies... May our G‑d and G‑d of our Fathers bless the whole community of chassidim - them, their households, their children and grandchildren among all our brothers the people of Israel (G‑d grant them eternal life) with all good things of soul and of flesh."
hayomYom.hebrew:
אין אומרים תחנון.

יום בו יצא כ"ק [כבוד קדושת] אדמו"ר [אדוננו מורנו ורבינו] שליט"א [שיחיה לימים טובים ארוכים] לחרות.

המאסר הותחל רבע על שעה השלישית אור ליום רביעי חמשה עשר בסיון תרפ"ז. התעכב בגלות - בעיר קאסטראמא - עד חצי שעה אחר חצות היום יום רביעי שלשה עשר בתמוז תרפ"ז.

ממכתב כ"ק [כבוד קדושת] אדמו"ר [אדוננו מורנו ורבינו] שליט"א [שיחיה לימים טובים ארוכים] לחג הגאולה: הנני שולח מאמר... השתתפותי עם ידידנו אנ"ש [אנשי שלומינו] שיחיו בכל מקום מושבותיכם להצלחה, ולהיות אתכם עמכם בהתועדותכם בדבר חיזוק דרכי החסידות בקביעות ושמירת זמני למודי דא"ח [דברי אלקים חיים] ולהתעורר בקיום עניני הלימוד... אלקינו ואלקי אבותינו יברך את כללות אנ"ש [אנשי שלומינו] הם ביתם זרעם וזרע זרעם בתוך כלל אחינו בני ישראל, השם עליהם יחיו, בכל מילי דמיטב מנפש ועד בשר.
hayomYom.clear:
The day the Rebbe shlita [the Rebbe Rayatz] went out to freedom.

The arrest began at a quarter past two in the night before Wednesday, 15 Sivan 5687 [1927]. He was held in exile, in the city of Kostroma, until half an hour past midday, Wednesday, 13 Tammuz 5687.

From a letter of the Rebbe shlita for the Festival of Redemption:

I am sending a maamar... my participation with our friends, the chassidim, wherever you live, for success, and to be with you at your farbrengen about strengthening the ways of Chassidus: setting and keeping times for the study of Chassidus, and being stirred to carry out what you learn... May our G‑d and the G‑d of our fathers bless all our fellow chassidim, them, their households, their children and their children’s children, among all our brothers the Children of Israel, may G‑d grant them life, with all good things, from soul to flesh.
translationNotes: אור ליום רביעי: “the night of Wednesday,” i.e. 2:15 a.m. Wednesday. Kehot’s civil dates (June 15, July 13, 1927) are not in the original; left out.
יצא לחרות: “went out to freedom.”
דא"ח: Divrei Elokim Chayim, the words of the living G‑d, i.e. Chassidus.

calendar.original5703: No tachanun.

hayomYom.english: The Tzemach Tzedek notes in one of his discourses: "On Tuesday of parshat Balak 5562 (1802) our master, of blessed memory, said to his sons as follows: To understand the problem posed by the astronomers, that since the earth is round and spherical like an apple, why do not those people fall who live on the side of the globe opposite to ours, 'down below,' in America?... Their answer is not the true one... Our master,1 of blessed memory, said that the answer lies in explanation of the Etz Chaim that the Nine Spheres are nurtured by that state termed igulim, 'Circles,' and in a circle there is no above or below. For this reason those who live opposite us, 'down below,' have their heavens high above them arching in one continuity with the heaven above us, and the earth there is below, relative to the heavens over it."
hayomYom.hebrew: ז"ל [זה לשון] הצ"צ [הצמח צדק] באחד מדרושיו: רבינו ז"ל [זכרונו לברכה] באמרותיו לבניו יום ג' פרשת בלק שנת תקס"ב אמר וזה דבריו: להבין קושית התוכנים מאחר שהארץ היא כדורית ועגולה כתפוח למה אינם נופלים אותם בני אדם הדרים כנגדינו מלמטה באמעריקא... ותירוצם אינו אמת... ורבינו ז"ל [זכרונו לברכה] אמר כי התירוץ הוא, דהנה מבואר בע"ח [בעץ חיים] שהתשעה גלגלים מקבלים מבחינת עיגולים, ובהעיגול אין בו מעלה ומטה, ומהאי טעמא הנה אותם בני אדם שהם כנגדנו למטה, הרי הרקיע שעליהם הוא למעלה בהשואה אחת עם הרקיע שעלינו, והארץ דשם היא מטה לגבי הרקיע שעליה.
hayomYom.clear:
The Tzemach Tzedek writes in one of his discourses:

Our Rebbe [the Alter Rebbe], of blessed memory, said to his sons on Tuesday of parshas Balak 5562 [1802], in these words:

To understand the astronomers’ question: since the earth is round and spherical like an apple, why do the people who live opposite us, below, in America, not fall off?... Their answer is not true...

Our Rebbe, of blessed memory, said that the answer is this. It is explained in Etz Chaim that the nine spheres receive from the level of igulim [circles], and a circle has no above or below. For this reason, the people opposite us, below, have the sky above them, level with the sky above us. And the earth there is below relative to the sky over it.
translationNotes: בהשואה אחת: “in one equal relation,” the sky there stands exactly as ours does.
Kehot’s English carries a stray footnote marker “1” after “Our master.” Removed.

hayomYom.english: My father writes in one of his maamarim: Fatness of the body can result from the spiritual pleasure and delight derived from G‑dliness. They say of R. Nachum of Chernobil that he became corpulent from answering amein y'hei sh'mei raba.
hayomYom.hebrew: אאמו"ר [אדוני אבי מורי ורבי] כותב באחד ממאמריו: תענוג נפשי על אלקות יכול להיות מזה שמנונית בגוף. אומרים על הר"נ [הרב ר' נחום] מטשרנאביל שהיה שמן בגופו מענית אמן יש"ר [יהא שמיה רבא].
hayomYom.clear: My father [the Rebbe Rashab] writes in one of his maamarim: Pleasure of the soul in G‑dliness can make the body fat. They say of R. Nachum of Chernobyl that he was fat in body from answering amen, yehei shmei raba.
translationNotes: תענוג נפשי: pleasure of the soul. Kehot adds “and delight.”
Matches the original otherwise. No meaning lost.

hayomYom.english: The Baal Shem Tov's ahavat yisrael (love of fellow Jew) was beyond imagination. The Maggid said: If only we could kiss a sefer-Torah with the same love that my Master kissed the children when he took them to cheder as a teacher's assistant!
hayomYom.hebrew:
אהבת ישראל של הבעש"ט [הבעל שם טוב] - אין לשער.

הרב המגיד אמר: הלואי היו נושקים הס"ת [הספר תורה] באותה האהבה, שהי'[ה] מורי מנשק את הילדים בהוליכו אותם אל ה"חדר" כשהי'[ה] "באהעלפער".
hayomYom.clear:
The Baal Shem Tov’s ahavas Yisrael was beyond measure.

The Maggid said: If only we would kiss a Sefer Torah with the same love with which my teacher kissed the children when he took them to cheder, when he was a belfer [teacher’s helper].
translationNotes: אין לשער: “cannot be estimated,” beyond measure.
באהעלפער: a belfer, the assistant who walked children to and from cheder.

hayomYom.english: The difference between the first tablets (of the Ten Commandments) and the second: In the tablets proper: The first were the "work of G‑d" but the second, "hew for yourself." In the script: According to the sages in Eiruvin 54a, only the first ones had (the spiritual quality described by the words) "engraved on the tablets." In the spiritual standing of the people Israel: When the first were given, they were tzadikim, for as they stood at Mt. Sinai "their defilement came to an end." But at the second tablets they were baalei teshuva, repentants. In the spiritual standing of Moshe: When the Torah was given, Moshe received one thousand "lights" as a gift; with the sin of the Golden Calf these were taken from him and were not restored with the second tablets (except on Shabbat, as stated in P'ri Eitz Chaim). The second tablets, however, did have this superior quality: That they were given along with halachot (laws), midrash and aggadot, etc., a "double gift of Torah-wisdom," as explained in Nedarim 22b. Also, at the second, Moshe's face shone with rays of light.
hayomYom.hebrew:
תענית, סליחות, אבינו מלכנו.

חלוק לוחות הראשונות ולוחות האחרונות:

בלוחות עצמן - הראשונות מעשה אלקים, השניות פסל לך. המכתב - חרות על הלוחות שכדרז"ל [שכדרשת רבותינו זכרונם לברכה] עירובין [נד. א] הוא רק בלוחה"ר [בלוחות הראשונות]. במעלת בני ישראל - בלוחה"ר [בלוחות הראשונות] צדיקים, כשעמדו על הר סיני פסקה זוהמתן, בשניות בעלי תשובה. במעלת משה - במתן תורה ניתן למשה אלף אורות במתנה, ובחטא העגל ניטלו ממנו ולא חזרו בלוחות שניות [רק בשבת נותנים לו כדאיתא בפע"ח [בפרי עץ חיים]. מעלת לוחה"ש [לוחות השניות] שניתן ג"כ [גם כן] הלכות מדרש אגדות כו', כפלים לתושי'[ה] כדאיתא בנדרים [כב. ב], וקירון עור פני משה.
hayomYom.clear:
Differences between the first tablets and the second:

The tablets themselves: the first were “the work of G‑d” (Shemos 32:16). The second: “carve for yourself” (Shemos 34:1).

The writing: “engraved on the tablets,” as the Sages taught (Eruvin 54a), was only on the first tablets.

The level of the Jewish people: at the first tablets they were tzaddikim, since when they stood at Mount Sinai their impurity ended. At the second, they were baalei teshuva.

The level of Moshe: at the giving of the Torah, Moshe was given a thousand lights as a gift. With the sin of the Golden Calf they were taken from him, and they did not return with the second tablets [only on Shabbos are they given to him, as stated in Pri Etz Chaim].

The advantage of the second tablets: they also came with halacha, midrash and aggada, and so on, “double the wisdom” (Iyov 11:6), as stated in Nedarim 22b. And the skin of Moshe’s face shone.
translationNotes: פסקה זוהמתן: “their impurity ceased” (Shabbos 146a).
קירון עור פני משה: “the skin of Moshe’s face shone” (Shemos 34:29). Kehot drops “skin.”

calendar.original5703: Fast day. Selichos. Avinu Malkeinu.

hayomYom.english: The Alter Rebbe said of R. Moshe Vilenker: "Moshe has mochin d'gadlut, magnitude of intellect and in his ten years of toil, he has attained through his labors a powerful, capacious, wide-ranging intellectuality - (mochin rechavim)." For three years R. Moshe Vilenker prepared himself for yechidus with the Alter Rebbe. Afterwards he remained in Lyozna for seven years to translate the yechidus into actual avoda.
hayomYom.hebrew:
דער אלטער רבי האט געזאגט אויף ר' משה ווילענקער: משה האט מוחין דגדלות, און אין די צען יאר וואס ער האט געהארעוועט, האט ער אויסגעהארעוועט מוחין רחבים.

דריי יאר האט ר' משה ווילענקער זיך מכין געווען צו יחידות באם אלטען רבי'ן, און נאכדעם איז ער געבליבען זיבען יאר אין ליאזנא אויף בריינגען די יחידות אין עבודה בפועל.
hayomYom.clear:
The Alter Rebbe said of R. Moshe Vilenker: Moshe has mochin d’gadlus [expansive mind], and in the ten years he toiled, he toiled his way to mochin rechavim [broad mind].

For three years R. Moshe Vilenker prepared himself for a yechidus with the Alter Rebbe. Afterward he stayed seven years in Lyozna to bring the yechidus into actual avoda.
translationNotes: געהארעוועט / אויסגעהארעוועט: hard, sweating labor, and “earned through hard labor.” The doubled verb is the point.
Kehot pads mochin rechavim with “powerful, capacious, wide-ranging intellectuality.” The original is just mochin rechavim.

hayomYom.english: A practice of my father's: When travelling, even when spending months in one place, he would recite t'filat haderech, the prayer for travellers (p. 86) daily after davening, omitting G‑d's name in the conclusion.
hayomYom.hebrew: מהנהגות אאמו"ר [אדוני אבי מורי ורבי]: כשנסע מביתו, אף שנשאר במקום אחד כמה חדשים. הי'[ה] אומר בכל יום אחר התפלה תפלת הדרך - בלא שם ומלכות.
hayomYom.clear: One of my father’s [the Rebbe Rashab’s] practices: when he traveled away from home, even if he stayed in one place for several months, he would say Tefillas HaDerech [the traveler’s prayer] every day after davening, without G‑d’s Name and Kingship.
translationNotes: בלא שם ומלכות: without G‑d’s Name and Kingship, i.e. with no blessing formula. Kehot says only “omitting G‑d’s name in the conclusion.”
Kehot adds a siddur page (p. 86) not in the original.

hayomYom.english: There are three forms of hitbon'nut (contemplation, meditation): (a.) Study-meditation: After mastering the concept thoroughly, one meditates on its profundity, until the intellectual element shines forth for him. (b.) Meditation before davening: This is directed toward sensing the vitality of the concept learned, in contrast to sensing the intellectual element emphasized in study-meditation. (c.) Meditation in davening: To sense the "G‑dly element" in the concept learned. These three are rungs on the ladder of sensitivity. It is only by G‑d's kindness towards us that we may occasionally sense G‑dhood spontaneously, without any avoda at all. This comes about by virtue of the quality of Ultimate Essential G‑dhood within the soul. For avoda by one's own efforts, however, these three forms of meditation are essential.
hayomYom.hebrew: שלשה מיני התבוננות הם: א) התבוננות למודית, אחר שמבין הענין על בוריו, הוא מתבונן בעומק הענין ההוא, עד שהשכלי מאיר אצלו. ב) שקודם התפלה, ענינה הרגש חיות הענין שלמד ולא הרגש השכלי כמו בהתבוננות למודית. ג) שבתפלה, ענינה הרגש האלקות שבהענין שלמד. שלש אלה הם שליבות סולם ההרגשה ורק בחסדי השי"ת [השם יתברך] עמנו מרגישים לפעמים - דערהערט מען - ג-טליכקייט בלי שום עבודה כלל, והוא מפני מעלת העצמות שיש בנשמה, אבל מצד העבודה שבכח עצמו מוכרחים שלש הנ"ל [הנזכרים לעיל].
hayomYom.clear:
There are three kinds of hisbonenus [contemplation]:

1. Study contemplation. After you understand the idea thoroughly, you contemplate its depth until the intellect of it shines for you.

2. Contemplation before davening. Its point is to feel the life of the idea you learned, not to feel its intellect as in study contemplation.

3. Contemplation in davening. Its point is to feel the G‑dliness in the idea you learned.

These three are rungs of the ladder of feeling. Only by G‑d’s kindness to us do we sometimes feel, “sense,” G‑dliness without any avoda at all. That comes from the quality of the Essence that is in the soul. But as far as avoda by your own strength goes, these three are a must.
translationNotes: דערהערט מען: the Yiddish “one senses,” inserted mid-sentence for an inner, direct perception.
מעלת העצמות שיש בנשמה: the Essence of G‑d present in the soul.

hayomYom.english: We do not say she’he’cheyanu during the Three Weeks, even on Shabbat. It is written: They shall make Me a sanctuary and I shall dwell within them. “Within them” means within every one of Israel. For within every Jew, the core point of the heart’s inner essence is a sanctuary for His dwelling (may He be blessed). The site of the sanctuary remains sacred, even in times of exile and desolation. In Midrash Sh’mot Raba Chapter 2, R. Acha says: “The Shechina (Divine Presence) never departs from the Western Wall.” All the desolation is limited to the buildings. So, too, is the case with the personal sanctuary within each of Israel; the foundation is whole, clear and pure, as it is written, I am asleep but my heart is alert. Midrash Raba comments: “I am asleep for mitzvot, but my heart is alert for acts of kindness; I am asleep for charities, but my heart is alert to perform them.” Every form of (spiritual) desolation (may G‑d rescue us from such) found in the people Israel is only in those aspects of the people analagous to buildings above the foundation. The foundation of the individual sanctuary, however, remains in its holy state.
hayomYom.hebrew:
אין מברכים שהחיינו בין המצרים ואפילו בשבת.

כתיב ועשו לי מקדש ושכנתי בתוכם בתוך כאו"א [כל אחד ואחד] מישראל, שבכאו"א [שבכל אחד ואחד] מישראל תוכיות נקודת פנימית לבבו הוא מקדש לשבתו יתברך. והנה מקום המקדש גם בזמן הגלות והשימום קדוש הוא. וכדאיתא בשמות רבה פ"ב [פרשה ב'] א"ר [אמר רב] אחא לעולם אין השכינה זזה מכותל המערבי. וכל ענין השימום הוא בהבנינים, וכן הוא גם במקדש הפרטי שבכאו"א [שבכל אחד ואחד] מישראל, דהיסוד הוא שלם זך וטהור וכמ"ש [וכמו שכתוב] אני ישנה ולבי ער, ואיתא במד"ר [במדרש רבה] אני ישנה מן המצות ולבי ער לגמ"ח [לגמילות חסדים] אני ישנה מן הצדקות ולבי ער לעשותן, דכל ענין השימום, ר"ל [רחמנא ליצלן], שישנו בישראל הוא רק בדוגמת הבנינים שמחוץ להיסוד, אבל היסוד דמקדש הפרטי הוא בקדושתו.
hayomYom.clear:
We do not say the blessing Shehecheyanu during the Three Weeks, even on Shabbos.

It is written: “They shall make Me a Sanctuary, and I will dwell within them” (Shemos 25:8). Within each and every Jew. In every Jew, the innermost point of the heart is a Sanctuary for G‑d’s dwelling.

Now, the site of the Sanctuary remains holy even in the time of exile and desolation. As it says in Shemos Rabba, chapter 2: R. Acha said, “The Shechina never moves from the Western Wall.” All the desolation is in the buildings.

So too with the personal Sanctuary in every Jew. The foundation is whole, clean and pure. As it is written, “I am asleep, but my heart is awake” (Shir HaShirim 5:2). The Midrash Rabba says: “I am asleep from the mitzvos, but my heart is awake to acts of kindness. I am asleep from tzedaka, but my heart is awake to do it.”

All the desolation, G‑d save us, found among Jews is only like the buildings outside the foundation. But the foundation of the personal Sanctuary stays in its holiness.
translationNotes: תוכיות נקודת פנימית לבבו: “the inside of the inner point of his heart,” three layers of inwardness.
שמחוץ להיסוד: “outside the foundation.” Kehot’s “above the foundation” shifts the image a little.

hayomYom.english: My father said: A chassidic aphorism makes the head clear and the heart clean; a chassidic virtuous practice fills the home with light; a chassidic melody fortifies hope and trust, brings joyousness, and places the home and family in a state of "light."
hayomYom.hebrew: אאמו"ר [אדוני אבי מורי ורבי] אמר: א חסידישער ווארט מאכט קלאר די קאפ און ריין די הארץ. א חסידישע הנהגה טובה מאכט ליכטיג אין שטוב. א חסידעשער ניגון שטארקט די תקוה ובטחון בריינגט שמחה און שטעלט אוועק די הויז מיט דער הויז געזינד אין קרן אורה.
hayomYom.clear: My father [the Rebbe Rashab] said: A chassidic saying makes the head clear and the heart clean. A good chassidic practice makes the home bright. A chassidic niggun strengthens hope and trust, brings joy, and sets the house and the whole household in a ray of light.
translationNotes: ווארט: a vort, a short teaching or saying.
קרן אורה: “a ray of light.” Kehot’s “a state of light” is flatter.

hayomYom.english: When Matot and Massai are separate, then on Shabbat at Mincha, as well as on Monday and Thursday, the Levi-aliya ends with the last journey.
hayomYom.hebrew: כאשר מטות ומסעי נפרדות קורין - במנחת שבת, ב', ה' - ללוי עד סוף כל המסעות.
hayomYom.clear: When Matos and Masei are read separately, at Shabbos Mincha and on Monday and Thursday, the Levi’s aliya goes until the end of all the journeys.
translationNotes: Matches the original. No meaning lost.

hayomYom.english: From the Tzemach Tzedek's aphorisms: For the p'nimi ("inward" person), asking for a blessing for avoda epitomizes, "Let them not pay attention to vain words." What is needed is to "make the avoda heavy on the people."
hayomYom.hebrew: מפתגמי הצ"צ [הצמח צדק]: א פנימי איז, אז בעטען א ברכה אויף עבודה איז דאס אל ישעו בדברי הבל, און עס דארף זיין תכבד העבודה על האנשים.
hayomYom.clear: From the Tzemach Tzedek’s sayings: For a pnimi [an inward person], asking for a blessing for avoda is “let them not pay attention to empty words.” What is needed is “let the work be heavy on the men” (Shemos 5:9).
translationNotes: The quote is Pharaoh’s order in Shemos 5:9, turned on its head: avoda is your own heavy work, not something to get by blessing.
דברי הבל: “empty words.” The verse itself reads דברי שקר.

hayomYom.english: There are two characteristic expressions in Chassidus: (a) A Jew recognizes G‑dliness and senses the supra-natural. He needs no proofs for these. (b) A Jew neither wants nor is able to be sundered from G‑dliness. The truth is that these two expressions are one and the same: A Jew recognizes G‑dliness and senses the higher-than-natural, and that is why he neither wants nor can he be torn away from G‑dliness.
hayomYom.hebrew:
אין חסידות איז פאראן צוויי זייער כאראקטעריסטישע אויסשפראכען: א) א איד דערקענט ג-טליכקייט און פילט די איבערנאטירליכקייט און בעדארף אויף דעם קיין באווייזען ניט האבען. ב) א איד ניט ער וויל און ניט ער קען זיין אפגעריסען פון ג-טליכקייט.

דער אמת איז אז די צוויי אויסשפראכין זיינען איין זאך: א איד דערקענט ג-טליכקייט און פילט דעם למעלה מן הטבע, דערפאר איז ניט ער וויל ניט ער קען זיין אפגעריסען פון ג-טליכקייט.
hayomYom.clear:
Chassidus has two very characteristic expressions:

1. A Jew recognizes G‑dliness and feels the supernatural, and needs no proofs for it.

2. A Jew neither wants to nor can be torn away from G‑dliness.

The truth is that these two expressions are one thing. A Jew recognizes G‑dliness and feels what is above nature. That is why he neither wants to nor can be torn away from G‑dliness.
translationNotes: אפגעריסען: “torn away,” a violent image. Kehot’s “sundered” is close.
Matches the original. No meaning lost.

hayomYom.english: In Torah-study the person is devoted to the subject that he wishes to understand and comes to understand. In davening the devotion is directed to what surpasses understanding. In learning Torah the Jew feels like a pupil with his master; in davening - like a child with his father.
hayomYom.hebrew:
אין לערנען איז די איבערגעגעבענקייט פון מענטשען צו א זאך, וועלכע ער וויל פארשטיין און פארשטייט. אין דאוונען איז די איבערגעגעבענקייט צו העכער ווי פארשטאנד.

אין לערנען תורה פילט זיך א איד ווי א תלמיד בא א רבי'ן, אין דאוונען - ווי א קינד בא א פאטער.
hayomYom.clear:
In learning, a person is devoted to something he wants to understand, and does understand. In davening, the devotion is to what is higher than understanding.

When learning Torah, a Jew feels like a student with his Rebbe. In davening, like a child with his father.
translationNotes: איבערגעגעבענקייט: devotedness, being given over.
Matches the original. No meaning lost.

hayomYom.english: A brilliant and renowned scholar, exceptionally gifted and remarkably profound in his studies, came to Lyozna and threw himself into the study of Chassidus. With his powerful intellectual propensity he amassed - within a short time - a great and broad knowledge in Chassidus. At his first yechidus with the Alter Rebbe, he asked: "Rebbe, what do I lack?" The Rebbe replied: "You lack nothing, for you are G‑d-fearing and a scholar. You do need, however, to rid yourself of the chametz - which is awareness of self, and arrogance - and to bring in matza, which is bitul, renunciation of self." An "implement" (such as a roasting-spit) may have been used with yeshut, awareness of self; the person imagines himself to be "light." Such pride repels the Shechina (G‑d's presence), for "he and (G‑d) cannot dwell together." That implement (or vessel, i.e. person) needs purging through such intense white heat that the "sparks" of the birurim (purification) fly out and are absorbed in the true light."
hayomYom.hebrew:
אחד מהעילוים המפורסמים בעל כשרון גדול ועמקן נפלא בא לליאזנא ושקד בלימוד החסידות, ובגודל כשרונותיו רכש לו במשך זמן קצר ידיעה גדולה ורחבה בתורת החסידות.

ביחידות הראשונה שנכנס לרבינו הזקן שאל: רבי מה חסר לי? ויענהו רבינו הזקן: אין חסר לך מאומה, כי ירא אלקים אתה ולמדן, רק צריך אתה להוציא את החמץ שהוא הישות וגסות הרוח, ולהכניס מצה שהוא ביטול. וכלי שנשתמש בו בישות שנדמה לו שהוא אור כגון שפודין, שדוחקין רגלי השכינה, דאין אני והוא יכולין לדור, צריך ליבון. והליבון הוא עד שיהיו הניצוצות דהבירורים ניתזין ונכללין בהאור האמיתי.
hayomYom.clear:
One of the famous prodigies, very talented and wonderfully deep, came to Lyozna and threw himself into studying Chassidus. With his great abilities, in a short time he gained a great and broad knowledge of Chassidus.

At his first yechidus with the Alter Rebbe, he asked: “Rebbe, what am I missing?”

The Alter Rebbe answered: “You are missing nothing, because you fear G‑d and you are a scholar. You only need to take out the chametz, which is yeshus [self-importance] and arrogance, and bring in matza, which is bittul [self-nullification].

“A vessel that was used with yeshus, where you imagine you are light, like spits [roasting spits], pushes away the feet of the Shechina, since ‘I and he cannot dwell together’ (Sotah 5a). It needs libun [purging by fire]. And the libun must go until the sparks of the birurim [refined elements] fly out and merge into the true light.”
translationNotes: שפודין and ליבון: kashering law. A roasting spit used for chametz must be heated red-hot. The Rebbe applies it to the ego.
דוחקין רגלי השכינה: “pushes away the feet of the Shechina” (Berachos 43b). Kehot’s “repels” drops the image.

hayomYom.english: Bless Rosh Chodesh Menachem-Av. Say all the Tehillim in the early morning. Day of farbrengen. Haftora: Shimu until elokecha Yehuda; then, Im tashuv until uvo yit'halalu. Each of the Rebbe'im had maamarim designated especially for the purpose of purifying the atmosphere. Every two or three years they would review and recite them publicly. One of (these special) maamarim of the Alter Rebbe was Hechaltzu printed in Likutei Torah (without the glosses). One of the Mitteler Rebbe's was Yafa sha'a achat; (its subject was the first ten chapters of the maamar Hinei kol echad v'echad in Derech Hachayim). One of the Tzemach Tzedek's was Ma tovu, printed in Likutei Torah. One of my grandfather's (the Rebbe Maharash) was Mi chamocha. One of my father's was V'yadata hayom, Moscow - 5657.
hayomYom.hebrew: לכל אחד מהרביים היו מאמרים קבועים ביחוד בשביל זה [לטהר אויר העולם], אשר פעם בשתים או בשלש שנים היו חוזרים עליהם ברבים. אחד ממאמרי רבינו הזקן - החלצו שבלקו"ת [שבלקוטי תורה] בלי ההגהות. אחד ממאמרי אדמו"ר [אדוננו מורנו ורבנו] האמצעי - יפה שעה אחת, ותוכנו עשרה פרקים הראשונים דד"ה [דדיבור המתחיל] הנה כאו"א [כל אחד ואחד] אומר אלקי נשמה בדרה"ח [בדרך החיים]. אחד ממאמרי הצ"צ [הצמח צדק] - מה טובו שבלקו"ת [שבלקוטי תורה]. אחד ממאמרי אאזמו"ר [אדוני אבי זקני מורי ורבי] - מי כמוכה באלים. אחד ממאמרי אאמו"ר [אדוני אבי מורי ורבי] - וידעת היום מאסקווא רנ"ז.
hayomYom.clear:
Each of the Rebbeim had set maamarim especially for this purpose [purifying the air of the world]. Every two or three years they would review them in public.

One of the Alter Rebbe's maamarim: Hechaltzu, in Likkutei Torah, without the glosses.

One of the Mitteler Rebbe's: Yafah sha'ah achas. Its content is the first ten chapters of the maamar Hinei kol echad v'echad omer Elokai neshamah, in Derech Chaim.

One of the Tzemach Tzedek's: Mah tovu, in Likkutei Torah.

One of my grandfather's [the Rebbe Maharash]: Mi chamocha ba'eilim.

One of my father's [the Rebbe Rashab]: V'yadata hayom, Moscow 5657 [1897].
translationNotes: בשביל זה [לטהר אויר העולם]: 'for this purpose,' purifying the air of the world. It links back to the previous day's entry.
קבועים ביחוד: set and fixed specifically for this, not just 'designated.'
Kehot shortens the full titles (אלקי נשמה, מי כמוכה באלים). Restored.

calendar.original5703: Shabbos Mevarchim Menachem Av. Say the whole Tehillim early in the morning. A day of farbrengen. Haftorah: Shim'u, to Elokayich Yehudah; then Im tashuv, to uvo yis'halalu.

hayomYom.dataFlag: Hebrew field lacks the calendar line (Shabbos Mevarchim, Tehillim, farbrengen, haftorah); cal taken from the Kehot English.

hayomYom.english: A handwritten note of the Tzemach Tzedek was discovered. Its contents: He had determined to study Talmudic and Halachic texts six hours every night, standing. He had, thank G‑d, fulfilled this and completed the study of the entire Talmud (Babylonian and Jerusalemite) and the four divisions of the Shulchan Aruch - all studied in depth.
hayomYom.hebrew: מצאו פתקא כי"ק [כתב יד קודש] הצ"צ [הצמח צדק] ותוכנה, שהחליט ללמוד בכל יום שש שעות בלילה בעמידה נגלה, ות"ל [ותודה לא-ל] שקיים ועבר על ש"ס בבלי וירושלמי וארבעה חלקי שלחן ערוך בעיון.
hayomYom.clear:
A note in the Tzemach Tzedek's holy handwriting was found. Its content: he had resolved to study nigleh [the revealed Torah: Talmud and halacha] six hours every night, standing.

And, thank G‑d, he kept it, and went through the entire Talmud, Bavli and Yerushalmi, and all four sections of the Shulchan Aruch, in depth.
translationNotes: כתב יד קודש: 'holy handwriting.' Kehot just says 'handwritten.'
עבר על: 'went through,' a complete pass over the material.

hayomYom.english: The unique quality of Mashiach is that he will be humble. Though he will be the ultimate in greatness, for he will teach Torah to the Patriarchs and to Moshe Rabeinu (alav hashalom), still he will be the ultimate in humility and self-nullification, for he will also teach simple folk.
hayomYom.hebrew: מעלת המשיח שיהי'[ה] עניו, דהגם שיהי'[ה] בתכלית הגדלות, וילמוד תורה עם האבות ומרע"ה [ומשה רבינו עליו השלום], בכל זה יהי'[ה] בתכלית הענוה והביטול ללמוד גם עם אנשים פשוטים.
hayomYom.clear:
The special quality of Mashiach is that he will be humble.

He will be at the height of greatness, for he will learn Torah with the Avos [Patriarchs] and with Moshe Rabbeinu, peace be upon him. Even so, he will be at the height of humility and bittul [self-nullification], and will learn with simple people too.
translationNotes: ילמוד תורה עם: 'learn Torah with,' studying together. Kehot's 'teach' is the sense but loses the togetherness.
בתכלית: 'the utmost,' used for both greatness and humility, deliberately parallel.

hayomYom.english: A directive for all: A boy begins putting on tefillin two months before his Bar Mitzva; at first without the b'racha, then a few weeks later with the b'racha.
hayomYom.hebrew: הוראה לרבים: מתחילין להניח תפילין שני חדשים קודם הבר מצוה. בתחלה בלא ברכה וכעבור איזה שבועות בברכה.
hayomYom.clear: A directive for everyone: A boy begins putting on tefillin two months before his bar mitzvah. At first without a bracha [blessing], and after a few weeks with the bracha.
translationNotes: Matches the original. No meaning lost.

hayomYom.english: From my father's sichot: When Mashiach will come (speedily in our time, amein), then we shall really long for the days of the exile. Then we will truly feel distress at our having neglected working at avoda; then will we indeed feel the deep pain caused by our lack of avoda. These days of exile are the days of avoda, to prepare ourselves for the coming of Mashiach, speedily in our time, amein.
hayomYom.hebrew: משיחת אאמו"ר [אדוני אבי מורי ורבי]: יעמאלט ווען משיח וועט קומען בב"א [במהרה בימינו אמן] וועט מען ערשט ביינקען נאך די גלות טעג. יעמאלט וועט ערשט פארדריסען פאר וואס מ'האט ניט געטאן אין עבודה. מען וועט ערשט דערהערען דעם גרויסען ווייטאג פון העדר העבודה. איצטער אין די ימי הגלות, איז די ימי העבודה צו מכין זיין זיך צו ביאת המשיח בב"א [במהרה בימינו אמן].
hayomYom.clear:
From my father's [the Rebbe Rashab's] sichos [talks]:

When Mashiach comes, speedily in our days, amen, only then will we truly long for the days of exile. Only then will we regret that we did not do our avoda [divine service]. Only then will we feel the great pain of having lacked avoda.

Now, in the days of exile, are the days of avoda: to prepare ourselves for the coming of Mashiach, speedily in our days, amen.
translationNotes: ערשט: 'only then,' said three times. The point is that the realization comes later, when it is too late. Kehot's 'really/truly/indeed' blurs this.
בענקען נאך: to long for, a homesick yearning.
פארדריסען: to vex, to feel regret. Stronger than 'distress.'

hayomYom.english: No matter how much effort is exerted, no-one can earn one cent more than G‑d has ordained that he - this particular person - shall earn. One must do what is necessary, but one must remember that all his work is but an adjunct. The main thing is G‑d's blessing, and that blessing is earned by being observant of G‑d's commands: Davening with a minyan, observing Shabbat b'hidur (beyond the minimum, with "beauty"), meticulous observance of kashrut, having children instructed by sincerely religious teachers.
hayomYom.hebrew: מיט דער גרעסטער הארעוואניע קען מען ניט פארדינען קיין איין סענט מעהר וויפיל השי"ת [השם יתברך] האט אפגעשטעלט, אז דער און דער מענש זאל פארדינען. מען בעדארף טאן וויפיל עס איז נויטיג, אבער מען מוז געדיינקען, אז די גאנצע ארבעט, איז מער ניט ווי א טפל, דער עיקר איז די ברכה פון השי"ת [השם יתברך], און די ברכה פארדינט מען ווען מען איז א ערליכער איד: תפלה בצבור, שמירת שבת בהידור, כשרות בהשגחה גדולה, חינוך הבנים בא מלמדים ערליכע אידען.
hayomYom.clear:
Even with the hardest toil, you cannot earn a single cent more than G‑d has set for this particular person to earn.

You must do as much as is necessary. But you must remember that all the work is nothing more than secondary. The main thing is G‑d's blessing.

And you earn the blessing by being an ehrlicher Yid [a sincerely observant Jew]: davening with a minyan, keeping Shabbos b'hiddur [beautifully, beyond the minimum], kashrus with great care, and educating your children with teachers who are ehrliche Yidden.
translationNotes: הארעוואניע: grinding, exhausting toil. Stronger than 'effort.'
ערליכער איד: a sincerely observant, honest Jew. Kehot's 'being observant of G‑d's commands' loses that this is who you are.
טפל: secondary, an accessory to the main thing.

hayomYom.english: Turn away from evil and do good; seek peace and pursue it. The Baal Shem Tov commented: Every physical object whose use is permissible possesses good and evil elements. The material element is evil, and the G‑dly life-force that gives life to the physical is good. The person utilizing the physical object must "turn from evil" - not desire the physical pleasure which is in its materiality, and "do good," i.e. he should desire to be nourished and supported by the G‑dly vitality in that object. "Seek peace and pursue it": Whoever fulfills "turn from evil and do good" must seek and pursue means for making peace between the physical and the G‑dly life-force that vitalizes it.
hayomYom.hebrew: סור מרע ועשה טוב בקש שלום ורדפהו, האט דער בעש"ט [בעל שם טוב] געזאגט: אין יעדער דבר גשמי פון דברים המותרים זיינען פאראן טוב ורע: דער גשמי איז רע און דער חיות אלקי וואס איז מחיה דעם גשמי איז טוב. באדארף דער מענטש וואס באנוצט דעם גשמי זיין א סור מרע, ניט וועלען דעם תענוג וואס איז פאראן אין דעם גשמי, און זיין ועשה טוב וועלען געשפייזט און געהאלפען ווערען פון דעם חיות אלקי וואס איז אין דעם דבר הגשמי. בקש שלום ורדפהו דער מענש וואס איז א סור מרע און א ועשה טוב, באדארף זוכען און נאכלויפען צו מאכען שלום צווישען דעם גשמי און חיות אלקי וואס איז איהם מחי'[ה]
hayomYom.clear:
'Turn away from evil and do good; seek peace and pursue it' (Tehillim 34:15).

The Baal Shem Tov said: In every physical thing that is permitted, there is good and evil. The physical part is evil. The G‑dly life-force that gives the physical thing life is good.

So the person who uses the physical thing must 'turn away from evil': not want the pleasure that is in its physicality. And he must 'do good': want to be nourished and helped by the G‑dly life-force in that physical thing.

'Seek peace and pursue it': the person who turns from evil and does good must seek and run after ways to make peace between the physical thing and the G‑dly life-force that gives it life.
translationNotes: געשפייזט און געהאלפען: 'nourished and helped.' Kehot's 'supported' is close.
נאכלויפען: to run after. The verse's 'pursue' taken literally.

hayomYom.english: The Alter Rebbe on his return from (his arrest in) Petersburg said a maamar for the Mitteler Rebbe, consisting in all of but a few lines: Raise your hands in holiness and bless Havayeh (G‑d). G‑d bless you from Zion, Maker of heaven and earth. "Raise your hands in holiness" - refers to the elevation of the emotive traits to the intellect, and the illumination of the emotive traits by the intellect... ..."And bless Havayeh" - thereby eliciting the Supernal Name Havayeh, the effect being... "G‑d bless you from Zion" - the Name Havayeh will be drawn forth from the essence of the soul, "Maker of heaven and earth" - and this maintains the existence of the worlds.*
hayomYom.hebrew: דער רבי [רבינו הזקן] בעת ער איז געקומען פון פעטערבורג, האט ער גיזאגט פאר'ן מיטעלען רבי'ן א מאמר - אינגאנצען עטליכע שורות: שאו ידיכם קדש - זהו העלאת המדות במוחין והארת המוחין במדות, וברכו את ה' - שממשיכים על ידי זה שם הוי' דלעילא, שעי"ז [שעל ידי זה] פועל שיהי'ה - יברכך ה' מציון - המשכת שם הוי' מעצמיות הנשמה, עושה שמים וארץ - שעי"ז [שעל ידי זה] הוא קיום העולמות.
hayomYom.clear:
When the Alter Rebbe came back from Petersburg, he said a maamar for the Mitteler Rebbe, only a few lines in all:

'Lift up your hands in holiness and bless G‑d. May G‑d bless you from Zion, Maker of heaven and earth' (Tehillim 134:2-3).

'Lift up your hands in holiness': this is raising the middos [emotions] into the mochin [intellect], and the mochin shining into the middos.

'And bless G‑d': through this you draw down the Name Havayah [the four-letter Name] above. And through this you bring about 'May G‑d bless you from Zion': the Name Havayah drawn down from the very essence of the soul.

'Maker of heaven and earth': through this the worlds are sustained.
translationNotes: שעי"ז פועל שיהי': 'through this it brings about.' Kehot leaves it as 'the effect being...' with an ellipsis; the Hebrew links straight to the next phrase.
שם הוי' דלעילא: the Name Havayah 'of Above,' the supernal level.
Kehot's ellipses suggest omitted text; the Hebrew has none.

hayomYom.english: The (sacred) letter beginning Potchin bivracha was written ten years before the letter which begins Katonti.
hayomYom.hebrew: אגרת הקדש פותחין בברכה, נכתבה עשרה שנים קודם כתיבת אגרת קטנתי.
hayomYom.clear: The Iggeres HaKodesh [holy letter] that begins Poschin b'vracha was written ten years before the letter Katonti.
translationNotes: Matches the original. No meaning lost.

hayomYom.english: The Six Remembrances are recited every day, including Shabbat, festivals, Rosh Hashana, and Yom Kippur. From my grandfather's aphorisms: What good is Chassidus and piety if the main quality is lacking - ahavat Yisrael, love of another - even to the extent of causing (G‑d forbid) anguish to another!
hayomYom.hebrew:
שש זכירות אומרים אותם בכל יום גם בשבת, יו"ט [יום טוב], ר"ה [ראש השנה] ויהכ"פ [ויום הכפורים].

מפתגמי אאזמו"ר [אדוני אבי זקני מורי ורבי]: וואס איז די פעולה פון חסידות און יראת שמים, אז עס פעלט דער עיקר - אהבת ישראל, און נאך גורם זיין ח"ו צער אל הזולת.
hayomYom.clear:
The Six Remembrances are said every day, including Shabbos, Yom Tov, Rosh Hashanah and Yom Kippur.

From my grandfather's [the Rebbe Maharash's] sayings: What does Chassidus and yiras Shamayim [fear of Heaven] accomplish, if the main thing is missing, ahavas Yisrael [love of a fellow Jew], and on top of that you cause, G‑d forbid, pain to someone else?
translationNotes: פעולה: 'effect.' What does it achieve, not 'what good is it.'
יראת שמים: fear of Heaven. Kehot's 'piety' is softer.
און נאך: 'and on top of that.' Kehot's 'even to the extent of' changes the logic.

hayomYom.english: Every year on Tisha B'Av my father studied Eicha Raba and the section of R. Yochanan in chapter Hanizakin. In the morning, after kinot - and he would say them all - he said Eicha. He was called to the Torah for maftir, sometimes both at Shacharit and Mincha.
hayomYom.hebrew:
במנחה: ק"ש [קריאת שמע], שש"י [שיר של יום], אכ"א [אין כאלקינו] וכל השיעורים השייכים לשחרית, ואח"כ [ואחר כך] סדר תפלת מנחה. אין מברכין שעשה לי כל צרכי עד למחר.

אאמו"ר [אדוני אבי מורי ורבי] היה לומד בכל שנה ושנה בת"ב [בתשעה באב] איכה רבה וסוגית ר"י [רבי יוחנן] דפרק הניזקין. בבוקר אחר אמירת הקינות - שהי'[ה] אומרם כולם - הי'[ה] אומר איכה. הי'[ה] עולה לתורה למפטיר, ולפעמים הן בשחרית הן במנחה.
hayomYom.clear:
Every year on Tisha B'Av, my father [the Rebbe Rashab] would study Eichah Rabbah and the passage of R. Yochanan in the chapter HaNizakin [Gittin, ch. 5].

In the morning, after the Kinos (and he said all of them), he would say Eichah.

He was called up to the Torah for maftir, sometimes both at Shacharis and at Mincha.
translationNotes: ולפעמים הן בשחרית הן במנחה: maftir every year; 'sometimes' applies to doing it at both.

calendar.original5703: At Mincha: Shema, the Song of the Day, Ein Kelokeinu, and all the daily study portions that belong to Shacharis; after that, the Mincha prayer. The blessing She'asah li kol tzorki is not said until the next day.

hayomYom.dataFlag: Hebrew opens with a Tisha B'Av Mincha order line that the Kehot English omits; translated into cal.

hayomYom.english: From what my grandfather related: a) Originally the epistle Katonti ended with the words "restrained spirit etc." Later, our Great Rabbi (the Alter Rebbe) delivered the maamar "As water reflects the face etc." three times in Lyozna, following the interpretation of Rashi and not of Targum. After that he made an addition to the epistle Katonti as follows: And maybe, through all that, G‑d will give it into the heart of their brethren that "as water (reflects) the face" etc. With this he implanted fine character traits in the chassidim. b) Had the Rebbe not inserted the three words b'midat emet leYaakov ("according to the attribute of Truth unto Yaakov"), he would have attracted fifty thousand more chassidim. But the Rebbe demands the trait of truth.
hayomYom.hebrew:
מספורי אאזמו"ר [אדוני אבי זקני מורי ורבי]: א) מתחלה הי'[ה] אגה"ק [אגרת הקדש] קטנתי מסיימת "ורוח נכאה כו'", ואחרי אשר אמר רבינו הגדול שלש פעמים - בליאזנא - המאמר כמים הפנים גו' כפירש"י [כפירוש רש"י] ולא כתרגומו, אז הוסיף התיבות "וכולי האי - הפנים וגו'", ובזה נטע בהחסידים מדות טובות.

ב) ווען דער רבי וואלט ניט געשטעלט די דריי ווערטער "במדת אמת ליעקב" - באגה"ק [באגרת הקדש] קטנתי - וואלט ער געהאט נאך פופציג טויזענט חסידים, אבער דער רבי מאנט מדת אמת.
hayomYom.clear:
From my grandfather's [the Rebbe Maharash's] stories:

a) Originally, the Iggeres HaKodesh Katonti ended with the words 'and a broken spirit, etc.' Then the Alter Rebbe said the maamar 'As water [reflects] face to face' (Mishlei 27:19) three times in Lyozna, following Rashi's explanation and not the Targum's. After that he added the words 'V'chulei hai... hapanim, etc.' [Kehot: 'And maybe, through all that, G‑d will put it into the heart of their brethren, "as water reflects the face," etc.']. With this he planted good character traits in the chassidim.

b) Had the Rebbe not put the three words 'b'midas emes l'Yaakov' ['with the attribute of truth to Yaakov'] into Katonti, he would have had fifty thousand more chassidim. But the Rebbe demands the attribute of truth.
translationNotes: ורוח נכאה: 'a broken (crushed) spirit.' Kehot's 'restrained spirit' misses it.
נטע: 'planted,' a lasting implant of traits.
מאנט: 'demands, insists on.'

hayomYom.english: The Alter Rebbe went to Mezritch with his brother, R. Yehuda Leib, in 5524 (1764). R. Yehuda Leib went without permission from his wife and therefore turned back. The Rebbe came to Mezritch and stayed there, that first time, until after Pesach 5525 (1765). For two weeks he was uncertain whether to remain there. The first maamar he heard was Nachamu nachamu. It is not clear, though, whether this was the first maamar after his arrival, or the first after the two weeks when he had decided to remain and had become bound (to the Maggid).
hayomYom.hebrew: רבינו הזקן הלך למעזריטש, ביחד עם אחיו מהרי"ל [מורנו הרב ר' יהודה ליב], בשנת תקכ"ד. מהרי"ל [מורנו הרב ר' יהודה ליב] הלך בלי רשות ביתו ולכן חזר מדרכו, ורבינו בא למעזריטש - ושהה שם, בפעם הראשונה, עד אחרי חה"פ [חג הפסח] תקכ"ה. שבועיים היה מסופק אם להשאר שם, והמאמר הראשון ששמע היה נחמו נחמו. ויש בזה ספק אם הוא המאמר הראשון לבואו, או הראשון לאחר השבועיים שהחליט להשאר ונתקשר.
hayomYom.clear:
The Alter Rebbe went to Mezritch in 5524 [1764], together with his brother, R. Yehudah Leib. R. Yehudah Leib went without his wife's permission, so he turned back on the way.

The Alter Rebbe reached Mezritch and stayed there, that first time, until after Pesach 5525 [1765].

For two weeks he was unsure whether to stay there. The first maamar he heard was Nachamu nachamu. But it is uncertain whether this was the first maamar after he arrived, or the first after the two weeks, when he decided to stay and became bound [to the Maggid].
translationNotes: רשות ביתו: literally 'permission of his household,' meaning his wife.
ונתקשר: became a mekushar, bound to the Rebbe.

hayomYom.english: The Alter Rebbe repeated what the Mezritcher Maggid said quoting the Baal Shem Tov: "Love your fellow like yourself" is an interpretation of and commentary on "Love Hashem your G‑d." He who loves his fellow-Jew loves G‑d, because the Jew has within himself a "part of G‑d Above." Therefore, when one loves the Jew - i.e. his inner essence - one loves G‑d.
