hayomYom.hebrew: דער רבי - אדמו"ר [אדוננו מורנו ורבינו] הזקן - האט געזאגט פון מעזריטשער מגיד פון בעש"ט'ס [בעל שם טוב'ס] וועגען: ואהבת לרעך כמוך איז א פירוש וביאור אויף ואהבת את ה' אלקיך. אז מ'האט האלט א אידען, האט מען האלט דעם אויבערשטען, ווייל א איד האט דאך אין זיך א חלק אלקה ממעל, איז אז מ'האט האלט דעם אידען, דעם אינוועניג פון איהם, ממילא האט מען האלט דעם אויבערשטען.
hayomYom.clear:
The Alter Rebbe said, from the Mezritcher Maggid, in the name of the Baal Shem Tov:

'Love your fellow as yourself' (Vayikra 19:18) is an explanation and commentary on 'Love G‑d your G‑d' (Devarim 6:5).

When you love a Jew, you love G‑d. Because a Jew has within him 'a part of G‑d above.' So when you love the Jew, his inner self, you automatically love G‑d.
translationNotes: האט האלט: warm love, fondness.
ממילא: 'automatically, as a result.' Kehot drops it.
דעם אינוועניג פון איהם: 'his inside,' the inner self.

hayomYom.english: "Speak of them when you sit..." Our sages explain that "speak of them" refers to words of Torah. However, in Torah-study itself there are many gradations, and all these gradations are here explained: "When you sit at home," refers to the soul's occupation with Torah when it is in the trove of souls, before its descent to this lowly world. "When you go on the way," refers to the time during which the soul descends from world to world, from plane to plane, until it comes below to this lowest world to be invested in a physical body. There the soul "goes in the way" of this world until the time of old age, until - "When you lie down," when man's appointed time arrives. Then, too, the Torah will protect him, as explained in Chapter Six of Avot, until - "When you rise up," as it is said, "When you awaken (it shall be your discourse)."
hayomYom.hebrew:
בשעת קריאת עשה"ד [עשרת הדברות] עומדים ופניהם אל הס"ת [הספר תורה].

ודברת בם בשבתך גו', ואמרז"ל [ואמרו רבותינו זכרונם לברכה] ודברת בם בדברי תורה הכתוב מדבר. אמנם בעסק התורה גופא יש כמה חלוקי מדריגות, ומבאר כאן כל המדריגות: בשבתך בביתך הוא מעמד הנשמה למעלה באוצר הנשמות, קודם ירידתה למטה, ועוסקת שם בתורה. בלכתך בדרך, - קאי על הזמן שהנשמה יורדת מעולם לעולם וממדריגה למדריגה, עד בואה למטה לעולם התחתון להתלבש בגוף גשמי ומתחיל ללכת בדרך עולם זה עד ימי זקנה ושיבה, עד ובשכבך בבוא ימי פקודתו, וגם אז הנה התורה תשמור עליו כמבואר בששי דאבות, עד ובקומך כאמור והקיצות גו'.
hayomYom.clear:
'And speak of them when you sit in your house, and when you go on the way, and when you lie down, and when you rise up' (Devarim 6:7).

Our Sages said: 'Speak of them' means words of Torah. But within Torah study itself there are many levels, and the verse here explains all of them.

'When you sit in your house': this is the soul's state above, in the treasury of souls, before it comes down. There it is occupied with Torah.

'When you go on the way': this is the time when the soul descends from world to world and from level to level, until it comes down to this lowest world, to be clothed in a physical body. It then begins to walk the path of this world, until old age and gray hair.

Until 'when you lie down': when his appointed time comes. Then too, the Torah will guard him, as explained in the sixth chapter of Avos.

Until 'when you rise up,' as it says, 'And when you awaken, it will speak with you.'
translationNotes: באוצר הנשמות: the treasury of souls. Kehot 'trove' is the same idea.
זקנה ושיבה: 'old age and gray hair.' Kehot keeps only 'old age.'
ומתחיל ללכת בדרך עולם זה: the soul 'begins to walk' this world's path once in the body.

calendar.original5703: During the reading of the Ten Commandments, stand facing the Sefer Torah.

hayomYom.dataFlag: Hebrew opens with a line about standing for the Ten Commandments that the Kehot English omits; translated into cal.

hayomYom.english: Tachanun is not said at Mincha. The 14th of Menachem Av 5701 (1941) marked fifty years since my father told me to begin recording the stories he told me. When the Tzemach Tzedek began writing on Talmudic and chassidic subjects, the Alter Rebbe said to him: Uknei l'cha chaver (lit. "acquire a friend for yourself"); read v'kaneh l'cha chaver (a slight change in vowels) - "the quill shall be your friend." My father once quoted the Alter Rebbe, "v'kaneh etc..., the quill shall be your friend" - and elaborated: This refers to the quill of the heart, meaning that whatever one learns one must experience emotionally.
hayomYom.hebrew:
במנחה אין אומרים תחנון.

יד מנ"א [מנחם אב] תש"א - נמלאו חמשים שנה מיום שאמר לי אאמו"ר [אדוני אבי מורי ורבי] שאתחיל לרשום הסיפורים שמספר לי. כאשר התחיל הצ"צ [הצמח צדק] לכתוב בעניני נגלה וחסידות, אמר לו אדמו"ר [אדוננו מורנו ורבנו] הזקן: וקנה לך חבר, וקנה [קוף בקמץ, נון בסגל] - לשון קולמוס - לך חבר. פעם אמר אאמו"ר [אדוני אבי מורי ורבי] בשם אדמו"ר [אדוננו מורנו ורבינו] הזקן וקנה - לשון קולמוס - לך חבר, ופירש אאמו"ר [אדוני אבי מורי ורבי] קולמוס הלב, אז יעדער זאך וואס מ'לערענט זאל מען איבערלעבען.
hayomYom.clear:
14 Menachem Av 5701 [1941] marked fifty years since my father [the Rebbe Rashab] told me to begin writing down the stories he told me.

When the Tzemach Tzedek began writing on topics of nigleh [the revealed Torah] and Chassidus, the Alter Rebbe told him: 'Ukneh l'cha chaver' ['acquire for yourself a friend'] (Avos 1:6). Read it as v'kaneh [with a kamatz under the kuf and a segol under the nun], meaning a quill: 'the quill shall be your friend.'

Once my father quoted the Alter Rebbe: 'V'kaneh, the quill, shall be your friend.' And he explained: the quill of the heart. Whatever you learn, you must live through inwardly.
translationNotes: איבערלעבען: to live through, to experience deeply. Kehot's 'experience emotionally' narrows it.
קוף בקמץ נון בסגל: the vowel change that turns 'acquire' into 'quill.'

calendar.original5703: Tachanun is not said at Mincha.

hayomYom.english: From my father's notes: The superior quality of 15 Av over the fifteenth of every other month is this: The fifteenth represents the visible completeness (of the moon), but (the moon) is still only a recipient (of light). However, on 15 Av the light is firmly fixed in it, for the ascent is in reverse proportion to the drastic descent of Tisha B'Av... This then is the meaning of "The sun's power is weakened" (on 15 Av after its summer intensity). The idolators calculate their calendar by the sun of evil, which on the 15th is weakened... In the days of the Sanctuary they (the nations) were subservient to Shlomo (King Solomon); certainly it shall be so in the Time-to-Come when "(the nations) will flow to Him" in a state of total bitul (nullification), and "I will remove the spirit of impurity etc." A token of this is expressed on the 15th of Av when the sun is weakened...
hayomYom.hebrew:
א"א [אין אומרים] תחנון.

רושם אאמו"ר [אדוני אבי מורי ורבי]: מעלת ט"ו באב על כל ט"ו בחדש, שזהו רק השלמות בהגילוי, אבל מ"מ [מכל מקום] היא רק בחינת מקבל, אבל בט"ו באב האור בה בקביעות, לפי שהעליה היא לפי ערך עוצם הירידה דת"ב [דתשעה באב]... וזהו תשש כחה של חמה, עכו"ם [עובדי כוכבים ומזלות] מונים לחמה בישא, ובט"ו תשש כו' במכל שכן מזמן הבית שהיו נכנעים לשלמה, כ"ש [כל שכן] לעתיד, ונהרו אליו, בבחינת ביטול לגמרי, ואת רוח הטומאה אעביר כו', ומעין זה בט"ו באב תשש כו'.
hayomYom.clear:
From my father's [the Rebbe Rashab's] notes:

15 Av is greater than the fifteenth of every other month. The fifteenth of a month is only completeness in what is revealed, and even then the moon is still only a receiver. But on 15 Av the light is fixed in it permanently, because the ascent matches the intensity of the descent of Tisha B'Av...

This is the meaning of 'the strength of the sun weakens' (Taanis 31a). The idol-worshippers count by the sun, the evil one, and on the fifteenth it weakens, etc.

All the more so: if in the time of the Beis HaMikdash they submitted to Shlomo, how much more so in the time to come, when 'they will stream to Him' (Yeshaya 2:2) in complete bittul, and 'I will remove the spirit of impurity' (Zecharya 13:2), etc. A taste of this comes on 15 Av, when the sun weakens, etc.
translationNotes: בחינת מקבל: the level of a receiver. On other months the moon only receives light.
בקביעות: permanently fixed, not just visible.
לפי ערך עוצם הירידה: in proportion to how deep the descent was.

calendar.original5703: Tachanun is not said.

hayomYom.english: The travels of the Baal Shem Tov when he first revealed himself were for three purposes: Redemption of captives, buttressing Torah and piety, and revealing the Inner Torah (Chassidus). The Mitteler Rebbe would explain: The Revealed Torah is called water; one goes to water. The Inner Torah is called fire; one fears fire. Therefore, the mashpiya (the one who gives to another) must go to the recipient and say to him, "Do not fear, for Hashem your G‑d is a consuming fire."
hayomYom.hebrew: נסיעות הבעש"ט [הבעל שם טוב] בתחילת ההתגלות שלו היו [על דבר] שלשה ענינים: פדיון שבוים, חיזוק התורה ויראת שמים, התגלות פנימיות התורה. אדמו"ר [אדוננו מורנו ורבנו] האמצעי היה מבאר בזה: גליא שבתורה נקרא מים און צו וואסער גייט מען. פנימיות התורה נקרא אש און פאר פייער האט מען מורא. דערפאר דארף דער משפיע גיין צום מקבל אן זאגען איהם: האב קיין מורא ניט ווייל ה' אלקיך אש אוכלה הוא.
hayomYom.clear:
The Baal Shem Tov's travels at the start of his revelation were for three things: redeeming captives, strengthening Torah and yiras Shamayim [fear of Heaven], and revealing pnimiyus haTorah [the inner Torah, Chassidus].

The Mitteler Rebbe explained: The revealed part of Torah is called water, and you go to water. The inner part of Torah is called fire, and you are afraid of fire.

So the mashpia [the one who gives, the mentor] has to go to the mekabel [the receiver] and tell him: Don't be afraid, because 'G‑d your G‑d is a consuming fire' (Devarim 4:24).
translationNotes: יראת שמים: fear of Heaven. Kehot's 'piety' is softer.
משפיע / מקבל: giver and receiver. Kehot glosses only the first.

hayomYom.english: The Rebbe Tzemach Tzedek explained the relationship of fire and Inner Torah. Inner Torah gives vitality to the Revealed Torah. When one learns an halacha and knows that after his 120 years on earth he will learn the same halacha in gan eden, that puts a little fire into him.
hayomYom.hebrew: אדמו"ר [אדוננו מורנו ורבנו] הצ"צ [הצמח צדק] ביאר מה שמיחסים אש לפנימיות התורה, לפי שהיא הנותנת חיות בגליא שבתורה: אז ער לערענט א הלכה און ווייס אז די זעלבע הלכה וועט ער לערנען נאך מאה ועשרים שנה אין גן עדן גיט עס אריין א פייערעל.
hayomYom.clear:
The Tzemach Tzedek explained why fire is associated with pnimiyus haTorah [the inner Torah]: because it is what gives life to the revealed Torah.

When you learn a halacha and know that after 120 years you will learn the same halacha in Gan Eden, that puts a little fire into you.
translationNotes: לפי שהיא הנותנת חיות: 'because it gives vitality.' This is the reason for the fire image, not a separate point as in Kehot.
פייערעל: a little fire, a spark. Diminutive.

hayomYom.english: The Mitteler Rebbe quoted the Alter Rebbe: Ahavat yisrael must consume a person entirely.
hayomYom.hebrew: אדמו"ר [אדוננו מורנו ורבנו] האמצעי אמר בשם רבינו הזקן: אהבת ישראל בעדארף דערנעמען ביז מיצוי הנפש.
hayomYom.clear: The Mitteler Rebbe said in the name of the Alter Rebbe: Ahavas Yisrael has to take hold of you, to the point of mitzui hanefesh [the soul poured out completely].
translationNotes: דערנעמען: to seize, grip.
מיצוי הנפש: the soul wrung out to the last drop. Kehot's 'consume entirely' is close.

hayomYom.english: Those who daven with four pairs of tefillin follow this procedure: 1. Put on Rashi hand - and head - tefillin before saying Chapter Eizehu (p. 23), and daven in them until after ach tzadikim... (p. 85). 2. Remove the Rashi tefillin from the head and put on - without a b'racha - Shimusha Raba tefillin for the head. Recite sh'ma... until emet; then recite the daily portion of Tehillim (as the Tehillim is divided into the days of the month). The meticulous would study those chapters with the commentaries of Rashi and Metzudot. 3. Then put on - without a b'racha - Rabeinu Tam tefillin, recite sh'ma... until emet, then chapter Kadeish... (p. 85) and the Remembrances printed in the Siddur (p. 86). Then study a chapter of Mishna, each according to his comprehension. 4. Remove the Rabeinu Tam tefillin from the head and put on the Ra'avad tefillin for the head - without a b'racha. Recite sh'ma... until emet; study the day's portion of Chumash with the commentary of Rashi - on Sunday (the first parsha) until sheini, Monday the second parsha, etc.
hayomYom.hebrew: המתפללים בארבעה זוגות תפילין כך נוהגים: א) מניחים תש"י [תפילין של יד] ותש"ר [ותפילין של ראש] דרש"י קודם אמירת פרק איזהו, ומתפללים בהם עד אחרי אך צדיקים גו'. ב) מסירים תש"ר [תפילין של ראש] דרש"י, ומניחים - בלא ברכה - תש"ר [תפילין של ראש] דשמושא רבא וקוראים שמע גו' עד אמת ואומרים מזמורי תהלים כפי שנחלק לימי החודש. והמהדרים היו לומדים אותם עם פירש"י [פירוש רש"י] ומצודות. ג) אח"כ [אחר כך] מניחים תפלין דר"ת [דרבנו תם] - בלא ברכה - וקוראים שמע גו' עד אמת, פרשת קדש גו' והזכירות שנדפסו בסידור. ולומדים פרק משניות כל אחד לפי הבנתו. ד) מסירים תש"ר [תפילין של ראש] דר"ת [דרבנו תם] ומניחים תש"ר [תפילין של ראש] דראב"ד - בלא ברכה - וקוראים שמע גו' עד אמת ולומדים פרשה חומש עם פירש"י [פירוש רש"י] - מפרשת השבוע: יום א' עד שני ביום ב' פרשה ב' וכו'.
hayomYom.clear:
Those who daven with four pairs of tefillin do it this way:

1. Put on Rashi tefillin, hand and head, before saying the chapter Eizehu mekoman, and daven in them until after Ach tzaddikim.

2. Remove the Rashi head-tefillin, and put on, without a bracha, the Shimusha Rabba head-tefillin. Say the Shema until emes, and say the Tehillim chapters as divided for the days of the month. Those who are meticulous would learn them with Rashi's commentary and the Metzudos.

3. Then put on Rabbeinu Tam tefillin, without a bracha. Say the Shema until emes, the passage Kadesh, and the Remembrances printed in the Siddur. Learn a chapter of Mishnayos, each person according to his understanding.

4. Remove the Rabbeinu Tam head-tefillin and put on the Raavad head-tefillin, without a bracha. Say the Shema until emes, and learn a section of Chumash with Rashi from the weekly portion: on Sunday until sheni [the second aliyah], on Monday the second section, and so on.
translationNotes: Kehot adds Siddur page numbers not in the Hebrew. Left out.
מפרשת השבוע: 'from the weekly portion.' Kehot leaves this implicit.

hayomYom.english: Just as with the mitzva of tefillin for example, there is a designated place for them on the head and arm, and one feels the weight of the head-tefilla and the tightness of the hand-tefilla, so too with the mitzvot of ahava and yira, love and fear (awe) of G‑d. As Rambam writes, in Yesodei Hatorah 2:1: It is a commandment to love and fear the revered and awesome G‑d, as it is said, "Love Hashem your G‑d", and "You shall fear Hashem your G‑d." Now the degree of fulfillment of these mitzvot is that there be a bodily sensation, that the very flesh of the heart actually feel (the love or the fear); just as, for example, when one meets a truly devoted friend. Not only does he feel good and forget all his troubles, he even enjoys a newly-awakened inner liveliness and optimism - all stemming from his cheerful mood. So, too, with (the opposite emotion of) fear (of G‑d); he is seized by a great dread and fright, for at that moment he recalls whatever was undesirable in his thoughts, words and deeds. His heart feels a palpable pain from his dread of punishment, his fear of Heaven. At times he may experience yirat boshet, an overwhelming shame, or yirat harom'mut, awe of G‑d's transcendent majesty.
hayomYom.hebrew: כשם שמצות תפילין, עד"מ [על דרך משל], יש לה מקום קבוע בראש ובזרוע, ומרגיש כובד התפלה של ראש וההידוק דתפלה של יד כן הוא במצות אהבה ויראה, וכמ"ש [וכמו שכתב] הרמב"ם [יסודי התורה פ"ב [פרק ב'] ה"א [הלכה א']]: "האל הנכבד והנורא הזה מצוה לאהבה וליראה אותו שנאמר ואהבת את ה"א [ה' אלוקיך] ונאמר את ה"א [ה' אלוקיך] תירא", הנה שיעור מצות אלו הוא אשר יורגשו בהרגש גופני בבשר הלב ממש, וכמו אדם הפוגש את אוהבו הנאמן, ולא זו בלבד אז אים זאל ווערען גוט פון דעם, שישכח על כל הדברים המעיקים אותו, אלא עוד שיתעורר בו חיות פנימי בתקוה טובה, כי לבו טוב עליו, וכן במדת היראה נופל עליו פחד גדול ומורא, כי בשעה ההיא הוא נזכר על כל עניניו הלא טובים במחשבה דבור ומעשה, ולבו יכאב בכאב מורגש מיראת העונש ביר"ש [ביראת שמים] ולפעמים הוא ברגש של ירא בושת או גם יראת הרוממות.
hayomYom.clear:
Take the mitzvah of tefillin, for example. It has a fixed place on the head and on the arm, and you feel the weight of the head-tefillin and the tightness of the hand-tefillin. So too with the mitzvos of love and fear [of G‑d].

As the Rambam writes (Yesodei HaTorah 2:1): 'This honored and awesome G‑d, it is a mitzvah to love Him and to fear Him, as it says, "You shall love G‑d your G‑d," and it says, "You shall fear G‑d your G‑d."'

The measure of these mitzvos is that they be felt physically, in the very flesh of the heart. It is like a person who meets his loyal friend. Not only does he feel good from it, so that he forgets everything weighing on him. More than that, a new inner vitality and hope wake up in him, because his heart is glad.

So too with fear. Great dread and awe fall on him, because at that moment he remembers everything that was not good in his thought, speech and action. His heart aches with a real, felt pain, from fear of punishment, in yiras Shamayim. And sometimes it is a feeling of yiras boshes [shame before G‑d], or even yiras haromemus [awe of G‑d's exaltedness].
translationNotes: בבשר הלב ממש: 'in the actual flesh of the heart.'
כי לבו טוב עליו: 'his heart is glad.' Kehot's 'cheerful mood' flattens it.
עניניו הלא טובים: 'his not-good matters.' Kehot's 'undesirable' softens it.

hayomYom.english: Activism on behalf of the ways of Chassidus means that even when a chassid is in the marketplace, deeply involved in his business, he still thinks about what he can do for chassidic concerns and the welfare of chassidim. When he encounters a business acquaintance among the market people he should seek to persuade him to attend the shi'urim (public study sessions) in Chassidus, or to attend a farbrengen. Activism on behalf of the ways of Chassidus is a personal obligation, regardless whether one is great or limited in knowledge of Chassidus.
hayomYom.hebrew: ההתעסקות בדרכי החסידות הוא, אשר גם בהלכו בשוק טרוד בעסקיו יחשוב מה הוא יכול לעשות בעד עניני החסידות וטובת החסידים, וכשהוא פוגש מי שהוא מאנשי השוק ממכיריו - בעניני מסחר - ידבר על לבו, כי יבוא אל שיעורי הלמודים בדא"ח [בדברי אלקים חיים] או לאיזו התוועדות. וההתעסקות בדרכי החסידות הוא חובת גברא מבלי הבדל בין גדול וקטן בידיעת דא"ח [דברי אלקים חיים].
hayomYom.clear:
Being active in the ways of Chassidus means this: even when you walk in the marketplace, busy with your business, you think about what you can do for the cause of Chassidus and for the good of chassidim.

And when you meet someone from the market whom you know through business, speak to his heart, so that he will come to the classes in Chassidus or to some farbrengen.

Being active in the ways of Chassidus is a personal obligation [chovas gavra], no matter whether you know a lot of Chassidus or a little.
translationNotes: התעסקות: active involvement, working at it. Kehot's 'activism.'
ידבר על לבו: 'speak to his heart,' warm, personal persuasion.
דא"ח (דברי אלקים חיים): 'words of the living G‑d,' a name for Chassidus.

hayomYom.english: My father said: One should not recite the Morning B'rachot before rinsing the mouth in the morning, except on fast days.
hayomYom.hebrew: אאמו"ר [אדוני אבי מורי ורבי] אמר: קודם רחיצת הפה שחרית, אין לברך מלבד בימי התעניות - ברכות השחר.
hayomYom.clear: My father [the Rebbe Rashab] said: Before rinsing your mouth in the morning, you should not say Birchos HaShachar [the morning blessings], except on fast days.
translationNotes: Matches the original. No meaning lost.

hayomYom.english: In the winter of 5652 (1891-2), when my father taught me in Tanya, "The second soul in Israel is actually part of G‑d above," he explained that the connotations of the words "above" and "actually" are contradictory. "Above" indicates the most spiritual of spiritual levels, while "actually" describes the most material of material things. He explained that this is the unique quality of the "second soul," that though it is the epitome of the spiritual it has an effect upon the most material of materiality.
hayomYom.hebrew: בחורף תרנ"ב כאשר אאמו"ר [אדוני אבי מורי ורבי] למד עמי בספר התניא "ונפש השנית בישראל היא חלק אלקה ממעל ממש", הסביר כי הנושאים בתיבת ממעל ובתיבת ממש הם הפכים. ממעל תוארו רוחניות שברוחניות וממש תוארו גשמיות שבגשמיות. ויבאר כי זהו מעלת נפש השנית, שעם היותה רוחניות שברוחניות פועלת בגשמיות שבגשמיות.
hayomYom.clear:
In the winter of 5652 [1891-92], when my father [the Rebbe Rashab] studied Tanya with me, 'The second soul in Israel is truly a part of G‑d above' (Tanya, ch. 2), he explained that the words 'above' and 'truly' carry opposite meanings.

'Above' describes the spiritual within the spiritual. 'Truly' [mamash, literally 'tangibly'] describes the physical within the physical.

And he explained that this is the special quality of the second soul: though it is the most spiritual of the spiritual, it acts upon the most physical of the physical.
translationNotes: ממש: literally 'tangible, concrete.' That is why it stands for physicality.
פועלת: 'acts upon, works on.'

hayomYom.english: A tradition handed down from Rebbe to Rebbe: During the well-known conflict (between chassidim and their opponents) the chassidim told the Alter Rebbe about the terrible abuse they suffered from the plain misnagdic folk. The Rebbe said: Grandfather (as he called the Baal Shem Tov) deeply loved simple folk. In my first days in Mezritch, the Rebbe, (the Maggid) said: "It was a frequent customary remark of the Rebbe (Baal Shem Tov) that love of Israel is love of G‑d. "You are children of Hashem your G‑d"; when one loves the father one loves the children.
hayomYom.hebrew: מקובל רבי מפי רבי: אין דער צייט פון מחלוקת הידועה, האבען חסידים דערציילט דעם אלטען רבי'ן די גרויסע יסורים וואס מ'האט פון די מתנגדישע פראסטע אידען. האט דער רבי געזאגט: דער זיידע - אזוי פלעגט דער רבי רופען דעם בעש"ט [בעל שם טוב] - האט זייער ליב געהאט די פראסטע אידען. אין די ערשטע טעג ווען איך בין געווען אין מעזריטש, האט דער רבי הה"מ [הרב המגיד] געזאגט: מרגלא בפומיה פון רבי'ן - הבעש"ט [הבעל שם טוב] - אהבת ישראל איז אהבת המקום, בנים אתם לה' אלקיכם, אז מען האט האלט דעם פאטער האט מען האלט די קינדער.
hayomYom.clear:
A tradition handed down from Rebbe to Rebbe:

At the time of the well-known controversy, chassidim told the Alter Rebbe about the great suffering they endured from the simple misnaged Jews.

The Rebbe said: The Zeide [grandfather], as the Rebbe used to call the Baal Shem Tov, loved simple Jews very much. In my first days in Mezritch, the Rebbe, the Maggid, said: The Rebbe, the Baal Shem Tov, would often say: Ahavas Yisrael is ahavas haMakom [love of G‑d]. 'You are children of G‑d your G‑d' (Devarim 14:1). When you love the father, you love the children.
translationNotes: יסורים: suffering, torment. Kehot's 'abuse' is close.
מרגלא בפומיה: his habitual saying.
פראסטע אידען: simple Jews, the very kind the Baal Shem Tov loved, which is the point of the answer.

hayomYom.english: My father writes in a letter: "I heard in the name of our holy fathers the Rebbe'im, that also when a daughter is born we are to say the words "to Torah," (May her parents bring her up to Torah, to marriage and to good deeds. p. 186). This is based on the statement by our Sages (Berachot 17a), "How do women earn merit? By seeing to it that their children go to study Torah, that their husbands go to the Study Hall and by awaiting (their husbands' return, etc.").
hayomYom.hebrew: אאמו"ר [אדוני אבי מורי ורבי] כותב באחד ממכתביו: שמעתי בשם כ"ק [כבוד קדושת] אבותינו הקדושים זצוקללה"ה [זכר צדיק וקדוש לברכה לחיי העולם הבא] נ"ע [נשמתם עדן] זי"ע [זכותם יגן עלינו] שגם על בת צ"ל [צריך לומר] לתורה [ולחופה ומע"ט [ומעשים טובים]] ע"פ [על פי] מה שארז"ל [שאמרו רבותינו זכרונם לברכה] [ברכות יז. א] נשי במאי זכיין באיקרוי כו' ובאתנוי כו' ונטרין כו'.
hayomYom.clear:
My father [the Rebbe Rashab] writes in one of his letters: I heard in the name of our holy fathers, the Rebbeim, that for a daughter too you should say 'l'Torah' ['to Torah, to the chuppah and to good deeds'].

This is based on what our Sages said (Berachos 17a): 'How do women earn merit? By bringing their children to learn Torah, by having their husbands go to learn, and by waiting for them.'
translationNotes: גם על בת: 'for a daughter too.' The point is that the word Torah is not left out for a girl.
צ"ל: 'must say.' Stronger than Kehot's 'are to say.'

hayomYom.english: From my father's sichot: In the chassidic "exodus from Egypt" there is the Mitzva of recounting the "Exodus" verbally, to tell chassidic stories and to "sense" and apprehend the story in one's deepest inwardness. One must know that every narrative is guidance for living. Every story must bring forth (in the listener) a fine character trait, an inner enthusiasm for hidur mitzva, and should enable the listener to sense the "ways of pleasantness" of chassidic teachings.
hayomYom.hebrew: משיחות אאמו"ר [אדוני אבי מורי ורבי]: אין דעם יציאת מצרים פון חסידות, איז פאראן די מצוה פון סיפור יצ"מ [יציאת מצרים] בדבור, דערציילען חסידישע ספורים און דערהערען דעם סיפור אין א פנימית דפנימית. מ'בעדארף וויסען אז יעדער סיפור איז א הוראה בחיים. יעדער ספור בעדארף בריינגען א מדה טובה און א חיות פנימי אין א הידור מצוה און דערהערען דעם דרכי נועם פון תורת החסידות.
hayomYom.clear:
From my father's [the Rebbe Rashab's] sichos:

In the 'Exodus from Egypt' of Chassidus, there is also the mitzvah of telling the story of the Exodus out loud: telling chassidic stories, and feeling the story deep inside, in the innermost of the inner.

You have to know that every story is a lesson for life. Every story has to bring out a good trait, an inner vitality in hiddur mitzvah [doing mitzvos beautifully], and a feeling for the 'ways of pleasantness' of the teachings of Chassidus.
translationNotes: פנימית דפנימית: 'the innermost of the inner.'
הוראה בחיים: a directive for life.
דערהערען: to sense, to feel it.

hayomYom.english:
Bless Rosh Chodesh Elul. Say all the Tehillim in the early morning.
Day of farbrengen.

The month of Elul is the month of reckoning. In the material world, if a businessman is to conduct his affairs properly and with great profit, he must periodically take an accounting and correct any deficiencies... Likewise in the spiritual avoda of serving G‑d. Throughout the year all Israel are occupied with Torah, Mitzvot and (developing and expressing) good traits. The month of Elul is the month of reckoning, when every Jew, each commensurate with his abilities, whether scholar or businessman, must make an accurate accounting in his soul of everything that occurred in the course of the year. Each must know the good qualities in his service of G‑d and strengthen them; he must also be aware of the deficiencies in himself and in his service, and correct these. Through this excellent preparation, one merits a good and sweet year, materially and spiritually.
hayomYom.hebrew:
מברכים ר"ח [ראש חודש] אלול, אמירת כל התהלים בהשכמה. יום התוועדות.

חודש אלול הוא חדש החשבון. דכמו בגשמיות הנה הבעל עסק.. בכדי שיהיה העסק כדבעי ויתן רוח רב, צריך מזמן לזמן לעשות חשבון ולתקן את כל החסרונות... כן הוא גם בעבודה הרוחנית בעבודת השי"ת [השם יתברך], דכל השנה הנה כל ישראל עוסקין בתורה ומצות ובמדות טובות, בחדש אלול הוא חדש החשבון אשר כל אחד ואחד מישראל, כל חד וחד לפום שיעורא דילי'[ה] הן היושב אהל והן הבעל עסק, צריכים לעשות חשבון צדק בנפשם מכל אשר עבר עליהם במשך השנה, ולידע המעלות בעבודתם ולחזקם, ואת החסרונות שבהם ובעבודתם לתקנם. דעל ידי הכנה טובה זו.. זוכים לשנה טובה ומתוקה בגשמיות ורוחניות.
hayomYom.clear:
The month of Elul is the month of accounting.

In material things, a businessman, if his business is to run as it should and bring in a good profit, must from time to time make an accounting and fix all the shortcomings...

So it is in spiritual avoda, in serving G‑d. All year, all Jews are busy with Torah, mitzvos and good traits. Elul is the month of accounting. Every single Jew, each according to his own measure, whether one who sits in the tent of Torah or a businessman, must make an honest accounting in his soul of everything that happened to him during the year.

He must know the strengths in his avoda and reinforce them. And he must know the shortcomings in himself and in his avoda, and fix them.

Through this good preparation... you merit a good and sweet year, materially and spiritually.
translationNotes: חשבון צדק: an honest, true accounting. Kehot's 'accurate' is close.
יושב אהל: one who sits in the tent [of Torah], a full-time scholar.
לפום שיעורא דיליה: each according to his own measure.

calendar.original5703: Shabbos Mevarchim Elul. Say the whole Tehillim early in the morning. A day of farbrengen.

hayomYom.dataFlag: Hebrew includes the Shabbos Mevarchim calendar line that the Kehot English lacks; translated into cal.

hayomYom.english: There are two general approaches in healing a bodily illness: a) To heal the particular organ or faculty that is defective, sick or weak; b) to strengthen the healthy organs and faculties so that they may overcome and heal the sick organ or faculty. The parallel in illnesses of the soul are the two approaches in service of G‑d - teshuva and good deeds.
hayomYom.hebrew:
דרכי הרפואה בחולי הגוף בכלל שנים הם: א) לרפאות את האבר או הכח המקולקל חולה וחלוש. ב) לחזק את האברים והכחות הבריאים, אשר הם יתגברו על האבר וכח החולה לרפאותו.

הדוגמא מזה בחולי הנפש הם שני דרכי העבודה: תשובה ומעשים טובים.
hayomYom.clear:
In general, there are two ways to heal an illness of the body:

1. Heal the limb or faculty that is damaged, sick and weak.

2. Strengthen the healthy limbs and faculties, so that they overpower the sick limb or faculty and heal it.

The parallel in illnesses of the soul is the two paths of avoda: teshuva [return to G‑d] and good deeds.
translationNotes: Matches the original. No meaning lost.

hayomYom.english: There must be avoda by one's own efforts. Superior heights are attained when one is taken by the hand and led; it is more precious though, when it is by one's own strength.
hayomYom.hebrew: עס דארף זיין עבודה בכח עצמו. העכער איז אז מ'נעהמט פאר'ן האנט און מ'פירט. טייערער איז אז עס איז בכח עצמו.
hayomYom.clear:
There has to be avoda by your own strength.

Higher is when you are taken by the hand and led. More precious is when it is by your own strength.
translationNotes: העכער / טייערער: 'higher' versus 'more precious.' Being led reaches higher; your own effort is dearer.

hayomYom.english: The Mitteler Rebbe at first used to say brief maamarim. For example, the maamar Zecher rav tuvcha and its amplification, published in the Siddur, was said in six sequential sections, at somewhat greater length than in its printed version.
hayomYom.hebrew: אדמו"ר האמצעי הי' אומר בתחלה מאמרים קצרים. ולדוגמא: ד"ה [דיבור המתחיל] זכר רב טובך - וביאורו - שבסידור נאמרו בששה המשכים - באריכות יותר קצת מהנדפס.
hayomYom.clear: At first, the Mitteler Rebbe used to say short maamarim. For example: the maamar Zecher rav tuvcha, with its explanation, printed in the Siddur, was said in six consecutive sections, somewhat longer than the printed version.
translationNotes: Matches the original. No meaning lost.

hayomYom.english: When the Tzemach Tzedek was nine years old the Alter Rebbe said to Him: I received from my Rebbe (the Maggid) who received from his Rebbe (the Baal Shem Tov) in the name of his well-known Rebbe that from the second day of Rosh Chodesh Elul until Yom Kippur we are to say three chapters of Tehillim every day. Then, on Yom Kippur, thirty six (chapters): Nine before Kol Nidrei, nine before sleeping, nine after Musaf, and nine after Ne'ila. Whoever did not start on the second day of Rosh Chodesh is to start with the Tehillim of the particular day on which he realizes his omission, and complete the missing Tehillim later.
hayomYom.hebrew: כשהיה הצ"צ [הצמח צדק] בן תשע שנים אמר לו רבינו הזקן: קבלתי ממורי [הרב המגיד] שקיבל ממורו הבעש"ט [הבעל שם טוב] בשם מורו הידוע, אשר מיום שני דר"ח [דראש חודש] אלול עד יום הכפורים, יאמרו בכל יום ויום במשך היום שלשה קאפיטלאך תהלים, וביוהכ"פ [וביום כפורים] שלשים וששה קאפיטלאך: ט' קודם כל נדרי, ט' קודם השינה, ט' אחר מוסף, ט' אחר נעילה. ומי שלא התחיל ביום ב דר"ח [דראש חודש] יתחיל באותו יום שהוא עומד בו, ואת אשר החסיר ישלים.
hayomYom.clear:
When the Tzemach Tzedek was nine years old, the Alter Rebbe told him:

I received from my teacher [the Maggid], who received from his teacher the Baal Shem Tov, in the name of his well-known teacher: from the second day of Rosh Chodesh Elul until Yom Kippur, three chapters of Tehillim should be said each day, during the day.

On Yom Kippur, thirty-six chapters: nine before Kol Nidrei, nine before going to sleep, nine after Musaf, and nine after Ne'ilah.

Whoever did not start on the second day of Rosh Chodesh should start with the day he is on, and make up what he missed.
translationNotes: מורו הידוע: 'his well-known teacher.' Chassidic tradition identifies him as Achiya HaShiloni; the text does not name him.
במשך היום: 'during the day,' i.e. by day.

hayomYom.english: The Children of Israel are called eretz cheifetz, for they possess numerous "precious articles" in the love and fear of G‑d, and in fine character traits. Bringing these traits to the surface depends entirely upon the individual stimulating them. It is clear that throughout the earth are wellsprings of living water; the difference between them is only that some are near the surface, others far. Everything therefore depends on the well-digger, his patience and perseverance. Now since ratzon ("will") is a superior faculty that "issues decrees," rules over all the other faculties, and compels them to act according to its orders - it follows that the essential avoda is to arouse one's will to exercise its effect - both upon the person himself and upon others.
hayomYom.hebrew:
בני ישראל נקראו ארץ חפץ, שיש בהם כמה חפצים יקרים באהבת השי"ת [השם יתברך] ויראתו ומדות טובות, ואין דבר גילוי המדות הטובות תלוי אלא במעורר. דבר ברור הוא, אשר בכל חלקי האדמה נמצאים מעינות מים חיים, וההבדל הוא רק בקירוב וריחוק, ואם כן הלא הכל תלוי בהחופר וכח סבלנותו ומתינותו.

וכיון שהרצון הוא כח עליון הגוזר ומפקד על כל הכחות, ומכריחם לעשות ולפעול כפי הפקודות שלו, א"כ [אם כן] איפוא עיקר העבודה הוא לעורר את הרצון לפעול ולעשות הן בעצמו הן בזולתו.
hayomYom.clear:
The Jewish people are called 'eretz chefetz' [a land of delight] (Malachi 3:12), because they have many precious treasures in love of G‑d, fear of Him, and good traits. Bringing out the good traits depends only on someone who will awaken them.

It is clear that in every part of the earth there are springs of living water. The only difference is whether they are near or far. So everything depends on the one who digs, on his patience and his steady perseverance.

And since will is a higher power that decrees and commands all the other powers and forces them to act according to its orders, the main avoda is to arouse the will to act and to do, both in yourself and in others.
translationNotes: ארץ חפץ / חפצים יקרים: wordplay. A 'land of chefetz' holds chafatzim, precious objects.
מעורר: one who awakens them.
מתינות: calm deliberateness, unhurried patience.

hayomYom.english: Whoever has faith in individual Divine Providence knows that "Man's steps are established by G‑d," that this particular soul must purify and improve something specific in a particular place. For centuries, or even since the world's creation, that which needs purification or improvement waits for this soul to come and purify or improve it. The soul too, has been waiting - ever since it came into being - for its time to descend, so that it can discharge the tasks of purification and improvement assigned to it.
hayomYom.hebrew: המאמין בהשגחה פרטית יודע כי מהשם מצעדי גבר כוננו, אשר נשמה זו צריכה לברר ולתקן איזה בירור ותיקון במקום פלוני. ומאות בשנים או גם משעת בריאת העולם הנה הדבר שצריך להתברר או להתתקן מחכה לאותה הנשמה שתבוא לבררו ולתקנו, וגם נשמה הלזו הנה מאז נאצלה ונבראה היא מחכה לזמן ירידתה לברר ולתקן את אשר הוטל עליה.
hayomYom.clear:
Whoever believes in hashgacha pratis [individual Divine Providence] knows that 'a man's steps are set by G‑d' (Tehillim 37:23): that this soul has to refine and repair some particular thing in a particular place.

For hundreds of years, or even since the creation of the world, the thing that needs refining or repairing has been waiting for that soul to come and refine and repair it.

And this soul too, ever since it was emanated and created, has been waiting for the time of its descent, to refine and repair what was placed upon it.
translationNotes: בירור ותיקון: 'refining and repairing,' Kabbalistic terms for elevating the world.
נאצלה ונבראה: 'emanated and created.' Kehot's 'came into being' flattens it.
הוטל עליה: 'placed upon it,' a duty imposed.

hayomYom.english: The order of birchot haTorah: With the tallit touch the beginning and ending of the reading, kiss the tallit where it touched the Torah, roll up the Torah, turn your face slightly to the right, say the b'racha, open the Torah and read. __________ In describing the unique qualities of humankind, four terms are used: Adam refers to the quality of mind and intellect; ish to the quality of heart and emotion; enosh, weakness in either intellect or emotion or both; gever, who overcomes inner weakness and removes obstacles and hindrances to the attainment of an intellectual or emotional quality. I.e. gever works upon enosh to elevate him to the plane of ish or adam. Since it is possible to turn enosh into ish or adam, it is obvious that enosh already possesses the qualities found in ish and adam.
hayomYom.hebrew:
סדר ברכות התורה: נוגע בטליתו בתחילת הקריאה ובסופה נושק הטלית במקום שנגע בס"ת [בספר תורה], גולל הס"ת [הספר תורה], מפנה פניו, קצת, לימין ומברך. פותח הס"ת [הספר תורה] וקורא.

במעלת מין האנושי, ישנם ארבעה תוארים: אדם - מעלת המוחין והשכל, איש - מעלת הלב והמדות, אנוש - החלישות באחד מהם בשכל או במדות, או בשתיהם, גבר - מתגבר על עצמו להסיר המניעות ועיכובים להשיג אחת המעלות או בשכל או במדות, היינו דגבר עוסק עם האנוש להגביהו למעלת איש או אדם.

ומאחר דאפשר לעשות מאנוש איש או אדם, הרי בהכרח דגם באנוש ישנם כל אותם המעלות שישנם באיש וגם באדם.
hayomYom.clear:
The order of the Torah blessings: With your tallis, touch [the Sefer Torah] at the beginning and the end of the reading. Kiss the tallis where it touched the Sefer Torah. Roll the Sefer Torah closed, turn your face slightly to the right, and say the bracha. Open the Sefer Torah and read.

Regarding the qualities of humankind, there are four titles:

Adam: the quality of mind and intellect.
Ish: the quality of heart and emotions.
Enosh: weakness in one of them, intellect or emotions, or in both.
Gever: one who overcomes himself to remove the obstacles and hindrances to reaching one of these qualities, in intellect or emotions. That is, gever works with enosh to raise him to the level of ish or adam.

And since it is possible to make enosh into ish or adam, it must be that enosh too has all the qualities found in ish and in adam.
translationNotes: גבר / מתגבר: gever is one who is misgaber, who overcomes himself. Kehot loses the wordplay.
עוסק עם: 'works with, deals with.'

hayomYom.english: Our custom in donning the tallit gadol: Place the folded tallit on the right shoulder. Inspect the tzitzit while reciting borchi nafshi (p. 11). Remove the tallit from the shoulder and open it. Kiss the top border. Twirl the tallit away from in front of the face to a position behind you. Begin the b'racha l'hitateif b'tzitzit. Complete the b'racha close to placing the two right corners (of the tallit) around the neck over the left shoulder. (See Sh'eirit Yehuda, Orach Chayim, 1, and Divrei Nechemya, Orach Chayim, 9.)
hayomYom.hebrew:
מנהגנו בלבישת טלית גדול: מניחים הט"ג [הטלית גדול] מקופל על כתף ימין ובודקים הציצית. בשעת הבדיקה אומרים ברכי נפשי גו'. אח"כ [אחר כך] לוקחים הטלית מן הכתף, פושטים אותו, מנשקים שפת הטלית, מחזיר אותו מכנגד פניו לאחוריו ומתחיל ברכת להתעטף בציצית, סיום הברכה סמוך לכריכת ב' כנפות ימין סביב צוארו לאחוריו בצד שמאל.

[עיין שארית יהודא או"ח [אורח חיים] ס"א [סימן אלף], דברי נחמיה או"ח [אורח חיים] ס"ט [סימן טית].
hayomYom.clear:
Our custom when putting on the tallis gadol:

Place the tallis gadol, folded, on the right shoulder, and check the tzitzis. While checking, say Barchi nafshi.

Then take the tallis off the shoulder, spread it open, and kiss the edge of the tallis. Swing it from in front of your face to behind you, and begin the bracha l'hisateif b'tzitzis.

Finish the bracha just before wrapping the two right corners around your neck to the back, on the left side.

(See Sh'eiris Yehudah, Orach Chaim 1; Divrei Nechemiah, Orach Chaim 9.)
translationNotes: Matches the original. No meaning lost.

hayomYom.english: The Tzemach Tzedek related: The Baal Shem Tov was very fond of light, and said, "Or ('light') is the numerical equivalent of raz ('secret'). Whoever knows the 'secret' contained in every thing can bring illumination."
hayomYom.hebrew: הצ"צ [הצמח צדק] סיפר: דער בעש"ט [בעל שם טוב] האט זייער האלט געהאט ליכטיקייט ואמר: אור בגימטריא רז, דער וואס ווייס דעם סוד וואס אין יעדער זאך, קאן ליכטיג מאכען.
hayomYom.clear: The Tzemach Tzedek related: The Baal Shem Tov loved light very much. He said: Or [light] has the same numerical value as raz [secret]. Whoever knows the secret that is in each thing can make it shine.
translationNotes: ליכטיקייט: brightness, a well-lit space.
ליכטיג מאכען: 'make it bright, make it shine.'

hayomYom.english: The Alter Rebbe instructed that in the phrase p'tzua daka, the word daka be written (in the Torah scroll) with an alef at the end, not with a hay. In Prague there is a Torah scroll which - according to local tradition - had been examined and emended by Ezra the Scribe. It is read only on Simchat Torah and is always rolled to the portion of sh'ma. When I was in Prague in 5668 (1908) I saw that scroll, and in it daka is spelled with an alef. So too when I was in Worms in 5667 (1907), I saw a sefer-Torah written - according to their tradition - by Rabbi Meir of Rotenberg, and there too the word daka was written with an alef. See also Sh'eirit Yehuda, (Yoreh De'a, 16) and Divrei Nechemya (Yoreh De'a, 22) Mishnat Avraham (Sect. 32) cites a number of works that deal with this subject.
hayomYom.hebrew:
אדמו"ר [אדוננו מורנו ורבנו] הזקן הורה לכתוב פצוע דכא באלף לבסוף ולא בהא.

בפראג יש ס"ת [ספר תורה] שקבלה בידם שהגי-ה עזרא הסופר, אין קורין בו אלא בשמח"ת [בשמחת תורה] וגוללין אותו תמיד בפרשת שמע. כשהייתי בפראג בשנת תרס"ח ראיתיה וכתוב בו "דכא" באלף. כן כשהייתי בוארמס בשנת תרס"ז ראיתי שם ס"ת [ספר תורה] אשר מקובל בידם שכתבו מהר"ם [מורנו הרב ר' מאיר] מרוטנבורג וגם בו כתוב דכא באלף. ועיין בשארית יהודא [יו"ד [יורה דעה] סימן ט"ז] ודברי נחמיה [יו"ד [יורה דעה] סימן כ"ב]. ובספר משנת אברהם [סימן ל"ב] מציין כמה ספרים הדנים בזה.
hayomYom.clear:
The Alter Rebbe instructed that petzua daka (Devarim 23:2) be written with an alef at the end, not a hei.

In Prague there is a Sefer Torah which, by their tradition, Ezra the Scribe proofread. They read from it only on Simchas Torah, and it is always kept rolled to the portion of Shema. When I was in Prague in 5668 [1908], I saw it, and in it daka is written with an alef.

Likewise, when I was in Worms in 5667 [1907], I saw a Sefer Torah there which, by their tradition, was written by the Maharam of Rothenburg, and in it too daka is written with an alef.

See Sh'eiris Yehudah (Yoreh De'ah 16) and Divrei Nechemiah (Yoreh De'ah 22). The book Mishnas Avraham (32) cites several works that discuss this.
translationNotes: הגיה: 'proofread, corrected.'
קבלה בידם: 'they have a tradition,' a received tradition, not just local lore.

hayomYom.english: The Tzemach Tzedek listed three things by whose virtue he was successful at the Rabbinical Convention in Petersburg in 5603 (1843). One of these was the merit of the thirty-two thousand hours that he labored over the Alter Rebbe's discourses over the span of the thirty years from 5564 to 5594. (In 5564 - 1804 - he designated a special period to study the Alter Rebbe's discourses, and in 5594 - 1834 - work was begun on their publication.
hayomYom.hebrew: הצ"צ [הצמח צדק] מנה שלשה דברים שבזכותם הצליח בשנת תר"ג בפטרבורג באסיפת הרבנים. ואחד מהם הוא זכות שלשים ושתים אלף השעות, אשר טרח ויגע בדרושי רבינו הזקן במשך שלשים השנים תקס"ד-תקצ"ד [בשנת תקס"ד קבע לו שיעור מיוחד ללמוד דרושי רבינו הזקן, בשנת תקצ"ד התחילו להתעסק בהדפסתם].
hayomYom.clear:
The Tzemach Tzedek listed three things in whose merit he succeeded at the rabbinical conference in Petersburg in 5603 [1843].

One of them was the merit of the thirty-two thousand hours he toiled and labored over the Alter Rebbe's maamarim during the thirty years from 5564 to 5594 [1804 to 1834]. (In 5564 he set himself a special fixed study time for the Alter Rebbe's maamarim, and in 5594 they began working on publishing them.)
translationNotes: טרח ויגע: 'toiled and labored,' two words for exhausting effort.
קבע לו שיעור: set himself a fixed study session.

hayomYom.english: My grandfather said in reference to hitbon'nut, the profoundly concentrated contemplation on a subject extremely difficult to comprehend: If the subject is of deep personal concern, the person will come to understand and comprehend it very well. The proof of this is in the Torah, in laws involving women, etc., and the ingenious arguments that they may put forth on their own behalf. These arguments are discussed by Tanaim, Amoraim and Gaonim, all exceptionally brilliant minds, and the Torah is the Torah of Truth. Yet this woman is far removed, intellectually, from being able to devise such (ingenious, brilliant) claims. But the truth is that when a subject is of deep concern to a person, even those of weak intellect will come up with profound concepts.
hayomYom.hebrew: אאזמו"ר [אדוני אבי זקני מורי ורבי] אמר - ביחס להתבוננות בהעמקת הדעת בענין קשה ההשגה: אם הענין נוגע אזי מבינים ומשיגים בכי טוב, וראיה מן התורה בדיני נשים וכו' וטענותיהן שיכולות לטעון. ומדברים בזה תנאים ואמוראים והגאונים שכולם הם בעלי השכלה מופלגה, והתורה היא תורת אמת, והלא האשה אינה בערך לטעון טענות אלו. אבל האמת הוא, דכאשר הענין נוגע הנה גם חלושי הדעת ממציאים שכליים עמוקים.
hayomYom.clear:
My grandfather [the Rebbe Maharash] said, about hisbonenus [deep contemplation] on a subject that is hard to grasp: If the subject truly matters to you personally, you will understand and grasp it very well.

The proof is from the Torah: the laws concerning women, and the claims a woman is able to make. Tannaim, Amoraim and Geonim discuss these claims, all of them men of outstanding intellect, and the Torah is a Torah of truth. Yet surely the woman herself is nowhere near the level to make such claims.

But the truth is: when a matter touches you personally, even people of weak intellect come up with deep ideas.
translationNotes: אם הענין נוגע: “if the matter touches you,” i.e. you have a personal stake. Kehot’s “of deep personal concern” is close.
Kehot adds “(ingenious, brilliant)” and “on their own behalf.” The Hebrew just says “these claims.”

hayomYom.english: Great elders of the Alter Rebbe's chassidim used to say that yechidus (private audience with the Rebbe) means: "clear," "designated," "united." The sources of these three interpretations are in Shekalim 6:2, Yevamot 62a, and Bereishit Raba 20. This means that the idea of yechidus is: To clarify one's own status; To designate a mode of avoda for him in "turn(ing) away from evil" and in the acquisition of fine character traits; And that he should bind himself in total oneness, and utterly dedicate himself1 with all his desires.
hayomYom.hebrew:
גדולי זקני חסידי רבינו הזקן היו אומרים, אשר "יחידות" פירושו: קלאר, אפגעשטעלט, פאראיינציגט - מקור ג' פירושים אלו הוא בדרז"ל [בדברי רבותינו זכרונם לברכה]: שקלים פ"ו [פרק ו'] מ"ב [משנה ב'], יבמות ס"ב. א, בראשית רבה פ"ך [פרק כ'] -

זאת אומרת כי ענין היחידות הוא לברר את מצבו, ולקבוע אופן עבודתו בסור מרע ולקרב את המדות הטובות, ולהתקשר בהתאחדות גמורה ולמסור עצמו, איבערגעבען זיך מיט אלע רצונות.
hayomYom.clear:
The great elder chassidim of the Alter Rebbe used to say that “yechidus” [private audience with the Rebbe] means three things: “clear,” “set in place,” and “united.” The sources for these three meanings are in the words of the Sages: Shekalim chapter 6, mishna 2; Yevamos 62a; and Bereishis Rabbah chapter 20.

That is to say, yechidus is about:
1. Clarifying where you stand.
2. Setting your way of avoda in “turning away from evil” and in drawing close to good character traits.
3. Binding yourself in complete unity and giving yourself over, surrendering yourself with all your desires.
translationNotes: The three Yiddish words: קלאר (clear), אפגעשטעלט (set in place, settled; Kehot “designated”), פאראיינציגט (united).
לברר את מצבו: “clarify your state.” Kehot’s “status” is slightly off.
איבערגעבען זיך מיט אלע רצונות: “hand yourself over with all your desires.” Kehot’s “utterly dedicate himself” softens it.

hayomYom.english: On Shabbat Teitsei 5603 (1843), at the Kiddush table by day, the Tzemach Tzedek said: "This world is a world of falsity, therefore even good is adulterated with chaff and must be purified 'from below upward' as well as from 'Above downward.' Olam haba (the Coming World) is the world of truth. In Torah there are discussions of matters which may appear negative, yet the same matters, as they are studied in gan eden - are actually positive qualities." Then the Rebbe began to sing, and indicated with a motion of his hand that everyone join him. His sons began singing, then all the chassidim joined in; the singing enflamed and aroused all hearts. When the Tzemach Tzedek stopped singing, he said: "In This World the meaning of the passage (Sanhedrin 99b) 'He who studies Torah liprakim,' means one who studies Torah intermittently; in gan eden they interpret the passage to mean that he studies Torah and the Torah 'takes him apart', the words of Torah possess him."
hayomYom.hebrew: ש"פ [שבת פרשת] תצא תר"ג בשולחן קדוש היום הואיל הצ"צ [הצמח צדק] לאמר: עוה"ז [עולם הזה] הוא עלמא דשיקרא, לכן הנה גם בהטוב מעורב פסולת, וצריך בירור בדרך מלמטה למעלה ובדרך מלמעלה למטה. העוה"ב [העולם הבא] הוא עלמא דקשוט - הנה גם הדברים בדברי תורה המדברים בענינים הנראים לחסרון, הרי כמו שלומדים אותם בג"ע [בגן עדן] הם מעלה. - והתחיל לנגן, והראה בידו הקדושה לאות כי ינגנו אתו. בני הצ"צ [הצמח צדק] התחילו לנגן ואחריהם ענו כל החסידים בקול שיר שהלהיב הלבבות. - כשגמר לנגן אמר הצ"צ [הצמח צדק]: בעלמא דין איז דער טייטש פון דעם מאמר [סנהדרין צט. ב] הלומד תורה לפרקים אז ער לערענט תורה צייטענווייז. אין ג"ע [גן עדן] טייטשט מען דעם מאמר אז ער לערענט תורה און די תורה נעהמט איהם פאנאנדער, די דברי תורה דערנעמען איהם.
hayomYom.clear:
On Shabbos parshas Teitzei 5603 (1843), at the daytime Kiddush meal, the Tzemach Tzedek said:

This world is a world of falsehood. So even in the good there is waste mixed in, and it needs refining, both from below upward and from Above downward. The World to Come is a world of truth. Even things in the Torah that discuss matters which look like a flaw are, as they are studied in Gan Eden, a virtue.

Then he began to sing, and signaled with his holy hand that they should sing with him. The Tzemach Tzedek’s sons began to sing, and all the chassidim joined them in song that set hearts on fire.

When he finished singing, the Tzemach Tzedek said: In this world, the saying (Sanhedrin 99b) “One who learns Torah liprakim” is understood to mean that he learns Torah from time to time. In Gan Eden they explain it to mean that he learns Torah and the Torah takes him apart: the words of Torah take hold of him.
translationNotes: עלמא דשיקרא / עלמא דקשוט: Aramaic, “world of falsehood” / “world of truth.”
לפרקים is a play on words: “at intervals,” and also “into pieces.” די תורה נעמט איהם פאנאנדער: “the Torah takes him apart.”
פסולת is waste, the refuse left after sorting. Kehot’s “chaff” is close.

hayomYom.english: The long hemsheich (series of maamarim) known as "B'sha'a shehikdimu, Te'erav" was begun by my father on the first day of Shavuot 5672 (1912) in Lubavitch. He finished it on the Shabbat of parsha Vayeira 5676 (1915) in Rostov - with the maamar which begins VaHashem amar. The hemsheich contains 144 maamarim. Extant in manuscript is a second section which he had not delivered orally, and which is not divided into maamarim.
hayomYom.hebrew:
המשך הגדול הידוע בשם "בשעה שהקדימו, תער"ב" התחיל אאמו"ר [אדוני אבי מורי ורבי] לאמרו יום א' דחגה"ש [דחג השבועות] תער"ב בליובאוויטש, וסיימו ש"פ [שבת פרשת] וירא תרע"ו ברוסטוב, במאמר המתחיל וה' אמר המכסה אני מאברהם. ובו קמ"ד מאמרים.

ויש בכתובים חלק שני שלא אמרו, ולא נחלק למאמרים.
hayomYom.clear:
The great hemshech [series of maamarim] known as “B’sha’ah shehikdimu, 5672” was begun by my father [the Rebbe Rashab] on the first day of Shavuos 5672 (1912) in Lubavitch. He finished it on Shabbos parshas Vayeira 5676 (1915) in Rostov, with the maamar that begins “Vahashem amar, hamechaseh ani me’Avraham.” It contains 144 maamarim.

There is also a second part in manuscript that he did not say aloud, and it is not divided into maamarim.
translationNotes: Kehot cuts the closing maamar’s title to “VaHashem amar.” The Hebrew gives the full opening: וה' אמר המכסה אני מאברהם (Bereishis 18:17).
תער"ב is the year 5672, part of the hemshech’s name.

hayomYom.english: The chassid R. Hendel related: It was known to all chassidim that at one's first yechidus the orla (insensitive "thick skin") was removed. Whatever else, one was immediately rid of the orla of the heart.
hayomYom.hebrew: החסיד ר' הענדיל סיפר: ידוע היה לכל החסידים, אשר ביחידות הראשונה היתה העברת הערלה, וואס ניט וואס, פון ערלת הלב איז מען גלייך פטור געווארען.
hayomYom.clear: The chassid R. Hendel related: All the chassidim knew that at your first yechidus, the orlah [the coarse “covering” on the heart] was removed. Whatever else happened, you were immediately rid of the orlah of the heart.
translationNotes: וואס ניט וואס: “whatever else,” “no matter what.”
העברת הערלה: “removal of the orlah.” Kehot’s “insensitive thick skin” is a gloss, not in the text.

hayomYom.english: From my father's guiding instructions: Keep away - to the ultimate degree - from a campaign of attack. Not because we lack the means of prevailing or because of timorousness, but because we must consecrate all our strength exclusively to strengthening our own structure, the edifice of Torah and mitzvot performed in holiness and purity. To this we must devote ourselves utterly, with actual mesirat nefesh, not merely with potential mesirat nefesh.
hayomYom.hebrew: מהוראות אאמו"ר [אדוני אבי מורי ורבי]: להנזר ממלחמת תנופה עד קצה האחרון, לא מפני שאין לנו במה לנצח או מפני מורך לב, אלא מפני שאת כל כוחותינו עלינו להקדיש אך ורק לחיזוק בנינינו, בנין התורה והמצות בקדושה ובטהרה. ועל זה עלינו למסור את נפשותינו במס"נ [במסירת נפש] בפועל ולא רק בכח.
hayomYom.clear:
From my father’s [the Rebbe Rashab’s] instructions:

Keep away, to the very last degree, from an offensive war. Not because we have nothing to win with, and not out of faintheartedness. It is because we must dedicate all our strength, only and exclusively, to strengthening our own building: the building of Torah and mitzvos, in holiness and purity.

For this we must give our very selves, with actual mesirus nefesh [self-sacrifice], not only potential.
translationNotes: מלחמת תנופה: an attacking war, an offensive. Kehot’s “campaign of attack” is fine.
במס"נ בפועל ולא רק בכח: actual mesirus nefesh, not just readiness for it.

hayomYom.english: The founding of Yeshivat Tomchei T'mimim was on Sunday, Elul 15, 5657 (1897). The beginning of studies in Talmud and Chassidus was on Wednesday, Elul 18, 5657 (1897). On Simchat-Torah-eve, 5659 (1898), after hakafot, my father proclaimed: The name of the Yeshiva is Tomchei T'mimim, and the students who study and conduct themselves in its spirit are to be called t'mimim.
hayomYom.hebrew:
התיסדות ישיבת "תומכי תמימים". יום א' ט"ו אלול תרנ"ז.

התחלת הלימוד בנגלה ודא"ח [ודברי אלקים חיים]: יום ד' ח"י אלול תרנ"ז.

בליל שמח"ת [שמחת תורה] תרנ"ט אחרי ההקפות הכריז אאמו"ר [אדוני אבי מורי ורבי]: הישיבה שמה "תומכי תמימים" ותלמידים הלומדים ומתנהגים ברוחה שמם "תמימים".
hayomYom.clear:
The founding of the Tomchei Temimim yeshiva: Sunday, 15 Elul 5657 (1897).

Study of nigleh [Talmud and halacha] and Chassidus began: Wednesday, 18 Elul 5657.

On the night of Simchas Torah 5659 (1898), after hakafos, my father [the Rebbe Rashab] proclaimed: The yeshiva’s name is “Tomchei Temimim,” and the students who learn and conduct themselves in its spirit are called “Temimim.”
translationNotes: Matches the original. No meaning lost.

hayomYom.english: The Alter Rebbe interpreted the statement, "Whoever saves a single person of (the people) Israel is as though he saved an entire world": One must perceive a Jew as he stands in the primordial thought of Adam Kadmon. There, each soul stands with all the generations destined to descend from it until the coming of Mashiach, the righteous Redeemer. When one does a favor to an individual, it is a favor to all those souls until the end of all generations.
hayomYom.hebrew: רבינו הזקן פירש מאמר כל המקיים נפש אחת מישראל כאלו קיים עולם מלא, אויף א אידען דארף מען קוקען ווי ער שטייט אין מחשבה הקדומה דא"ק [דאדם קדמון], און דארטען שטייט יעדער נשמה מיט אלע דורות וואס קומען ארויס פון איהר ביז ביאת המשיח גואל צדק, און אז מען טוט א אידען א טובה, טוט מען א טובה, אט די אלע נשמות עד סוף כל הדורות.
hayomYom.clear:
The Alter Rebbe explained the saying “Whoever sustains one soul of Israel is as if he sustained an entire world” (Sanhedrin 37a):

You have to look at a Jew as he stands in the primordial thought of Adam Kadmon. There, each soul stands together with all the generations that will come from it, until the coming of Mashiach, the righteous redeemer. So when you do a favor for one Jew, you are doing a favor for all those souls, to the end of all generations.
translationNotes: אויף א אידען דארף מען קוקען: “you have to look at a Jew.” It is a way of seeing, not just a teaching.
המקיים: “sustains,” not only “saves.”

hayomYom.english: The Alter Rebbe himself was the regular Torah-reader. Once he was away from Lyozna on the Shabbat of parsha Tavo, and the Mitteler Rebbe, then not yet Bar Mitzva, heard the Torah-reading from another. His anguish at the curses in the tochacha (section of admonition) caused him so much heartache, that on Yom Kippur the Alter Rebbe doubted whether his son would be able to fast. When they asked the Mitteler Rebbe - "Don't you hear this parsha every year?" - he replied, "When Father reads, one hears no curses."
hayomYom.hebrew:
רבינו הזקן הי-ה בעצמו הקורא בתורה. פעם אחת לא הי-ה בליאזנא ש"פ [שבת פרשת] תבא, ושמע אדמו"ר [אדוננו מורנו ורבנו] האמצעי - והוא עודנו נער קודם הבר מצוה - הקריאה מאחר. העגמת נפש מהקללות שבתוכחה הביאתו לכאב לב, עד שביוהכ"פ [שביום הכפורים] נסתפק רבינו הזקן אם יוכל להתענות.

כששאלו את אדמו"ר [אדוננו מורנו ורבנו] האמצעי הרי בכל שנה קורים פרשה זו, ענה: כשאבא קורא "הערט זיך ניט קיין קללות".
hayomYom.clear:
The Alter Rebbe himself was the one who read the Torah. Once he was away from Liozna on Shabbos parshas Tavo, and the Mitteler Rebbe, who was still a boy before his bar mitzvah, heard the reading from someone else. The anguish from the curses in the tochacha [the section of rebuke] caused him such heartache that on Yom Kippur the Alter Rebbe was unsure whether he would be able to fast.

They asked the Mitteler Rebbe: “But this parsha is read every year!” He answered: “When Father reads, you don’t hear any curses.”
translationNotes: הערט זיך ניט קיין קללות: “no curses are heard,” in Yiddish in the original.
עגמת נפש ... כאב לב: grief of the soul that turned into heartache. Kehot keeps both.

hayomYom.english: Birth of the Baal Shem Tov in 5458 (1698). The day his holy teacher and master appeared to him in 5484 (1724). The day the Baal Shem Tov became revealed in 5494 (1734). Birth of the Alter Rebbe 5505 (1745). Outline of the Baal Shem Tov's discourse on Shabbat Tavo, Chai (18th) Elul 5652 (1892), after Kabalat Shabbat: It will be when you come into the land (eretz) that the Eternal your G‑d gives you for an inheritance, and you will inherit it and dwell in it. The Midrash notes that eretz is an idiom of merutza (running) and of ratzon (will, desire). When you attain the level of ratzon, "desire," that is a gift from Above and an inheritance for every one of Israel, then your avoda is "...you will dwell in it" - to internalize all you have attained, "bringing it down" in a settled manner. "You shall take...and place it in a basket," - draw down the (spiritual) lights into (appropriate) vessels. "You shall go to the place the Eternal your G‑d will choose" - a Jew must know that when he goes from one place to another, he is not going on his own, but is being directed from Above. And the intention and purpose in this is... "...to cause His Name to dwell there" - that is, to make G‑d known in his (that Jew's) locale. After Maariv the Baal Shem Tov repeated this discourse and added: "It will be when you come..." For you to attain the level of "desire" etc. it is necessary that... "you shall go to the place, etc... to cause His Name to dwell there." You are to utterly dedicate yourself to making G‑d known there. How does one "make G‑d known"? With a b'racha and a verse of Tehillim.
hayomYom.hebrew: לששי עולה הבעל קורא, ומעצמו.
hayomYom.clear:
Birthday of the Baal Shem Tov, 5458 (1698).
The day his holy teacher and master appeared to him, 5484 (1724).
The day the Baal Shem Tov was revealed, 5494 (1734).
Birthday of the Alter Rebbe, 5505 (1745).

An outline of the Baal Shem Tov’s teaching on Shabbos Tavo, Chai Elul, after Kabbalas Shabbos:

“It will be, when you come into the land (eretz) that Hashem your G‑d gives you as an inheritance, and you inherit it and settle in it.” The Midrash says that “eretz” is related to running (merutzah) and to will (ratzon). When you reach the level of ratzon, a gift from Above and an inheritance for every Jew, then your avoda is “and you settle in it”: to make what you have reached part of you, and bring it down in a settled way.

“You shall take ... and put it in a basket”: draw the lights down into vessels.

“You shall go to the place that Hashem your G‑d will choose”: a Jew must know that when he goes from one place to another, he is not going on his own. He is being led from Above, and the intention and purpose is “to make His Name dwell there”: to make G‑d known in that place.

After Maariv the Baal Shem Tov repeated this teaching and added: “It will be, when you come ...”: for you to reach the level of ratzon, you have to “go to the place ... to make His Name dwell there.” You must give yourself over completely to making G‑d known there.

How do you make G‑d known? With a blessing, and with a verse of Tehillim.
translationNotes: The Hebrew field holds only a calendar line, so this follows the Kehot English. The year printed in the English (5652) cannot be the Baal Shem Tov’s own Shabbos Tavo, so it is left out; check against the Hebrew original.

calendar.original5703: The Torah reader takes the sixth aliyah [the tochacha] himself, calling himself up.

hayomYom.dataFlag: Hebrew field holds only the calendar line (לששי עולה הבעל קורא, ומעצמו); main text missing. Translated from English. English dates the Baal Shem Tov’s discourse “Chai Elul 5652 (1892),” which is impossible (he passed in 1760); year omitted, needs checking against the Hebrew original.

hayomYom.english: When the Alter Rebbe was still in Vitebsk he once expounded on the verse "You stand..." Taking eitz (wood) as an idiom of eitza (counsel), he interpreted "choppers of wood" to mean that one must chop out "the many thoughts (counsels) in the heart of man." "Those who draw water," he interpreted - one must drain out the water that "makes all enjoyments grow."
hayomYom.hebrew: רבינו הזקן זייענדיג נאך אין וויטעבסק, האט אמאל געזאגט א תורה אויפ'ן פסוק אתם נצבים גו', און האט געטייטשט מחוטב עצך לשון עצה, מ'דארף אויסהאקען די רבות מחשבות בלב איש, שואב מימיך אויסשעפען די מים וואס מצמיחים כל מיני תענוג..
hayomYom.clear: While the Alter Rebbe was still in Vitebsk, he once said a teaching on the verse “You are standing ...” (Devarim 29:9). He explained “the hewer of your wood (eitzecha)” as related to eitzah, “counsel”: you must chop away “the many thoughts in a man’s heart” (Mishlei 19:21). And “the drawer of your water”: you must drain out the water that makes every kind of pleasure grow.
translationNotes: אויסהאקען: “chop out.” אויסשעפען: “scoop out, drain out.”
כל מיני תענוג: “every kind of pleasure,” not only “all enjoyments.”

hayomYom.english: One who is lowly and crass does not sense his own crassness and lowliness.
hayomYom.hebrew: דער וואס איז נידעריג און גראב הערט ניט אן די אייגענע גראבקייט און נידעריקייט.
hayomYom.clear: Someone who is low and coarse does not sense his own coarseness and lowness.
translationNotes: הערט ניט אן: “does not feel, does not sense.” Matches Kehot.

hayomYom.english: Our first father, Avraham, as a result of his avoda with self-sacrifice to make G‑d - the one G‑d - widely known among all mankind, merited to bequeath to his descendants (to the end of all generations) pure faith in G‑d and His Torah. Hence, every Jewish man and woman has the power and fortitude to offer his life for the holy Torah.
hayomYom.hebrew: אבינו הראשון אברהם בגלל עבודתו במסירת נפש לפרסם אלקותו יתברך - אל אחד - לכל בני העולם, זכה להנחיל לזרעו עד סוף כל הדורות את האמונה הטהורה בה' ובתורתו, וכל איש ואשה בישראל יש להם הכח והעוז למסור נפשם על התורה הקדושה.
hayomYom.clear: Our first father, Avraham, through his avoda with mesirus nefesh to publicize G‑d’s Divinity, the One G‑d, to all the people of the world, earned the merit to pass down to his descendants, to the end of all generations, pure faith in G‑d and His Torah. And so every Jewish man and woman has the strength and the courage to give their life for the holy Torah.
translationNotes: לפרסם: “to publicize,” make widely known.
הכח והעוז: “the strength and the boldness.”

hayomYom.english: Chassidic doctrine demands that before reproving another, one must pare his own "fingernails," in order not to gash the other. "They (the forces of evil) seize by the fingernails"; every stab is k'lipa and sitra achra. After the "nails" are pared there must be "laving the hands," as explained in Chassidus - calling forth intellect into emotion.
hayomYom.hebrew: תורת החסידות דורשת, כי תחלה להוכחה צריכים להסיר את הצפרנים, ניט שטעכען זיך, כי בטופרהא אחידן, יעדער שטאך איז קליפה וסטרא אחרא, ואחר נטילת הצפרנים צריך להיות נטילת ידים, כמבואר ענינה בדא"ח [בדברי אלקים חיים], המשכת המוחין למדות.
hayomYom.clear:
The teaching of Chassidus demands that before you rebuke someone, you must first remove your fingernails, so as not to stab. Because “they [the forces of evil] grab hold by the nails,” and every stab is kelipah and sitra achra [the side of unholiness].

After cutting the nails, there must be washing of the hands, which, as Chassidus explains, means drawing the intellect down into the emotions.
translationNotes: ניט שטעכען זיך: “not to stab,” Yiddish in the original. Kehot’s “gash” is close.
בטופרהא אחידן: Aramaic, “they hold on by the nails.”

hayomYom.english: When R. Moshe, son of the Alter Rebbe, was between eight and eleven years old, he was studying the passage in Gittin 67a lauding the virtues of the sages. There R. Shimon bar Yochai said, "Learn my midot." R. Moshe was in doubt about the meaning of that last word, since there is Rashi's interpretation, "my teachings," and the simple meaning, "traits of character." At that moment the Alter Rebbe came in and said, in the chant he habitually used: "The Torah given us is all fine character-traits. Even the punishments there, are in truth acts of kindness and goodness. The two interpretations are one, and interdependent. There can be no fine character-traits without Torah; there can be no Torah without fine character." Exactly the same incident happened to the Tzemach Tzedek, when he was between eight and eleven.
hayomYom.hebrew: ר' משה, בנו של רבינו הזקן בלמדו - והוא אז כבן ח' - י"א שנה - הסוגיא בשבחן של חכמים בגטין [ס"ז א] נסתפק במאמר רשב"י [רבי שמעון בן יוחאי] שם שנו מדותי שיש בזה שני פירושים: לימדו תורתי [רש"י] או מדותי כפשוטו. בתוך כך נכנס רבינו הזקן ואמר - בניגון, כדרכו בקדש: תורה שניתנה לנו כולה מדות טובות, אפילו העונשין שבה הם באמת חסד וטוב, ושני הפירושים אחד הם והא בהא תליא: אי אפשר להיות מדות טובות בלי תורה, ואי אפשר לתורה בלי מדות טובות. ככל הנ"ל [הנזכר לעיל] קרה גם להצ"צ [להצמח צדק] בהיותו בגיל ח' - י"א שנה.
hayomYom.clear:
When R. Moshe, son of the Alter Rebbe, was about eight to eleven years old, he was studying the passage in Gittin (67a) in praise of the Sages. He was unsure about the words of R. Shimon bar Yochai there, “Learn my middos,” since there are two explanations: “my teachings” (Rashi), or “my character traits” in the plain sense.

Just then the Alter Rebbe came in and said, in a chant, as was his holy way: The Torah that was given to us is all good character traits. Even its punishments are truly kindness and good. The two explanations are one, and each depends on the other: there cannot be good traits without Torah, and there cannot be Torah without good traits.

All of the above happened to the Tzemach Tzedek as well, when he was eight to eleven years old.
translationNotes: והא בהא תליא: “this one depends on that one,” mutual dependence.
בניגון, כדרכו בקדש: “in a chant, as was his holy way.”

hayomYom.english: There was a time when every brief saying one heard was regarded as a "Torah" (teaching, guidance), and everything one saw was perceived as an instruction in his avoda and conduct.
hayomYom.hebrew: אמאל איז יעדער ווארט וואס מ'האט געהערט געווען א תורה, און יעדער זאך וואס מ'האט געזעהן - א הוראה אין עבודה און הדרכה.
hayomYom.clear: There was a time when every word you heard was a “Torah” [a teaching], and everything you saw was a lesson in avoda and in how to conduct yourself.
translationNotes: אמאל: “once,” “in the past,” with a note of longing.
הוראה ... והדרכה: an instruction and guidance.

hayomYom.english: Say the entire Tehillim in the early morning. Day of farbrengen. S'lichot immediately after midnight, but on the remaining s'lichot days - in the early morning. When Nitzavim and Vayeilech are separate, the Maftir and Shevi'i of Nitzavim begin at Re'ei natati l'fanecha... The Alter Rebbe related: When I was in Mezritch I heard from my Rebbe, the Maggid, in the name of the Baal Shem Tov: The seventh month (Tishrei), first of the months of the year, is blessed by G‑d Himself, on Shabbat mevarchim - last Shabbat in the month of Elul. With this power Israel blesses the other months eleven times a year. It is written, Atem nitzavim hayom, "You stand this day." This day refers to Rosh Hashana which is the day of Judgment (as it is written, "The day came," which Targum renders, the day of the great judgment came). Yet you remain standing firmly upright (nitzavim), meaning - you will be vindicated in judgment. On the Shabbat preceding Rosh Hashana, the last Shabbat in Elul, we read the parsha of Atem nitzavim, which is G‑d's blessing on the Shabbat-of-blessing the seventh month (Shabbat mevarchim). That seventh month (Tishrei) is itself sated - and in turn satiates all Israel - with an abundance of good for the duration of the (coming) year."
hayomYom.hebrew: אדמו"ר [אדוננו מורנו ורבינו] הזקן סיפר: בהיותי במעזריטש שמעתי ממורי ורבי הה"מ [הרב המגיד] בשם מורו רבו הבעש"ט [הבעל שם טוב] נ"ע [נשמתו עדן]: החדש השביעי שהוא החדש הראשון לחדשי השנה, הקב"ה [הקדוש ברוך הוא] בעצמו מברכו בשבת מברכים שהוא השבת האחרון דחדש אלול, ובכח זה ישראל מברכים את החדשים י"א פעמים בשנה, כתיב אתם נצבים היום, דהיום קאי על ראש השנה שהוא יום הדין, וכמ"ש [וכמו שכתוב] ויהי היום גו' ותרגם והוה יום דינא רבא, ואתם נצבים קיימים ועומדים, והיינו שזוכים בדין, ובשבת שלפני ר"ה [ראש השנה] שהוא שבת האחרון דחדש אלול קוראין אז פרשת אתם נצבים, דזהו ברכתו של הקב"ה [הקדוש ברוך הוא], בשבת מברכים חדש השביעי שהוא המשובע והמשביע ברוב טוב לכל ישראל על כל השנה.
hayomYom.clear:
The Alter Rebbe related: When I was in Mezritch, I heard from my teacher and master, the Maggid, in the name of his teacher and master, the Baal Shem Tov:

The seventh month is the first of the months of the year. G‑d Himself blesses it on Shabbos Mevarchim, which is the last Shabbos of Elul. With this power, the Jewish people bless the other months, eleven times a year.

It is written: “You are standing (nitzavim) today” (Devarim 29:9). “Today” refers to Rosh Hashanah, which is the day of judgment, as it is written, “And it was the day ...” which the Targum renders, “the day of the great judgment came.” And yet “you are standing,” firm and upright: that is, you are found innocent in the judgment.

On the Shabbos before Rosh Hashanah, the last Shabbos of Elul, we read the parsha “You are standing.” This is G‑d’s blessing, on Shabbos Mevarchim, of the seventh month, which is itself full and fills all of Israel with abundant good for the whole year.
translationNotes: המשובע והמשביע: “sated and satiating,” full itself and filling others.
קיימים ועומדים: “standing firm and enduring.”

calendar.original5703: Say the entire Tehillim early in the morning. A day of farbrengen. Selichos right after midnight; on the remaining days of Selichos, early in the morning. When Nitzavim and Vayeilech are read separately, Shevi’i and Maftir of Nitzavim begin at “Re’eh nasati lefanecha.”

hayomYom.dataFlag: Hebrew field lacks the calendar lines (Tehillim, farbrengen, Selichos, Nitzavim aliyos) found in the English; cal translated from the English.

hayomYom.english: The procedure of "kashering" meat for eating - by purging it of forbidden blood - is: Soaking, salting and rinsing. These concepts in avoda: "Soaking" - immersing oneself in the Rebbe's words; "salting" - yechidus; "rinsing" - chassidic song (niggun).
hayomYom.hebrew: סדר הכשר בשר לאכילה להוציא ממנו דם האסור הוא: שרי'[ה], מליחה, הדחה. ענינם בעבודה: שרי-ה - ווייקען זיך אין דברי הרב, מליחה - יחידות, הדחה - ניגון.
hayomYom.clear:
The order of making meat kosher to eat, by drawing out the forbidden blood, is: soaking, salting, rinsing.

What they mean in avoda:
Soaking: soak yourself in the Rebbe’s words.
Salting: yechidus.
Rinsing: a niggun.
translationNotes: ווייקען זיך אין דברי הרב: “soak yourself in the Rebbe’s words,” Yiddish in the original.
Matches the original otherwise.

hayomYom.english: From the holy teachings of the Alter Rebbe: "Israel, one nation on the earth." The nation of Israel, even in the earthly world, is bound up with the one G‑d. G‑d transforms the spiritual into something material; Israel transforms the material into something spiritual.
hayomYom.hebrew: מדברי קודש רבינו הזקן: ישראל גוי אחד בארץ, דער עם ישראל אויך אין דער ערדישער וועלט איז פארבונדען מיט ה' אחד, השי"ת [השם יתברך] מאכט פון רוחניות גשמיות, און דער עם ישראל מאכט פון גשמיות רוחניות.
hayomYom.clear: From the holy words of the Alter Rebbe: “Israel, one nation on the earth” (Shmuel II 7:23). The Jewish people, even in the earthly world, are bound up with the One G‑d. G‑d makes the spiritual into the physical, and the Jewish people make the physical into the spiritual.
translationNotes: ערדישער וועלט: “earthly world,” a play on בארץ, “on the earth.”

hayomYom.english: "G‑d's blessing brings wealth." This is so in general, but especially to whoever gives of his time to occupy himself with the community's needs in matters of charity and strengthening Judaism; as the saying goes, "G‑d does not remain in debt". For every good thing a person does, he is recompensed grandly by G‑d, with children, health and livelihood, in abundance.
hayomYom.hebrew: ברכת ד' היא תעשיר, בכלל ובפרט להנותן מעתו ומזמנו לעסוק בצרכי צבור בעניני צדקה וחזוק היהדות, וכמאמר: דער אויבערשטער ב"ה [ברוך הוא] בלייבט ניט קיין בעל חוב, פאר יעדער גוטער זאך וואס א איד טוט, צאלט ער במיטב מיט בני חיי ומזוני רויחי.
hayomYom.clear: “The blessing of G‑d makes rich” (Mishlei 10:22). This is true in general, and especially for someone who gives of his time to work on the community’s needs: tzedakah and strengthening Yiddishkeit. As the saying goes: “The Almighty does not stay anyone’s debtor.” For every good thing a Jew does, He pays with the very best: with children, life and abundant livelihood.
translationNotes: במיטב: “with the best.” Kehot’s “grandly” loses the idea of top quality.
בני חיי ומזוני רויחי: Aramaic, “children, life and ample sustenance” (Moed Katan 28a). Kehot has “health.”
מעתו ומזמנו: “of his time,” said twice for emphasis.

hayomYom.english: Birth of the Tzemach Tzedek, 5549 (1789). From the Alter Rebbe's aphorisms: We have absolutely no conception how precious to G‑d is the body of a Jew.
hayomYom.hebrew:
יום הולדת את הצמח צדק - שנת תקמ"ט.

מפתגמי רבינו הזקן: מען האט גאר קיין השגה ניט, ווי עס איז טייער בא השי"ת [השם יתברך] דער גוף פון א אידען.
hayomYom.clear:
Birthday of the Tzemach Tzedek, 5549 (1789).

From the Alter Rebbe’s sayings: We have no conception at all how precious the body of a Jew is to G‑d.
translationNotes: Matches the original. No meaning lost.

hayomYom.english: In the b'racha of Candle-lighting: ...shel yom hazikaron (p.127). Shehecheyanu. L'Eila is said only once in kadish, except at Ne'ila. L'david...ha-aretz um'loa... (p. 276) before Aleinu. Daytime kidush: Tiku, ki chok (p. 269); do not say Eileh mo'adei or askinu. At Tashlich (p. 295) shake out corners of the tallit katan. Say Yehi ratzon (p. 277) for the apple after the b'racha, before tasting. Lamb's head is eaten, but Yehi ratzon is said only for the apple.
hayomYom.hebrew:
ברכת הדלקת הנרות: של יום הזכרון. שהחינו. אין כופלין "לעילא" בקדיש, לבד מנעילה. לדוד גו' הארץ ומלואה גו' - קודם עלינו. בקדוש היום: תקעו, כי חק. וא"א [ואין אומרים] אלה מועדי ואתקינו. לתשליך: מנערים שולי הט"ק [הטלית קטן].

יהי רצון שעל התפוח - אחר הברכה וקודם האכילה. אוכלים ראש איל, אבל א"א [אין אומרים] יהי רצון כי אם על התפוח.
hayomYom.clear:
Blessing over the candles: “shel Yom HaZikaron,” and Shehecheyanu.

In Kaddish, “l’eila” is not doubled, except at Ne’ilah.

“L’David ... la’Shem ha’aretz u’melo’ah” is said before Aleinu.

At the daytime Kiddush: “Tiku ... ki chok.” “Eileh mo’adei” and “Askinu” are not said.

At Tashlich, shake out the corners of the tallis katan.

The “Yehi ratzon” over the apple is said after the blessing, before eating. A ram’s head is eaten, but the “Yehi ratzon” is said only over the apple.
translationNotes: אין כופלין לעילא: “l’eila is not repeated” (as in l’eila ul’eila of the Ten Days).
ראש איל: a ram’s head. Kehot’s “lamb’s head” is loose.
Kehot’s page numbers refer to its Siddur and are not in the Hebrew; left out.

hayomYom.english: At Mincha do not say Hodu (p. 124); do say Patach Eliyahu (p. 125). The statement in the Alter Rebbe's Siddur, (Shaar haKriat Sh'ma, in the maamar L'havin hahefresh, p. 74a of that siddur) that prior to sounding the shofar we say Ana b'choach, means this: In general terms they are the kavanot (mystical devotions) of the verses whose initial letters are the second Name of the Name mem-bet. However, some keep the kavanot of the words Ana b'choach in thought, but do not pronounce the letters or words. One who is involved with kavanot must study those subjects in the Arizal's writings until he knows them clearly, and then his kavanot are acceptable and favored.
hayomYom.hebrew:
לאל עורך דין - בתפלת מוסף.

במנחה א"א [אין אומרים] הודו, אבל אומרים פתח אלי']הו[.
