מ"ש [מה שכתוב] בסידור שער הק"ש [הקריאת שמע] ד"ה [דבור המתחיל] להבין ההפרש [ע"ד ע"א [עמוד א']] שקודם תקיעת שופר אומרים אנא בכח, פירושו: בדרך כלל הם הכוונות מהפסוקים שר"ת [שראשי תיבות] שלהם שם שני משם מ"ב, אמנם יש שמכונים התיבות אנא בכח כו' במחשבה, אבל אין אומרים האותיות והתיבות. והעוסק בכוונות צריך ללמוד הענינים ברור בכתהאריז"ל [בכתבי האר"י זכרונו לברכה], ואז כוונתו רצוי'[ה].
hayomYom.clear:
In Musaf: “La’Kel orech din.”

What is written in the Siddur, in Sha’ar HaKrias Shema, in the maamar beginning “L’havin hahefresh” (74a), that before blowing the shofar we say “Ana b’choach,” means this: in general, these are the kavanos [mystical intentions] of the verses whose first letters form the second Name of the 42-letter Name. But some have in mind the words “Ana b’choach” in thought, without saying the letters and words aloud.

Whoever deals in kavanos has to learn these matters clearly in the writings of the Arizal, and then his kavanah is desirable.
translationNotes: The Musaf line לאל עורך דין is dropped by Kehot; restored.
שם מ"ב: the 42-letter Name of G‑d, which “Ana b’choach” encodes.
רצויה: “desirable, accepted.”

calendar.original5703: At Mincha, “Hodu” is not said, but “Pasach Eliyahu” is said.

hayomYom.english: The Tzemach Tzedek had yechidus with the Alter Rebbe on Monday of Teitzei, 6 Elul 5564 (1804); the Rebbe told him: "On Shabbat Tavo 5528 (1768), my Rebbe (the Maggid of Mezritch) said a "Torah" beginning V'shavta ad Havayeh Elokecha He explained that the avoda of teshuva must attain a level at which Havayeh, transcendent Divinity beyond worlds, becomes Elokecha - Elokim being numerically equivalent to hateva (nature), and as we find, "in the beginning Elokim created the heavens and the earth etc." All the Holy Society (disciples of the Maggid) were profoundly stirred by this teaching. The tzadik R. Meshulam Zusya of Anipoli said that he could not attain the heights of such a teshuva; he would therefore break down teshuva to its components, for each letter of the word teshuva is the initial of a verse: T: Tamim - "Be sincere with the Eternal your G‑d." Sh: Shiviti - "I have set G‑d before me always." U: V'ahavta - "Love your fellow as yourself." V: B'chol - "In all your ways, know Him." H: Hatznei'a - "Walk discreetly with your G‑d." When my father told me this, he concluded: "The word teshuva comprises five (Hebrew) letters, each letter a path and a method in the avoda of teshuva." (He explained each method at length). Each moves from a potential state to actuality through the avoda of davening.
hayomYom.hebrew:
מתחילין מזמור לדוד ולא לכו נרננה וכן בכל שבת מוציו"ט [מוצאי יום טוב] הפטורה: שובה - יכשלו בם. מי אל כמוך - מימי קדם.

ביחידות הצ"צ [הצמח צדק] אצל רבינו הזקן ב' תצא בששי באלול תקס"ד סיפר לו רבינו: ש"פ [שבת פרשת] תבוא תקכ"ח אמר מורי ורבי [הרב המגיד ממעזריטש] - תורה והתחלתה ושבת עד הוי' אלקיך, וביאר כי עבודת התשובה צריכה להיות עד אשר הוי', שהוא למעלה מהעולמות, יהי'[ה] אלקיך, אלקים בגימטריא הטבע, בראשית ברא אלקים. כל החבריא קדישא היו בהתעוררות גדולה מתורה ההיא. הרה"צ [הרב הצדיק] ר' משולם זוסיא מאניפאלי אמר, כי הוא אינו יכול להגיע למעלת תשובה כזו, ועל כן יחלק את התשובה לחלקים, כי תשובה ר"ת [ראשי תיבות]: ת, תמים תהיה עם הוי' אלקיך. ש, שויתי הוי' לנגדי תמיד. ו, ואהבת לרעך כמוך. ב, בכל דרכיך דעהו. ה, הצנע לכת עם ה' אלקיך.

כשסיפר לי אאמו"ר [אדוני אבי מורי ורבי] את הנ"ל [הנזכר לעיל], סיים: תיבת תשובה צרופה מחמש אותיות, אשר כל אות הוא דרך ואופן בעבודת התשובה, - וביאר באריכות חמשה האופנים - וכולם באים מכח אל הפועל ע"י [על ידי] עבודת התפלה.
hayomYom.clear:
At the Tzemach Tzedek’s yechidus with the Alter Rebbe, on Monday of parshas Teitzei, 6 Elul 5564 (1804), the Alter Rebbe told him:

On Shabbos parshas Tavo 5528 (1768), my teacher and master [the Maggid of Mezritch] said a teaching beginning “V’shavta ad Havayeh Elokecha” [“You shall return to Havayeh your G‑d”]. He explained that the avoda of teshuvah must reach the point where Havayeh, which is above the worlds, becomes “Elokecha,” your G‑d. Elokim has the same numerical value as hateva, “nature,” as in “In the beginning Elokim created.”

The whole holy group [the Maggid’s disciples] was deeply stirred by that teaching. The tzaddik R. Meshulam Zusya of Anipoli said that he could not reach such a high level of teshuvah, so he would divide teshuvah into parts. For the letters of “teshuvah” are the first letters of:
Tav: “Be wholehearted with Havayeh your G‑d.”
Shin: “I have set Havayeh before me always.”
Vav: “Love your fellow as yourself.”
Beis: “In all your ways, know Him.”
Hei: “Walk humbly with your G‑d.”

When my father [the Rebbe Rashab] told me this, he concluded: The word teshuvah is made of five letters, and each letter is a path and a way in the avoda of teshuvah. (He explained the five ways at length.) And all of them are brought from potential into actual through the avoda of prayer.
translationNotes: Kehot names the letters by their English sounds (U, V). The Hebrew letters are ו (Vav) and ב (Beis).
הצנע לכת: “walk modestly, humbly.” Kehot has “discreetly.”
Kehot opens with “the Rebbe told him,” then shifts to “my father told me” with no clear speaker. The second part is the Rebbe Rayatz quoting the Rebbe Rashab.

calendar.original5703: Begin [Kabbalas Shabbos] with “Mizmor l’David” and not “Lechu neranenah,” and so on every Shabbos that falls on the night after a Yom Tov. Haftorah: “Shuvah” until “yikashlu vam,” then “Mi Kel kamocha” until “mimei kedem.”

hayomYom.english: A résumé of my father's explanation of the first method (of teshuva, see above): T: Tamim..., "Be sincere with G‑d." This represents the avoda of teshuva that comes through sincerity. Sincerity, or "wholeness," takes any number of forms and has many levels. In reference to teshuva the highest form is wholeness of heart - called "earnestness"; as Torah says of Avraham, "you found his heart faithful before You."
hayomYom.hebrew:
צום גדליה נדחה. אבינו מלכנו. סליחות.

קיצור ביאור אאמו"ר [אדוני אבי מורי ורבי] באופן הא': ת, תמים תהיה עם ה"א [הוי' אלקיך], עבודת התשובה הבאה ע"י [על ידי] התמימות, כמה בחינות ומדריגות בענין התמימות, וביחס אל התשובה העולה על כולנה היא תמימות הלב - הנקראת ערנסטקייט - כאמור באברהם ומצאת את לבבו נאמן לפניך.
hayomYom.clear:
A summary of my father’s [the Rebbe Rashab’s] explanation of the first way:

Tav: “Be wholehearted with Havayeh your G‑d.” This is the avoda of teshuvah that comes through temimus [wholeheartedness]. Temimus has many levels and grades. In relation to teshuvah, the highest of all is wholeness of heart, called “earnestness,” as it says of Avraham, “You found his heart faithful before You” (Nechemiah 9:8).
translationNotes: ערנסטקייט: Yiddish “earnestness,” seriousness. Kehot keeps it.
Matches the original otherwise.

calendar.original5703: The Fast of Gedaliah, postponed [to Sunday]. Avinu Malkeinu. Selichos.

hayomYom.english: A resume of the second method: Sh: - Shiviti..., "I have set G‑d (Havayeh) before me always." Havayeh indicates the creation of the universe and creatures. Bringing all of Creation into being and sustaining it is accomplished by bridging an infinite gap - from ayin (non-being, nihilo) to yesh (being). This form of the avoda (service) of teshuva results from one's constant awareness of the way in which the universe and all that is in it, is (constantly) brought into being.
hayomYom.hebrew: קיצור ביאור באופן הב': ש, שויתי הוי' לנגדי תמיד, הוי' מורה על התהוות העולם והתהוות הנבראים, אשר התהוות הבריאה כולה וחיותה הוא בדרך אין ערוך מאין ליש. והיא עבודת התשובה הבאה עי"ז [על ידי זה] אשר תמיד לנגד עיניו ענין ההוי' של העולם ומלואו.
hayomYom.clear:
A summary of the explanation of the second way:

Shin: “I have set Havayeh before me always.” The Name Havayeh points to the bringing into being of the world and of all created things. The creation of everything, and its life, happens across an infinite gap: from nothing to something.

This is the avoda of teshuvah that comes from always having before your eyes how the world and everything in it is being brought into being.
translationNotes: הוי' ... התהוות: wordplay. The Name Havayeh shares its root with hithavus, “coming into being.” Kehot loses this.
אין ערוך: “no comparison,” an infinite gap.

hayomYom.english: A résumé of the third method: U - V'ahavta..., "Love your fellow as yourself." The Alter Rebbe taught that this love is an instrument, a means to "Love the Eternal your G‑d." This is explained in the statement, "Whoever is pleasing to man is pleasing to G‑d." This service of teshuva stems from goodness of heart.
hayomYom.hebrew: קיצור ביאור אופן הג': ו, ואהבת לרעך כמוך, כמו שאמר רבינו הזקן, אשר זהו כלי לואהבת את הוי' אלקיך, וביאור במאמר כל שרוח הבריות נוחה הימנו רוח המקום נוחה הימנו. עבודת התשובה בסיבת לב טוב.
hayomYom.clear:
A summary of the explanation of the third way:

Vav: “Love your fellow as yourself.” As the Alter Rebbe said, this is a vessel for “Love Havayeh your G‑d.” This is the meaning of the saying, “Whoever is pleasing to people is pleasing to G‑d” (Avos 3:10).

This is the avoda of teshuvah that comes from a good heart.
translationNotes: כלי: “a vessel,” the means for loving G‑d.
Matches the original otherwise.

hayomYom.english: A résumé of the fourth method: V - B'chol..., "In all your ways, know Him." A person who sets his heart and mind to observe all that happens to him and around him, will perceive G‑dliness tangibly in evidence; as the Mitteler Rebbe pointed out, men of affairs have an advantage over secluded scholars, in that the former can witness actual manifestations of G‑dliness. This form of the service of teshuva comes from one's perceiving hashgacha p'ratit, (particular Divine Providence).
hayomYom.hebrew: קיצור ביאור אופן הד': ב, בכל דרכיך דעהו, האדם השם לבו ודעתו על כל הנעשה עמו ומסביב לו, רואה הוא אלקות במוחש, וכמו שאמר אדמו"ר [אדוננו מורנו ורבנו] האמצעי ביתרון הבעלי עסקים על היושבי אהל בענין ראית אלקות במוחש. עבודת התשובה הבאה מראיית השגחה פרטית.
hayomYom.clear:
A summary of the explanation of the fourth way:

Beis: “In all your ways, know Him.” A person who sets his heart and mind on everything that happens to him and around him sees G‑dliness tangibly. As the Mitteler Rebbe said about the advantage that businesspeople have over those who sit and study, in seeing G‑dliness tangibly.

This is the avoda of teshuvah that comes from seeing hashgachah pratis [specific Divine Providence].
translationNotes: יושבי אהל: “those who sit in the tent,” full-time learners.
במוחש: “tangibly, palpably.”

hayomYom.english: A résumé of the fifth method: H - Hatznei'a..., "Walk discreetly with your G‑d,". One must take care not to be conspicuous or ostentatious in the slightest. It is said "Man should always be artful in piety." The artfulness lies in seeing that his piety not be noticed at all. We know that a number of the early chassidim concealed their true selves, and when discovered were sincerely distressed. This is the avoda of teshuva that comes from hatznei'a lechet, being discreet.
hayomYom.hebrew: קיצור ביאור אופן הה': ה, הצנע לכת עם הוי' אלקיך, זהירות שלא תהי שום בליטה, וכמאמר לעולם יהא אדם ערום ביראה, וענין הערמומית הוא שלא יהיה ניכר כלל, ידוע דכמה מחסידים הראשונים היו מסתירים עצמם ואם התגלו היו מצטערים. וזהו עבודת התשובה הבאה מהצנע לכת.
hayomYom.clear:
A summary of the explanation of the fifth way:

Hei: “Walk humbly with Havayeh your G‑d.” Take care that nothing about you stands out at all. As the saying goes, “A person should always be shrewd in fear of G‑d” (Berachos 17a). And the shrewdness is that it should not be noticeable at all.

It is known that a number of the early chassidim hid themselves, and if they were found out, they were pained.

This is the avoda of teshuvah that comes from walking humbly.
translationNotes: שום בליטה: “any protrusion,” anything that sticks out.
ערום ביראה: “shrewd in yiras Shamayim.” Kehot’s “artful in piety” is close.

hayomYom.english: Kaparot: B'nei adam until ul'shalom (p. 296) is said three times, rotating (the fowl) three times around the head at each reading, a total of nine rotations. Until the end of Tishrei no tachanun is said. Malkot: The one administering and the one receiving the "flogging" together recite v'hu rachum three times. On Erev Yom Kippur the avoda is remorse for the past; on Yom Kippur - resolve for the future.
hayomYom.hebrew:
כפרות: "בני אדם - ולשלום" שלש פעמים, ובכל פעם מסבב ג"פ [ג' פעמים] ס"ה [סך הכל] מסבב ט"פ [ט' פעמים].

עד סוף תשרי א"א [אין אומרים] תחנון. מלקות: המלקה והנלקה שניהם אומרים והוא רחום שלש פעמים.

בעריוהכ"פ [בערב יום הכפורים] העבודה היא חרטה על העבר, ביוהכ"פ [ביום הכפורים] - קבלה על להבא.
hayomYom.clear:
Kaparos: “Bnei adam ... u’l’shalom” is said three times. Each time, the kaparah is circled three times, nine times in all.

Until the end of Tishrei, Tachanun is not said.

Malkos [the symbolic lashes]: the one giving the lashes and the one receiving them both say “V’hu rachum” three times.

On Erev Yom Kippur, the avoda is regret for the past. On Yom Kippur, resolve for the future.
translationNotes: חרטה / קבלה: regret, and taking on a resolution.
Matches the original. No meaning lost.

hayomYom.english: Yom Kippur eve begin Hashem malach tageil etc. The verse Or zarua is said once, aloud. (p. 296) Al daat hakahal...is said three times, softly. Ki hinei kachomer is not repeated. Bedtime sh'ma as every Shabbat and Festival. Avinu malkeinu z'chor rachamecha etc. is said in every tefilla. On Rosh Hashana and Yom Kippur the Thirteen Attributes of Mercy (p. 183) are recited when the Scrolls are removed from the Ark, even on Shabbat. The daily Tehillim is said after Musaf. Haftora at Mincha: Va'yhi d'var until uv'heima raba, then Mi Keil kamocha etc. L'David ori said at Mincha too. Open the Ark for Ne'ila service at Ashrei, and it remains open until after the entire Ne'ila Service. Kaddish in Ne'ila - l'eila ul'eila. Ein k'Elokeinu, Aleinu, no blessing by the kohanim. Hayom yifneh is said even after dark. She'assa li kol tzorki (p. 8) is not said until tomorrow. On Yom Kippur it works out that we actually fast 26 hours.
hayomYom.hebrew:
ליל יוהכ"פ [יום הכפורים] מתחילים ה' מלך תגל גו'. פסוק אור זרוע - פעם אחת ובקול רם. על דעת הקהל כו' ג"פ [ג' פעמים] ובקול נמוך. אין כופלים החרוז כי הנה כחומר. קשעהמ"ט [קריאת שמע שעל המטה] כמו בשיו"ט [בשבת ויום טוב]. א"מ [אבינו מלכנו] זכור רחמיך כו' - בכל תפלות היום. בר"ה [בראש השנה] ויוהכ"פ [ויום הכפורים] אומרים יגמה"ר [י"ג מדות הרחמים] בהוצאת הס"ת [הספר תורה] גם כשחל בשבת. שיעור תהלים אחר מוסף.

הפטורת מנחת יוהכ"פ [יום הכפורים]: ויהי דבר - ובהמה רבה. מי אל כמוך גו'. גם במנחה אומרים לדוד ה' אורי. פתיחת הארון בנעילה לאשרי, ונשאר פתוח עד אחרי כל תפלת נעילה. בקדיש דנעילה - לעילא ולעילא, אין כאלקינו, עלינו. ואין נ"כ [נושאים כפים].

אומרים היום יפנה, גם אם העריב היום. אין מברכים שעשה לי כל צרכי עד למחר.

יוהכ"פ [יום הכפורים] קומט אויס צו פאסטען זעקס און צוואנציג שעה.
hayomYom.clear:
On Yom Kippur night we begin [Kabbalas Shabbos] with “Hashem malach tagel.” The verse “Or zarua” is said once, aloud. “Al da’as hakahal” is said three times, quietly. The refrain “Ki hinei kachomer” is not repeated. Krias Shema at bedtime is as on Shabbos and Yom Tov. “Avinu Malkeinu, zechor rachamecha” is said in all the prayers of the day. On Rosh Hashanah and Yom Kippur the Thirteen Attributes of Mercy are said when the Torah is taken out, even on Shabbos. The daily portion of Tehillim is said after Musaf.

Haftorah for Mincha of Yom Kippur: “Vayehi dvar” until “u’vehemah rabbah,” then “Mi Kel kamocha.” “L’David, Hashem ori” is said at Mincha too. The Ark is opened for Ne’ilah at Ashrei, and stays open until after the whole Ne’ilah prayer. In the Kaddish of Ne’ilah: “l’eila ul’eila.” Ein Kelokeinu, Aleinu. There is no Birkas Kohanim.

“HaYom yifneh” is said even if night has already fallen. The blessing “She’asah li kol tzorki” is not said until the next day.

Yom Kippur works out to a fast of twenty-six hours.
translationNotes: אין כופלים החרוז: “the refrain is not repeated.”
גם אם העריב היום: “even if night has fallen.” Kehot’s “even after dark” is fine.
קומט אויס: Yiddish, “it comes out to,” as a practical matter.

hayomYom.english: At the conclusion of Yom Kippur 5556 (1795) in Lyozna, the Alter Rebbe delivered a public discourse (his discourses were brief, as usual then) on the verse "Who is like the Eternal our G‑d whenever we call upon Him," on which the Sages comment - "...upon Him" and not upon His attributes: Pardes Rimonim explains that "upon Him" (2) refers to the orot ("radiances" or "illuminations") as they are invested in the "vessels" of the Ten Sefirot of Atzilut. The Rebbe, the Baal Shem Tov, says that "upon Him" refers to the G‑dhood invested in the "vessels" of the Ten Sefirot of Atzilut. The simple meaning is: "upon Him" refers to the Essence of the En Sof of which every ordinary Jew has inherent knowledge through his simple faith. This is the meaning of "close to him" (4) to the person) and "whenever we call to Him (G‑d)" - (These two expressions referring respectively to) the Essence of the En Sof and the essence of the soul. Davening with simple faith joins the essence of the soul with the essence of the Infinite, so that the Essence of the En Sof will be the Healer of the ill, and He Who blesses the years.
hayomYom.hebrew: במוצאי יוהכ"פ [יום הכפורים] תקנ"ו בליאזנא אמר רבינו הזקן תורה ברבים. כנהוג אז דרושים קצרים - ע"פ [על פסוק] מי כהשם אלקינו בכל קראנו אליו, אליו ולא למדותיו, דער פרדס זאגט אליו איז אורות המתלבשים בכלים דע"ס [דעשר ספירות] דאצילות, דער רבי דער בעש"ט [בעל שם טוב] זאגט אליו איז דער אלקות וואס אין כלים דע"ס [דעשר ספירות] דאצילות, דער פירוש הפשוט איז: אליו עצמות א"ס [אין סוף] וואס עס איז בא יעדען פשוט'ן אידען בידיעה עצמית דורך אמונה פשוטה, און דאס איז קרובים אליו און בכל קראנו אליו עצמות א"ס [אין סוף] און עצמות הנשמה, תפלה באמונה פשוטה איז מחבר עצמות הנשמה מיט עצמות א"ס [אין סוף], אז עצמות א"ס [אין סוף] זאל זיין דער רופא חולים און מברך השנים.
hayomYom.clear:
On the night after Yom Kippur 5556 (1795), in Liozna, the Alter Rebbe said a public teaching. (At the time, short discourses were the custom.) It was on the verse “like Hashem our G‑d, whenever we call to Him” (Devarim 4:7), which the Sages explain: “to Him,” and not to His attributes.

The Pardes says: “to Him” means the lights as they are enclothed in the vessels of the Ten Sefiros of Atzilus. The Rebbe, the Baal Shem Tov, says: “to Him” means the G‑dliness that is in the vessels of the Ten Sefiros of Atzilus. The plain meaning is: “to Him” means the Essence of the Ein Sof, which every simple Jew knows from within, through simple faith.

This is “close to Him” and “whenever we call to Him”: the Essence of the Ein Sof and the essence of the soul. Prayer with simple faith joins the essence of the soul with the Essence of the Ein Sof, so that the Essence of the Ein Sof will be the Healer of the sick and the One who blesses the years.
translationNotes: בידיעה עצמית: “knowledge from his very essence,” innate, not learned.
קרובים אליו: from the same verse, “so close to it.” Kehot’s stray markers (2) and (4) are removed.
The Pardes is R. Moshe Cordovero’s Pardes Rimonim.

hayomYom.english: We are assured by covenant that any wide-ranging effort and labor pursued wisely and with friendship is never fruitless.
hayomYom.hebrew: ברית כרותה לתעמולה ועבודה במועצות חכמה ובקירוב הדעת שאינה חוזרת ריקם.
hayomYom.clear: There is a covenant made: outreach and work done with wise counsel and with friendly closeness never return empty.
translationNotes: ברית כרותה: “a covenant is made,” a guaranteed promise.
תעמולה: outreach, campaigning. בקירוב הדעת: with closeness of mind, friendly agreement.

hayomYom.english: The Rebbe Maharash passed away on this day in 5643 (1882). He was interred in Lubavitch. The beginning of Igeret 22 and its close were not published in Igeret Hakodesh. (It was printed in the publication Hatamim No. 2.)
hayomYom.hebrew:
הסתלקות אדמו"ר [אדוננו מורנו ורבנו] מהר"ש . תרמ"ג - ומ"כ [ומנוחתו כבוד] בליובאוויטש.

תחלת אגרת סימן כב וסופה - לא בא בדפוס באגה"ק [באגרת הקודש]. [נדפס בקובץ התמים חוברת שני'].
hayomYom.clear:
Passing of the Rebbe Maharash, 5643 (1882). He is buried in Lubavitch.

The beginning and end of Letter 22 were not printed in Iggeres HaKodesh. (They were printed in the journal HaTamim, issue 2.)
translationNotes: ומ"כ: “and his resting place is honored.”
Matches the original otherwise.

hayomYom.english: Eiruv Tavshilin (p. 249). No more than two aravot are used, but many hadassim may be used. We make a point of binding the lulav in the suka and on erev yomtov. Two rings are placed on the lulav proper, and these should be covered by the hadassim and aravot, even the top ring, at least somewhat. In addition, three rings are used to bind the hadassim and aravot to the lulav. These three rings are to be all within one handbreadth.
hayomYom.hebrew:
עירוב תבשילין.

אין מוסיפין על שתי ערבות, משא"כ [מה שאין כן] בהדסים.

מהדרים לאגוד הלולב בסוכה ובערב יו"ט [יום טוב]. על הלולב שתי כריכות - ומשתדלים ששתיהם תהיינה מכוסות בהדסים וערבות, גם כריכה העליונה במעט על כל פנים - ומלבד זה שלש כריכות שבהם אוגד ההדסים והערבות עם הלולב, שלש אלו במשך טפח אחד.
hayomYom.clear:
No more than two aravos are used, unlike hadassim, where more may be added.

We take care to bind the lulav in the sukkah, and on Erev Yom Tov.

On the lulav itself there are two rings. We try to have both covered by the hadassim and aravos, even the top ring, at least a little. Besides these, there are three rings that bind the hadassim and aravos to the lulav, and these three are within one tefach [handbreadth].
translationNotes: מהדרים: “we are particular,” going beyond the minimum.
Matches the original otherwise.

calendar.original5703: Eruv Tavshilin.

hayomYom.english: When giving the etrog-lulav set to another for him to pronounce the b'racha, say explicitly that this is a gift conditional on its return, particularly on the first day. This is of value for the giver and the recipient. My father instructed that one should start saying shehecheyanu with the lulav in one hand and etrog in the other. The verses Ki amarti, etc. (p. 326) are said only on Hosha'ana Raba. During the day, the b'racha of leisheiv ba'suka (p. 251) is also said after kiddush (p. 250), not after hamotzi. We know the procedure (for the congregant) during the blessing of the kohanim because the Alter Rebbe would take the Tzemach Tzedek, before the latter's marriage, under his tallit during the blessing of the kohanim.
hayomYom.hebrew:
כשנותנים הד' מינים לאחר לברך עליהם אומרים בפירוש שהוא במתנה על מנת להחזיר, ובפרט ביום ראשון. והוא תועלת לנותן ולמקבל. הורה אאמו"ר [אדוני אבי מורי ורבי] שיתחילו ברכת שהחינו כשהלולב בידו אחת והאתרוג בשני'[ה].

הפסוקים כי אמרתי גו' - רק בהו"ר [בהושענא רבה].

גם ביום מברכים לישב בסוכה אחר קדוש ולא אחר המוציא.

ההנהגה בעת ברכת כהנים [כנ"ל [כנזכר לעיל] יום ב' דחה"ש [דחג השבועות]] אנו יודעים עי"ז [על ידי זה] שרבינו הזקן היה לוקח את הצ"צ [הצמח צדק], קודם חתונתו, תחת טליתו לנ"כ [לנשיאת כפים].
hayomYom.clear:
When you give the four kinds to someone else to make the blessing, say clearly that it is a gift on condition that it is returned, especially on the first day. This benefits both the giver and the receiver.

My father [the Rebbe Rashab] instructed that you begin the Shehecheyanu blessing with the lulav in one hand and the esrog in the other.

The verses “Ki amarti” are said only on Hoshanah Rabbah.

In the daytime too, “Leishev basukkah” is said after Kiddush and not after Hamotzi.

We know how to conduct ourselves during Birkas Kohanim (as noted above, on the second day of Shavuos) because the Alter Rebbe used to take the Tzemach Tzedek, before his wedding, under his tallis for Birkas Kohanim.
translationNotes: על מנת להחזיר: “on condition to return,” the halachic gift-and-return.
Kehot drops the cross-reference [כנ"ל יום ב' דחה"ש], “as above, second day of Shavuos.” Restored.

hayomYom.english: The Tzemach Tzedek related: In 5569 (1808) we heard from my grandfather (the Alter Rebbe) for the sixth time the maamar Ush'avtem mayim (the first of that title in Likutei Torah) and the experience was reminiscent of the Talmudic statement (Yerushalmi Suka 5:1) "From there they drew (the holy spirit)." Yona received, at the celebration of the water-drawing, the gift of prophetic revelation; we received revelation without end. The end will be when Mashiach comes, for the end is rooted in the beginning.
hayomYom.hebrew:
בקדוש הלילה: שהחינו ואח"כ [ואחר כך] לישב בסוכה. במנחה א"א [אין אומרים] הודו, אבל אומרים פתח אליהו.

הצ"צ [הצמח צדק] סיפר: תקס"ט האבען מיר געהערט פון זיידען דעם זעקסטען מאל דעם ושאבתם מים - הראשון - פון לקו"ת [לקוטי תורה], און עס איז געווען ע"ד [על דרך] ווי די גמרא זאגט [ירושלמי סוכה פ"ה [פרק ה'] ה"א [הלכה א']] שמשם שואבים. יונה האט מקבל געווען בשמחת בית השואבה גילוי הנבואה, מיר האבען מקבל געווען עד אין סוף, דער סוף איז אז משיח וועט קומען, שנעוץ תחלתן בסופן.
hayomYom.clear: The Tzemach Tzedek related: In 5569 (1808) we heard from my grandfather [the Alter Rebbe], for the sixth time, the maamar “Ush’avtem mayim” (the first one) in Likkutei Torah. It was like what the Gemara says (Yerushalmi Sukkah 5:1): “From there they drew” [ruach hakodesh]. At the Simchas Beis HaShoevah, Yonah received the revelation of prophecy. We received without end (ad ein sof). And the end is that Mashiach will come, for “their beginning is wedged in their end.”
translationNotes: עד אין סוף: “without end,” also a play on the Ein Sof, the Infinite.
שנעוץ תחלתן בסופן: “their beginning is wedged in their end” (Sefer Yetzirah 1:7). Kehot reverses it to “the end is rooted in the beginning.”

calendar.original5703: At night Kiddush: Shehecheyanu, then Leishev basukkah. At Mincha, “Hodu” is not said, but “Pasach Eliyahu” is said.

hayomYom.english: In Kabalat Shabbat we say: gam b'simcha uv'tzahala. (p. 132). Shalom aleichem, Eishet Chayil, Mizmor L'David, Da hee s'udata (pp. 144-6) and V'yitein l'cha (p. 235) are said in an undertone. At Musaf - uminchatam v'nisskeihem (p. 260) is said after each verse recounting that day's offering. On Shabbat do not say Hosha'anot (p. 326). The soul-aspect of yechida emerges through the avoda of being tested. As is written (in the Hosha'anot service, p. 327): "She clings and cleaves to you" - the binding of the soul to G‑d. This leads to... "She bears your yoke," observing Torah and mitzvot with self-sacrifice; and then... "She, the One People (yechida), affirms Your Oneness" - yechida of the soul is revealed. Through this revelation the yechida of the animal soul is transformed into G‑dliness. This finds expression in the intensity with which one fulfills Torah and mitzvot, with an inner enthusiasm, with a sense of great delight and tremendous pleasure in serving G‑d. (To a person on that lofty level) there is total equanimity to all worldy matters; "yes" and "no" have become absolutely equal to him, for he is now divested of the sense of delight in and appetite for material things.
hayomYom.hebrew:
גם בשמחה ובצהלה.

שלום עליכם, אשת חיל, מזמור לדוד, דא היא סעודתא, ויתן לך - אומרים בלחש.

במוסף - ומנחתם ונסכיהם אחרי פסוקי כל יום ויום. בשבת א"א [אין אומרים] הושענות.

על ידי העבודה דנסיונות מתגלה בחינת יחידה שבנפש, כמאמר חבוקה ודבוקה בך - התקשרות הנשמה באלקות, ועי"ז [ועל ידי זה] - טוענת עולך - בקיום התורה ומצות במסירת נפש, הנה - יחידה ליחדך - שמתגלה בחינת יחידה שבנפש, דע"י [דעל ידי] התגלות זו נהפך יחידה שבנפש הבהמית לאלקות, שהו"ע [שהוא ענין] התוקף בקיום התומ"צ [התורה ומצות] בחיות פנימי, ובהרגש תענוג גדול והנאה מרובה בעבודת ה', ובכל עניני העולם הן ולאו שוין אצלו בהשואה אמיתית, כי נלקח ממנו התענוג וטוב טעם שבענינים הגשמיים.
hayomYom.clear:
Through the avoda of tests, the level of yechidah [the soul’s innermost core] is revealed. As it says [in the Hoshanos]: “She is embraced and cleaves to You”: the soul’s bond with G‑dliness. Through this, “she bears Your yoke”: keeping Torah and mitzvos with mesirus nefesh. Then “the unique one, to declare Your Oneness”: the yechidah of the soul is revealed.

Through this revelation, the yechidah of the animal soul is transformed into G‑dliness. This shows in the strength with which you keep Torah and mitzvos: with inner life, with a feeling of great delight and much pleasure in serving G‑d. And toward all the matters of the world, “yes” and “no” are truly equal to him, because the delight and the taste for physical things have been taken away from him.
translationNotes: יחידה ליחדך: a pun. In the Hoshanos it means “the unique nation”; here it is the soul-level yechidah.
חיות פנימי: “inner vitality,” life from within. Kehot’s “inner enthusiasm” is close.
נלקח ממנו: “taken from him,” not something he sheds himself.

calendar.original5703: “Gam b’simchah uv’tzahalah.” “Shalom aleichem,” “Eishes chayil,” “Mizmor l’David,” “Da hi se’udasa,” and “V’yiten lecha” are said quietly. In Musaf, “U’minchasam v’niskeihem” after the verses of each day. On Shabbos, Hoshanos are not said.

hayomYom.english: Say both Om ani choma (p. 327) and Adon hamoshia, but make only one circuit. Say the word hosha'ana before and after those alphabetical phrases which the chazan says aloud; for the other phrases say hosha'ana only once. Our custom is to start saying aloud with the letter samach or ayin. One should be certain to make a complete circuit, ending with tav.
hayomYom.hebrew:
אומרים אום אני חומה וגם אדון המושיע, אבל אין מקיפים אלא פ"א [פעם אחת]. אומרים תיבת "הושענא", הן בראש והן בסוף - באותם האותיות שאומרם הש"ץ [השליח ציבור] בקול רם, בהשאר אומרים רק פעם אחת.

מנהגינו להתחיל בקול רם מאות "ס" או "ע".

מדייקים לעשות היקף שלם ומשלימים באות "ת".
hayomYom.clear:
Both “Om ani chomah” and “Adon hamoshia” are said, but only one circuit is made.

The word “Hoshana” is said both before and after the lines that the chazzan says aloud. For the rest, it is said only once.

Our custom is to begin saying it aloud from the letter Samech or Ayin.

We are careful to make a complete circuit, finishing at the letter Tav.
translationNotes: מדייקים: “we are careful, precise.”
Matches the original. No meaning lost.

hayomYom.english: It is written that all through the year, when saying in sh'mona essrei "and all the varieties of its produce for good" (p. 54), one should have in mind wheat for matza and the etrog (elsewhere, wine for kiddush is also mentioned); then naturally all the produce will be for good.
hayomYom.hebrew: איתא שכל השנה באמרו בש"ע [בשמונה עשרה] ואת כל מיני תבואתה לטובה, צריך לכוון לחטים למצה ואתרוג - במקום אחד נזכר מלבד הנ"ל [הנזכר לעיל] גם יין לקדוש - ואז במילא תהיה כל התבואה לטובה.
hayomYom.clear: It is written that all year, when you say in Shemoneh Esrei “and all the kinds of its produce for good,” you should have in mind wheat for matzah and the esrog. (In one place, wine for Kiddush is also mentioned.) Then all the produce will be for good as a matter of course.
translationNotes: במילא: “automatically, as a matter of course.”
Matches the original otherwise.

hayomYom.english: During the movements of the lulav (p. 240) one should touch the chest with the lulav at the spot one strikes his heart for ashamnu. My father once said at a farbrengen that this (practice) is similar to the idea that only through the earnestness before davening, when one is embittered over his sins, can there afterwards be an emotional excitement in davening.
hayomYom.hebrew:
בעת הנענועים צריך להגיע עד החזה מקום שמכים באמירת אשמנו.

אמר אאמו"ר [אדוני אבי מורי ורבי] באחת ההתוועדות, שיש לומר שזהו כמו הענין שע"י [שעל ידי] הכובד ראש שקודם התפלה, שמתמרמר בנפשו, עי"ז [על ידי זה] דוקא יכול להיות אח"כ [אחר כך] התפעלות המדות בתפלה.
hayomYom.clear:
During the lulav movements, bring the lulav all the way to your chest, to the spot where you strike yourself when saying Ashamnu.

My father once said at a farbrengen that this can be understood like the following idea: specifically through the serious, heavy-hearted mood before davening, when you feel bitter inside about yourself, can you afterwards come to an emotional arousal in davening.
translationNotes: כובד ראש is solemn earnestness, a weighty seriousness of mind.
שמתמרמר בנפשו: he feels bitter within his own soul. Kehot adds “over his sins,” which is implied but not stated.
דוקא: “specifically” through this, not “only.”

hayomYom.english: In the Tikun of Hosha'ana Raba night, the parsha of B'racha is also said only once. (My father instructed certain individuals to say it with Rashi's commentary on Hosha'ana Raba, but this was not a general instruction.) On erev Simchat Torah, B'racha is said twice and its Targum once. Before Hallel remove the (top) two rings from the lulav, leaving the three rings that bind the lulav with the hadassim and aravot. Eiruv Tavshilin (p. 249). On Hosha'ana Raba the piece of bread on which one says hamotzi is dipped in honey, but not on Sh'mini Atzeret or Simchat Torah.
hayomYom.hebrew:
בתקון ליל הו"ר [הושענא רבה] גם פרשה ברכה אומרים רק פ"א [פעם אחת] מקרא - היו יחידים שאאמו"ר [שאדוני אבי מורי ורבי] ציום לאומרה בהו"ר [בהושענא רבה] עם פירש"י [פירוש רש"י] ואינה הוראה לרבים - ובערב שמחת תורה אומרים אותה שנים מקרא ואחד תרגום.

קודם הלל מסירים שתי הכריכות שעל הלולב, ונשארים רק הג' מאגדים ג' המינים יחד. עירוב תבשילין. בהושענא רבה טובלים פרוסת המוציא בדבש, אבל לא בשמע"צ [בשמיני עצרת] ושמח"ת [ושמחת תורה].
hayomYom.clear:
In the Tikkun of Hoshana Rabbah night, the parsha of V'zos HaBracha is also read only once, in the original text. (There were certain individuals whom my father instructed to say it on Hoshana Rabbah with Rashi's commentary, but this is not an instruction for the public.) On the eve of Simchas Torah, it is said twice in the original and once in Targum.

Before Hallel, remove the two bands on the lulav, leaving only the three that bind the three species together.

On Hoshana Rabbah, dip the piece of bread of hamotzi in honey, but not on Shemini Atzeres or Simchas Torah.
translationNotes: מקרא: the verses in the original Hebrew, as opposed to תרגום, the Aramaic translation.
כריכות are bands or wrappings. The Hebrew does not say “top” rings; Kehot adds that.

calendar.original5703: Eruv tavshilin.

hayomYom.english: One makes kiddush and eats and drinks in the suka, both by night and during the (following) day. Hakafot on Sh'mini Atzeret night. Haftora: Vay'hi k'chalot until ul'yisrael amo. We do not say the (specially designated prayer) Yehi ratzon upon leaving the suka. Sh'mini Atzeret and Rosh Hashana are parallel in many of the kavanot and higher yichudim. On Rosh Hashana, though, these are in a mode of elevation and on Sh'mini Atzeret in a mode of elicitation from On High downward. On Rosh Hashana man's avoda is with supplication, submission and intense bitterness; on Sh'mini Atzeret it is with joy.
hayomYom.hebrew:
מקדשים ואוכלים ושותים בסוכה בין בלילה ובין ביום. הקפות בליל שמע"צ [שמיני עצרת]. הפטורה: ויהי ככלות - ולישראל עמו.

אין אומרים היהי רצון ביציאה מן הסוכה.

שמע"צ [שמיני עצרת] ור"ה [וראש השנה] משתווים בכמה עניני כוונות ויחודים עליונים, אלא שבר"ה [שבראש השנה] הם בענין העלי'[ה] ובשמע"צ [ובשמיני עצרת] הם בענין ההמשכה. בר"ה [בראש השנה] העבודה בתחנונים בהכנעה ובמרירות עצומה, ובשמע"צ [ובשמיני עצרת] היא בקו השמחה.
hayomYom.clear:
We make kiddush and eat and drink in the sukkah, both at night and during the day.

We do not say the Yehi ratzon when leaving the sukkah.

Shemini Atzeres and Rosh Hashanah are alike in many of their kavanos [mystical intentions] and supernal unions. But on Rosh Hashanah these are in the mode of ascent from below, and on Shemini Atzeres in the mode of drawing down from above. On Rosh Hashanah the avoda is with pleading, submission and intense bitterness. On Shemini Atzeres it is along the line of joy.
translationNotes: עליה and המשכה: ascent upward versus drawing down. Kehot's “elevation” and “elicitation” are accurate but stiff.
בקו השמחה: “in the line (mode) of joy,” a whole path of avoda, not just a mood.

calendar.original5703: Hakafos on the night of Shemini Atzeres. Haftorah: Vayehi k'chalos, to ul'Yisrael amo.

hayomYom.english: On Simchat Torah 5540 (1779) the Alter Rebbe said: It is a tree of life for those who hold fast to it - this refers to people of intellect who study Torah. ...and those who support it are fortunate - these are the people of avoda (davening) who occupy themselves with Torah. They are fortunate (me'ushar) as the Zohar (III 53b) interprets: Do not read the word as me'ushar but (through a transposition of letters) as meirosho, "from his head." Through their avoda they call forth (the spiritual level of) "His head," the inwardness of the En Sof. This is similar to the unique quality of the foot which provides the support of the head.
hayomYom.hebrew:
אין קוראים בתורה בלילה. נ"כ [נשיאת כפים] בשחרית. אין נוהגים לפרוש טלית על ראשי העולים לחתן תורה או לחתן בראשית. גם העולה לתורה אומר חזק חו"נ [חזק ונתחזק].

בשמחת תורה תק"מ אמר רבינו הזקן: עץ חיים היא למחזיקים בה - אלו בעלי השגה הלומדים תורה. ותומכיה מאושר - אלו בעלי עבודה העוסקים בתורה. מאושר - גליקלאך, כדאיתא בזהר [ח"ג [חלק ג'] נג. ב] אל תקרי מאושר אלא מראשו, דע"י [דעל ידי] עבודתם ממשיכים מראשו היינו מפנימיות הא"ס [האין סוף] ב"ה [ברוך הוא], וכמעלת הרגל המקיים את הראש דוקא.
hayomYom.clear:
We do not read the Torah at night. Birkas Kohanim [the Priestly Blessing] is said at Shacharis. Our custom is not to spread a tallis over the heads of those called up as Chassan Torah or Chassan Bereishis. The one called up to the Torah also says Chazak chazak v'nischazek.

On Simchas Torah 5540 [1779], the Alter Rebbe said:

“It is a tree of life to those who hold fast to it” (Mishlei 3:18): these are the people of understanding who study Torah.

“And those who support it are fortunate”: these are the people of avoda who occupy themselves with Torah.

“Fortunate” (me'ushar) means happy, as the Zohar (III, 53b) says: Do not read me'ushar, but mei'rosho, “from His head.” Through their avoda they draw down from “His head,” that is, from the innermost level of the Ein Sof, blessed be He. This is like the special quality of the foot, which is specifically what holds up the head.
translationNotes: גליקלאך: the Alter Rebbe glosses מאושר with the Yiddish “happy, lucky.”
ממשיכים: they “draw down,” not just “call forth.”
המקיים את הראש דוקא: it is specifically the foot that holds up the head.
hayomYom.dataFlag: English is missing the opening Simchas Torah customs (no Torah reading at night, Birkas Kohanim at Shacharis, no tallis over the Chassanim, the oleh says Chazak). Translated from the Hebrew and included.

hayomYom.english: Bless Rosh Chodesh Marcheshvan. Say the entire Tehillim in the early morning. Day of farbrengen. Haftora: Ko amar - v'yadir. A public farbrengen in general, and on Shabbat or motzo'ei Shabbat in particular, is one of the foundations in the ways of chassidim and Chassidus. It is an opening and entry-way to the fundamental Mitzva of ahavat Yisrael. At the great majority of farbrengens, the principal speakers demand of the participants to improve their conduct and practices, to designate times for the study of Chassidus and keep those times diligently, and that their study be directed to learning and fulfillment. (The general concept and method of reproving another is well explained in the maamar V'im ruach hamosheil (Kuntres 30). Every chassid would do well to learn it thoroughly and take it deeply to heart.) But this reproving at a farbrengen is only for such matters that will not cause any embarrassment whatsoever. This has been the way since the earliest days - one reproved another with love and deep affection.
hayomYom.hebrew:
מברכים ר"ח מ"ח [ראש חדש מרחשון]. אמירת כל התהילים בהשכמה. יום התועדות.

הפטורה: כה אמר - ויאדיר.

ההתוועדות - פארבריינגען - ברבים בכלל, ובשבת או במוצאי שבת בפרט, היא אחת היסודות בדרכי החסידים והחסידות, ופתח ומבוא למצוה היסודית דאהבת ישראל.

רובא דרובא הנה בכל התוועדות הרי ראשי המדברים תובעים מאת המסובים שיטיבו הנהגותיהם ודרכיהם, שיקבעו עתים ללמוד דא"ח [דברי אלקים חיים] ושישמרו הקביעות, ואשר הלמוד יהיה על מנת ללמוד ולקיים. - והנה כללות ענין ואופן התוכחה מבואר היטב בד"ה [בדיבור המתחיל] ואם רוח המושל [קונטרס למ"ד] אשר ראוי לכל אחד ואחד מאנ"ש [מאנשי שלומינו] ללמדו היטב אדעתא דנפשיה - אמנם הוכחה זו בעת ההתוועדות היא רק על דברים וענינים שאין בהם משום הלבנת פנים ולא כלום, כמו שהי'[ה] מאז ומקדם, אשר איש את רעהו הוכיחו באהבה ובחיבה גדולה.
hayomYom.clear:
A public farbrengen [chassidic gathering], in general, and on Shabbos or Motzaei Shabbos in particular, is one of the foundations of the ways of chassidim and Chassidus. It is an opening and entryway to the fundamental mitzvah of ahavas Yisrael [love of a fellow Jew].

At the vast majority of farbrengens, the main speakers demand of those present that they improve their conduct and their ways, that they set times to study Chassidus and keep to them, and that they study in order to learn and to do.

(The general idea and method of rebuke is well explained in the maamar V'im ruach hamoshel [Kuntres 30]. Every one of our chassidim should study it well and take it to heart for himself.)

But this rebuke at a farbrengen is only about things and matters that involve no embarrassment at all. This is how it has been from the earliest days: one rebuked another with love and great affection.
translationNotes: על מנת ללמוד ולקיים: “in order to learn and to fulfill,” study aimed at action.
הלבנת פנים: literally “whitening the face,” public shaming, which the Talmud treats with great severity.
אדעתא דנפשיה: “with his own mind,” applying it to himself.

calendar.original5703: Shabbos Mevarchim Mar-Cheshvan. The entire Tehillim is said early in the morning. It is a day of farbrengen. Haftorah: Ko amar, to v'yadir.

hayomYom.english: Ten melodies, some only singular stanzas, are attributed to the Alter Rebbe as having been composed by him. Those attributed to the Mitteler Rebbe were composed in his time and sung in his presence, but he did not compose them. He had a group of musically-gifted young men known as "the Mitteler Rebbe's kapelle," divided into two groups, vocalists (baalei shir) and musicians who played various instruments (baalei zimra).
hayomYom.hebrew:
עשרה נגונים - מהם תנועות בלבד - מיוחסים לרבנו הזקן שהוא בעצמו חברם.

המיוחסים לרבינו האמצעי, היינו שנתחברו בזמנו והיו מנגנים אותם לפניו, אבל לא שהוא מחברם. והיתה אצלו קבוצת אברכים מנגנים - וידועה בשם "דעם מיטעלען רבי'ס קאפעלע" - ונחלקה לשתי פלוגות: בעלי שיר - בפה, ובעלי זמרה - בכלים שונים.
hayomYom.clear:
Ten melodies, some of them only single movements, are attributed to the Alter Rebbe as having been composed by him personally.

Those attributed to the Mitteler Rebbe were composed in his time and sung in his presence, but he did not compose them. He had a group of young married men who were musicians, known as “the Mitteler Rebbe's kapelle” [band]. It was split into two groups: baalei shir, who sang with their voices, and baalei zimra, who played various instruments.
translationNotes: תנועות בלבד: some are only single “movements” or sections of a melody, not full multi-part nigunim.
אברכים: young married men, not just “young men.”

hayomYom.english: The interpretation of the verse, "Forever, O G‑d, Your word stands firm in the heavens." (Tanya II:I and IV:25) is quoted by the Alter Rebbe in the Baal Shem Tov's name although that interpretation is found in Midrash Tehillim, as quoted in Likutei Torah in the maamar Ki bayom hazeh yechapeir. But the Alter Rebbe had a special reason for this: It was on the second day of Creation when G‑d said: "Let there be a Heaven," and it is this utterance which "stands firm in the Heavens." Associating the quotation with the Baal Shem Tov was to be an eternal memorial that the Baal Shem Tov was born on the second day of the week, on the eighteenth (chai) of Elul.
hayomYom.hebrew: הענין ע"פ [על פסוק] לעולם ה' דברך נצב בשמים מביא רבינו הזקן [שער היחוה"א [היחוד והאמונה] פ"א [פרק א'], אגה"ק [אגרת הקודש] כ"ה] בשם הבעש"ט [הבעל שם טוב] , הגם שיש ענין זה במדרש תהלים, וכמש"נ [וכמו שנתבאר] גם בלקו"ת [בלקוטי תורה] בד"ה [בדיבור המתחיל] כי ביום הזה יכפר, וכוונה מיוחדת בזה, כי ביום שני הי'[ה] המאמר יהי רקיע - שהוא הנצב בשמים - וזה יהי'[ה] לזכרון עולם, כי ביום שני ח"י אלול נולד הבעש"ט [הבעל שם טוב].
hayomYom.clear:
The Alter Rebbe brings the teaching on the verse “Forever, G‑d, Your word stands firm in the heavens” (Tehillim 119:89) in the name of the Baal Shem Tov (Tanya, Shaar HaYichud VehaEmunah, ch. 1, and Iggeres HaKodesh, ch. 25). He does so even though this idea is found in Midrash Tehillim, as is also explained in Likkutei Torah, maamar Ki vayom hazeh yechaper.

There is a special intention in this. On the second day of Creation came the utterance “Let there be a firmament,” which is what “stands firm in the heavens.” This is meant as an everlasting reminder that the Baal Shem Tov was born on the second day of the week, on Chai [18] Elul.
translationNotes: רקיע is the firmament; the utterance of the second day is the very “word” that stands in the heavens.
לזכרון עולם: an everlasting memorial, as Kehot says.

hayomYom.english: Torah and mitzvot encompass man from the instant of emergence from his mother's womb until his final time comes. They place him in a light-filled situation, with healthy intelligence and acquisition of excellent moral virtues and upright conduct - not only in relation to G‑d but also in relation to his fellow-man. For whoever is guided by Torah and the instructions of our sages has a life of good fortune, materially and in spirit.
hayomYom.hebrew: התורה והמצות מקיפות את חיי האדם מיום גיחו מבטן אמו עד עת פקודתו, ומעמידות אותו בקרן אורה בשכל בריא ובקנין מדות נעלות והנהגות ישרות לא רק בין אדם למקום אלא גם בין אדם לחברו, כי המתנהג ע"פ [על פי] התורה והוראות חז"ל [חכמינו זכרונם לברכה] הוא חי חיים מאושרים בגשם וברוח.
hayomYom.clear:
Torah and mitzvos surround a person's whole life, from the day he comes out of his mother's womb until his time comes. They set him in a place full of light: with a healthy mind, and with fine character traits and upright conduct, not only between man and G‑d but also between man and his fellow.

Because whoever lives by the Torah and the instructions of our Sages lives a happy life, physically and spiritually.
translationNotes: מקיפות: they “encircle” a person's whole life.
בקרן אורה: “in a ray (corner) of light,” a bright, well-lit position.

hayomYom.english: "If you go in my statutes... I will give your rains in their season..." Torah-study and mitzvot-observance are the wedding-ring with which G‑d betrothed Israel and obligated Himself to provide them with sustenance and livelihood.
hayomYom.hebrew: אם בחוקתי תלכו גו' ונתתי גשמיכם בעתם.. לימוד התורה וקיום המצות הם טבעת הקדושין שבהם קידש הקב"ה [הקדוש ברוך הוא] את ישראל להתחייב לזון אותם ולפרנסם.
hayomYom.clear: “If you walk in My statutes... I will give your rains in their season” (Vayikra 26:3-4). Studying Torah and keeping the mitzvos are the wedding ring with which G‑d betrothed the Jewish people, binding Himself to feed them and provide their livelihood.
translationNotes: טבעת הקדושין: the betrothal ring. A husband's kiddushin obligates him to support his wife.
להתחייב: G‑d took on an obligation, not merely a promise.

hayomYom.english: We do recite the b'racha upon seeing the rainbow (p. 87); we do not follow those (authorities) who are hesitant in this matter. A resident of Mezibuz had a quarrel with another. Once, while in the Baal Shem Tov's shul, he shouted that he would tear the other fellow to pieces like a fish. The Baal Shem Tov told his pupils to hold one another's hand, and to stand near him with their eyes closed. Then he placed his holy hands on the shoulders of the two disciples next to him. Suddenly the disciples began shouting in great terror: They had seen that fellow actually dismembering his disputant. This incident shows clearly that every potential has an effect - either in physical form or on a spiritual plane that can be perceived only with higher and more refined senses.
hayomYom.hebrew:
מברכים ברכת הקשת, ולא כיש מפקפקים בזה.

איינער פון די מעזיבוזשער בעלי בתים האט געהאט א מחלוקת מיט נאך א בעל הבית, און זייענדיג אמאל בא דעם בעש"ט [בעל שם טוב] אין שוהל האט ער געשריען, אז ער וואלט זיין בר פלוגתא קורע כדג זיין.

דער בעש"ט [בעל שם טוב] האט געהייסען די תלמידים געבען איינע די אנדערע די הענט, און זיך שטעלען לעבען אים מיט צוגעמאכטע אויגען. דער בעש"ט [בעל שם טוב] האט ארויפגעלייגט זיינע הייליגע הענט אויף די אקסלען פון די צוויי תלמידים, וועלכע זיינען געשטאנען לעבען אים, פלוצלונג האבען די תלמידים אנגעהויבען שרייען פון גרויס שרעק: זיי האבען געזעהן ווי דער בעל הבית איז קורע כדג זיין בר פלוגתא.

דאס באווייזט קלאהר, אז פון יעדער כח איז פאראן א פועל דבר: אדער אין א לבוש חומרי, אדער א רוחני וואס מי קאן אים אנעמען נאר מיט העכערע און איידעלערע געפילען.
hayomYom.clear:
We do say the blessing on seeing a rainbow, and do not follow those who have doubts about it.

One of the householders of Mezhibuzh had a dispute with another householder. Once, while in the Baal Shem Tov's shul, he shouted that he would tear his opponent apart like a fish.

The Baal Shem Tov told his students to give each other their hands and to stand next to him with their eyes closed. He placed his holy hands on the shoulders of the two students standing beside him. Suddenly the students began to scream in great fright: they had seen that man tearing his opponent apart like a fish.

This clearly shows that every power produces an actual effect: either in a physical garment, or in a spiritual one that can be perceived only with higher and finer senses.
translationNotes: קורע כדג: “tear like a fish” (Pesachim 49b). Kehot drops “like a fish” in the vision.
פועל דבר: a real, concrete effect. לבוש: a “garment,” physical or spiritual.

hayomYom.english: In Hallel - repeat Hodu LaHashem (p. 243) after each of the next three verses, Yomar na, etc., even if davening alone. The verses V'Avraham zakein, etc. and Zevadya yish'mreini etc. are said three times.
hayomYom.hebrew: הלל: כופלין הודו לה' אחר כל אחד מהג' פסוקים יאמר נא, וגם כשמתפללים ביחיד. - ואברהם זקן גו' זבדי' ישמרני כו' - ג"פ [ג' פעמים].
hayomYom.clear:
In Hallel: repeat Hodu laShem after each of the three verses Yomar na, even when davening alone.

V'Avraham zaken and Zevadyah yishmereini are said three times each.
translationNotes: Matches the original. No meaning lost.

hayomYom.english: At Mincha, and on Monday and Thursday of the approaching week (Lech L'cha), the third aliya ("Yisrael") begins with Vayeira Hashem el Avram etc. The Rebbe my father told someone at yechidus: Ever since G‑d told our father Avraham, "Go from your land etc." and it is then written "Avram kept travelling southward," we have the beginning of the mystery of birurim. By decree of Divine Providence man goes about his travels to the place where the "sparks" that he must purify await their redemption. Tzadikim, who have vision, see where their birurim await them and go there deliberately. As for ordinary folk, The Cause of all causes and the Prime Mover brings about various reasons and circumstances that bring these people to that place where lies their obligation to perform the avoda of birurim.
hayomYom.hebrew:
במנחה - וכן בשני ובחמישי דשבוע הבע"ל [הבא עלינו לטובה] - קורין לישראל מפסוק וירא ה' אל אברם גו'.

כ"ק [כבוד קדושת] אאמו"ר [אדני אבי מורי ורבי] אמר לאחד על יחידות: מאז שאמר הקב"ה [הקדוש ברוך הוא] לאברהם אבינו ע"ה [עליו השלום] לך לך מארצך גו' וכתיב ויסע אברם הלוך ונסוע הנגבה, הותחל סוד הבירורים. וע"פ [ועל פי] גזירת ההשגחה העליונה האדם הולך למסעיו במקום אשר הניצוצות הצריכים להתברר על ידו מחכים לגאולתם.

הצדיקים שהם בעלי ראי'[ה] רואים הם באיזה מקום הבירורים שלהם מחכים להם והולכים שמה בעצמם, ועמא דבר, הנה עילת כל העילות וסיבת כל הסיבות מסבב כמה עילות וסיבות שיבואו למקום ההוא אשר שם הוטלה עליהם העבודה בעבודת הבירורים.
hayomYom.clear:
At Mincha, and also on Monday and Thursday of the coming week, the Yisrael aliya [the third aliya] is read from the verse Vayeira Hashem el Avram.

My father told someone at yechidus [a private audience]: Ever since G‑d told our father Avraham, “Go from your land,” and it is written, “Avram traveled, going steadily southward,” the secret of the birurim [refining and elevating the sparks of holiness in the world] began. By decree of Divine Providence, a person travels to the places where the sparks that must be refined through him are waiting for their redemption.

Tzaddikim, who are people of vision, see where their birurim are waiting for them, and go there on their own. As for ordinary people, the Cause of all causes and Reason of all reasons arranges many causes and reasons to bring them to that place, where the avoda of birurim has been placed upon them.
translationNotes: ניצוצות ... מחכים לגאולתם: the sparks are waiting for their redemption.
הוטלה עליהם: the task was “placed upon them,” an assigned duty.
עמא דבר: ordinary folk, the general public.

hayomYom.english: From a sicha of my father, after the conclusion of Shabbat Lech L'cha 5651 (1890): In the early years of his leadership the Alter Rebbe declared publicly, "One must live with the time." From his brother, R. Yehuda Leib, the elder chassidim discovered that the Rebbe meant one must live with the sedra of the week and the particular parsha of the day. One should not only learn the weekly parsha every day, but live with it.
hayomYom.hebrew: משיחת אאמו"ר [אדני אבי מורי ורבי] מוצש"ק [מוצאי שבת קודש] לך לך תרנ"א: אין די ערשטע יאהרען פון זיינע נשיאות האט דער אלטער רבי געזאגט ברבים "מען בעדארף לעבן מיט דער צייט". דורך זיין ברודער מהרי"ל [מורינו הרב ר' יהודה ליב] האבען זקני החסידים אויסגעפונען, אז דער רבי מיינט אז מ'דארף לעבען מיט דער פרשת השבוע און פרשת היום פון דער סדרה פון דער וואך. ניט נאר לערנען די פרשת השבוע יעדען טאג, נאר לעבען מיט איר.
hayomYom.clear:
From a sicha [talk] of my father, Motzaei Shabbos Lech Lecha 5651 [1890]:

In the first years of his leadership, the Alter Rebbe said publicly: “You have to live with the times.” Through his brother, R. Yehuda Leib, the elder chassidim found out what the Rebbe meant: you have to live with the weekly Torah portion and with the day's section of that week's portion.

Not only to study the weekly portion every day, but to live with it.
translationNotes: לעבן מיט דער צייט: “live with the time.” It sounds like modernizing; it really means living with the parsha.
פרשת היום: the day's section (aliya) of the weekly portion.

hayomYom.english: (Continuing the above sicha:) Bereishit is a cheerful sedra, even though its ending is not all that pleasant. Noach has the Flood, but the week ends on a happy note with the birth of our father Avraham. The really joyous week is that of parshat Lech L'cha. We live every day of the week with Avraham, the first to dedicate his very life to spreading G‑dliness in the world. And Avraham bequeathed his self-sacrifice as an inheritance to all Jews.
hayomYom.hebrew: [המשך שיחה הנ"ל [הנזכר לעיל]]: בראשית איז א פרייליכע סדרה, אפילו דער סוף איז ניט גאר אזוי געשמאק. נח איז דער מבול, אבער א פרייליכער סוף וואך - געבארן געווארן אברהם אבינו. די אמת פרייליכע וואך איז פרשת לך לך, אלע טעג פון דער וואך לעבט מען מיט אברהם אבינו, דער ערשטער וועלכער האט זיך מוסר נפש געווען אויף מפרסם זיין געטליכקייט אויף דער וועלט, און זיין מסירת נפש האט אברהם אבינו איבערגעגעבען בירושה צו אלע אידען.
hayomYom.clear:
(Continuing the above talk:) Bereishis is a joyful portion, even though its ending is not so pleasant. Noach has the Flood, but the week has a happy ending: our father Avraham is born.

The truly joyful week is Lech Lecha. Every day of that week we live with our father Avraham, the first one who gave himself with mesirus nefesh [self-sacrifice] to make G‑dliness known in the world. And Avraham passed on his mesirus nefesh as an inheritance to all Jews.
translationNotes: געשמאק: “tasty, enjoyable.” The end of Bereishis is not so delightful.
מוסר נפש ... אויף מפרסם זיין: he gave his very soul to publicize G‑dliness.

hayomYom.english: Torah-study every day is crucial to life itself. This applies not only to the soul of the one studying but also to the souls of his family. For then (through Torah-study), the atmosphere of the home becomes an atmosphere of Torah and piety.
hayomYom.hebrew: למוד התורה בכל יום ויום נוגע בנפשות ממש לא לבד בנפש הלומד, כי אם גם בנפשות בני ביתו, שאז אויר הבית הוא אויר תורה ויראת שמים.
hayomYom.clear: Studying Torah each and every day is truly a matter of life itself. Not only for the soul of the one who studies, but also for the souls of his household. Because then the air of the home is an air of Torah and fear of Heaven.
translationNotes: נוגע בנפשות ממש: literally “touches souls,” a matter of life and death.
אויר הבית: the very air the household breathes. יראת שמים is “fear of Heaven,” stronger than “piety.”

hayomYom.english: The Jewish people are compared to the stars twinkling in the high heavens. By their light, even he who walks in the darkness of night shall not blunder. Every Jew, man or woman, possesses enough moral and spiritual strength to influence friends and acquaintances, and bring them into the light.
hayomYom.hebrew:
ישראל נמשלו לכוכבים המתנוצצים בשמי רקיע, אשר לאורם לא יתעה גם ההולך במחשכי הלילה.

כל אחד מישראל, בין איש ובין אשה, יש בו די כח מוסרי ורוחני, להשפיע להעמיד גם את מכיריו ומיודעיו בקרן אורה.
hayomYom.clear:
The Jewish people are compared to stars sparkling in the sky. By their light, even someone walking in the darkness of night will not lose his way.

Every Jew, man or woman, has enough moral and spiritual strength to influence even his friends and acquaintances, and set them in the light.
translationNotes: להעמיד ... בקרן אורה: to “stand them up” in a place of light, to set them firmly there.
לא יתעה: will not stray or get lost.

hayomYom.english: When the Alter Rebbe wished to bless R. Yekusiel Liepler with wealth, the latter said he did not want it; he did not want wealth to distract him from studying Chassidus and from his involvement with avoda. When the Rebbe wished to bless him with longevity, his answer was: But not "peasant years" - men that have eyes but do not see, who have ears but do not hear, who do not perceive G‑dliness nor do they hear G‑dliness.
hayomYom.hebrew: כשרצה רבינו הזקן לברך את ר' יקותיאל ליעפלער בעשירות, אמר שאינו חפץ בזה, שלא תטרידו העשירות מלימוד החסידות והתעסקות בעבודה. וכשרצה לברכו באריכות ימים אמר: אבער ניט מיט פויערשע יאהרן, וואס עינים להם ולא יראו אזנים להם ולא ישמעו, מען זעהט ניט קיין ג-טליכקייט און מען הערט ניט קיין ג-טליכקייט.
hayomYom.clear:
When the Alter Rebbe wanted to bless R. Yekusiel Liepler with wealth, he said he did not want it. He did not want wealth to distract him from studying Chassidus and from working on his avoda.

When the Rebbe wanted to bless him with long life, he said: “But not with peasant years: ‘They have eyes but do not see, they have ears but do not hear’ (Tehillim 115:5-6). You do not see any G‑dliness and you do not hear any G‑dliness.”
translationNotes: פויערשע יאהרן: “peasant years,” years lived with no spiritual awareness.
His answer is in Yiddish, a direct quote.

hayomYom.english: Since Torah was given, the correct sequence is: First, removal of the orla of the body, then of the tongue, then of the heart - deed, speech, then thought. Our father Avraham, who lived prior to the giving of the Torah, however, first recognized his Creator - thought; then he disseminated G‑dliness - speech; and finally circumcision - deed.
hayomYom.hebrew: הסדר לאחר מתן תורה הוא: הסרת ערלת הגוף, הלשון, הלב - מעשה דבור מחשבה, אברהם אבינו שהיה קודם מ"ת [מתן תורה] הרי בתחילה הכיר את בוראו - מחשבה, אח"כ [אחר כך] פרסם אלקותו, - דבור, ואח"כ [ואחר כך] מילה - מעשה.
hayomYom.clear:
The order after the giving of the Torah is: removing the foreskin of the body, of the tongue, of the heart. That is: deed, speech, thought.

Our father Avraham, who lived before the giving of the Torah, first recognized his Creator: thought. Then he made G‑dliness known: speech. And afterwards came circumcision: deed.
translationNotes: ערלה: a “covering” or blockage. There is an orla of body, tongue and heart.
The order is reversed: after Sinai we go from deed inward; Avraham went from thought outward.

hayomYom.english: Mitzva is an idiom of tzavta - "joining," "attachment." Whoever performs a mitzva becomes joined to the Essence of G‑d - may He be blessed - Who issues that particular command. This is the meaning of "The reward of a mitzva is the mitzva (itself)": His becoming attached to the Essence of the En Sof Who ordained the command, is itself his reward. The above can be understood through an analogy from the physical world: An extremely simple person has an inner sense of bitul (nullity) before the wisdom and greatness of a scholar - a bitul in which he senses himself to be an utter nonentity. The sage in turn, does not sense or perceive the simpleton as belonging at all to the category of human beings! Not that the scholar dismisses or rejects him, G‑d forbid, for that would be an evil trait; he simply sees no connection or relationship with him whatsoever. Now, when the sage instructs the simple man to do something for him, that command brings the simpleton "into being." In his own self-perception he is no longer a nonentity but a "somebody"; he has assumed a status unto himself in that he is able to carry out an order of the sage, and it is him that the sage addressed and instructed. In the eyes of the sage too, the simpleton now "exists"; he is a "somebody" to whom he (the sage) can speak and instruct. What is more, the command actually unites the lofty, exalted sage with the gross simpleton. The analogue is obvious. It is understood that in the above analogy there is no difference at all what the command is about, whether a great, lofty matter or a simple trivial one.
hayomYom.hebrew:
מצוה לשון צוותא וחבור, והעושה מצוה מתחבר עם העצמות ב"ה [ברוך הוא], שהוא המצוה את הציווי ההוא. וזהו שכר מצוה מצוה, דזה מה שנתחבר עם עצמות אוא"ס [אור אין סוף] מצוה הציווי, זהו שכרו. ויובן במשל גשמי: איש פשוט ביותר יש לו בטול פנימי אל החכמה ומעלת חכם, בבטול דהעדר תפיסת מקום לגמרי. וכן גם בהרגש החכם הרי איש הפשוט אינו נכנס אצלו בגדר אנושי כלל - ואין זה דמבטלו ודוחה אותו, ח"ו [חס ושלום], דזהו מדה רעה - ונחשב בעיניו שאין לו קשר של יחס עמו כלל. והי'[ה] כאשר החכם יצווה לאיש הפשוט לעשות איזה דבר בשבילו, הנה בציווי זה נולד מצאותו של האיש הפשוט, הן לעצמו שמרגיש מציאותו אשר הוא יכול לקיים מצות החכם ולו ציווה החכם לעשות דבר, והן בעיני החכם נחשב למציאות אשר אליו ידבר ויצווה, ולבד זאת הרי ציווי זה מאחד החכם הרם ונעלה עם האיש הפשוט ביותר. והנמשל מובן.

ומובן ג"כ [גם כן] אשר ביחס להנ"ל [להנזכר לעיל] אין הבדל כלל במה יהיה הציווי, אם דבר גדול ונעלה או קטן ופשוט..
hayomYom.clear:
The word mitzvah is related to tzavta, joining and connection. When you do a mitzvah, you become joined with the Essence of G‑d, blessed be He, the One who gives that command. This is the meaning of “The reward of a mitzvah is the mitzvah” (Avos 4:2): the fact that you became joined with the Essence of the Ein Sof who commands the mitzvah, that itself is your reward.

This can be understood through a physical analogy. A very simple person has an inner bittul [self-nullification] toward wisdom and toward the greatness of a sage. It is a bittul in which he takes up no space at all.

Likewise, in the sage's own perception, the simple person does not even enter the category of human. (This is not that he looks down on him and pushes him away, G‑d forbid, which would be a bad trait.) He simply considers that he has no connection or relationship with him at all.

Now, when the sage commands the simple person to do something for him, that command gives birth to the simple person's existence. It does so for the simple person himself: he feels he exists, because he can fulfill the sage's command, and it was he whom the sage commanded to do something. And it does so in the sage's eyes: now he counts as someone who exists, someone the sage speaks to and commands. Beyond this, the command unites the lofty, exalted sage with the very simplest person.

The lesson is clear.

It is also clear that, in this respect, it makes no difference at all what the command is about, whether something great and lofty or something small and simple.
translationNotes: העצמות: G‑d's very Essence, beyond any level or revelation.
נולד מציאותו: the command “gives birth to his existence.” Kehot's “brings into being” is right; the image is a birth.
העדר תפיסת מקום לגמרי: he takes up no place at all in his own eyes.

hayomYom.english: When my father was four or five years old he went to his grandfather, the Tzemach Tzedek, on Shabbat Vayeira, and began to cry as he asked, "Why did G‑d show Himself to our father Avraham - but He does not show Himself to us?" The Tzemach Tzedek answered him: "When a tzadik decides at the age of ninety-nine years that he should be circumcised, he deserves that G‑d appear to him."
hayomYom.hebrew: בהיות אאמו"ר [אדוני אבי מורי ורבי] בן ד' או ה' שנים נכנס אל זקנו הצ"צ [הצמח צדק] בש"ק [בשבת קודש] פ' וירא והתחיל לבכות באמרו: מפני מה נראה ה' אל אברהם אבינו ולנו אינו נראה. ויענהו הצ"צ [הצמח צדק] אז א איד א צדיק, צו ניין און ניינציק יאר איז מחליט אז ער דארף זיך מל זיין, איז ער ווערט אז דער אויבערשטער זאל זיך באווייזען צו אים.
hayomYom.clear:
When my father was four or five years old, he went in to his grandfather, the Tzemach Tzedek, on Shabbos Parshas Vayeira, and began to cry. He asked: “Why did G‑d appear to our father Avraham, and He does not appear to us?”

The Tzemach Tzedek answered him: “When a Jew, a tzaddik, at ninety-nine years old, decides that he needs to circumcise himself, he deserves to have G‑d reveal Himself to him.”
translationNotes: א איד א צדיק: “a Jew, a tzaddik.” Kehot drops “a Jew.”
איז מחליט אז ער דארף: he resolves on his own that he must do it.

hayomYom.english: The Alter Rebbe used to refer to Atzilut as "Above." They say that because of intense emotion, when writing the word he could get no further than "Atzi -."
hayomYom.hebrew: דער רבי [רבנו הזקן] פלעגט זאגען אויף אצילות "אויבען". מען דערציילט אז אין כתב פלעגט ער פון התרגשות, מער ווי "אצי" ניט קענען אנשרייבען.
hayomYom.clear: The Rebbe [the Alter Rebbe] used to call Atzilus [the highest of the spiritual worlds] “Above.” It is told that when writing, out of intense emotion, he could not write more than “Atzi...”
translationNotes: פון התרגשות: from deep inner excitement and awe.
אויבען: simply “up there,” a plain Yiddish word he used for so lofty a level.

hayomYom.english: (At this point there appears in the Hebrew text emendations of Torah Or on this week's sedra, meaningful only in Hebrew. Translator). The maamar Patach Eliyahu has glosses by my father that he began writing in the winter of 5652 (1891-2).
hayomYom.hebrew:
בתו"א [בתורה אור] ד"ה [דבור המתחיל] פתח אליהו [פרשת וירא] בסעיף המתחיל והנה הצמצום: "שבחינת עינים היא מקור בחינת כלים", צ"ל [צריך להיות] "שהם בחינת עינים ומקור בחינת כלים". שם ד"ה [דבור המתחיל] ארדה נא בסעיף המתחיל והנה בזהר: "דפי'[רוש] משוטטים". צ"ל [צריך להיות] "דפי'[רוש] משוטטות".

לד"ה [לדבור המתחיל] פתח אליהו ישנם הגהות מאאמו"ר [מאדני אבי מורי ורבי] שהתחיל לכתבם בחורף רנ"ב.
hayomYom.clear:
In Torah Or, maamar Pasach Eliyahu (Parshas Vayeira), in the section beginning V'hinei hatzimtzum: “that the level of eyes is the source of the level of vessels” should read “which are the level of eyes and the source of the level of vessels.”

There, maamar Eirda na, in the section beginning V'hinei baZohar: “meaning, meshotetim” should read “meaning, meshotetos” [the feminine form].

The maamar Pasach Eliyahu has glosses by my father, which he began writing in the winter of 5652 [1891-92].
translationNotes: Kehot skips the corrections as relevant only in Hebrew. Translated here so they can still be read.
משוטטים / משוטטות: masculine versus feminine plural of “roaming,” matching עיני (eyes), which is feminine.

hayomYom.english: One of the Alter Rebbe's early teachings, then called verter (lit. "words," short sayings): Sh'ma Yisrael - a Jew senses that Havayeh Elokeinu - our strength and life is beyond nature, and Havayeh Echad - Havayeh is One.
hayomYom.hebrew: אחת מתורות הראשונות של רבינו הזקן - ונקראו אז בשם "ווערטער": שמע ישראל - א איד דערהערט - הוי'[ה] אלקינו - אז כוחנו וחיותינו איז דאס למעלה מן הטבע, און - הוי'[ה] אחד.
hayomYom.clear:
One of the Alter Rebbe's earliest teachings, which were then called “verter” [sayings]:

Shema Yisrael: a Jew senses that
Havayeh Elokeinu: our strength and our life is above nature,
and Havayeh Echad.
translationNotes: דערהערט: “perceives, catches on.” Shema read as an inner sensing, not just hearing.
כוחנו וחיותנו: our strength and life-force come from Havayeh, which is above nature, though they are called Elokeinu.

hayomYom.english: The Baal Shem Tov used to instruct his disciples in a regular Gemara study-session. His style of study was with great acuity and brilliance, and included a study of Rambam, Alfasi, Rosh and other commentaries of the Rishonim (early commentators) germane to the Gemara-text under examination. The Baal Shem Tov would translate the words (of the text) into Yiddish. When studying in Eirchin 15b the passage "The third tongue kills three persons," the Baal Shem Tov translated and explained: Lashon hara (the evil tongue; slander) kills all three, the inventor of the slander, the one who relates it and the listener. This is all in spiritual terms, which is more severe than physical murder.
hayomYom.hebrew: דער בעש"ט [בעל שם טוב] פלעגט לערנען מיט זיינע תלמידים א שיעור גמרא. דער אופן פון דעם לערנען איז געווען מיט גרויס חריפות און גאונות, און מ'האט געלערענט דעם רמב"ם אלפס רא"ש און אנדערע מפרשים פון די ראשונים וועלכע זיינען שייך געווען צו דער גמרא וואס מ'האט געלערענט. דער בעש"ט [בעל שם טוב] פלעגט אפטייטשען די ווערטער אין אידיש. אז מ'האט געלערענט ערכין און געקומען צום מארז"ל [מאמר רבותינו זכרונם לברכה] [טו ב] לשון תליתאי קטיל תליתאי, האט דער בעש"ט [בעל שם טוב] דאס אויסגעטייטשט: לשון הרע הארג'ט אלע דריי: דעם אויסטראכטער דעם דערציילער און דעם צוהערער, נאר דאס איז אין לבושים רוחנים, וואס דאס איז שווערער, ווי רציחה אין גשמיות.
hayomYom.clear:
The Baal Shem Tov used to give his students a regular class in Gemara. The study was with great sharpness and brilliance. They studied the Rambam, the Rif, the Rosh and other commentators from the Rishonim [early authorities] that were relevant to the Gemara they were learning. The Baal Shem Tov used to translate the words into Yiddish.

When they studied Arachin and came to the Sages' saying (15b), “The third tongue kills three,” the Baal Shem Tov explained it this way: Lashon hara [evil speech] kills all three: the one who makes it up, the one who tells it, and the one who listens. Only, this is in spiritual garments, which is more severe than murder in the physical.
translationNotes: אויסטראכטער: the one who “thinks it up,” the inventor of the slander.
לבושים רוחנים: “spiritual garments,” the killing takes a spiritual form.

hayomYom.english: "From G‑d are man's steps established." Every one of Israel has a spiritual mission in life - which is to occupy himself with the work of construction, to make a "dwelling-place" for G‑d. Every one, regardless of his station or location, must, through an exhaustive search, seek out a spiritual livelihood with all the intensity of his strength, just as he seeks a material livelihood. This is so because, (as the above verse concludes) "he desires His (G‑d's) way." As it is written of Avraham: "For I know and love him because etc. and they will keep the way of Havayeh." There are two "ways": The way of nature and the way that transcends nature. G‑d created the universe in such a way that, in man's eyes, it appears to follow a set pattern of nature; this is the "way" of Elokim. Torah and Mitzvot are the "way" of Havayeh, drawing that which transcends nature into nature. By virtue of this (conduct of Israel) G‑d endows Israel from that which is beyond nature into the natural.
hayomYom.hebrew: מה' מצעדי גבר כוננו, לכל אחד מישראל יש לו תעודה רוחנית בחיים, והוא להתעסק בעבודת הבנין לעשות דירה לו יתברך. וכל אחד באשר הוא ובכל מקום שהוא צריך להתענין בכל מאמצי כוחו לחפש בחפש מחופש למצוא איזה פרנסה רוחנית כמו שהוא מחפש אחר פרנסה גשמיית. והוא לפי שדרכו - של הקב"ה [הקדוש ברוך הוא] - יחפץ, כדכתיב באברהם כי ידעתיו גו' ושמרו דרך ה', כי יש שני דרכים: דרך הטבע ושלמעלה מן הטבע, העולם בראו הקב"ה [הקדוש ברוך הוא] להיות נראה כמו שהוא בדרך הטבע - בעיני בשר - והוא דרך אלקים. תורה ומצות הם דרך הוי'[ה] והוא המשכה שלמעלה מן הטבע בטבע, אשר בגלל זאת הנה הקב"ה [הקדוש ברוך הוא] משפיע לישראל למעלה מן הטבע בטבע.
hayomYom.clear:
“A man's steps are set by G‑d” (Tehillim 37:23). Every Jew has a spiritual mission in life: to be busy with the work of building, of making a dwelling place for G‑d.

Every person, whoever he is and wherever he is, must exert all his strength and search thoroughly to find some spiritual livelihood, just as he searches for a material livelihood. This is because, as the verse ends, “He desires His way,” the way of G‑d. As it is written about Avraham, “For I know him... and they will keep the way of Havayeh” (Bereishis 18:19).

There are two ways: the way of nature, and the way above nature. G‑d created the world so that, to physical eyes, it appears to run by nature. That is the way of Elokim. Torah and mitzvos are the way of Havayeh: drawing what is above nature into nature. Because of this, G‑d gives to the Jewish people from above nature, within nature.
translationNotes: לחפש בחפש מחופש: “search with a thorough search,” a phrase from Tehillim 64:7.
פרנסה רוחנית: a spiritual “livelihood,” a deliberate parallel to earning a living.
בעיני בשר: “to eyes of flesh.” Kehot's “in man's eyes” is close.

hayomYom.english: The soul above awaits the time it will be privileged to descend into a body. For the soul senses how much it can accomplish here below; it can attain the level of "delighting with G‑d." So what is everyone waiting for?
hayomYom.hebrew: די נשמה ווארט אויבען אויף דעם זמן, ווען זי וועט זוכה זיין אראפגעהן אין א גוף, ווייל די נשמה פילט, וואס זי קען אויפטאן זייענדיק דא למטה. זי קען קומען צו דעם להתענג על הוי'[ה]. איז אויף ווען לייגט מען עס אפ?
hayomYom.clear:
The soul up above waits for the time when it will merit to come down into a body. Because the soul feels how much it can accomplish while it is here below. It can reach the level of “delighting in G‑d” (Yeshaya 58:14).

So for when are you putting it off?
translationNotes: איז אויף ווען לייגט מען עס אפ: “for when do we postpone it?” A challenge about procrastination. Kehot's “what is everyone waiting for” softens it.

hayomYom.english: Thought is a garment and servant of the intellect and emotions. Even when it is not serving the intellect or emotions, it continues to function, thinking and meditating. However, this activity is then not only devoid of content, but also open to depravement... It is explained that alien or evil thoughts are caused by "emptiness of the head." For when the mind is occupied, the thought has something to serve, and there is no room for stupid and vain thoughts devoid of substance.
hayomYom.hebrew: המחשבה היא לבוש ומשרת השכל והמדות. בשעה אשר אין לה שירות בשכל או במדות, גם אז פועלת פעולתה לחשוב ולהרהר, אבל פעולתה לא לבד שאינה תוכנית, אלא היא גם פרועה לשמצה... ומבואר כי סיבת המחשבות זרות או רעות הוא די פוסטקייט פון קאפ, דכאשר השכל עסוק אז יש להמחשבה מה לשרת ואין מקום למחשבות של שטות והבל שאין בהם ממש.
hayomYom.clear:
Thought is a garment and servant of the intellect and the emotions. When it has nothing to serve in the intellect or the emotions, it still does its job, thinking and musing. But then its work not only has no content, it also runs wild, to its shame...

It is explained that the cause of foreign or bad thoughts is an empty head. When the mind is busy, thought has something to serve, and there is no room for foolish and empty thoughts that have no substance.
translationNotes: פרועה לשמצה: “let loose, to disgrace” (from Shemos 32:25). Kehot's “open to depravement” is vague.
די פוסטקייט פון קאפ: “the emptiness of the head,” a blunt Yiddish phrase.

hayomYom.english: Time must be guarded. It is urgent to "accept the yoke of Torah." Every bit of time, every day that passes, is not just a day but a life's concern. Days go by; as the Talmud says (Yerushalmi Berachot 1:1), "A day enters and a day departs, a week enters etc.,... a month etc.,... a year etc.,..." My father quoted the Alter Rebbe: A summer day and a winter night are a year.
hayomYom.hebrew: מ'דארף היטען דעם זמן, מ'דארף מקבל זיין עולה של תורה. יעדער זמן, יעדער טאג וואס גייט אוועק, איז דאס ניט נאר א טאג נאר א ענין אין לעבען, די טעג גייען כמאמר [ירושלמי ברכות פ"א [פרק א'] ה"א [הלכה א']] יום נכנס ויום יוצא שבת נכנס כו' חדש כו' שנה כו'. דער טאטע האט געזאגט בשם רבינו הזקן: אזומערדיגער טאג און אווינטערדיגע נאכט איז א יאהר.
hayomYom.clear:
You must guard your time. You must accept upon yourself the yoke of Torah. Every bit of time, every day that goes by, is not just a day, but a matter of your life.

The days go by, as the saying goes (Yerushalmi Berachos 1:1): “A day comes in and a day goes out, a week comes in... a month... a year...”

My father said in the name of the Alter Rebbe: A summer day and a winter night are a year.
translationNotes: היטען: to “guard, watch over” time. Kehot's “urgent” is not in the original.
דער טאטע: “Father,” the warm Yiddish word, not the formal אאמו"ר.

hayomYom.english: (At this point there appears in the Hebrew text emendations of Torah Or on this week's sedra, meaningful only in Hebrew. Translator).
hayomYom.hebrew: בתו"א [בתורה אור] פרשת חיי שרה סד"ה [סוף דיבור המתחיל] להבין משארז"ל [מה שאמרו רבותינו זכרונם לברכה] יפה שעה יש טה"ד [טעות הדפוס]. וכך צ"ל [צריך להיות]: "ויהי'[ה] בבחינת ביטול [אבל עכשיו.. היינו בחינת איסר ועמ"ש [ועיין מה שכתוב] לקמן בפירוש אוסרי לגפן] שהוא בחינת חפץ וכתיב הודו.. תוך כ"ע [כל עלמין], אבל תכלית הכוונה".
hayomYom.clear: In Torah Or, Parshas Chayei Sarah, at the end of the maamar L'havin mah she'amru Rabboseinu: Yafeh sha'ah, there is a printing error. It should read: “And it will be in a state of bittul [but now... that is, the level of isser (binding); see what is written below on the explanation of osri lagefen] which is the level of chefetz (desire), and it is written Hodu... within all worlds, but the ultimate intention.”
translationNotes: Kehot skips this as relevant only in Hebrew. Translated here so the correction can still be read.
טה"ד: a printer's error. The bracketed words are part of the corrected text, not additions.
hayomYom.dataFlag: Hebrew emendation is elliptical; the corrected passage is fragmentary and only partly clear without the Torah Or text.

hayomYom.english: A response of the Alter Rebbe in a yechidus: Chassidus is Sh'ma Yisrael. The word sh'ma is an acronym of s'u marom eineichem, "Raise your eyes on high." The verse says "on high" (marom), and not "to the heavens" (shamayim). "On high" means higher and still higher, to attain a level beyond intellect, and grasp this itself intellectually - as the verse concludes, "and see Who created these."
hayomYom.hebrew: מענה רבינו הזקן ליחידות: חסידות איז שמע ישראל, שמע איז ר"ת [ראשי תיבות] שאו מרום עיניכם, ואומר מרום ולא שמים, מרום איז העכער און העכער, להגיע למעלה מן השכל. וזה גופא להבינו בשכל, וכמו שאומר וראו מי ברא אלה.
hayomYom.clear:
The Alter Rebbe's answer at a yechidus: Chassidus is Shema Yisrael. Shema is an acronym of Se'u marom eineichem, “Lift your eyes on high” (Yeshaya 40:26).

It says “on high” and not “to the heavens.” “On high” means higher and higher, to reach above intellect. And that itself, to grasp it with the intellect, as it continues, “and see Who created these.”
translationNotes: העכער און העכער: “higher and higher,” endless ascent.
וזה גופא להבינו בשכל: the goal is to grasp in the mind what is itself above the mind.

hayomYom.english: Birth of R. Shalom Dovber in the year which the Tzemach Tzedek termed Kitra ("crown") - 5621 (1860). He was named for the Mitteler Rebbe and half the name of the Tzemach Tzedek's father.
