Every year my father delivered a maamar on his birthday, but he did so secretly except when it coincided with Shabbat. On his last birthday here on earth he said the maamar Natata lirei'echa neiss... When he concluded he said to me, "on one's birthday he should say Chassidus. May G‑d give you a gift that you may say Chassidus on your birthday, but it should be with kindness and mercy." It took seven years for this to happen.
hayomYom.hebrew:
יום הולדת את אדמו"ר [אדננו מורנו ורבנו] מהורש"ב [מורנו הרב ורבינו רבי שלום בער] נ"ע [נשמתו עדן]- שנת כתר"א - כלשון הצ"צ [הצמח צדק]. נקרא ע"ש [על שם] אדמו"ר האמצעי וחצי שם אביו של הצ"צ [הצמח צדק].

בכל שנה ביום הולדתו היה אאמו"ר [אדני אבי מורי ורבי] אומר דא"ח [דברי אלקים חיים], אלא שהיה בחשאי, מלבד כשאירע בש"ק [בשבת קודש]. ביום ההולדת האחרון בעלמא דין אמר מאמר נתת ליראך נס להתנוסס מפני קושט סלה. כשסיים אמר לי ביום הולדת צריך לומר חסידות. יתן השם יתברך לך מתנה שתאמר חסידות ביום הולדת שלך אלא שיהיה בחסד וברחמים - האט עס געדויערט זיבען יאהר.
hayomYom.clear:
Birthday of our Rebbe, R. Shalom DovBer [the Rebbe Rashab], in the year 5621 [1860], “Kesra” [crown], as the Tzemach Tzedek called it. He was named after the Mitteler Rebbe and with half the name of the Tzemach Tzedek's father.

Every year on his birthday, my father would say Chassidus, but quietly, except when it fell on Shabbos. On his last birthday in this world, he said the maamar Nasata liyrei'echa nes l'hisnoses mipnei koshet selah. When he finished, he said to me: “On a birthday you should say Chassidus. May G‑d give you a gift, that you say Chassidus on your birthday, but it should be with kindness and mercy.”

It took seven years.
translationNotes: כתר"א: the letters of 5621 spell “kesra,” crown.
בחשאי: quietly, privately. Kehot's “secretly” is a bit strong.
בחסד וברחמים: he blessed it to come about in a kind and merciful way.

hayomYom.english: It is the avoda of davening which brings the comprehension of the brain into the emotional sensitivity of the heart - and (also brings) both of them together into the practical avoda of performing mitzvot with fear-of-Heaven and acquiring fine character-traits.
hayomYom.hebrew: עבודת התפלה היא המביאה השגת המוח בהרגשת הלב, ושניהם יחד בעבודה בפועל המצות ביראת שמים וקנין מדות טובות.
hayomYom.clear: It is the avoda of davening that brings the mind's understanding into the heart's feeling. And it brings both of them together into actual avoda: doing the mitzvos with fear of Heaven, and acquiring good character traits.
translationNotes: Matches the original. No meaning lost.

hayomYom.english: One of the teachings of the Maggid of Mezritch, heard by the Alter Rebbe when he was in Mezritch for the first time, from late summer 5524 (1764) until after Pesach 5525 (1765): "I (Anochi) have made the earth, and upon it created man." Anochi, He who is the true "I", unknown to and concealed from even the loftiest emanations, clothed His blessed Essence through numerous condensations to give rise to the emanations and creatures, to Serafim, Chayot, Ofanim, angels and "worlds" beyond number. Through countless condensations, "I made this (physical) world and upon it created (barati) man." Man is the end-purpose of Creation, and barati is the end-purpose of man. (Barati, "I created," has the numerical equivalent of 613, the number of scriptural commandments). As (the book of) Pardes quotes Sefer Habahir: "Said the attribute of Chessed (kindness) before the Holy One Blessed-be-He, Master of the Universe, since the days Avram has been on earth, I have not had to perform my task, because Avram stands and serves in my stead." Because Avraham - a soul clothed in a body, occupying himself with hospitality to strangers as a means of disseminating the idea of G‑d in this lowly world - is actually on a higher plane and level than the attribute of kindness of Atzilut. The complaint ("Said the attribute of Chessed before the Holy One etc.") is an expression of envy of Avraham's service by the attribute of kindness of Atzilut.
hayomYom.hebrew:
אחת מתורות המגיד ממעזריטש ששמע רבינו הזקן בהיותו שם בפעם הראשונה - שלהי קיץ תקכ"ד עד אחרי חה"פ [חג הפסח] תקכ"ה:

אנכי עשיתי ארץ ואדם עליה בראתי. אנכי מי שאנכי, שהוא נעלם ונסתר גם מנאצלים היותר עליונים, הלביש עצמותו יתברך בכמה צמצומים להאציל הנאצלים ולברוא הנבראים, שרפים חיות ואופנים מלאכים ועולמות עד אין מספר, ובצמצומים עד אין שיעור עשיתי ארץ הלזו הגשמית. ואדם עליה בראתי, האדם הוא תכלית ההתהוות, ובראתי בגמטריא תרי"ג הוא תכלית האדם, וכדאיתא בפרדס בשם ספר הבהיר, אמרה מדת החסד לפני הקב"ה [הקדוש ברוך הוא], רבונו של עולם מימי היות אברם בארץ לא הוצרכתי אני לעשות מלאכתי, שהרי אברם עומד ומשמש במקומי. כי אברהם שהוא נשמה בגוף, ועוסק בהכנסת אורחים לפרסם אלקותו יתברך בעולם הזה התחתון הוא למעלה במעלה ובמדריגה לגבי מדת החסד דאצילות. ואמרה מדת החסד לפני הקב"ה [הקדוש ברוך הוא], הוא קנאת מדת החסד דאצילות, אשר קנאה בעבודת אברהם ע"ה [עליו השלום].
hayomYom.clear:
One of the teachings of the Maggid of Mezritch, which the Alter Rebbe heard when he was there for the first time, from late summer 5524 [1764] until after Pesach 5525 [1765]:

“I made the earth, and created man upon it” (Yeshaya 45:12).

“I”: the One who is “I,” who is hidden and concealed even from the highest emanated beings. He clothed His blessed Essence in many contractions in order to emanate the emanated beings and create the created beings: Seraphim, Chayos, Ofanim, angels and worlds without number. And through contractions without measure, “I made” this physical earth.

“And created man upon it”: Man is the purpose of all existence. And barasi [“I created”] has the numerical value of 613, which is the purpose of man.

As the Pardes brings in the name of Sefer HaBahir: The attribute of Chessed said before G‑d, “Master of the world, ever since Avram has been on earth, I have not needed to do my work, because Avram stands and serves in my place.”

Because Avraham, a soul in a body, busy with hospitality in order to make G‑dliness known in this lowly world, is on a higher plane and level than the attribute of Chessed of Atzilus. And “the attribute of Chessed said before G‑d” expresses the envy of the attribute of Chessed of Atzilus, which envied the avoda of Avraham.
translationNotes: אנכי מי שאנכי: “I, who is I,” G‑d's own self, hidden even from the highest levels.
צמצומים עד אין שיעור: contractions beyond measure.
קנאה: envy. A divine attribute envies a human being's service.

hayomYom.english: The Tzemach Tzedek was arrested twenty-two times during the Rabbinical conference in Petersburg, in 5603 (1843), for opposing the demands of the government regarding changes in education, etc. The minister in charge confronted him: "Is this not rebellion against the government?!" The Tzemach Tzedek answered: "A rebel against the government is liable to be punished by death of the body; a rebel against the Kingdom of Heaven is punishable by death of the soul. Now which is worse?"
hayomYom.hebrew: צוויי און צוואנציג מאל האט מען ארערסטירט דעם צ"צ [צמח צדק] אויף דער אסיפת הרבנים אין פעטערבורג, תר"ג, פאר זיין אנטקעגענשטעלען זיך דער פאדערונג פון דער מלוכה וועגען שינוים בחנוך וכו'. דער מיניסטער האט אים געפרעגט: דאס איז דאך מרידה במלכות? דער צ"צ [צמח צדק] האט געענטפערט: מורד במלכות איז חייב מיתה בגוף, אבער מורד במלכות שמים איז חייב מיתה בנפש. איז וואס איז גרעסער?
hayomYom.clear:
The Tzemach Tzedek was arrested twenty-two times during the rabbinical conference in Petersburg, 5603 [1843], for standing up against the government's demand for changes in education, etc.

The minister asked him: “But this is rebellion against the government?”

The Tzemach Tzedek answered: “A rebel against the government deserves death of the body. But a rebel against the Kingdom of Heaven deserves death of the soul. So which is greater?”
translationNotes: מורד במלכות: a legal term, “rebel against the kingdom,” from the Talmud (Sanhedrin 49a).
איז וואס איז גרעסער: “so which is greater?” Kehot's “worse” is fine.

hayomYom.english: In material matters one should always look at he whose situation is lower than one's own, and thank the good G‑d for His kindness to him. In spiritual matters one should always look at he who is higher than oneself, and plead with G‑d to grant him the intelligence to learn from the other, and the ability and strength to rise higher.
hayomYom.hebrew:
בענינים הגשמיים צריך להסתכל במי שהוא למטה ממנו, ולהודות להשי"ת [לה' יתברך] כי טוב על חסדו אתו עמו. -

בענינים הרוחניים צריך להסתכל במי שהוא למעלה ממנו ולהתחנן לה' שיתן לו דיעה טובה להתלמד ממנו וכח ועוז שיוכל לעלות בעילוי.
hayomYom.clear:
In material things, always look at someone who has less than you, and thank G‑d, for He is good, for the kindness He has shown you.

In spiritual things, always look at someone who stands higher than you, and plead with G‑d to give you a good mind to learn from him, and the strength and power to rise higher.
translationNotes: דיעה טובה is “a good mind,” a little more than “intelligence.”
כי טוב echoes the verse “Thank G‑d, for He is good” (Tehillim 136:1).

hayomYom.english: Divine Providence leads everyone to his place of residence for the purpose of strengthening yiddishkeit and disseminating Torah. When you plow and you sow - things will grow.
hayomYom.hebrew:
השגחה העליונה בריינגט יעדען אין זיין וואוינארט צוליב חיזוק היהדות והרבצת התורה.

ווען מען אקערט און מען פארזייט - וואקסט.
hayomYom.clear:
Divine Providence brings each person to the place where he lives so that he can strengthen Yiddishkeit and spread Torah there.

When you plow and sow, things grow.
translationNotes: Matches the Yiddish closely. No meaning lost.

hayomYom.english: The true way is to know one's character, truly recognizing one's own deficiencies and one's good qualities. And when one knows his deficiencies - he should correct them with actual avoda, and not satisfy himself merely with bemoaning them.
hayomYom.hebrew: הדרך האמיתי הוא שצריכים לדעת מהות עצמו, בהכרה אמיתית בחסרונות עצמו ובמעלות עצמו. וכאשר יודעים את החסרונות - לתקנם בעבודה בפועל, ולא לצאת ידי חובתו באנחות בלבד.
hayomYom.clear:
The true path is to know yourself: to honestly recognize both your shortcomings and your strengths.

Once you know your shortcomings, fix them through real, practical avoda [spiritual work]. Don’t think that sighing over them fulfills your duty.
translationNotes: באנחות בלבד means “with sighs alone.” “Bemoaning” softens a pointed Chassidic idea: a sigh is not a substitute for action.
לצאת ידי חובתו is “to discharge one’s obligation,” not just “satisfy himself.”

hayomYom.english: R. Aizik Homiler related: When I came to Lyozna I met elder chassidim who had been chassidim of the Maggid and of R. Menachem Mendel of Horodok. They used to say: Have affection for a fellow-Jew and G‑d will have affection for you; do a kindness for a fellow-Jew and G‑d will do a kindness for you; befriend a fellow-Jew and G‑d will befriend you.
hayomYom.hebrew: ר' אייזיק הלוי מהאמלי סיפר: כשבאתי לליאזנא מצאתי מזקני החסידים שהיו מחסידי הה"מ [הרב המגיד] והרה"ק [והרב הקדוש] הרמ"מ [הרב מנחם מענדל] מהאראדאק, והוה מרגלא בפומייהו: האב האלט א אידען, וועט השי"ת [השם יתברך] דיר האלט האבען, טו א טובה א אידען, וועט השי"ת [השם יתברך] דיר א טובה טאן, זיי מקרב א אידען וועט השי"ת [השם יתברך] דיר מקרב זיין.
hayomYom.clear:
R. Aizik HaLevi of Homil related: When I came to Lyozna, I met elderly chassidim who had been followers of the Maggid and of R. Menachem Mendel of Horodok. They had a saying that was always on their lips:

Love a fellow Jew, and G‑d will love you.
Do a favor for a fellow Jew, and G‑d will do a favor for you.
Draw a fellow Jew close, and G‑d will draw you close.
translationNotes: זיי מקרב א אידען is “draw a Jew close.” The old English “befriend” loses the core idea of kiruv.
האב האלט is warm fondness: “love,” not just “affection.”
והוה מרגלא בפומייהו means it was a habitual saying of theirs.

hayomYom.english: The concept of Divine Providence is this: Not only are all particular movements of the various creatures directed by Providence, and not only is that Providence itself the life-force and maintained existence of every creature - but even more, the particular movement of any creature is in general terms related to the grand design of Creation... The aggregate of all individual acts brings to completion G‑d's grand design in the mystery of all Creation. Ponder this: If the swaying of a blade of grass is brought about by Divine Providence and is crucial to the fulfillment of the purpose of Creation, how much more so with regard to mankind in general, and Israel (the people close to him) in particular!
hayomYom.hebrew:
ענין ההשגחה פרטית הוא, דלא זו בלבד דכל פרטי תנועות הנבראים למיניהם הם בהשגחה פרטית, והיא היא חיות הנברא וקיומו, אלא עוד זאת דתנועה פרטית של נברא יש לה יחס כללי לכללות כונת הבריאה... דבצרוף ואיחוד כל הפעולות הפרטיות... נשלמה כונה העליונה בסוד הבריאה כולה.

ויתבונן האדם: ומה אם תנועת עשב באה בהשגח"פ [בהשגחה פרטית] ונוגעת להשלמת כונת הבריאה, מין המדבר בכלל וישראל עם קרובו בפרט על אחת כמה וכמה.
hayomYom.clear:
This is what Divine Providence means. It is not only that every movement of every kind of creature is directed by Providence. And it is not only that this Providence is itself the life of each creature and what keeps it in existence. More than that: each individual movement of any creature has a connection to the overall purpose of Creation... By combining and uniting all the individual actions, G‑d’s supreme intent within the mystery of all Creation is brought to completion.

Think about it: if even the swaying of a blade of grass comes about through Divine Providence and matters to fulfilling Creation’s purpose, how much more is this true of humankind in general, and of Israel, His close people, in particular!
translationNotes: בסוד הבריאה is “the mystery of Creation.” Kept.
ונוגעת is “matters to,” softer than the old “crucial.”
מין המדבר (“the speaking species”) is humankind.

hayomYom.english:
Bless Rosh Chodesh Kislev. Say the entire Tehillim in the early morning. Day of farbrengen.

We cannot adequately describe the great merit of those who participate in the sacred avoda of saying Tehillim with a minyan, and the great pleasure this avoda causes On High, as discussed in sacred texts and in very tiny part in Kuntres Takanat Amirat Tehillim B'rabim (Koveitz Michtavim 1). How fortunate are you Israel, and for this may you all be blessed with proper health and with super-abundant livelihood - you, your wives, your sons and your daughters (G‑d grant them eternal life.) In your merit may all the congregation of Israel in your communities be helped (among all our Jewish brethren) in all they need, materially and spiritually.
hayomYom.hebrew:
מברכים ר"ח [ראש חדש] כסלו. אמירת כל התהילים בהשכמה. יום התוועדות.

עבודה הקדושה באמירת תהלים בצבור, אין די באר גודל הזכות של המשתתפים בזה, וגודל הנחת רוח של מעלה כמבואר בספרי קודש, ואפס קצהו בקונטרס תקנת אמירת תהלים ברבים [קובץ מכתבים, א], ואשריכם ישראל, ובגלל זאת תתברכו אתם נשיכם בניכם ובנותיכם, ה' עליהם יחיו, בבריאות נכונה ובפרנסה בהרחבה גדולה, ולרגליכם יושעו כל עדת ישראל שיחיו במחנכם הט'[הורה] בתוך כלל אחב"י [אחינו בני ישראל] בהדרוש להם בגשם וברוח.
hayomYom.clear:
Words cannot fully describe the great merit of those who take part in the holy avoda of saying Tehillim together with a minyan, or the great pleasure it brings On High. This is explained in sacred texts, and to a very small extent in Kuntres Takanat Amirat Tehillim B’rabim (Koveitz Michtavim 1).

Fortunate are you, Israel! For this, may you be blessed, you, your wives, your sons and your daughters (may G‑d be with them, may they live), with good health and abundant livelihood. And in your merit, may every Jew in your pure camp, along with all our Jewish brethren, be helped in everything they need, materially and spiritually.
translationNotes: ה’ עליהם יחיו (Yeshayahu 38:16) is “may G‑d be with them, may they live.” The old “eternal life” overreaches.
במחנכם הטהורה is “your pure camp.” The old English drops “pure.”
The old English leaves out the calendar line entirely.

calendar.original5703: Shabbos Mevarchim Kislev. Say the entire Tehillim early in the morning. A day of farbrengen.
calendar.thisYear5787: This year Shabbos Mevarchim Kislev is Shabbos, Nov 7 (27 Cheshvan).

hayomYom.english: There were periods of time when R. Yekusiel Liepler, a chassid of the Alter Rebbe, davened Shacharit, Mincha and Maariv one right after the other; there was no time for intervals.
hayomYom.hebrew: בא ר' יקותיאל ליעפלער [דעם אלטען רבי'ס א חסיד] איז געווען צייטען, וואס ער האט געדאווענט שחרית מנחה און מעריב איינע נאך די אנדערע, עס איז ניט געווען קיין זמן מפסיק זיין.
hayomYom.clear: There were times when R. Yekusiel Liepler, a chassid of the Alter Rebbe, davened Shacharis, Mincha and Maariv one right after another. There was no time to stop in between.
translationNotes: קיין זמן מפסיק זיין: “no time to pause.” His davening was long enough to run straight into the next prayer.

hayomYom.english: My grandfather once explained in a maamar the statement, R. Elazar first gave a coin to a pauper and then davened: "Davening must be with life. By giving, before davening, charity to a pauper - thereby giving him life - one's davening is suffused with a great increase of 'aliveness'." So saying he motioned with his hand in an upwards gesture to indicate that the increase is beyond imagination. Indeed my father would often seek out a pauper before davening to give him food.
hayomYom.hebrew: אאזמו"ר [אדני אבי זקני מורי ורבי] ביאר פעם במאמר, הא דרבי אלעזר יהיב פרוטה לעני והדר מצלי, כי הרי התפלה צ"ל [צריכה להיות] בחיות, וע"י [ועל ידי] שנותנים צדקה לעני קודם התפלה ומחיים אותו, ניתוסף חיות הרבה בתפלה. ונענע בידו ממטה למעלה לרמז שהרבוי בהפלאה. - וכמה פעמים קודם התפלה היה אאמו"ר [אדני אבי מורי ורבי] מחזר אחרי עני ליתן לו לאכול.
hayomYom.clear:
My grandfather [the Rebbe Maharash] once explained, in a maamar [Chassidic discourse], the teaching that R. Elazar would first give a coin to a poor man and only then daven. Davening must be full of life. When you give charity to a poor man before davening, you give him life, and so your davening gains a great deal of life.

As he said this, he moved his hand from low to high, to hint that the increase is wondrous.

Indeed, many times before davening, my father [the Rebbe Rashab] would look for a poor man so he could give him something to eat.
translationNotes: אאזמו"ר is the Rebbe Maharash; אאמו"ר is the Rebbe Rashab.
The source is Bava Basra 10a.
בהפלאה is “wondrous.” The Hebrew is indirect speech, so the old English’s quote marks are dropped.

hayomYom.english: One difference between the ways of the Baal Shem Tov and of the Maggid was that the Baal Shem Tov went on all sorts of journeys, while the Maggid stayed home. Moreover, when the Maggid was Rebbe, Chassidus was already widely known, even in distant places, because of the extensive journeys of the Holy Society. Many average laymen had thus become devoted to Chassidus and used to make pilgrimages to Mezritch.
hayomYom.hebrew: מההפרש בין הנהגת הבעש"ט [הבעל שם טוב] להנהגת המגיד, כי הבעש"ט היה עסוק בנסיעות שונות, והמגיד ישב בביתו. עוד זאת: בימי נשיאות המגיד, כבר היה מפורסם ענין החסידות גם במרחקים, ע"י [על ידי] נסיעות החבריא קדישא, ורבים מבע"ב [מבעלי בתים] בינונים נתקשרו לתורת החסידות והיו נוסעים למעזריטש.
hayomYom.clear:
One difference between the way the Baal Shem Tov led and the way the Maggid led: the Baal Shem Tov was busy with all kinds of journeys, while the Maggid stayed home.

Also, by the time the Maggid led the movement, Chassidus was already known even in distant places, because of the journeys of the Holy Society [the Baal Shem Tov’s circle of disciples]. Many ordinary householders had bound themselves to the teachings of Chassidus and would travel to Mezritch.
translationNotes: בעלי בתים בינונים: ordinary householders, not scholars.
נתקשרו לתורת החסידות: “bound themselves” to it, stronger than “devoted.”

hayomYom.english: With mayim acharonim, wash the fingertips and, while they are still moist, pass them over the lips.
hayomYom.hebrew: למים אחרונים נוטלים קצה האצבעות, ואחר כך מעבירים אותם, כשהם לחים עדיין, על השפתים.
hayomYom.clear: For mayim acharonim [the washing at the end of a meal], wash just the tips of the fingers. Then, while they are still wet, pass them over your lips.
translationNotes: Matches the Hebrew. No meaning lost.

hayomYom.english: "A ladder was standing on the ground." Prayer is the ladder that connects souls and G‑dhood. And although it stands "...on the ground," the start of davening being no more than acknowledgement, yet "its top reaches the Heavens" - a state of total bitul, self-nullification. But one reaches this level through the prior attainment of comprehension and understanding inherent in p'sukei d'zimra, in the b'rachot of sh'ma and in sh'ma proper.
hayomYom.hebrew: והנה סולם מוצב ארצה - תפלה היא סולם ההתקשרות של הנשמה באלקות. והגם שהוא מוצב ארצה, התחלת התפלה היא בהודאה לבד, אבל וראשו מגיע השמימה, בבחינת ביטול עצמי אבל בא לזה ע"י [על ידי] הקדמת ההשגה וההבנה בפסוקי דזמרה ברכות ק"ש [קריאת שמע] וק"ש [וקריאת שמע].
hayomYom.clear:
“A ladder was set on the ground” (Bereishis 28:12). Prayer is the ladder that binds the soul to G‑dliness.

It is “set on the ground”: davening begins with simple acknowledgment and nothing more. Yet “its top reaches the heavens”: it rises to complete self-nullification [bittul].

But you reach that only by first gaining comprehension and understanding in Pesukei d’Zimra, the blessings of Shema, and the Shema itself.
translationNotes: סולם ההתקשרות של הנשמה באלקות: the ladder of the soul’s bond with G‑dliness. “Connects souls and G‑dhood” is stiff.
השגה והבנה: comprehension and understanding come first. The order is the point.

hayomYom.english: My father said that the reciting of sh'ma before retiring at night (p. 118-124) is, in miniature form, like the Confession before death. But then one leaves the marketplace permanently, and the commerce of "Today to perform them" is finished. With the Bedside Sh'ma every night, however, one is still in the middle of the "market" and can still accomplish and achieve.
hayomYom.hebrew: אאמו"ר [אדני אבי מורי ורבי] אמר: קריאת שמע שעל המטה איז, אין זעיר אנפין, ווי דער ווידוי וואס קודם צאת הנפש מהגוף. נאר יעמאלט גייט מען שוין אינגאנצען אוועק פון יריד, און עס ענדיגט זיך שוין דער מסחר פון היום לעשותם, און אין קשעהמ"ט [קריאת שמע שעל המטה] פון יעדער נאכט האלט מען נאך אין מיטן יריד, און מען קען נאך אויפטאן.
hayomYom.clear:
My father said: The Shema said at bedtime is, on a small scale, like the viduy [confession] said before the soul leaves the body.

The difference: at that final moment, you leave the fair for good, and the business of “today, to do them” [this world, the time for doing mitzvos] is over. But at the bedtime Shema each night, you are still in the middle of the fair, and you can still get things done.
translationNotes: יריד is a trade fair. Life is a busy market where deals can still be made.
“Today, to do them” is Devarim 7:11, read in Eruvin 22a as: today is for doing, tomorrow is for reward.
זעיר אנפין: “in miniature.”

hayomYom.english: There are three schools of thought: 1. The school of thought that negates [preoccupation with] materiality by pointing out the disgusting and abhorrent nature of all bodily and material things. This is the school of Mussar. 2. The school of recognition of the superiority of the "inner form" and the spiritual - the dimension of character-traits and intellectuality - and instruction as to how one may come closer to attaining these. This is the school of Chakira, philosophy. 3. The discipline of predominance of form over matter. This school teaches the unique quality of the material when it is purified, and the unique quality of "form" when integrated with the material; the two are to be so thoroughly fused that one cannot detect where either of them begins or ends - for "Their beginning is wedged into their end, and their end into their beginning." The One G‑d created them both, and for one purpose - to reveal the light of Holiness of His hidden power. Only both of them together will complete the perfection desired by the Creator. This is the school of (the teachings/instruction of) Chassidus.
hayomYom.hebrew:
הפטורה: ועמי - תלמי שדי. ויברח יעקב - ובאשה שמר. ובנביא העלה - ובנביא נשמר.

שלש חכמות הן: חכמת ביטול החומר, ע"י [על ידי] הוראת שקוץ ותיעוב כל ענינים הגופניים והחומריים - חכמת המוסר.

חכמת הכרת מעלת הצורה והרוחני במדות ובמושכלות והוראת אופני הקירוב אליהם - חכמת החקירה.

חכמת הגברת הצורה על החומר, הוראה במעלת חומר מזוכך ובמעלת הצורה כשנקבעה בהחומרי, והתכללותם יחד מבלי אשר ימצא ראש וסוף, להיות כי נעוץ תחלתן בסופן וסופן בתחלתן, אל אחד בראם, ולכוונה אחת לגלות אור קדושת חביון עוזו יתברך נבראו, ושניהם כאחד דוקא משלימים אותה השלימות, אשר עלה ברצונו יתברך - חכמת תורת החסידות.
hayomYom.clear:
There are three disciplines:

1. The discipline that negates the physical by teaching how repulsive and loathsome all bodily and material things are. This is Mussar.

2. The discipline that teaches the superiority of form and the spiritual, in character traits and in intellect, and teaches ways to draw closer to them. This is Chakirah [philosophy].

3. The discipline that makes form prevail over matter. It teaches the virtue of refined matter, and the virtue of form once it is set within the material, and how the two merge so completely that no beginning or end can be found, since “their beginning is wedged in their end, and their end in their beginning” (Sefer Yetzirah 1:7). One G‑d created them both, and they were created for one purpose: to reveal the light of the holiness of His hidden power. And specifically both of them together complete the perfection that G‑d desired. This is the teaching of Chassidus.
translationNotes: חביון עוזו is from Chavakuk 3:4, “there His power is hidden.”
דוקא: it is specifically the two together. The old English “only” is close.
Old English adds “[preoccupation with]” to the first school. The Hebrew just says “negating the physical.” Left out.

calendar.original5703: Haftorah: V’ami s’luyim, to talmei sadai. Vayivrach Yaakov, to uv’isha shamar. Uv’navi he’ela, to uv’navi nishmar.
calendar.thisYear5787: This is the Vayeitzei haftorah. This year Vayeitzei is Shabbos, Nov 21 (11 Kislev).

hayomYom.english: Man should ponder thoughtfully how great are the kindnesses of the Creator: Such a puny insignificant being, Man, can bring great delight to the "Greatest of all great"' of Whom it is written, "There is no delving into His greatness." Man ought therefore always be inspired, and perform his avoda with an eager heart and spirit.
hayomYom.hebrew: א מענטש זאל זיך מתבונן זיין, ווי גרויס חסדי הבורא ב"ה [ברוך הוא] זיינען, אז אזא קטן שבקטנים ווי דער מענטש איז, קען ער מאכען א נחת רוח גדול צום גדול הגדולים וכמ"ש [וכמו שכתוב] ולגדולתו אין חקר, דארף דער מענטש זיין תמיד באגייסטערט און טאן די עבודה בלב ונפש חפצה.
hayomYom.clear:
A person should think deeply about how great the Creator’s kindness is: man, the smallest of the small, can bring great pleasure to the Greatest of the great, of Whom it is written, “His greatness is beyond searching” (Tehillim 145:3).

So a person should always be inspired, and do his avoda with a heart and soul that truly want it.
translationNotes: קטן שבקטנים / גדול הגדולים: “smallest of the small” against “Greatest of the great.” The mirror is kept.
באגייסטערט (Yiddish): fired up, inspired.
בלב ונפש חפצה echoes Divrei Hayamim I 28:9.

hayomYom.english: Birth of the Mitteler Rebbe in 5534 (1773), and the day of his passing in 5588 (1827). He is interred in Niezhin. On 9 Kislev 5554 (1793) the Alter Rebbe said a maamar, now part of Chapter 53 of the Sefer Shel Benonim (Tanya), discussing the First Sanctuary. The next day he said Chassidus again - the conclusion of that chapter. The maamarim from Rosh Hashana 5550 (1789) until 10 Kislev 5554 (1793) which included assembled words of counsel from earlier years, were the basis for the 53 chapters of the Sefer Shel Benonim.
hayomYom.hebrew:
יום הולדת את אדמו"ר [אדננו מורנו ורבנו] האמצעי - תקל"ד - ויום הסתלקותו - תקפ"ח. ומ"כ [ומנוחתו כבוד] בניעזשין.

ט' בכסלו תקנ"ד אמר רבינו הזקן מאמר - והוא חלק פרק נ"ג מספר של בינונים [תניא] המדבר על דבר בית ראשון. למחרתו אמר חסידות עוד הפעם - סיום פרק הנ"ל [הנזכר לעיל] עד גמירא. כי המאמרים מר"ה [מראש השנה] תק"ן עד י' כסלו תקנ"ד [אשר בהם נכללו לקוטי עצות משנים הקודמות] מהם נסדרו נ"ג פרקי ספר של בינונים.
hayomYom.clear:
Birthday of the Mitteler Rebbe, in 5534 (1773), and the day of his passing, in 5588 (1827). He is buried in Niezhin.

On 9 Kislev 5554 (1793), the Alter Rebbe said a maamar that is now part of Chapter 53 of Sefer Shel Beinonim [Tanya], which discusses the First Temple. The next day he said Chassidus again: the rest of that chapter, to its end.

The 53 chapters of Sefer Shel Beinonim were arranged from the maamarim he said from Rosh Hashanah 5550 (1789) until 10 Kislev 5554 (1793), which included collected words of counsel from earlier years.
translationNotes: בית ראשון is the First Temple. “First Sanctuary” is less clear.
עד גמירא: to the very end of the chapter.

hayomYom.english: On this day in 5587 (1826) the Mitteler Rebbe was released from his imprisonment in the city of Vitebsk. During the preceding Chol Hamo'ed Sukot it became known that the Mitteler Rebbe had been slandered. On Sunday of parshat Noach, 28 Tishrei, he left Lubavitch accompanied by officers. At noon he arrived in Dobromisl, where he said the maamar Mayim rabim etc. On Monday he left there, and travelled to Lyozna, where he said the maamar Reshafeha rishpei etc. On Tuesday he left there for Vitebsk where he remained imprisoned until the Sunday of Vayishlach, 10 Kislev.
hayomYom.hebrew: אדמו"ר [אדננו מורנו ורבנו] האמצעי יצא לחירות - תקפ"ז - ממאסרו בעיר וויטעפסק. בחוהמ"ס [בחול המועד סוכות] נודע אשר הלשינו את אדמו"ר [אדננו מורנו ורבנו] האמצעי. ביום א' פרשת נח כח תשרי נסע בלוית פקידים מליובאוויטש, בצהרים בא לדאבראמיסל, אמר שם דא"ח [דברי אלקים חיים] מים רבים גו', יום ב' נסע משם עד ליאזנא, אמר שם דא"ח [דברי אלקים חיים] רשפיה רשפי גו', יום ג' משם לוויטעפסק, וישב שם תפוס עד יום א' וישלח י' כסלו.
hayomYom.clear:
On this day in 5587 (1826), the Mitteler Rebbe was freed from imprisonment in the city of Vitebsk.

During Chol Hamoed Sukkos it became known that people had informed against him. On Sunday of parshas Noach, 28 Tishrei, he left Lubavitch escorted by officials. At noon he reached Dobromisl, where he said the maamar Mayim rabim. On Monday he went on to Lyozna, where he said the maamar Reshafeha rishpei. On Tuesday he went from there to Vitebsk, where he was held prisoner until Sunday of Vayishlach, 10 Kislev.
translationNotes: הלשינו: “informed against him” to the authorities. More exact than “slandered.”
דא"ח (Divrei Elokim Chaim) is a Chassidic discourse.

hayomYom.english: (At this point there appears in the Hebrew text emendations to the Siddur-With-Chassidus, that have meaning only in the Hebrew original. Translator).
hayomYom.hebrew:
מהגהות אאמו"ר [אדני אבי מורי ורבי] על הסידור "סדר התפלה" [עם הדא"ח [הדברי אלקים חיים]]: ח"א [חלק א'] ד"ה [דיבור המתחיל] ברוך שאמר והיה העולם [לט. ד]: "משא"כ [מה שאין כן] בחינת רדל"א [רישא דלא אתידע]", ניתקן "ומעתה יובן פירוש וענין בחינת רדל"א".

ח"ב [חלק ב'] ד"ה [דיבור המתחיל] עד הגל [דש. ד]: "לרבנן והלכה כר"י [כרבי יהודה] שבירך", ניתקן "לרבנן אם בירך".

שם: "דעת ר"י [רבי יהודה] וכן האמת" העביר קולמוס על "וכן האמת".

שם [שה. א]: "התהו דנקודים" ניתקן "התהו דעקודים".
hayomYom.clear:
From my father’s corrections to the Siddur with Chassidus (Seder HaTefillah im Dach):

Part 1, maamar Baruch She’amar v’haya ha’olam [39d]: “whereas the level of Radla [Reisha d’lo Isyada, the Unknowable Head]” is corrected to “And from this, the meaning and concept of the level of Radla will be understood.”

Part 2, maamar Ad hagal [304d]: “according to the Rabbis, and the halacha follows R. Yehuda that he made the blessing” is corrected to “according to the Rabbis, if he made the blessing.”

Same place: “the view of R. Yehuda, and so is the truth.” He crossed out “and so is the truth.”

Same place [305a]: “the Tohu of Nekudim” is corrected to “the Tohu of Akudim.”
translationNotes: The old English skips this entry. This is a direct translation of the Hebrew corrections, so they can still be read.

hayomYom.english: Baruch shepetarani (Sidur p. 70) is said without mentioning G‑d's Name or Kinghood. It is said on Mondays, Thursdays or Rosh Chodesh, not only on Shabbat. We have a tradition attributed to the Baal Shem Tov: When one hears an uncomplimentary report about another Jew, even if he does not know the individual referred to, he should be very deeply pained. For one of these two is certainly in the wrong: If what they are saying about the individual is true, then he is defective; and if it is not true, then the talebearer is in an unhealthy situation.
hayomYom.hebrew:
ברכת שפטרני מברכים בלא שם ומלכות, ומברכים אותה גם ביום ב', ה', בר"ח [בראש חודש], ולאו דוקא בשבת.

מקובל בידינו בשם מורנו הבעש"ט [הבעל שם טוב]: כששומעים דבר לא טוב על אחד מישראל, גם אם אין מכירים אותו, צריך להצטער צער רב, כי אחד מהם הוא בודאי לא טוב: אם אמת הדבר שמספרים על פלוני, הלא הוא לא טוב, ואם אינו אמת הלא המספר נמצא במצב לא טוב.
hayomYom.clear:
The blessing Baruch shepetarani [said by a father when his son becomes bar mitzvah] is said without G‑d’s Name and Kingship. It is said on Monday, Thursday or Rosh Chodesh as well, not only on Shabbos.

We have a tradition in the name of our teacher, the Baal Shem Tov: When you hear something not good about a fellow Jew, even if you don’t know him, you should be deeply pained. Because one of the two is certainly not good. If what they say about him is true, then he is not good. And if it isn’t true, then the one telling it is in a situation that is not good.
translationNotes: The Hebrew says לא טוב (“not good”) three times on purpose. The old English breaks the echo with “defective” and “unhealthy.”

hayomYom.english: My father said: Chassidus changes what exists, and uncovers the essence-character. The essence-character of the Jewish person is beyond estimation and assessment, for he is a part of (G‑d's) Essence, and whoever lays hold of a part of The Essence is as though he lays hold of it all. Just as The Essence is unlimited, so is the part unlimited. This is similar to tzitzit being "on the corner" - i.e. "of the same material as the corner" of the garment. (The existence of the soul as an entity discrete from G‑d's Essence) is only because G‑d created the soul to be a created being; and Chassidus reveals the essence-character (of the soul).
hayomYom.hebrew: אמר אאמו"ר [אדני אבי מורי ורבי]: חסידות משנה את המציאות ומגלה את המהות. והמהות של האיש הישראלי אין להעריך ולשער, כי הוא חלק מן העצם, והתופס במקצתו כאלו תופס בכולו, וכשם שהעצם אין לו שעור כך החלק אין לו שעור, ע"ד [על דרך] הכנף מין כנף - עס איז מעהר ניט וואס עצמות האט בורא געווען א נשמה אז זי זאל זיין א נברא - וחסידות מגלה את המהות.
hayomYom.clear:
My father said: Chassidus changes a person’s existing state [metzius] and reveals his essence [mahus].

The essence of a Jew cannot be measured or assessed, because he is a part of G‑d’s very Essence. When you grasp part of the Essence, it is as if you grasp all of it. And just as the Essence has no limit, so the part has no limit. This is like the rule that tzitzis “on the corner” must be of the same kind as the corner [of the garment].

The only thing that makes the soul a separate being is that G‑d’s Essence created it to be a created being. And Chassidus reveals the essence.
translationNotes: מציאות / מהות: “existing state” against “essence.” These are technical terms, kept in brackets.
הכנף מין כנף: the tzitzis share the garment’s nature, as the soul shares G‑d’s.

hayomYom.english: Birkat hamazon (pp. 88-94) is said over a cup of wine even without ten (people having dined together). The cup is held in the palm of the hand, the fingers extending upward. Hold the cup from Rabossai mir velen benchen until after the third b'racha, when it is placed on the table. In one of my father's sichot, he explained a subject, of which this is the core: There are tzadik, yashar, tamim and chassid. Tzadik is so called regarding his fulfillment of the positive mitzvot, thereby eliciting revelations inherent in the creative order. Yashar is so called regarding his fulfillment of the negative mitzvot - which draws forth revelations beyond the creative order. Tamim, (man of) earnestness elicits revelations (from a level of G‑dliness at which) "the taste of the tree and its fruit is the same" - the co-joining of the Encompassing (soveiv) and Permeating (memalei) modes of Divine influence. Highest of all is Chassid, and here there are three levels: (a) Worldly affairs do not disturb or distract him. Every individual can, and every individual must, attain this level. (b) All his affairs "are G‑dliness." Though this level "is not distant from you etc.," it is still not within everyone's reach. (c) The level described in Tikunei Zohar, "Who is a chassid? He who conducts himself with benevolence towards his Creator - towards His nest" - which means that he seeks to unite the Holy One blessed be He, and His Shechina within those who dwell in the lower worlds - not merely to quench the thirst of his own soul; as explained in Tanya.
hayomYom.hebrew:
מברכין ברכת המזון בכוס של ברכה, אף שאין עשרה. הכוס על כף היד והאצבעות זקופות. אוחז הכוס מאמירת "רבותי מיר וועלען בענטשען" עד אחרי סיום ברכה שלישית, שאז מעמידו על השלחן.

באחת משיחותיו ביאר אאמו"ר [אדני אבי מורי ורבי] ותוכן דבריו: יש צדיק ישר תמים חסיד. צדיק ע"ש [על שם] קיום מ"ע [מצות עשה] - ממשיך גילוים דסדר ההשתלשלות. ישר ע"ש [על שם] קיום ל"ת [לא תעשה] - גילוים למעלה מסדר ההשתלשלות. תמים - ערנסטקייט - גילויים דטעם עצו ופריו שוים, התחברות סוכ"ע [סובב כל עלמין] וממכ"ע [וממלא כל עלמין]. למעלה מכולם חסיד, ויש בזה ג' מדריגות: א) שעניני העולם אינם מטרידים ומבלבלים אותו. כאו"א [כל אחד ואחד] יכול להגיע לזה וכאו"א [וכל אחד ואחד] מחוייב להגיע לזה. ב) שכל עניניו הם אלקות. ואף שלא רחוקה היא ממך גו', מ"מ [מכל מקום] אין זה שייך לכאו"א [לכל אחד ואחד]. ג) מ"ש [מה שכתוב] בת"ז [בתקוני זהר]: איזהו חסיד המתחסד עם קונו עם קן דיליה, ופירש בסש"ב [בספר של בינונים] שזהו ליחדא קובו"ש [קודשא בריך הוא ושכינתיה] בתחתונים ולא לרוות נפשו הצמאה בלבד.
hayomYom.clear:
Birkas Hamazon is said over a kos shel bracha [a cup of wine], even without ten. The cup rests on the palm of the hand with the fingers pointing up. Hold the cup from “Rabbosai mir velen bentchen” until the end of the third blessing, then put it on the table.

In one of his sichos, my father explained the following, in essence:

There are tzaddik, yashar, tamim and chassid.

Tzaddik is named for keeping the positive mitzvos. This draws down revelations within the order of the worlds [hishtalshelus].

Yashar is named for keeping the prohibitions. This draws down revelations beyond the order of the worlds.

Tamim means earnestness. It draws down revelations where “the taste of the tree and its fruit is the same”: the joining of the light that surrounds all worlds [sovev] and the light that fills all worlds [memalei].

Above all of them is chassid, which has three levels:
(a) Worldly matters do not trouble or confuse him. Everyone can reach this, and everyone must.
(b) Everything he does is G‑dliness. Though “it is not far from you,” still, it is not for everyone.
(c) As Tikkunei Zohar says: “Who is a chassid? One who is kind to his Maker, to His nest.” Tanya explains this to mean uniting the Holy One, blessed be He, with His Shechinah in the lower worlds, and not only quenching his own thirsty soul.
translationNotes: ערנסטקייט (Yiddish, “ernstkeit”) is seriousness or earnestness. The Rebbe Rashab chose a Yiddish word here.
“Taste of the tree and its fruit”: Bereishis 1:11 with Rashi.
The Tanya source is Chapter 10.

hayomYom.english: (An emendation to Torah Or parshat Vayeishev appears here, relevant only in Hebrew. Translator.) The Alter Rebbe told his son the Mitteler Rebbe: Grandfather (the Baal Shem Tov) said that one must have mesirat nefesh (total self-sacrifice and dedication) ahavat Yisrael (love of one's fellow), even towards a Jew whom one has never seen.
hayomYom.hebrew:
בתו"א [בתורה אור] ד"ה [דיבור המתחיל] וישב: "ואינה יכולה לראות באהבה" צ"ל [צריך להיות] "ואינה יכולה להיות באהבה".

רבינו הזקן סיפר לבנו אדמו"ר [אדננו מורנו ורבנו] האמצעי: דער זיידע [הבעש"ט [הבעל שם טוב]] זאגט אז מ'דארף האבען מסירת נפש אויף אהבת ישראל, אפילו צו א אידען, וועלכען מ'האט קיינמאל ניט געזעהן.
hayomYom.clear:
In Torah Or, maamar Vayeishev: “and cannot see in love” should read “and cannot be in love.”

The Alter Rebbe told his son, the Mitteler Rebbe: The Zeide [the Baal Shem Tov] says that you must have mesirus nefesh [total self-sacrifice] for ahavas Yisrael [love of a fellow Jew], even for a Jew you have never seen.
translationNotes: The old English skips the Torah Or correction. Translated here.
זאגט is present tense: the Baal Shem Tov “says.” The teaching is still alive.
“Zeide”: the Baal Shem Tov was the Alter Rebbe’s spiritual grandfather, his teacher’s teacher.

hayomYom.english: A fundamental principle of Chabad philosophy is that the mind, which by its innate nature rules over the heart,) must subordinate the heart to G‑d's service by utilizing the intellectualization, comprehension and profound contemplation of the greatness of the Creator of the universe.
hayomYom.hebrew: יסוד עיקרי בשיטת חב"ד הוא, אשר המוח השליט על הלב בתולדתו, ישעבד את הלב לעבודת השי"ת [ה' יתברך], מתוך השכלה הבנה והעמקת הדעת בגדולת בורא העולם ב"ה [ברוך הוא].
hayomYom.clear: A fundamental principle of the Chabad approach: the mind, which by its inborn nature rules over the heart, must harness the heart to serve G‑d. It does this by grasping, understanding and deeply contemplating the greatness of the Creator of the world.
translationNotes: השכלה, הבנה, והעמקת הדעת line up with Chochmah, Binah and Daas: the three letters of Chabad. That is the point of naming three steps.
ישעבד: “harness” or “subjugate” the heart.

hayomYom.english: Chassidus Chabad opens the gates to the chambers of chochma and bina, enabling one to know and to recognize - with intellectual comprehension - "He who spoke and the world came into being. It awakens the feelings of the heart so that it is aroused with the emotion engendered by that particular intellectual comprehension. And Chassidus Chabad shows the way that each individual - commensurate with his innate abilities - can "approach the Sacred," to serve G‑d with his mind and heart.
hayomYom.hebrew: חסידות חב"ד פותחת שערי היכלי חכמה ובינה, לידע ולהכיר את מי שאמר והיה העולם בהשגה שכלית, מעוררת רגשי הלב להתפעל באותה מדה שבלב המחוייבת מהשכלה זו, ומורה דרך אשר כל אחד ואחד לפום שיעורא דיליה יכול לגשת אל הקדש לעבוד את הוי'[ה] במוחו ולבו.
hayomYom.clear:
Chabad Chassidus opens the gates to the chambers of Chochmah and Binah, so that you can know and recognize, through intellectual grasp, “He Who spoke and the world came into being.”

It awakens the feelings of the heart, so the heart is stirred with exactly the emotion that this understanding calls for.

And it shows the way that each person, according to his own capacity, can approach the holy and serve G‑d with his mind and heart.
translationNotes: המחוייבת מהשכלה זו: the emotion the understanding requires. Emotion grows out of comprehension.
לפום שיעורא דיליה: each person by his own measure.

hayomYom.hebrew:
במנחה אין אומרים תחנון.

הצ"צ [הצמח צדק] כותב: אהבה דבחינת ועמך לא חפצתי [היינו] שלא לחפוץ שום דבר זולתו יתברך, ולא אפילו שמים וארץ שהם ג"ע [גן עדן] עליון ותחתון, כי רק ביו"ד נברא כו', אלא תהי'[ה] האהבה רק לו יתברך לבד, דהיינו למהו"ע [למהותו ועצמותו] יתברך ממש. וכך היה נשמע הלשון ממו"ר [ממורי ורבי] נ"ע [נשמתו עדן] רבינו הזקן בדביקותו, שהיה אומר בזה הלשון:

איך וויל זע גאר ניסט, איך וויל ניט דיין ג"ע [גן עדן] איך וויל ניט דיין עוה"ב [עולם הבא] כו' איך וויל מער ניט אז דיך אליין.

גוט יום טוב
לשנה טובה
בלימוד החסידות
ודרכי החסידות
תכתבו ותחתמו.

The Tzemach Tzedek writes: The love described in “Besides You I desire nothing” (Tehillim 73:25) means desiring nothing other than G‑d. Not even “heaven and earth,” meaning the Higher and Lower Gan Eden, since they were created with merely a yud [the smallest letter]... The love is to be for Him alone, for His very Being and Essence.

This is how my master and teacher, the Alter Rebbe, was heard to speak in his state of d’veikus [cleaving to G‑d]. He would say these words:

“I want nothing at all! I don’t want Your Gan Eden, I don’t want Your Olam Haba... I want nothing but You alone.”

Gut Yom Tov! May you be inscribed and sealed for a good year in the study of Chassidus and the ways of Chassidus.
translationNotes: “Created with a yud”: Menachos 29b, the World to Come was created with the letter yud.
איך וויל זע גאר ניסט is the Alter Rebbe’s famous Yiddish cry. The Yiddish is in the original column.
